The admonition to show rather than tell only applies to dramatized dialogue in acted scenes. Skillful, straightforward telling, whether on page, stage, or screen, whether in narratized dialogue or third-person narration, has two vital virtues: speed and counterpoint.

“展示而非讲述”的告诫仅适用于戏剧表演场景中的对话。无论是在书页、舞台还是银幕上，无论是叙述对话还是第三人称叙述，巧妙而直白的讲述都具有两个至关重要的优点：速度和对比。

1) Speed. Narration can pack a lot of exposition into a few fast words, plant understanding in the reader/audience, and move on. Inner monologues have the power to turn subtext into text in a blink. A character’s conversations with herself can leap randomly from memory to memory in free association, or flash with images that bob up from her subconscious. Such passages, beautifully written, can move emotion within a sentence. For example, from the Gabriel García Márquez novel One Hundred Years of Solitude : “Many years later, as he faced the firing squad, Colonel Aureliano Buendía was to remember that distant afternoon when his father took him to discover ice.” This is swift, vivid telling—a complex, concentrated image in a single sentence.

1）速度。叙述可以用寥寥数语快速传递大量信息，让读者/观众迅速理解，然后继续推进。内心独白能够瞬间将潜台词转化为明文。人物的内心对话可以自由联想，在记忆间跳跃，或者闪现潜意识中浮现的画面。这些优美的段落，能在短短一句话中传递情感。例如，在加西亚·马尔克斯的小说《百年孤独》中：“多年以后，当奥雷里亚诺·布恩迪亚上校面对行刑队时，他想起了父亲带他去发现冰的那个遥远的下午。”这是一种简洁生动的叙述——一个复杂而浓缩的画面浓缩于一句话之中。

However, all too often, filmic narration becomes a device to pump out bland exposition in the format of “and then… and then… and then.” This practice substitutes the easy work of telling for the arduous task of showing. Dialogue scenes on film and television that dramatize complex characters demand talent, knowledge, and imagination; word-thick narrations need only a keyboard.

然而，电影旁白常常沦为一种机械式的叙述工具，用“然后……然后……然后”的句式生硬地交代剧情。这种做法用简单的讲述取代了艰辛的展现。电影和电视剧中，刻画复杂人物的对话场景需要技巧、知识和想象力；而冗长的文字旁白只需要键盘敲击即可。

To turn narratized exposition into a dramatized scene, call upon one of two techniques:

要将叙述性的说明转化为戏剧化的场景，可以采用以下两种技巧之一：

One, interpolate a scene. Convert the “and then… and then… and then” of telling into a narrated scene of dramatized “I said/(s)he said.” Narrators (whether first person in prose, onstage, or voice-over onscreen) can either act out a scene’s dialogue verbatim from memory or use indirect dialogue to suggest it.

第一种方法是插入场景。将叙述中“然后……然后……然后”的句式转化为戏剧化的“我说/（她）说”的场景叙述。叙述者（无论是散文的第一人称、舞台上的表演者还是屏幕上的画外音）既可以凭记忆逐字逐句地表演场景对话，也可以使用间接对话来暗示场景。

The Netflix series HOUSE OF CARDS, for example, often interpolates scenes of indirect dialogue. Kevin Spacey’s Frank Underwood frequently turns to the camera and talks to us as if he were a professor and we his students in a course on political tradecraft. In the aside below, Underwood dramatizes exposition by giving us insights into himself as well as a character named Donald. Underwood acts out Donald’s character flaw in this vivid, two-sentence metaphorical scene:

例如，Netflix剧集《纸牌屋》经常穿插间接对话场景。凯文·史派西饰演的弗兰克·安德伍德经常转向镜头，仿佛在给我们上一堂政治技巧课，而我们则是他的学生。在下面的旁白中，安德伍德通过展现他自己以及一个名叫唐纳德的角色，将剧情交代得更加生动形象。在这段生动的两句话隐喻场景中，安德伍德演绎了唐纳德的性格缺陷：

What a martyr craves more than anything is a sword to fall on. So you sharpen the blade, hold it at the right angle, and then 3, 2, 1…

殉道者最渴望的莫过于一把可以用来殉身的剑。于是你磨利剑刃，调整好角度，然后3、2、1……

In the next beat, just as Professor Frank predicted, Donald takes the fall for Underwood’s misdeeds.

紧接着，正如弗兰克教授所预言的那样，唐纳德替安德伍德的罪行承担了责任。

Two, generate inner conflict. Stage a self-to-self duel in which one side of a narrating character argues with another. Two film examples: Frank Pierce (Nicolas Cage) in Martin Scorsese’s BRINGING OUT THE DEAD, or the adult Ralphie Parker (Jean Shepherd) in Bob Clark’s A CHRISTMAS STORY.

第二，制造内心冲突。安排一场自我对决，让叙述角色的两面性相互争辩。两个电影例子：马丁·斯科塞斯执导的《午夜惊魂》中的弗兰克·皮尔斯（尼古拉斯·凯奇饰），以及鲍勃·克拉克执导的《圣诞故事》中的成年拉尔夫·帕克（简·谢泼德饰）。

2) Counterpoint. In my experience, the narration technique that most enriches a story is counterpoint. Rather than using a narrator to tell the tale, some writers fully dramatize their story, then appoint a narrator to contradict or ironize its themes. They may use wit to ridicule the dramatic, or the dramatic to deepen the satire. They may counterpoint the personal with the social, or the social with the personal.

2）对位。依我之见，最能丰富故事的叙事技巧莫过于对位。有些作家并不直接用叙述者讲述故事，而是先将故事戏剧化，然后再安排一个叙述者来反驳或讽刺故事的主题。他们或许会用机智来嘲讽戏剧化的情节，或者用戏剧化的情节来加深讽刺。他们或许会将个人经历与社会经历进行对位，或者将社会经历与个人经历进行对位。

Take, for example, John Fowles’s postmodern, historical, antinovel novel, The French Lieutenant’s Woman . Half the pages dramatize the story of Charles Smithson, a Victorian gentleman, and his involvement with Sarah Woodruff, a disgraced governess. Interlaced with this tale, however, a narrator with modern knowledge of nineteenth-century culture and class conflicts undercuts the Charles and Sarah romance. Counterpoint after counterpoint, the narrator argues that the nineteenth century offered women without means far more misery than romance.

以约翰·福尔斯的后现代历史反小说《法国中尉的女人》为例。这部小说一半的篇幅都在讲述维多利亚时代绅士查尔斯·史密森与落魄女家庭教师莎拉·伍德拉夫的爱情故事。然而，在这个故事中，一位拥有十九世纪文化和阶级冲突现代知识的叙述者却对查尔斯和莎拉的爱情进行了批判。叙述者通过一系列对比论证，指出十九世纪贫困女性所遭受的苦难远多于爱情。

Other examples: In Y TU MAMÁ TAMBIÉN the voice-over narrator frequently reminds the audience of Mexico’s social suffering as a counterpoint to the coming-of-age drama. Woody Allen’s witty voice-over in ANNIE HALL counterpoints his protagonist’s self-inquisition. In Samuel Beckett’s play Play , a trio of characters, buried to the neck in urns, stare out over the audience and narrate their seemingly random thoughts in a three-way system of counterpoint.

其他例子：在《你妈妈也一样》中，旁白经常提醒观众墨西哥的社会苦难，以此与成长故事形成对比。伍迪·艾伦在《安妮·霍尔》中诙谐的旁白与主人公的自我审视形成对比。在塞缪尔·贝克特的戏剧《游戏》中，三个角色被埋在骨灰瓮中，只露出脖子，他们凝视着观众，以一种三方对位的方式叙述着看似随机的想法。

Prose is the natural medium for direct telling. The novelist and short-story writer can foreground exposition as nakedly as they wish, and draw it out for as many pages as they wish, so long as their language captivates and satisfies. Charles Dickens, for example, opens A Tale of Two Cities with a burst of counterpointing exposition that hooks the reader’s curiosity:

散文是直接叙述的天然媒介。小说家和短篇小说作家可以随心所欲地突出背景介绍，并根据需要展开叙述，只要他们的语言能够吸引读者并令其满意即可。例如，查尔斯·狄更斯在《双城记》的开头就用一段对比鲜明的叙述抓住了读者的好奇心：

It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity, it was the season of Light, it was the season of Darkness, it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair, we had everything before us, we had nothing before us, we were all going direct to Heaven, we were all going direct the other way…

这是最好的时代，也是最坏的时代；这是智慧的时代，也是愚昧的时代；这是信仰的时代，也是怀疑的时代；这是光明的季节，也是黑暗的季节；这是希望的春天，也是绝望的冬天；我们拥有一切，我们一无所有；我们都将直达天堂，我们也都将直达地狱……

Notice how Dickens’s omniscient third-person narration uses “we” to put an arm around the reader’s shoulder and draw him into the telling. Compare that to the confrontational first-person, fast-paced voice of “I” that opens Ralph Ellison’s Invisible Man :

注意狄更斯的全知全能的第三人称叙述是如何运用“我们”来亲切地将读者拉入故事之中的。与之形成鲜明对比的是拉尔夫·埃里森的《看不见的人》开篇采用的第一人称、快节奏的“我”的叙述方式：

I am an invisible man. No, I am not a spook like those who haunted Edgar Allan Poe; nor am I one of your Hollywood-movie ectoplasms. I am a man of substance, of flesh and bone, fiber and liquids—and I might even be said to possess a mind. I am invisible, understand, simply because people refuse to see me. Like the bodiless heads you see sometimes in circus sideshows, it is as though I have been surrounded by mirrors of hard, distorting glass. When they approach me they see only my surroundings, themselves, or figments of their imagination—indeed, everything and anything except me.

我是一个隐形人。不，我不是像爱伦·坡笔下那些幽灵一样的鬼魂；也不是好莱坞电影里那种虚无缥缈的幽灵。我是一个有血有肉的人，有骨有肉，有纤维有液体——甚至可以说我拥有思想。我之所以隐形，仅仅是因为人们拒绝看见我。就像你有时在马戏团杂耍表演中看到的那些没有身体的头颅一样，我仿佛被坚硬扭曲的镜子包围着。当他们靠近我时，他们看到的只有我的周围环境、他们自己，或者他们想象中的幻影——总之，除了我之外，他们什么都看不到。

In later chapters, both Dickens and Ellison dramatize scenes, but some prose writers never do. Instead, they pave page after page with direct telling narration, never acting out a single event.

在后文中，狄更斯和埃里森都运用了戏剧化的手法来描写场景，但有些散文作家却从未这样做过。相反，他们用直接叙述的方式铺满一页又一页，从不描绘任何事件。

Try to imagine how you might dramatize the exposition in the two passages above into scenes of actable dialogue. In theory it could be done. Shakespeare could have managed it, but with what difficulty? When writing for readers, telling works wonders. When writing for actors, the reverse is true.

试着想象一下，如何将上面两段文字的铺陈改编成可表演的对话场景。理论上是可以做到的。莎士比亚或许也能做到，但难度又有多大呢？为读者写作时，叙述往往效果显著。而为演员写作时，情况则恰恰相反。

Ideally, in the performance arts of stage and screen, exposition flows to the audience unnoticed within the spoken words. As we’ve seen, the craft of rendering exposition invisible takes patience, talent, and technique. Lacking those three qualities, impatient and uninspired screenwriters force exposition on the audience and hope to be forgiven.

理想情况下，在舞台和银幕的表演艺术中，剧情交代应该自然而然地融入到台词之中，让观众浑然不觉。正如我们所见，要做到这一点，需要耐心、天赋和技巧。缺乏这三点的编剧，往往会急躁且缺乏灵感，强行将剧情交代强加给观众，并寄希望于观众的谅解。

Forced Exposition

强制说明

Since the dawn of cinema, filmmakers have inserted shots of newspapers with foot-high headlines announcing events such as “War!” They have walked characters past televisions or radios conveniently tuned to a news broadcast of exactly what the audience needs to know precisely when it needs to know it. Rapidly edited montages and split-screen collages have packed screens with as much information as possible in the briefest possible time. Filmmakers rationalize these devices with the notion that if exposition comes fast and flashy, it won’t bore the audience. They would be wrong.

自电影诞生以来，电影制作人就经常在镜头中插入报纸，上面赫然印着“战争！”之类的耸人听闻的头条新闻。他们还会让角色走过电视或收音机，这些电视或收音机恰好播放着观众需要知道的新闻，而且播出时间也恰到好处。快速剪辑的蒙太奇和分屏拼贴手法，在最短的时间内将尽可能多的信息塞进屏幕。电影制作人认为，如果信息传递快速而炫目，就不会让观众感到厌烦，以此来合理化这些手法。但他们错了。

Similar thinking governs opening films with a title roll, as did STAR WARS (which delivered rapid-fire exposition and a tone of grandiosity), or closing with one, as did A FISH CALLED WANDA (which got laughs and a touch more closure). When thrillers race against time, hopscotching from place to place, they often superimpose location names and dates over establishing shots. In such cases, a little telling goes a long way. With a brief halt for a cogent image or a quick-printed fact, the story stubs its toe but then strides on, and the audience shrugs it off.

类似的思路也适用于以片名字幕开场的电影，例如《星球大战》（它以快节奏的叙事和宏大的基调呈现），或者以片名字幕结尾的电影，例如《一条名叫旺达的鱼》（它带来了笑声，也让故事更加完整）。当惊悚片争分夺秒、场景跳跃时，它们通常会在场景交代的镜头上叠加地点名称和日期。在这种情况下，少量的旁白就能起到很大的作用。通过一个简洁的画面或快速标注的事实，故事虽然会稍稍停顿，但随后会继续推进，观众也会对此不以为意。

But audiences will not forgive a deluge of facts artlessly shoehorned into dialogue for no reason intrinsic to the characters or the scene. When inept writing forces characters to tell each other facts they already know, the pace trips over a high hurdle, falls face-first in the cinders, and may never get up.

但观众绝不会原谅生硬地将大量事实塞进对话中，而这些事实与角色或场景本身并无内在联系。当拙劣的编剧强迫角色互相讲述他们早已知晓的事实时，剧情节奏就会被绊倒，一头栽进灰烬中，而且可能永远无法恢复。

For example:

例如：

INT. LUXURIOUS GREAT ROOM—DAY

室内豪华大客厅—日间

John and Jane sit on a silk-tasseled sofa, sipping martinis.

约翰和简坐在丝绸流苏沙发上，啜饮着马提尼酒。

JOHN

约翰

Oh my goodness, darling, how long have we known and loved each other now? Why, it’s over twenty years, isn’t it?

我的天哪，亲爱的，我们认识、相爱多久了？哎呀，都二十多年了，对吧？

JANE

简

Yes, ever since we were at the university together, and your fraternity threw a mixer and invited the Women’s Socialist Club. Your house was so rich, we poor girls called Beta Tau Zeta Billions, Trillions, and Zillions.

是的，自从我们一起上大学，你们兄弟会举办联谊会邀请了妇女社会主义俱乐部之后，你们的宿舍就一直很豪华，我们这些穷女生就把Beta Tau Zeta兄弟会叫做“亿万 ...

JOHN

约翰

(gazing around their magnificent home)

（环顾他们宏伟的家）

Yes, and then I lost my inheritance. But we both worked very hard over the years to make our dreams come true. And they did, didn’t they, my little Trotskyite?

是的，后来我失去了继承权。但这些年来，我们俩都非常努力地工作，才实现了我们的梦想。而且它们确实实现了，不是吗，我的小托洛茨基主义者？

This exchange tells the audience seven fictional facts: This couple is rich, they are in their forties, they met within the elite of their university, he was born to a wealthy family, she came up from poverty, they once had opposite political views but no longer, and over the years they’ve developed a banter that’s so sweet it hurts your teeth.

这段对话向观众讲述了七个虚构的事实：这对夫妇很富有，他们都四十多岁了，他们在大学的精英圈子里相识，他出生于富裕家庭，她出身贫寒，他们曾经政治观点截然相反，但现在不再如此，多年来，他们之间发展出了一种甜蜜到让人牙疼的斗嘴。

The scene is false and its dialogue tinny because the writing is dishonest. The characters are not doing what they seem to be doing. They seem to be reminiscing, but in fact they’re mouthing exposition so the eavesdropping audience can overhear it.

场景虚假，对话生硬，因为剧本写得不诚实。角色们并没有做他们表面上在做的事情。他们看似在回忆往事，实际上却是在偷听，好让旁观的观众听到。

As mentioned above, prose writers can avoid these fake scenes by sketching a brief marital history that strings facts together with a pleasing style. If they wish, prose writers can, within limits, simply tell their readers what they need to know. Some playwrights and screenwriters ape novelists by resorting to narration, but with rare exceptions, direct address onstage and voice-over onscreen cannot mete out exposition with the intellectual power and emotional impact of fully dramatized dialogue.

如上所述，散文作家可以通过简略地勾勒婚姻史，以流畅优美的文风串联事实，来避免这些虚假的场景。如果他们愿意，散文作家可以在一定范围内，直接告诉读者他们需要知道的信息。一些剧作家和编剧效仿小说家，采用叙述的方式，但除了极少数例外，舞台上的直接对话和银幕上的旁白都无法像完整的戏剧对话那样，以深刻的内涵和强烈的感染力来阐述故事背景。

To make this point for yourself, do an exercise in exposition as ammunition. Rewrite the scene above so that the two characters use their expositional facts as weapons during a fight in which one character forces the other to do something that he or she does not want to do.

为了更好地理解这一点，不妨做个练习，把背景介绍当作武器。重写上面的场景，让两个角色在争吵中利用他们掌握的背景信息作为武器，其中一个角色强迫另一个角色做他/她不愿意做的事情。

Now do it again. But this time, put the same facts into a seduction scene in which one character uses what he or she knows as ammunition to subtly manipulate the other into doing something the other does not wish to do.

现在再来一遍。但这一次，把同样的事实放到一个诱惑场景中，其中一个角色利用自己掌握的信息作为筹码，巧妙地操纵另一个角色去做对方不愿意做的事情。

Write the scene so that the exposition becomes invisible and the characters’ behaviors credible. In other words, write it so that the conflict or seduction fascinates the reader/audience, and the exposition they need to know slips unawares, invisibly, as it were, into their minds.

撰写场景时，要让背景交代变得自然而然，人物行为也显得合情合理。换句话说，要让冲突或诱惑深深吸引读者/观众，而他们需要了解的背景信息则在不知不觉中悄然渗入他们的脑海。

CHARACTERIZATION

特征描述

The second function of dialogue is the creation and expression of a distinctive characterization for each character in the cast.

对话的第二个功能是为剧中的每个角色创造和表达独特的性格特征。

Human nature can be usefully divided into two grand aspects: appearance (who the person seems to be) versus reality (who the person actually is). Writers, therefore, design characters around two corresponding parts known as true character and characterization.

人性可以有效地分为两大方面：外表（一个人看起来是什么样的人）和内在（一个人实际上是什么样的人）。因此，作家在塑造人物时，会围绕这两个相互关联的部分——真实性格和人物刻画——展开。

True character , as the term implies, names a character’s profound psychological and moral being, a truth that can only be revealed when life backs the character into a pressure-filled corner and forces him to make choices and take actions. The Principle of Choice is foundational to all storytelling, fictional and nonfictional: to wit, a character’s true self can only be expressed through risk-filled choices of action in the pursuit of desire.

正如其字面意思，真正的性格指的是人物深层的心理和道德本质，这种本质只有在生活将人物逼入绝境，迫使其做出选择和采取行动时才能显露出来。选择原则是所有故事讲述的基础，无论虚构还是非虚构：也就是说，人物的真实自我只能通过在追求欲望的过程中做出充满风险的行动选择来展现。

Characterization denotes a character’s total appearance, the sum of all surface traits and behaviors. It performs three functions: to intrigue, to individualize, to convince.

人物刻画指的是人物的整体外在形象，包括所有表面特征和行为的总和。它具有三种功能：引人入胜、个性鲜明、令人信服。

1) To intrigue. The reader/audience knows that a character’s appearance is not her reality, that her characterization is a persona, a mask of personality suspended between the world and the true character behind it. When the reader/audience encounters a one-of-a-kind personality, they listen to the character’s words and naturally wonder: “That’s who she seems to be, but who is she really? Is she actually honest or a liar? Loving or cruel? Wise or foolish? Cool or rash? Strong or weak? Good or evil? What is the core identity behind her intriguing characterization? What is her true character?”

1）引人入胜。读者/观众知道，角色的外表并非其真实面目，其性格塑造是一种伪装，一种介于现实世界与真实自我之间的面具。当读者/观众遇到一个独一无二的角色时，他们会聆听角色的言语，自然而然地产生疑问：“她表面上是这样，但她真正的身份是什么？她究竟是诚实还是说谎？是慈爱还是残忍？是睿智还是愚蠢？是冷静还是鲁莽？是坚强还是软弱？是善良还是邪恶？在她引人入胜的性格塑造背后，隐藏着怎样的核心身份？她真正的性格是什么？”

Having hooked the reader/audience’s curiosity, the story becomes a series of surprising revelations that answer these questions.

故事成功地引起了读者/观众的好奇心，接下来将展开一系列令人惊讶的揭秘，解答这些问题。

2) To convince. A well-imagined, well-designed characterization assembles capacities (mental, physical) and behaviors (emotional, verbal) that encourage the reader/audience to believe in a fictional character as if she were factual. As the poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge noted two centuries ago, the reader/audience knows that stories and characters are not actual. But they also know that to involve themselves in the telling, they must temporarily believe, or more precisely, they must willingly suspend their disbelief and accept the character’s actions and reactions without doubt, without argument.

2）说服力。精心构思、巧妙设计的人物形象，能够巧妙地融合各种能力（心理、生理）和行为（情感、语言），从而促使读者/观众相信虚构人物的存在，如同相信真实存在一般。正如诗人塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治两个世纪前所指出的，读者/观众明白故事和人物并非真实存在。但他们也明白，要沉浸于故事之中，就必须暂时相信，或者更准确地说，必须心甘情愿地放下怀疑，毫无保留地接受人物的行为和反应，不加质疑。

If your reader/audience thinks the thought, “I don’t believe a word she says” because they sense your character is a liar, that could be a revelation of true character. But if they think the same thought because they don’t simply believe in your character, then it’s time for a rewrite.

如果读者/观众因为感觉你的角色是个骗子而产生“我不相信她说的任何一个字”的想法，这或许恰恰揭示了角色的真实性格。但如果他们产生同样的想法仅仅是因为他们不相信你的角色，那么就该重写了。

3) To individualize. A well-imagined, well-researched characterization creates a unique combination of biology, upbringing, physicality, mentality, emotionality, education, experience, attitudes, values, tastes, and every possible nuance of cultural influence that has given the character her individuality. Moving through her days, pursuing career, relationships, sexuality, health, happiness, and the like, she gathers behaviors into a one-of-a-kind personality.

3）塑造个性。精心构思、考究的角色塑造，融合了生物学、成长经历、体态、心智、情感、教育背景、人生阅历、态度、价值观、品味以及所有可能的文化影响，最终造就了角色独特的个性。在日常生活中，她追求事业、人际关系、性、健康、幸福等等，这些经历和行为最终汇聚成她独一无二的人格。

And the most important trait of all: talk. She speaks like no one we have ever met before. Her language style not only sets her apart from all other cast members but also, if the writing is masterful, from all other fictional characters. A recent example: Jeanette “Jasmine” Francis (Cate Blanchett) in Woody Allen’s BLUE JASMINE. (Dialogue to characterize will be fully explored in Chapters Ten and Eleven.)

而最重要的特质是：说话。她的说话方式与我们之前见过的任何人都截然不同。她的语言风格不仅使她与其他所有演员区别开来，而且，如果剧本写得精彩绝伦，她还能与其他所有虚构角色区分开来。最近的一个例子是伍迪·艾伦的电影《蓝色茉莉》中的珍妮特·“茉莉”·弗朗西斯（凯特·布兰切特饰）。（关于如何通过对话塑造人物性格，我们将在第十章和第十一章中进行深入探讨。）

ACTION

行动

Dialogue’s third essential function is to equip characters with the means for action. Stories contain three kinds of action: mental, physical, and verbal.

对话的第三个重要功能是赋予角色行动的手段。故事包含三种行动：心理行动、身体行动和语言行动。

Mental Action: Words and images compose thoughts, but a thought does not become a mental action until it causes change within a character—change in attitude, belief, expectation, understanding, and the like. A mental action may or may not translate into outer behavior, but even if it stays secret and unexpressed, the character who took the mental action is not quite the same person afterward as she was before. Character change through mental action impels much of modern storytelling.

心理活动：文字和图像构成思想，但思想只有当它引发人物内心的变化——态度、信念、期望、理解等方面的改变——才能转化为心理活动。心理活动或许会转化为外在行为，或许不会，但即便它保持隐秘和未表达的状态，采取心理活动的人也与之前截然不同。人物通过心理活动发生的转变，是现代故事叙述的主要驱动力。

Physical Action: Physical action comes in two fundamental kinds: gestures and tasks.

身体动作：身体动作主要分为两种类型：姿势和动作。

By gestures, I mean all varieties of body language: facial expression, hand movements, posture, touch, proxemics, vocalics, kinesics, and the like. These behaviors either modify spoken language or substitute for it, expressing feelings words cannot. 1

我所说的手势指的是各种肢体语言：面部表情、手部动作、姿势、触摸、空间关系、语音语调、体态语调等等。这些行为要么修饰口语，要么替代口语，表达语言无法表达的情感。

By tasks, I mean activities that get something done: working, playing, traveling, sleeping, lovemaking, fighting, daydreaming, reading, admiring a sunset, and the like—all those actions that do not require talk.

所谓“任务”，我指的是能完成某事的活动：工作、玩耍、旅行、睡觉、做爱、打架、做白日梦、阅读、欣赏日落等等——所有这些不需要说话的活动。

Verbal Action: As novelist Elizabeth Bowen put it, “Dialogue is what characters do to each other.” 2

语言行为：正如小说家伊丽莎白·鲍恩所说，“对话是角色之间相互做的事情。”

On the level of outer behavior, a character’s dialogue style melds with his other traits to create his surface characterization, but at the inner level of true character, the actions he takes into the world reveal his humanity or lack of it. What’s more, the greater the pressure in the scene (the more he stands to lose or gain in that moment), the more his actions tell us who he really is.

从外在行为层面来看，人物的对话风格与其他特质共同塑造了其表面形象；而从内在性格层面来看，人物在现实世界中的行动则揭示了他的人性，或者说，是人性的缺失。此外，场景中的压力越大（即他此刻可能失去或得到的越多），他的行动就越能展现他真实的自我。

What a character says, however, only moves the reader/audience if the actions he takes beneath his lines ring true to that specific character in that specific moment. Therefore, before writing a line, ask these questions: What does my character want out of this situation? At this precise moment, what action would he take in an effort to reach that desire? What exact words would he use to carry out that action?

然而，只有当角色在特定时刻的行动与他的言语相符时，他的言语才能真正打动读者/观众。因此，在写下任何一句台词之前，请先问自己以下问题：我的角色想要从这种情况中得到什么？在这一刻，他会采取什么行动来实现这个愿望？他会用什么样的话语来表达这个愿望？

Spoken words suggest what a character thinks and feels; the action he takes beneath his words expresses his identity. To uncover a character’s inner life, seek the subtextual action and label it with an active gerund (“-ing”) phrase. Below are the four dialogue quotes from the preface. Look into the subtext of each, and name the character’s action with a gerund. When done, compare your interpretations to mine.

言语暗示着人物的所思所想；而言语之外的行动则展现了他的身份。要揭示人物的内心世界，就要寻找言外之意，并用动名词（“-ing”）短语来描述。以下是序言中的四段对话摘录。请分析每段对话的言外之意，并用动名词来描述人物的行动。完成后，请将你的解读与我的进行比较。

Tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow,

明天，明天，还有明天，

Creeps in this petty pace from day to day,

日复一日，这种琐碎的速度悄然滋生。

To the last syllable of recorded time,

直至记录时间的最后一个音节，

And all our yesterdays have lighted fools

我们所有的过去都照亮了愚人。

The way to dusty death.

通往尘土死亡之路。

—Macbeth in The Tragedy of Macbeth

——《麦克白》中的麦克白

“Of all the gin joints in all the towns in all the world she walks into mine.”

“全世界所有城镇里那么多酒吧，她偏偏走进了我的酒吧。”

—Rick in CASABLANCA

——里克在卡萨布兰卡

“Towards thee I roll, thou all-destroying but unconquering whale; to the last I grapple with thee; from hell’s heart I stab at thee; for hate’s sake I spit my last breath at thee.”

“我向你滚去，你这毁灭一切却又无法征服的巨鲸；我与你搏斗到最后一刻；我从地狱之心刺向你；为了仇恨，我向你吐出我的最后一口气。”

—Ahab in Moby Dick

——《白鲸记》中的亚哈船长

“Not that there’s anything wrong with that.”

“这倒没什么错。”

—Jerry in SEINFELD

——《宋飞正传》中的杰瑞

All four quotes above imply disgust, but Macbeth, Rick Blaine, Ahab, and Jerry Seinfeld express their disdain in such radically different speech styles that their personalities could not be more unalike. (Dialogue style as the door to characterization will be the focus of Part Three.)

以上四段引语都表达了厌恶之情，但麦克白、里克·布莱恩、亚哈船长和杰瑞·宋飞表达厌恶的方式却截然不同，他们的性格也完全相反。（对话风格作为人物塑造的切入点，将是第三部分的重点。）

My sense of the deep character under the four speeches suggests these subtextual actions: Macbeth—denouncing existence; Rick Blaine—lamenting lost love; Ahab—blaspheming God’s power; Jerry Seinfeld—ridiculing the political correctness that protects asinine behavior from ridicule. Your interpretations of implied action may differ from mine (not that there’s anything wrong with that), but the purpose of this exercise is to reveal the difference between the activity of talk and the taking of action.

我对这四段演讲背后深层人物性格的理解暗示了以下潜台词：麦克白——谴责存在；里克·布莱恩——哀悼逝去的爱情；亚哈——亵渎上帝的力量；杰瑞·宋飞——嘲讽那种保护愚蠢行为免受嘲讽的政治正确。你对这些隐含行为的解读可能与我的不同（这并没有什么错），但这项练习的目的在于揭示言语活动与实际行动之间的区别。

Part Four will further demonstrate this technique by parsing seven scenes beat by beat to separate their outer language from their inner actions and trace how these dynamic designs motivate what’s said as they arc scenes around their turning points.

第四部分将通过逐节分析七个场景来进一步展示这种技巧，将它们的外在语言与内在动作分开，并追踪这些动态设计如何激发所说的话，以及它们如何围绕转折点推动场景发展。

#↩

3

EXPRESSIVITY I: CONTENT

表达能力 I：内容

As You Like It , Act 2, Scene 7

《皆大欢喜》第二幕第七场

Jaques (to Duke Senior)

雅克（对杜克老先生）

All the world’s a stage,

世界是一个舞台，

And all the men and women merely players:

而所有男男女女都只是演员而已：

They have their exits and their entrances;

它们有自己的出口和入口；

And one man in his time plays many parts…

一个人一生中会扮演许多角色……

Jaques believes that in the theatre of life, everyone acts out his own cast of characters decade after decade from infant to adult to geezer. Jaques steps back to survey this pattern from a philosophical, objective, long-term, outside-in, public point of view. But in order to create Jaques’s dark doctrine, Shakespeare worked (my guess) from the reverse perspective—psychological, subjective, here and now, inside-out, and profoundly private.

雅克认为，在人生这出戏里，每个人都在一代又一代地扮演着自己的角色，从婴儿到成人再到老人，周而复始。雅克退后一步，从哲学、客观、长远、由外而内、公共的视角审视着这种模式。但为了构建雅克那套晦涩的理论，莎士比亚（我猜）采用了截然相反的视角——心理的、主观的、此时此地的、由内而外的、极其私密的视角。

As you compose dialogue, I think it’s useful to imagine character design as three concentric spheres, one inside the other—a self within a self within a self. This three-tiered complex fills dialogue with content of thought and feeling while shaping expression in gesture and word. The innermost sphere churns with the unsayable; the middle sphere restrains the unsaid; the outer sphere releases the said.

在构思对话时，我认为将角色设计想象成三个同心球会很有帮助，一个嵌套在另一个里面——一个自我嵌套另一个自我。这种三层结构赋予对话以思想和情感的内容，同时塑造了人物的姿态和言语表达。最内层的球体翻腾着难以言说的情感；中间的球体抑制着未说出口的话语；最外层的球体则释放出已说出口的话语。

THE SAID

据说

The surface level of things said supports the more or less solid meanings that words, spoken or written, directly express with both denotations and connotations. “Snake,” for example, literally means “a legless reptile,” but in Western culture it also symbolizes treachery and evil. The word “house” connotes more than domicile. It carries overtones of home, hearth, and family, plus undertones of shack, crash pad, and flophouse.

言语的表面含义支撑着词语（无论是口头的还是书面的）直接表达的或多或少坚实的意义，这些意义既包含字面意义，也包含引申意义。例如，“蛇”的字面意思是“无腿的爬行动物”，但在西方文化中，它也象征着背叛和邪恶。“房子”一词的含义远不止住所。它既包含家、炉火和家庭的字面含义，也包含棚屋、临时住所和廉价旅馆的隐含含义。

This is why quotable dialogue such as “Get busy livin’ or get busy dyin’” (Ellis Boyd “Red” Redding in THE SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION) and “I’m just one stomach flu away from my goal weight” (Emily Charlton in THE DEVIL WEARS PRADA) outlive their stories and their characters. These sentences express their meaning no matter who says it or when.

这就是为什么像“要么好好活，要么好好死”（埃利斯·博伊德·“瑞德”·雷丁在《肖申克的救赎》中说的）和“我离理想体重只差一场肠胃炎了”（艾米莉·查尔顿在《穿普拉达的女王》中说的）这样的经典台词，会超越它们的故事和人物本身而流传下去。无论谁说的，无论何时说的，这些句子都表达着它们的意义。

Word choices (busy dyin’, stomach flu) naturally enrich the lines with connotations from the culture outside their fictional setting. But because a specific character in a specific situation speaks the lines with a specific purpose, a wholly new and deeper realm comes into play: the character’s intelligence, imagination, and other genetic givens.

用词（比如“忙着死去”、“肠胃炎”）自然而然地赋予台词虚构背景之外的文化内涵。但由于特定角色在特定情境下怀着特定目的说出这些台词，一个全新的、更深层次的层面便随之显现：角色的智力、想象力以及其他与生俱来的特质。

By creating an original dialogue style of vocabulary, diction, syntax, grammar, tone, tropes, and accent, the writer characterizes a role. Verbal choices express the character’s education or lack of it, wit or lack of it, his outlook on life, the range of his emotional behavior—all the observable traits that jigsaw into a personality.

作者通过创造独特的对话风格，运用词汇、措辞、句法、语法、语气、修辞手法和口音，来塑造角色形象。语言的选择表达了角色的教育程度（或缺乏教育）、机智程度（或缺乏机智）、人生观、情感行为的丰富程度——所有这些可观察的特征共同构成了人物性格。

THE UNSAID

未说出口的话

A second sphere, the unsaid, revolves within a character. From this inner space the self gazes out at the world. As thoughts and feelings form at this level, the self deliberately withholds them. Nonetheless, once the character speaks (text), readers and audiences instinctively look past the words to intuit the unsaid, to glimpse what the character actually thinks and feels (subtext) but chooses not to put into words. The writer, therefore, must hone dialogue so that this is possible, so that the unsaid can be sensed by implication. 1

第二个领域，即未言之境，存在于角色的内心深处。从这个内在空间，自我凝视着世界。当思想和情感在这个层面形成时，自我会刻意地将它们隐藏起来。然而，一旦角色开口说话（文本），读者和观众便会本能地透过字里行间，去领悟那些未言之意，窥见角色内心真正的想法和感受（潜台词），而这些想法和感受却被他们选择不诉诸言语。因此，作家必须精心打磨对话，使之成为可能，使未言之意能够通过言外之意被感知。

When Emily Charlton (Emily Blunt) says to Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway) “I’m just one stomach flu away from my goal weight,” what she does not say, but we know she is thinking, might go something like this: “The fashion world forces me to live an anorexic life, but I want my career more than my health. Perpetual hunger is a price I’m happy to pay. If you value your job future, you will do the same.”

当艾米莉·查尔顿（艾米莉·布朗特饰）对安迪·萨克斯（安妮·海瑟薇饰）说“我离目标体重只差一场肠胃炎了”时，她没说出口，但我们知道她心里想的可能是这样的：“时尚圈逼我过着厌食症般的生活，但我更看重事业而不是健康。我乐意付出永无止境的饥饿。如果你珍惜你的职业生涯，你也会这么做。”

Novels thrive at the level of the unsaid. In Chapter One of Ian McEwan’s Enduring Love , a violent accident kills a man. In the next chapter, as Joe Rose stands among the other survivors, surveying the aftermath, he confides to the reader:

小说的魅力在于那些未言明的部分。在伊恩·麦克尤恩的《持久的爱》第一章中，一场惨烈的意外夺走了一个人的生命。在下一章中，当乔·罗斯站在其他幸存者中间，环顾着残局时，他向读者吐露心声：

Clarissa came up behind me and looped her arms around my waist and pressed her face into my back. What surprised me was she was already crying (I could feel the wetness on my shirt) whereas to me, sorrow seemed a long way off. Like a self in a dream I was both first and third persons. I acted, and saw myself act. I had my thoughts, and I saw them drift across a screen. As in a dream, my emotional responses were nonexistent or inappropriate. Clarissa’s tears were no more than a fact, but I was pleased by the way my feet were anchored to the ground and set well apart, and the way my arms were folded across my chest. I looked out across the fields and the thought scrolled across: That man is dead . I felt a warmth spreading through me, a kind of self-love, and my folded arms hugged me tight. The corollary seemed to be And I am alive . It was a random matter, who was alive or dead at any given time. I happened to be alive.

克拉丽莎走到我身后，双臂环住我的腰，脸埋在我的背上。令我惊讶的是，她已经哭了（我能感觉到衬衫湿了），而我却感觉悲伤离我很远。就像梦境中的自我，我同时是第一人称和第三人称。我行动，也看到自己的行动。我的思绪涌动，我看到它们在屏幕上飘荡。如同梦境一般，我的情绪反应要么不存在，要么不合时宜。克拉丽莎的眼泪只是一个事实，但我却很欣慰自己的双脚稳稳地立在地上，双臂交叉抱在胸前。我眺望着田野，一个念头闪过：那个人死了。我感到一股暖流涌遍全身，一种自爱的感觉油然而生，我紧紧地抱着自己。由此似乎可以推断出：而我还活着。在任何特定时刻，谁是生是死，都只是随机的。而我，恰好还活着。

THE UNSAYABLE

不可言说的

Deepest yet, concealed beneath the unsaid, the sphere of the unsayable roils with subconscious drives and needs that incite a character’s choices and actions.

更深层次上，隐藏在未言之事之下的不可言说之境，涌动着潜意识的驱动力和需求，激发着人物的选择和行动。

A character’s truest nature can only be expressed when, under the pressures of life, he chooses to act in pursuit of a life-defining desire. As antagonistic pressures build greater and greater power, the character’s choices of action reveal his hidden self, until a final choice under the maximum pressure of life exposes the character’s primal, irreducible self. How deliberate versus instinctive the motivations are that propel human choice of action has been debated for centuries. But whatever the case, choices begin in this innermost sphere.

只有当一个人在生活的重压下选择行动，去追求一个足以定义人生的渴望时，他最真实的本性才能得以展现。随着对抗性压力的不断累积，人物的行动选择逐渐揭示出他隐藏的自我，直到在人生最大压力下做出最终抉择，才会展现出他原始的、不可化约的本性。几个世纪以来，人们一直在争论，究竟是深思熟虑还是本能驱使着人类做出行动选择。但无论如何，选择都始于这最深层的内心世界。

Language, therefore, cannot express who a character actually is, only who he seems to be. As the Bible teaches, a person is known not by his words but his deeds. The truth comes full circle, however, once the writer realizes that words are deeds.

因此，语言无法表达人物的真实面目，只能展现其表面形象。正如《圣经》所教导的，了解一个人并非看他的言语，而是看他的行为。然而，一旦作者意识到言语即是行为，真理便会完整呈现。

Talk is the foremost vehicle for human action. When a character says something, he is, in fact, doing something. By speaking, he could be comforting a loved one, bribing an enemy, begging for help, refusing to help, obeying authority, defying authority, paying the price, remembering the day, and so on down the limitless list of human actions. Dialogue expresses far more than the meanings of its words. As language, dialogue conveys characterization, but as action, dialogue expresses true character.

言语是人类行动最重要的载体。当一个角色开口说话时，他实际上就是在做某件事。通过言语，他可以安慰亲人、贿赂敌人、乞求帮助、拒绝帮助、服从权威、违抗权威、付出代价、回忆往事，等等，人类行为的范畴无穷无尽。对话所表达的远不止字面意思。作为语言，对话塑造人物形象；作为行动，对话展现人物的真实性格。

Moment by moment, your character struggles in pursuit of her desires; she takes actions and uses her spoken words to carry them out. At the same time, however, her language choices convey her inner life, conscious and subconscious, without announcing it. Whether read or acted, fine dialogue creates a transparency that allows the reader/audience to gaze through the text of talk. This phenomenon turns the story-goer into a mind reader.

你的角色在追逐欲望的过程中，时时刻刻都在挣扎；她采取行动，并用言语来实现这些欲望。然而，与此同时，她的语言选择也在不言而喻地传达着她意识和潜意识中的内心世界。无论是阅读还是表演，精妙的对话都能创造一种透明感，让读者/观众能够透过对话的文本窥视角色的内心。这种现象使故事的听众仿佛变成了读心者。

When you read a page of expressive dialogue or watch a fine actor perform a complex scene, your sixth sense invades the character. You become a telepathist, often better aware of what’s going on inside her than she knows herself. Your story-trained sonar traces vibrations down through the character’s subconscious currents, until the actions she takes in the subtext of her lines enunciate her identity and you discover her profound personal dimensions.

当你阅读一段富有表现力的对话，或观看一位优秀演员演绎一段复杂的场景时，你的第六感会与角色产生共鸣。你仿佛拥有了心灵感应的能力，往往比角色自己更了解她内心的想法。你那经过故事训练的敏锐洞察力，如同声呐般追踪着角色潜意识深处的脉动，直至她言外之意中的行为最终揭示出她的身份，让你得以发现她深邃的个人特质。

If, as some people believe, anything and everything can be expressed in words, we should stop telling stories and write essays instead. But we don’t, because at the rock bottom of being, the unsayable energies in the subconscious mind are real and demand expression.

如果像某些人认为的那样，任何事物都可以用语言表达，那我们应该停止讲故事，转而写文章。但我们并没有这样做，因为在存在的最深处，潜意识中那些无法言说的能量是真实存在的，它们需要被表达出来。

Dialogue unites these realms because the spoken word resonates through all three spheres. Dialogue wields the double power to express the effable (characterization) while it illumines the ineffable (true character)—what can be put into words versus what can only be put into action. Dialogue, therefore, is the writer’s foremost vehicle for character content.

对话将这些领域联系起来，因为口语能够贯穿所有三个层面。对话拥有双重力量：既能表达可言说的（人物刻画），又能揭示不可言说的（人物的真实性格）——即哪些可以用语言表达，哪些只能用行动体现。因此，对话是作家塑造人物性格的最重要载体。

ACTION VERSUS ACTIVITY

行动与活动

The axiom “nothing is what it seems” expresses the primal duality of life: What seems is the surface of life, the activity we see and hear, the outer behavior of what a character says and how she behaves. What is is the substance of life, the action the character takes below the surface of activity.

“眼见未必为实”这句格言表达了生命最原始的二元性：表象是生命的表面，是我们所见所闻的活动，是人物言行举止等外在表现；而本质则是生命的实质，是人物在这些表象之下所采取的行动。

Outer goings-on such as playing cards, working out, sipping wine, and, most of all, talking are simply activities. These textual behaviors mask the truth of what the character is actually doing. For even though an activity like chatting with a stranger at a bus stop may seem without purpose, it never is. Therefore, no line of dialogue is finished until you’ve answered this question: In the subtext of my character’s verbal activity, what action is he in fact taking?

诸如打牌、锻炼、品酒，尤其是聊天之类的外在行为，仅仅是表面活动。这些文字描述的行为掩盖了角色真正想做的事情。即使像在公交车站和陌生人聊天这样的行为看似漫无目的，实际上也并非如此。因此，只有回答了这个问题，对话才算真正完成：在我的角色言语行为的潜台词中，他实际上在做什么？

Consider ice cream. We never eat ice cream simply because we’re hungry. Like all behaviors, a conscious or subconscious action underlies this activity. What is the ice cream eater really doing? Perhaps he’s drowning his sorrows in something sweet or rebelling against doctor’s orders or rewarding himself for sticking to his diet. Those actions—drowning sorrows, rebelling, or rewarding—find expression in the activity of eating ice cream.

想想冰淇淋。我们吃冰淇淋从来不是因为饿了。就像所有行为一样，这种行为背后都有意识或潜意识的驱动。吃冰淇淋的人究竟在做什么？也许他是在用甜食来排解忧愁，或者在违抗医嘱，又或者在奖励自己坚持节食。这些行为——排解忧愁、违抗医嘱或奖励自己——都体现在吃冰淇淋这一行为中。

The same of talk. As Character A and Character B converse, what are they doing? Are the words Character A uses consoling Character B or ridiculing her? When B reacts, does her dialogue suggest that she is submitting to A or dominating him? Is A feigning interest or falling in love? Is B deceiving A or confessing to him? And on the questioning goes. Behind the textual activities of the characters, what subtextual actions actually drive the scene?

对话也是如此。当角色A和角色B交谈时，他们在做什么？角色A的话语是在安慰角色B还是在嘲讽她？当角色B做出反应时，她的对话是表明她在顺从角色A还是在支配角色A？角色A是在假装感兴趣还是真的爱上了角色B？角色B是在欺骗角色A还是在向角色A坦白？诸如此类的问题层出不穷。在人物的文本行为背后，究竟是哪些潜台词在推动着剧情发展？

An activity, therefore, is simply the surface manifestation of an action; it’s the way a character carries out an action. Action is foundational to storytelling, and every activity contains one.

因此，活动仅仅是行动的表面表现；它是角色执行行动的方式。行动是故事讲述的基础，而每项活动都包含行动。

“Drama” is the ancient Greek word for action, derived from the verb draoō , meaning “to do” or “to act.” The audiences of classical Greece knew that no matter what was happening on the surface of a play, an inner action drives all outer activity. Extending this principle to the writing of a scene, we realize that even silence has underlying action. Not speaking when a situation calls for talk is an action, perhaps a cruel one, aimed at another person. When a character speaks, he is doing something: helping or hurting, begging or bribing, persuading or dissuading, explaining or misleading, attacking or defending, complimenting or insulting, complaining or thanking, and so on down an endless list of actions. Even pauses play into a beat of action/reaction: When a character pauses, she’s either reacting to the scene’s previous action or preparing her next move.

“戏剧”（Drama）一词源于古希腊语，意为“行动”，来自动词draoō，即“做”或“行动”。古希腊的观众深知，无论戏剧表面呈现何种景象，内在的行动都驱动着一切外在的活动。将这一原则延伸至剧本创作，我们便会发现，即使是沉默也蕴含着行动。在需要说话的情况下保持沉默，本身就是一种行动，或许是一种针对他人的残酷行动。当一个角色开口说话时，他/她也在做着某种事情：帮助或伤害、乞求或贿赂、说服或劝阻、解释或误导、攻击或辩护、赞美或侮辱、抱怨或感谢，等等，不胜枚举。就连停顿也构成了一种行动/反应的节奏：当一个角色停顿时，她要么是在对之前的动作做出反应，要么是在为下一步行动做准备。

The term “dialogue” is often contrasted with “monologue,” as if dialogue were always a two-way process. But that’s misleading. As I mentioned in Chapter One, dialogue is a contraction of two Greek terms ( dia and legein ) meaning “through” and “speak.” “Dialogue” connotes actions taken through talk. Therefore, when a character talks to herself, she takes action within herself. “Monologue” connotes someone talking to no one or nothing, but in reality, that’s impossible. Someone, something, or some aspect of the self is on the receiving end of every word ever spoken or thought.

“对话”一词常与“独白”形成对比，仿佛对话总是双向的。但这种说法具有误导性。正如我在第一章中提到的，“对话”一词源于两个希腊词根（dia 和 legein），分别意为“通过”和“说话”。“对话”意味着通过言语采取的行动。因此，当一个角色自言自语时，她实际上是在内心采取行动。“独白”则意味着某人对着空气或虚空说话，但实际上，这是不可能的。每个人所说或所想的每一个字、每一件事，最终都会被某个人、某件事或自我的某个方面所接收。

TEXT AND SUBTEXT

文本与潜台词

Activity and action run parallel to another pair of terms: text and subtext.

活动和行动与另外一对术语——文本和潜台词——并行发展。

Text means the surface of a work of art and its execution in its medium: paint on canvas, chords from a piano, steps by a dancer. In the art of story, text names the words on the page of a novel, or the outer life of character behavior in performance—what the reader imagines, what an audience sees and hears. In the creation of dialogue, text becomes the said, the words the characters actually speak.

文本指的是艺术作品的表面及其在媒介中的呈现方式：画布上的颜料、钢琴上的和弦、舞者的舞步。在故事艺术中，文本指的是小说页面上的文字，或是表演中人物行为的外在表现——读者的想象，观众的所见所闻。在对话创作中，文本则成为“所说”，即人物实际说出的话语。

Subtext names the inner substance of a work of art—the meanings and feelings that flow below the surface. In life, people “speak” to each other, as it were, from beneath their words. A silent language flows below conscious awareness. In story, subtextual levels enclose the hidden life of characters’ thoughts and feelings, desires and actions, both conscious and subconscious—the unsaid and unsayable.

潜台词指的是艺术作品的内在内涵——那些隐藏在表面之下的意义和情感。在生活中，人们仿佛在言语之下“交流”。一种无声的语言在意识层面流动。在故事中，潜台词层层递进，囊括了人物思想、情感、欲望和行为的隐秘层面，包括意识层面和潜意识层面——那些未说出口、不可言说的东西。

Skillful dialogue creates a kind of transparency. The text of a character’s spoken words conceals her inner life from other characters, while at the same time allowing the reader/audience to see through the surface of her behavior. Adept dialogue delivers the sensation of insight, the sense of reading a character’s mind and knowing what she is really thinking, really feeling, really doing to the point of understanding her inner life better than the character herself.

精妙的对话能营造一种透明感。人物的言语既能向其他角色隐藏其内心世界，又能让读者/观众看穿其行为表象。娴熟的对话能带来洞察人心的感觉，仿佛能读懂人物的内心，了解她真正的所思所想、所感所为，甚至比人物本人更了解她的内心世界。

We who live in the word-centric culture of European heritage tend to believe that language sets the limits of experience. While there can be no doubt that language molds thinking in subtle ways, a writer must come to grips with how other modes of expression—the paralanguage of gesture and facial expression, along with tone of voice, dress, movement, and the like—influence a character’s experience of his inner self and outer life, and most importantly, how he expresses himself with or without words.

我们这些生活在以语言为中心的欧洲文化中的人，往往认为语言限制了经验的范畴。语言无疑会以微妙的方式塑造思维，但作家必须理解其他表达方式——例如手势和面部表情等副语言，以及语调、穿着、动作等等——如何影响人物对自身内心世界和外部生活的体验，以及最重要的是，如何影响人物如何用语言或不用语言表达自己。

When, for example, Character A says to Character B: “Hi, how ya doing? Oh look, you’ve lost weight!” On the text, Character A’s actions greet and compliment Character B. But depending on the nature and history of their relationship, in the subtext Character A could be doing anything from encouraging to seducing to taunting to insulting Character B. The possible subtextual actions under the most seemingly neutral expressions are as varied as the beings who take them.

例如，当角色A对角色B说：“嗨，你好吗？哦，你看，你瘦了！” 字面上，角色A的举动是对角色B的问候和赞美。但根据他们关系的性质和过往，言外之意可能是角色A在鼓励、诱惑、嘲讽甚至侮辱角色B。即使是最看似中性的表达，其背后可能隐藏的潜台词也如同说话者本身一样千差万别。

Human nature constantly combines an outer behavior (text) with subterranean selves (subtext). Those rare and rather strange people who put their unsaid directly into their said seem mechanical, unreal, inhuman, disconnected, even insane. Hitler, for example, had no subtext. Mein Kampf was not a metaphor; it was a timetable for the holocaust. He stated his full intentions in the text, but because his visions were too horrible to believe, allied politicians spent the 1930s searching for consolation in a nonexistent subtext.

人性总是将外在行为（言外之意）与内在自我（潜台词）融合在一起。那些罕见且颇为怪异的人，将未言之意直接融入言外之意，显得机械、不真实、非人、疏离，甚至疯狂。例如，希特勒就没有潜台词。《我的奋斗》并非隐喻，而是大屠杀的时间表。他在书中阐述了自己的全部意图，但由于他的设想过于恐怖，令人难以置信，因此盟军政客在整个20世纪30年代都在试图从并不存在的潜台词中寻求慰藉。

#↩

4

EXPRESSIVITY II: FORM

表现力 II：形式

The qualities and quantities of dialogue vary with the levels of conflict used in the storytelling.

对话的质量和数量会随着故事中冲突程度的变化而变化。

THE CONFLICT COMPLEX

冲突复合体

Conflict disrupts our lives from any one of four levels: the physical (time, space, and everything in it), the social (institutions and the individuals in them), the personal (relationships of intimacy—friends, family, lovers), and the private (conscious and subconscious thoughts and feelings). The difference between a complicated story and a complex story, between a story with minimum dialogue versus maximum dialogue, hinges on the layers of conflict the writer chooses to dramatize.

冲突会从四个层面扰乱我们的生活：物质层面（时间、空间及其中的一切）、社会层面（制度及其中的个体）、个人层面（亲密关系——朋友、家人、爱人）以及私人层面（意识和潜意识的思想和情感）。复杂的故事与精炼的故事、对话最少的故事与对话最多的故事之间的区别，取决于作者选择戏剧化的冲突层次。

The action genres put their protagonists up against physical conflict almost exclusively. For example, J. C. Chandor’s film ALL IS LOST. On the other hand, the novelistic technique of stream of consciousness submerges the telling entirely at the layer of inner conflict. There, it churns crosscurrents of dream and memory, of regret and yearning that flood the protagonist’s mind. For example, Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway .

动作片几乎总是让主角直面肢体冲突。例如，J·C·钱德尔的电影《一切尽失》。另一方面，意识流小说技巧则完全将叙事沉浸于内心冲突的层面。在那里，梦境与记忆、悔恨与渴望交织的暗流涌动，充斥着主角的内心世界。例如，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《达洛维夫人》。

Filmmakers like Chandor, who strive for a purity of objectivity, or authors like Woolf, who seek a purity of subjectivity, complicate their works at the extreme of only one level of conflict. As a result, their genius crafts a compelling story with little or no need for spoken dialogue. Stories told with highly kinetic concentration at just one level of life are complicated, often dazzlingly so, but, in my definition, not complex.

像钱德尔这样追求客观纯粹的电影人，或者像伍尔夫这样追求主观纯粹的作家，都将作品的复杂性局限于单一层面。因此，他们的才华在于能够创作出引人入胜的故事，而无需或只需极少的对白。以高度集中的笔触，聚焦于生活某一层面的故事固然复杂，往往令人叹为观止，但在我看来，它并非晦涩难懂。

Complex stories embrace two, three, or even all four levels of human conflict. Authors with worldviews both wide and deep often bracket their tellings with inner conflict at one level, physical strife at another, and then concentrate on the middle ranges of social and personal conflicts—the two venues of talk.

复杂的故事往往包含两到三个层次的人类冲突，甚至全部四个层次的冲突。拥有广阔而深刻世界观的作者常常会先描写内心冲突，再描写肢体冲突，最后聚焦于社会冲突和个人冲突这两个中间层面——这也是故事的两种主要叙述方式。

Personal conflicts embroil friends, family, and lovers. Intimacy, by its nature, begins in talk, then builds, changes, and ends in talk. Personal conflicts, therefore, roil with multilayered, multi-meaning dialogue.

个人冲突牵涉到朋友、家人和爱人之间。亲密关系本质上始于交谈，然后发展、变化，最终又回归交谈。因此，个人冲突往往伴随着多层次、多义的对话。

For example, this exchange between Walter White and his wife, Skyler, in Season 4, Episode 6 of BREAKING BAD. From the first season’s first episode on, Walter White’s characterization portrays a nervous, insecure, defensive man. But by the end of this scene we glimpse his true character.

例如，《绝命毒师》第四季第六集中沃尔特·怀特和他妻子斯凯勒的这段对话。从第一季第一集开始，沃尔特·怀特的形象就被塑造成一个紧张、缺乏安全感、充满防备的男人。但到了这场戏的结尾，我们得以窥见他真实的性格。

INT. BEDROOM—DAY.

内景。卧室—日。

Husband and wife sit on the bed.

夫妻二人坐在床上。

SKYLER

斯凯勒

I said before, if you are in danger, we go to the police.

我之前说过，如果你有危险，我们就报警。

WALTER

沃尔特

No, I don’t want to hear about the police.

不，我不想听关于警察的事。

SKYLER

斯凯勒

I do not say that lightly. I know what it could do to this family, but if it is the only real choice we have, if it’s either that or you getting shot when you open your front door—

我这么说并非轻率之举。我知道这会给这个家庭带来怎样的打击，但如果这是我们唯一的选择，如果要么这样，要么你一开门就被枪杀——

WALTER

沃尔特

—I don’t want to hear about the police.

—我不想听到任何关于警察的事情。

SKYLER

斯凯勒

You’re not some hardened criminal, Walt. You are in over your head. That’s what we tell them, that’s the truth.

沃尔特，你不是什么穷凶极恶的罪犯。你只是力不从心罢了。我们就是这么跟他们说的，这才是实话。

WALTER

沃尔特

That’s not the truth.

那不是事实。

SKYLER

斯凯勒

Of course it is. A schoolteacher, cancer, desperate for money—

当然是这样。一位小学老师，身患癌症，急需用钱——

WALTER

沃尔特

(getting up)

（起床）

—We’re done.

—我们完成了。

SKYLER

斯凯勒

—roped into working, unable to quit. You told me that yourself, Walt. Jesus, what was I thinking?

——被迫工作，无法辞职。你自己也跟我说过，沃尔特。天哪，我当时到底在想什么？

(pause)

（暂停）

Walt, please, let’s both of us stop trying to justify this whole thing, and admit you’re in danger.

沃尔特，求你了，我们俩都别再试图为这件事辩解了，承认你现在很危险吧。

Walter slowly turns to her.

沃尔特缓缓转向她。

WALTER

沃尔特

Who are you talking to right now? Who is it you think you see?

你现在在和谁说话？你觉得你看到的是谁？

(pause)

（暂停）

Do you know how much I make a year? Even if I told you, you wouldn’t believe it. Do you know what would happen if I suddenly decided to stop going to work? A business big enough that it could be listed on the NASDAQ goes belly up. Disappears. It ceases to exist without me.

你知道我一年挣多少钱吗？就算我说了，你也不会相信。你知道如果我突然不去上班会发生什么吗？一家规模大到可以在纳斯达克上市的公司会倒闭，消失，没有我，它就不复存在了。

(pause)

（暂停）

No, you clearly don’t know who you’re talking to, so let me clue you in. I am not in danger, Skyler. I am the danger. A guy opens a door and gets shot. You think that’s me? No, I am the one who knocks.

不，你显然不知道你在跟谁说话，让我来告诉你。我没有危险，斯凯勒。我就是危险本身。有人开门就被枪杀了。你以为那是我？不，我是敲门的人。

He walks out of the bedroom; Skyler stares after him.

他走出卧室；斯凯勒目送他离去的背影。

Walter is describing his new, other self, the doppelgänger we come to know as Heisenberg. Skyler, dumbfounded by her husband’s words, can only grasp for the meaning.

沃尔特正在描述他的新自我，也就是我们后来所知的那个分身——海森堡。斯凯勒被丈夫的话弄得目瞪口呆，只能努力理解其中的含义。

Social conflicts surge through institutions of public purpose: medical, educational, military, religious, governmental, corporate—all societal enterprises, legal and criminal. As people move from personal to social relationships, they often speak with less sincerity and greater formality. When public conflicts peak, characters break into speeches.

社会冲突在公共机构中此起彼伏：医疗、教育、军事、宗教、政府、企业——所有社会机构，无论合法与否。当人们从私人关系转向社会关系时，他们的言谈举止往往不再那么真诚，反而更加正式。当公共冲突达到顶峰时，人们便会发表长篇大论。

Consider this example from HOUSE OF CARDS. A political operative rejects a proposal from Frank Underwood. As the operative walks off, Frank turns to camera with this aside:

以《纸牌屋》中的这个例子为例。一位政治掮客拒绝了弗兰克·安德伍德的提议。掮客走开后，弗兰克转向镜头，说道：

FRANK

坦率

Such a waste of talent. He chose money over power. In this town a mistake nearly everyone makes. Money is the McMansion in Sarasota that starts falling apart after ten years; power is the old stone building that stands for centuries. I cannot respect someone who does not see the difference.

真是浪费才华。他选择了金钱而非权力。在这个城市，几乎每个人都会犯这个错误。金钱就像萨拉索塔的豪宅，十年后就开始摇摇欲坠；而权力则像屹立数百年的古老石屋。我无法尊重那些看不出其中区别的人。

To generalize: The more physical and social a story’s conflicts, the less the dialogue; the more personal and private the conflicts, the more the dialogue.

总的来说：故事中的冲突越是涉及身体和社会因素，对话就越少；冲突越是涉及个人和私人因素，对话就越多。

Therefore, to create a complex story, the writer must master the double dimension of dialogue—the outer aspect of what is said versus the inner truth of what is thought and felt. When first spoken, a line of dialogue conveys a surface meaning, the meaning the speaker hopes other characters will believe in and act on. This first meaning seems logical in its context, conveys a sense of character purpose and tactic, and arouses curiosity as we glance across the scene to see its effect. The language itself may also delight us with tropes or wordplay, especially when written for the stage. In the next moment, however, this solid speech seems to dissolve, and we sense a second, deeper meaning hidden behind the words.

因此，要创作一个复杂的故事，作家必须掌握对话的双重维度——言语的外在表现和内心所想所感的内在真相。一句台词初次开口时，传达的是一种表面含义，说话者希望其他角色相信并付诸行动。这种表面含义在语境中似乎合情合理，传达出角色的目的和策略，并激发我们的好奇心，让我们不禁扫视场景，观察其效果。语言本身也可能运用修辞手法或文字游戏，尤其是在舞台剧中，令我们感到愉悦。然而，下一刻，这看似严谨的言语仿佛消解，我们感受到隐藏在字里行间的第二层、更深层次的含义。

Thanks to our powers of intuition and perception, character-specific dialogue inspires a sudden insight into the character’s ineffable inner self, his unseen needs and desires. True-to-character talk lets us read past conscious thoughts and sense unspoken feelings down to a character’s subconscious urges. This effect is so powerful that the fullness and depth of insight we have into fictional characters often surpasses what we glimpse in the living people around us.

凭借我们的直觉和感知力，人物对话能够让我们瞬间洞察人物难以言喻的内心世界，以及他们不为人知的需求和欲望。符合人物性格的对话让我们能够读懂人物意识之外的想法，感知他们未曾言明的情感，甚至触及他们潜意识的冲动。这种效果如此强大，以至于我们对虚构人物的理解之深刻和全面，往往超越了我们对身边真实人物的认知。

Dialogue, at its best, hangs suspended between a character’s public face and her secret self. Like multifaceted crystals, her spoken words refract and reflect aspects of her inner and outer lives. Because personal and social lives begin, evolve, and end through talk, the complex relationships and conflicts between human beings cannot be fully dramatized without expressive, character-specific dialogue.

对话，在最佳状态下，悬于人物的公众形象与内心世界之间。如同多面切割的水晶，她口中的话语折射并映照出她内心世界和外在生活的方方面面。因为个人生活和社会生活都始于对话，发展于对话，最终也结束于对话，所以，如果没有富有表现力、贴合人物性格的对话，人与人之间复杂的关系和冲突就无法得到充分的戏剧化展现。

Inept dialogue, on the other hand, not only rings false, but also shallows out the characters who speak it. Weak dialogue suffers from many faults such as poor word choices, but the root cause runs much deeper:

另一方面，拙劣的对话不仅听起来不真实，还会使说话的角色形象变得苍白无力。糟糕的对话存在诸多缺陷，例如用词不当，但其根本原因远不止于此：

Dialogue problems are story problems.

对话问题也是故事问题。

With almost algebraic symmetry, the worse the storytelling, the worse the dialogue. And because stories are so often hackneyed, we suffer dissonant dialogue in countless films and plays and on hundreds of TV channels. The same is true of the novel. Although modern prose often speeds the read with page after page of dialogue, when was the last time you were deeply moved by a chapter of talk? The majority of dialogue published or performed is serviceable at best and instantly forgotten.

几乎是遵循着代数对称的规律：故事讲得越差，对话也越糟糕。由于故事常常陈腐不堪，我们在无数的电影、戏剧和数百个电视频道中都饱受不和谐对话的折磨。小说亦是如此。尽管现代散文常常用一页又一页的对话来加快阅读速度，但你上一次被一段对话深深打动是什么时候？大多数已出版或表演的对话充其量只能算得上合格，而且很快就会被遗忘。

We’re drawn to stories not only because they reflect the life around us, but also because they illuminate the life within. One of the great pleasures of story is staring, self-absorbed, into the mirror of fiction. Dialogue shows us how we lie to others, how we lie to ourselves, how we love, how we beg, how we fight, how we see the world. Dialogue teaches us what could or should be said in life’s harshest or most rapturous moments.

我们之所以被故事吸引，不仅因为它们反映了我们周围的生活，更因为它们照亮了我们内心的世界。故事的一大乐趣在于，我们可以沉浸其中，凝视着虚构的镜子。对话向我们展示了我们如何欺骗他人，如何欺骗自己，如何去爱，如何乞求，如何争斗，以及我们如何看待这个世界。对话教会我们在人生最艰难或最狂喜的时刻，哪些话该说，哪些话该说。

DIALOGUE ONSTAGE

舞台对话

The stage is a symbolic space. From that moment untold millennia ago when the first actor stood up to perform a story for his tribe, audiences have instinctively understood that what is said and done in that precious space means far more than words and gestures. 1

舞台是一个象征性的空间。从数千年前第一位演员站上舞台为他的族人表演故事的那一刻起，观众们就本能地明白，在这个珍贵的空间里所说所做的一切，其意义远不止于言语和姿态。

The stage puts the artificiality of art on open display. In the ritual of theatre, actors act out fictional people in the living presence of other people, everyone breathing the same air, all the while pretending that this unreality is, for the moment, real. By taking her seat, the theatergoer signs an implicit contract with the playwright: He may turn the onstage space into any world he imagines, symbolic of whatever meaning he wishes to express; she in turn will suspend her disbelief and react to his characters as if they were living their lives in front of her.

舞台将艺术的虚构性公之于众。在戏剧的仪式中，演员们在活生生的观众面前演绎虚构人物，所有人呼吸着同样的空气，却都假装这虚构的场景在此刻是真实的。观众入座的那一刻，就与剧作家签订了一份无形的契约：他可以将舞台空间变成他想象中的任何世界，象征着他想要表达的任何意义；而观众则要暂时放下怀疑，对剧中人物做出反应，仿佛他们就在她面前真实地生活着。

Are there limits to the “as if” convention? Apparently not. Since the advent of Dada over a century ago, audiences have signed on for the wildest rides, embracing surrealist plays such as André Breton’s If You Please (1920), Theatre of the Absurd pieces such as Eugène Ionesco’s anti-play The Bald Soprano (1950), the fragmentations of the Furth and Sondheim concept musical Company (1970), and the literally hundreds of avant-garde plays performed at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe every August.

“仿佛”这种手法有限制吗？显然没有。自从一个多世纪前达达主义诞生以来，观众们就乐于接受各种天马行空的表演，包括安德烈·布勒东的超现实主义戏剧《请你》（1920）、尤金·尤内斯库的反戏剧《秃头歌女》（1950）等荒诞派戏剧作品、弗斯和桑德海姆的概念音乐剧《公司》（1970）的碎片化结构，以及每年八月在爱丁堡艺穗节上演的数百部先锋戏剧。

The “as if” conspiracy between author and audience licenses playwrights to write dialogue at heights and depths of sublimity no human being has ever actually spoken. From the master dramatists of classical Greece, through Shakespeare, Ibsen, and O’Neill, to contemporaries like Jez Butterworth, Mark O’Rowe, and Richard Marsh, playwrights have used imagistic language and verse rhythms to intensify dialogue with poetic force. And the audience listens because in the theatre we want to hear first, see second.

作者与观众之间那种“仿佛”的默契，赋予了剧作家创作对话的权力，使其达到人类从未真正说过的崇高境界。从古希腊的戏剧大师，到莎士比亚、易卜生和奥尼尔，再到杰兹·巴特沃斯、马克·奥罗和理查德·马什等当代剧作家，他们都运用意象丰富的语言和韵律，以诗意的力量强化对话。而观众之所以会倾听，是因为在剧院里，我们首先想要听到声音，其次才是看到画面。

What’s more, the stage inspires the constant exploration and reinvention of language. When Shakespeare couldn’t find the word he wanted, he made one up: barefaced, obscene, eyeball, lonely, zany, gloomy, gnarled, bump, elbow, amazement, torture, and over 1,700 other words are Shakespeare’s invention.

此外，舞台激发了人们对语言的不断探索和重塑。当莎士比亚找不到他想要的词时，他就自己造一个：barefaced（赤裸裸的）、obscene（淫秽的）、eyeball（眼球）、lonely（孤独的）、zany（古怪的）、gloomy（阴郁的）、gnarled（扭曲的）、bump（碰撞）、elbow（肘部）、amazement（惊奇）、torture（酷刑）等等，超过1700个其他词汇都是莎士比亚的创造。

From the naturalistic barroom grit of Eugene O’Neill’s The Iceman Cometh to the poetic elegance of T. S. Eliot’s Murder in the Cathedral , the spectrum of language in the theatre is unmatched in the other media of story.

从尤金·奥尼尔的《送冰人来了》中自然主义的酒吧场景，到T·S·艾略特的《大教堂谋杀案》中诗意的优雅，戏剧语言的丰富性在其他叙事媒介中是无法比拟的。

For example, consider the coffee table talk in Yasmina Reza’s play God of Carnage as translated by Christopher Hampton. Two couples begin the evening discussing a playground fight between their children. Their civilized conversation, lubricated with alcohol, descends into ugly truths about their marriages. In the dialogue below, both wives use sharp “as if” similes to belittle their husbands.

例如，不妨看看克里斯托弗·汉普顿翻译的雅丝米娜·雷扎的戏剧《杀戮之神》中的一段茶几闲聊。两对夫妇在傍晚时分开始讨论他们孩子在操场上的一场打架。在酒精的作用下，他们原本文明的谈话逐渐演变成对婚姻中丑陋真相的揭露。在下面的对话中，两位妻子都使用了尖锐的“仿佛”比喻来贬低她们的丈夫。

MICHAEL: Drinking always makes you unhappy.

迈克尔：喝酒总是让人不开心。

VERONICA: Michael, every word that comes out of your mouth is destroying me. I don’t drink. I drank a mouthful of this shitty rum you’re waving about as if you were showing the congregation the Shroud of Turin. I don’t drink and I bitterly regret it. It’d be a relief to be able to take refuge in a little drop at every minor setback.

维罗妮卡：迈克尔，你说的每一个字都让我难受。我不喝酒。我喝了一小口你挥舞着的这劣质朗姆酒，就好像你在向会众展示都灵裹尸布一样。我不喝酒，我为此后悔不已。如果每次遇到小挫折都能借酒消愁，那该多好啊。

ANNETTE: My husband’s unhappy as well. Look at him. Slumped. He looks as if someone left him by the side of the road. I think it’s the unhappiest day of his life. 2

安妮特：我丈夫也不开心。你看他，垂头丧气的，好像被人丢在路边似的。我觉得这是他一生中最难过的一天。

Now compare the phlegmatic ridicule of these two wives to this vibrant speech from Blood Wedding (1933) by Federico García Lorca, translated by Fernanda Diaz. As a servant sets the table for a wedding, she warns the bride of a coming tragedy, spinning trope upon trope:

现在，请将这两位妻子冷漠的嘲讽与费德里科·加西亚·洛尔卡 (Federico García Lorca) 的小说《血婚》(Blood Wedding, 1933) 中这段充满活力的独白进行比较，该小说由费尔南达·迪亚兹 (Fernanda Diaz) 翻译。一位女仆正在为婚礼布置餐桌，她警告新娘即将到来的悲剧，并反复吟诵着各种比喻：

SERVANT:

仆人：

For the wedding night

新婚之夜

let the warping moon

让扭曲的月亮

part the black leaves

拨开黑色的叶子

and gaze down

向下凝视

from her white window.

从她白色的窗户望出去。

For the wedding night

新婚之夜

let the frost burn,

让霜冻燃烧吧，

let the acid almond

让酸性杏仁

turn sweet as honey.

变得像蜂蜜一样甜。

O exquisite woman

哦，绝世佳人

your wedding night nears.

你的婚礼之夜即将到来。

Tighten your gown, hide

拉紧你的长袍，藏好

beneath your husband’s wing.

在丈夫的庇护下。

He is a dove

他是一只鸽子

with a breast of fire.

胸中燃起一团火焰。

Never leave the house.

永远不要离开家。

The fields wait for the cry

田野等待着哭泣

of eloping blood.

私奔之血。

To the ancient “as if” convention of the legit theatre, the musical theatre adds yet another glaze, transfiguring the poetics of spoken lines into lyrics and arias that heighten emotion the way dance enhances gesture. Indeed, all the principles and techniques of dialogue discussed in this book apply to musical theatre. From the recitativo of opera to the sung-through scenes of the modern musical, characters who sing and dance vocalize dialogue into music. Songs are simply another form of in-character talk.

在传统戏剧“仿佛”的古老惯例基础上，音乐剧又增添了一层光彩，将对白的诗意转化为歌词和咏叹调，如同舞蹈强化肢体语言一般，极大地提升了情感表达。事实上，本书探讨的所有对话原则和技巧都适用于音乐剧。从歌剧的宣叙调到现代音乐剧的歌唱式场景，歌舞演员们将对话化作音乐。歌曲不过是角色对话的另一种形式。

Theatre audiences hold to their belief in the “as if” so long as the play creates an internally consistent setting in which characters talk (or sing) in a manner that seems true to their world and to themselves; in other words, as long as dialogue stays in-character. For without credibility, stories risk billowing into meaningless, emotionless spectacles.

只要戏剧营造出一个内在逻辑自洽的场景，让角色们的言谈（或歌唱）符合他们所处的世界和自身形象，观众们就会坚持“仿佛如此”的信念；换句话说，只要对话符合角色设定。因为缺乏可信度，故事就有可能沦为毫无意义、冷漠无情的闹剧。

DIALOGUE IN FILM

电影中的对话

A camera can fly through 360 degrees of global reality, devouring every object, shape, and color in its path. Anything a writer can dream, CGIs can duplicate beyond his dreams. Because the big screen foregrounds images and backgrounds sounds, film audiences instinctively absorb the story through their eyes, while they half listen to the score, sound effects, and dialogue.

摄像机可以360度环游世界，捕捉沿途的每一个物体、形状和色彩。作家能想象到的一切，电脑特效都能将其完美呈现，甚至超越他的想象。由于大银幕将图像置于前景，声音置于背景，观众会本能地通过视觉来吸收故事，同时又会半听半听地聆听配乐、音效和对白。

In fact, for some cinema purists, the ideal film would be wordless. I appreciate their aesthetic, but while it’s true that moving moments in film are often mute, when I compare the best silent films with the finest sound films, for me, stories told with audible dialogue win hands down. The image of Thelma and Louise driving over a cliff into the Grand Canyon shines vividly in my memory, but as I recall, they were shouting a joyful “Keep going!” as they did. Without that line, the impact of their suicide would have been halved.

事实上，对一些电影纯粹主义者来说，理想的电影应该是无声的。我欣赏他们的审美，但尽管电影中许多感人的瞬间的确是无声的，但如果让我比较最好的默片和最优秀的有声电影，对我而言，有声对白的故事无疑更胜一筹。塞尔玛和路易丝驾车冲下悬崖坠入大峡谷的画面至今仍清晰地印在我的脑海里，但我记得，她们当时还在欢呼着“继续前进！”。如果没有这句台词，她们自杀的冲击力将会减半。

Although storytelling on the big screen clearly favors image over language, the balance varies greatly from genre to genre. An Action/Adventure film, such as ALL IS LOST, is told with no dialogue, whereas an education plot, such as MY DINNER WITH ANDRE, is told in all dialogue.

虽然大银幕上的叙事明显更注重画面而非语言，但这种平衡在不同类型的影片中差异很大。例如，动作冒险片《一切尽失》完全没有对白，而教育题材影片《与安德烈共进晚餐》则全部采用对白。

The greatest difference between the screen versus stage and page, therefore, is not the quantity of dialogue but the quality. The camera and microphone so magnify and amplify behavior, that every phony glance, every false gesture, every affected line looks and sounds more amateur than the worst dinner party charade. Screen acting calls for a naturalistic, believable, and seemingly offhanded technique. To make this possible, screen dialogue must feel spontaneous. When forced to deliver ornamented dialogue, even the finest actors sound ludicrous, cueing the audience to react with “People don’t talk like that.” This holds true in all genres, realistic and nonrealistic, in television and film.

因此，银幕与舞台和书页之间最大的区别不在于对白的数量，而在于对白的质量。摄像机和麦克风会放大和强化演员的行为，使得每一个虚假的眼神、每一个做作的手势、每一句矫揉造作的台词，都显得比最糟糕的晚宴闹剧还要业余。银幕表演需要一种自然、可信且看似漫不经心的技巧。为了达到这种效果，银幕对白必须显得自然流畅。即使是最优秀的演员，如果被迫说一些华丽的辞藻，也会显得滑稽可笑，让观众不禁发出“人们根本不会那样说话”的感叹。这一点在电视和电影的各种类型作品中都适用，无论是现实主义还是非现实主义。

There are, of course, exceptions.

当然，也有例外情况。

One: Stylized Realism

一：风格化现实主义

Realism bends with a certain elasticity. Setting a story in an unfamiliar world allows the writer to enhance dialogue with greater figurative language than a commonplace location, but the talk must still stay within the realm of believability that the story’s world sets for itself. A film or television series in a foreign setting (THE GRAND BUDAPEST HOTEL and HOMELAND), a criminal society (PULP FICTION and DEADWOOD), a regional culture (BEASTS OF THE SOUTHERN WILD and JUSTIFIED), or the distant past (SPARTACUS and VIKINGS) can take dialogue well beyond the everyday, so long as it maintains credibility within its self-imposed limits.

现实主义具有一定的弹性。将故事设定在一个陌生的世界，可以让作者运用比在寻常地点更为丰富的比喻性语言来增强对话效果，但对话内容仍须符合故事世界本身设定的可信度。以异国风情（如《布达佩斯大饭店》和《国土安全》）、犯罪社会（如《低俗小说》和《朽木》）、地域文化（如《南方的野兽》和《火线警探》）或遥远的过去（如《斯巴达克斯》和《维京传奇》）为背景的电影或电视剧，只要在自身设定的界限内保持可信度，就可以将对话发挥到远超日常的程度。

In these exotic cases consistency becomes a problem. The writer must be able to sustain an eccentric yet believable style over a full-length film or even long-form television series such as THE WIRE. No easy task.

在这些特殊情况下，风格一致性就成了问题。编剧必须能够在一整部电影，甚至是像《火线》这样的长篇电视剧中，保持一种古怪却又令人信服的风格。这绝非易事。

Two: Nonrealism

二：非现实主义

Genres of nonrealism (science fiction, musical, animation, fantasy, horror, and farce) tend to tell allegorical stories, acted out by archetypal or symbolic characters. In these genres, audiences not only accept but also enjoy highly stylized dialogue. Think of THE MATRIX, 300, CORPSE BRIDE, THE LORD OF THE RINGS, DR. SEUSS’ THE CAT IN THE HAT, GAME OF THRONES, or GLEE.

非现实主义类型（科幻、音乐剧、动画、奇幻、恐怖和闹剧）往往讲述寓言故事，由原型或象征性的角色演绎。在这些类型中，观众不仅接受，而且欣赏高度风格化的对话。例如《黑客帝国》、《300勇士》、《僵尸新娘》、《指环王》、《戴帽子的猫》（苏斯博士著）、《权力的游戏》或《欢乐合唱团》。

Three: Extreme Characters

三、极端人物

In life, some people outfeel, outthink, and outtalk the people around them. Such characters deserve and should get imaginative, one-of-a-kind dialogue.

生活中，有些人比周围的人更有感觉、更有智慧、更能言善辩。这样的人物值得拥有也应该拥有充满想象力、独一无二的对话。

Suppose you were writing for extreme characters such as Walter White (Bryan Cranston) in BREAKING BAD; Captain Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp) in PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN; Melvin Udall in AS GOOD AS IT GETS, Jimmy Hoffa in HOFFA, or Frank Costello in THE DEPARTED (all played by Jack Nicholson); or Sophie Zawistowski in SOPHIE’S CHOICE, Suzanne Vale in POSTCARDS FROM THE EDGE, or Margaret Thatcher in THE IRON LADY (all played by Meryl Streep). Excellent writers gave these bigger-than-life characters image-rich language that attracted actors who knew what to do with it.

假设你要为一些性格鲜明的角色创作剧本，比如《绝命毒师》中的沃尔特·怀特（布莱恩·克兰斯顿饰）；《加勒比海盗》中的杰克·斯派洛船长（约翰尼·德普饰）；《尽善尽美》中的梅尔文·尤德尔、《霍法》中的吉米·霍法、《无间道风云》中的弗兰克·科斯特洛（均由杰克·尼科尔森饰演）；或者《苏菲的选择》中的苏菲·扎维斯托夫斯基、《边缘明信片》中的苏珊娜·韦尔、《铁娘子》中的玛格丽特·撒切尔（均由梅丽尔·斯特里普饰演）。优秀的编剧会赋予这些极具个性的人物形象，并运用生动形象的语言来吸引那些懂得如何演绎这些角色的演员。

Consider these two characters: Philip Marlowe (Humphrey Bogart) and Vivian Rutledge (Lauren Bacall) from THE BIG SLEEP (1946). William Faulkner, Leigh Brackett, and Jules Furthman adapted the film from Raymond Chandler’s novel. In Hollywood jargon, the film is a crimedy, the merger of two genres: crime story and romantic comedy. Repartee and mimicry leaven the intrigue and gunplay. In one sequence, for example, Marlowe, a private detective, pretends to be a gay rare book collector.

想想电影《夜长梦多》（1946）中的这两个角色：菲利普·马洛（亨弗莱·鲍嘉饰）和薇薇安·拉特利奇（劳伦·白考尔饰）。威廉·福克纳、莉·布拉克特和朱尔斯·弗斯曼根据雷蒙德·钱德勒的小说改编了这部电影。用好莱坞的行话来说，这部电影是一部犯罪喜剧，融合了犯罪故事和浪漫喜剧两种类型。机智的对话和模仿为悬疑和枪战增添了趣味。例如，在其中一个场景中，私家侦探马洛假扮成一位同性恋珍本书收藏家。

In the scene below, Marlowe meets his client’s daughter, Vivian. The two use racehorses as metaphors for themselves, and horse racing as a metaphor for sex. Their flirtation characterizes them as quick-witted, worldly-wise, self-assured, amusing, and mutually attracted. (To “rate” a Thoroughbred means to restrain the horse early in a race in order to conserve its energy for the finish.)

在下面的场景中，马洛遇到了他委托人的女儿薇薇安。两人用赛马来比喻自己，又用赛马来比喻性。他们的调情展现了他们机智、世故、自信、风趣以及彼此吸引的特质。（“给纯种马配速”是指在比赛初期控制马匹的节奏，以便节省体力冲刺。）

VIVIAN

薇薇安

Speaking of horses, I like to play them myself. But I like to see them work out a little first to see if they’re front-runners or come from behind, find out what their hole card is, what makes them run.

说到赛马，我自己也喜欢玩。但我喜欢先观察一下它们的表现，看看它们是领跑型选手还是后程发力型选手，找出它们的底牌，了解它们的冲刺动机。

MARLOWE

马洛

Find out mine?

找出我的？

VIVIAN

薇薇安

I think so. I’d say you don’t like to be rated, you like to get out in front, open up a lead, take a little breather in the backstretch, then come home free.

我想是的。我觉得你不喜欢被评分，你喜欢冲到前面，拉开差距，在后半程稍微喘口气，然后轻松冲过终点线。

MARLOWE

马洛

You don’t like to be rated yourself.

你不喜欢别人评价自己。

VIVIAN

薇薇安

I haven’t met anyone yet who could do it. Any suggestions?

我还没遇到能做这件事的人。有什么建议吗？

MARLOWE

马洛

Well, I can’t tell till I’ve seen you over a distance of ground. You got a touch of class but… I don’t know how far you can go.

嗯，没看过你远一点，我不好说。你有点气质，但是……我不知道你能走多远。

VIVIAN

薇薇安

That depends on who’s in the saddle.

那取决于谁掌舵。

MARLOWE

马洛

There’s one thing I still can’t figure out.

有一件事我至今仍想不明白。

VIVIAN

薇薇安

What makes me run?

是什么让我奔跑？

MARLOWE

马洛

Uh-huh.

嗯哼。

VIVIAN

薇薇安

I’ll give you a little hint. Sugar won’t work. It’s been tried.

我给你一点提示。糖行不通。已经试过了。

When writing for the screen, even within the most fantasied genres, always write for the actor. Language knows no limits, but acting does. Once your work is in production, an actor will have to act your lines with clarity and conviction. Therefore, what’s said must be kept within the realm of what’s actable. This demand leads to a major difference between dialogue for the stage versus the screen: improvisation.

即使是创作最具奇幻色彩的剧本，在为电影剧本写作时，也务必始终以演员为中心。语言没有界限，但表演却有。一旦作品投入制作，演员就必须清晰而充满感染力地演绎你的台词。因此，台词必须控制在可表演的范围内。这一要求导致了舞台剧和电影对白的一个主要区别：即兴发挥。

In the theatre, the playwright owns the play’s copyright. As a result, actors may not improvise or paraphrase dialogue without the author’s permission. In film and television, however, the writer assigns copyright to the production company, so that when the need arises, directors, editors, and actors can cut, change, or add dialogue. The professional reality of writing for the screen is that the script you write may not be performed verbatim as you wrote it. As a result, sadly, an actor’s improvisations may diminish your work.

在戏剧界，剧作家拥有剧本的版权。因此，未经作者许可，演员不得即兴发挥或改写台词。然而，在电影和电视领域，编剧会将版权转让给制作公司，这样，在需要时，导演、剪辑师和演员可以删减、修改或添加台词。影视剧本创作的现实是，你写的剧本可能不会被逐字逐句地搬上银幕。因此，令人遗憾的是，演员的即兴发挥可能会降低你的作品价值。

Inept improvisations are easy to spot. When spontaneity blears and actors lose track, they often buy time by repeating each other’s cues until the scene sounds like an echo chamber:

拙劣的即兴表演很容易被发现。当自发性消失，演员失去节奏时，他们常常会通过重复彼此的提示来拖延时间，直到场景听起来像一个回音室：

ACTOR A

演员A

I think it’s time for you to leave.

我觉得你该走了。

ACTOR B

演员B

So you want me to leave, huh? Well, I’m not going anywhere until you listen to what I have to say.

所以你想让我走，是吗？哼，除非你听我说完，否则我是不会走的。

ACTOR A

演员A

I’ve listened to everything you have to say and none of it makes sense.

你说的我全都听了，但没有一句是合情合理的。

ACTOR B

演员B

Sense? Sense? You want me to make sense? What did I say that didn’t make sense?

有道理吗？有道理吗？你想让我说的话有道理吗？我说的话哪一句不合逻辑？

And on they ramble.

于是他们继续漫无目的地游荡。

In rare cases, however, such as Robert DeNiro’s “You talkin’ to me?” riff in TAXI DRIVER, an actor’s improvisation eclipses the script. In FORREST GUMP, for example, Forrest (Tom Hanks) joins the army and befriends fellow enlistee Bubba Blue (Mykelti Williamson). During a montage of their boot-camp labors, Williamson improvises this passage as transcribed from the screen:

然而，在极少数情况下，例如罗伯特·德尼罗在《出租车司机》中那句“你在跟我说话吗？”的即兴发挥，演员的即兴表演甚至盖过了剧本。再比如在《阿甘正传》中，福雷斯特（汤姆·汉克斯饰）参军入伍，结识了新兵巴布·布鲁（迈克尔蒂·威廉姆森饰）。在一段展现他们新兵训练营生活的蒙太奇中，威廉姆森根据屏幕上的台词即兴发挥了以下这段话：

Bubba Blue: Anyway, like I was sayin’, shrimp is the fruit of the sea. You can barbecue it, boil it, broil it, bake it, sauté it. Dey’s uh, shrimp kabobs, shrimp creole, shrimp gumbo. Pan-fried, deep-fried, stir-fried. There’s pineapple shrimp, lemon shrimp, coconut shrimp, pepper shrimp, cave shrimp, shrimp stew, shrimp salad, shrimp and potatoes, shrimp burger, cave shrimp. That– that’s about it.”

巴布·布鲁：总之，就像我刚才说的，虾是海里的水果。你可以烤着吃，煮着吃，煎着吃，烤着吃，炒着吃。有虾串、克里奥尔虾、秋葵虾汤。煎的、炸的、炒的。还有菠萝虾、柠檬虾、椰子虾、胡椒虾、洞穴虾、虾炖菜、虾沙拉、虾仁土豆、虾汉堡、洞穴虾。就这些了。”

Notice that Williamson used “cave shrimp,” a colorless crustacean found in the subterranean streams of Alabama and Kentucky, twice. Even the best of improvisations are prone to accidental repetition.

请注意，威廉姆森两次使用了“洞穴虾”这个词，这是一种生活在阿拉巴马州和肯塔基州地下溪流中的无色甲壳类动物。即使是最好的即兴创作也容易出现无意的重复。

DIALOGUE ON TELEVISION

电视对话

Comparing film to television, film (with exceptions) likes to take the camera out-of-doors onto the streets and into nature; television (with exceptions) gravitates toward indoor stories of families, friends, lovers, and coworkers. For that reason, television tends to write more face-to-face scenes, leaning the balance of dialogue versus image toward talk for three reasons:

与电影相比，电视（除少数例外）更倾向于将镜头搬到户外，拍摄街头巷尾和自然风光；而电视（除少数例外）则更偏爱室内场景，讲述家庭、朋友、恋人和同事之间的故事。因此，电视往往更注重面对面的场景，在对话与画面比例上倾向于对话，原因有三：

1) The small screen. Facial expressions are hard to read in full-length shots. This motivates the television camera to close in on a character’s face, and when it does, that face talks.

1）小屏幕。在全身镜头中很难解读面部表情。这促使电视摄像机拉近拍摄人物的脸部，而当镜头对准脸部时，表情便会说话。

2) Genre. Television favors genres such as family comedy, family drama, the love story, the buddy story, and professional dramas of all kinds (cops, criminals, lawyers, doctors, psychologists, etc.). These series frame personal relationships in homes and workplaces where intimacy begins, changes, and ends first and foremost through talk.

2）类型。电视节目偏爱家庭喜剧、家庭剧、爱情剧、兄弟情剧以及各种职业剧（警察、罪犯、律师、医生、心理学家等）。这些剧集以家庭和工作场所中的人际关系为框架，展现亲密关系的开始、变化和终结，而这些关系的开始、变化和终结首先都离不开对话。

3) Small budgets. Image costs money, resulting in high film budgets. Because dialogue is relatively inexpensive to stage and shoot, television’s limited budgets encourage talk.

3）预算有限。影像制作需要成本，因此电影预算很高。由于对话的制作和拍摄成本相对较低，电视预算有限，所以鼓励多说对话。

Looking toward the future, if wall-mounted screens continue to grow in size and popularity, TV budgets will also rise, causing a spike in subscription fees. In time, large home screens will merge film and television into one grand medium—the screen. On the other hand, when not at home, people will consume stories on their iPads and iPhones, thus keeping dialogue critical to the tellings. In either case, however, movie theatres will close.

展望未来，如果壁挂式屏幕的尺寸和普及程度持续增长，电视预算也将随之增加，导致订阅费用飙升。最终，大型家用屏幕将把电影和电视融合为一个宏大的媒介——屏幕。另一方面，人们不在家时，会通过iPad和iPhone等设备观看故事，因此对话对于故事叙述仍然至关重要。但无论如何，电影院都将关闭。

DIALOGUE IN PROSE

散文对话

Prose translates conflicts from the private, personal, social, and physical realms into word-pictures, often colored by the inner lives of characters, before projecting them onto the reader’s imagination. Consequently, prose writers pour their most vivid, high-intensity language into first-or third-person narration rather than exchanges of dialogue. Indeed, free indirect dialogue turns speech itself into narration. When prose writers do use direct dialogue in dramatized scenes, they often restrict themselves to very naturalist language in order to contrast the plainness of talk with the figurative potency of their narration. With exceptions, such as Stephen King’s Dolores Claiborne , many novelists and short-story writers use quoted dialogue as a technique to simply change pace or break up blocks of prose.

散文将私人、个人、社会和物质领域的冲突转化为文字画面，这些画面往往融入人物的内心世界，最终投射到读者的想象之中。因此，散文作家更倾向于将生动、强烈的语言运用到第一人称或第三人称叙述中，而非对话交流。事实上，自由间接引语本身就是一种叙述。当散文作家在戏剧化的场景中使用直接对话时，他们通常会限制自己使用非常自然的语言，以形成对话的朴实无华与叙述中丰富的象征意义之间的对比。除了像斯蒂芬·金的《多洛雷斯·克莱本》这样的例外，许多小说家和短篇小说作家使用引用对话仅仅是为了改变节奏或打破大段文字的叙述。

The stage and screen confine dialogue to acted scenes and occasional direct address that soliloquizes or narrates. Both media rely on actors to enrich their characters with subtext and the paralanguages of tonality, gesture, and facial expression. For that reason, an author’s expressivity in the theatre or on film and television has to work within the possibilities of the actor’s art. But because prose performs in the reader’s imagination, it offers the writer the widest spectrum of dialogue styles.

舞台和银幕上的对话仅限于表演场景和偶尔出现的独白或叙述。这两种媒介都依赖演员通过语调、手势和面部表情等潜台词和辅助语言来丰富角色。因此，作者在戏剧、电影或电视中的表达必须符合演员的艺术表现力。但由于散文是在读者的想象中呈现，它为作者提供了最广泛的对话风格选择。

At one end of the continuum, prose creates conventional scenes that could be transplanted directly to the stage or screen without changing a word. In the middle ranges, the first-person voice becomes a novel-length, uninterrupted speech composed of tens of thousands of words, all spoken to the reader. Some authors turn away from the reader, as it were, and distill thought into inner dialogues—secret conversations argued between the many voices of a multifaceted self. Finally, at the far opposite edge of the spectrum, third-person prose often eliminates quotation marks and characterized voices altogether to subsume character talk into free indirect dialogue.

在连续谱的一端，散文构建出传统的场景，可以直接移植到舞台或银幕上，无需改动一个字。在中间的范围内，第一人称叙述演变成一部篇幅堪比小说的、不间断的独白，由数万字组成，全部内容都直接对读者说。有些作者仿佛背离了读者，将思想提炼成内心对话——一个多面自我的不同声音之间进行的秘密对话。最后，在谱系的另一端，第三人称散文常常完全摒弃引号和人物声音，将人物对话融入自由间接引语中。

Chapter One looked at the three categories of point of view in prose and how they affect the qualities and quantities of dialogue. Now, let’s take those distinctions into more depth and detail by grouping the many varieties of prose dialogue into two grand modes: in-character versus non-character.

第一章探讨了散文中三种视角类型及其对对话质量和数量的影响。现在，让我们通过将散文对话的多种形式归纳为两大类——人物对话和非人物对话——来更深入、更详细地探讨这些区别。

Non-Character Narration

非角色叙述

The non-character side of prose tells its stories through a third-person narrator, an intelligence that is neither a character nor the real-life voice of the author, but a guiding awareness a writer invents and then endows with varying degrees of omniscience and objectivity to describe characters and events as well as provide commentary in various kinds of discourse.

散文的非人物描写部分通过第三人称叙述者讲述故事，这种叙述者既不是人物，也不是作者的真实声音，而是作者创造的一种指导意识，并赋予其不同程度的全知和客观性，以描述人物和事件，并在各种话语中提供评论。

A non-character narrator can present dialogue explicitly in dramatized scenes or implicitly via narratized indirect dialogue. Consider this from the short story “The Widow Predicament” by David Means:

非角色叙述者既可以在戏剧化的场景中明确地呈现对话，也可以通过叙述性的间接对话来隐含地呈现对话。请看大卫·米恩斯短篇小说《寡妇的困境》中的一个例子：

They sat across from each other at the Hudson House and conversed. His skin was weathered and he talked about Iceland most of the time until rising naturally out of his talk was the suggestion that perhaps she might want to see the country someday; nothing about dancing on the lip of volcanoes, or throwing themselves into one sacrificially, but a hint of it. 3

他们在哈德逊旅馆对面而坐，开始交谈。他皮肤黝黑，大部分时间都在谈论冰岛，直到他自然而然地提出，或许她有一天也想去看看这个国家；他并没有说要在火山口跳舞，或者纵身跃入火山自尽，只是略微提了一下。

Indirect dialogue in non-character narration gives the writer the usual assets of direct dialogue. It channels exposition when the reader needs to know that the talk took place and the upshot of what was said. It characterizes the speaker in terms of what the character talks about, although not how he says it. And as in the example above, the narration that surrounds indirect dialogue can express its subtext. Note how Means describes subtext as something “rising naturally out of his talk,” and uses the words “suggestion” and “hint” to convey a sense of ineffability.

在非人物叙述中，间接对话赋予作者与直接对话相同的优势。当读者需要了解对话发生过以及对话内容的最终结果时，间接对话便能起到交代背景的作用。它通过人物谈论的内容来刻画说话者的性格，而非通过说话的方式。正如上文所述，围绕间接对话的叙述可以表达其潜台词。请注意米恩斯如何将潜台词描述为“自然而然地从他的谈话中浮现出来的东西”，并使用“暗示”和“提示”等词语来传达一种难以言喻的感觉。

The two chief benefits of indirect dialogue in non-character narration are 1) acceleration of pace, and 2) protection against banality. The dinner table talk about Iceland that Means summarized in a phrase could have gone on for an hour. He saved us from that. And unless his character could describe with a Hemingwayesque eye, Means knew best to leave landscape adjectives off-page.

在非人物叙述中，间接对话的两大主要优点是：1）加快节奏；2）避免平庸。米恩斯用一句话概括了餐桌上关于冰岛的谈话，否则这些谈话可能会持续一个小时。他让我们免于此。除非他笔下的人物能像海明威那样描绘风景，否则米恩斯深知最好不要在书中赘述风景。

The characterless voice of a third-person narration can be quite distant, observant, and objective.

第三人称叙述的声音不带任何个人色彩，往往显得疏离、冷静和客观。

For example, a Joseph Conrad narrator describes a tropical dawn:

例如，约瑟夫·康拉德笔下的叙述者描述了热带地区的黎明：

The smooth darkness grew paler and became blotchy with ill-defined shapes, as if a new universe were being evolved out of somber chaos. Then outlines came out, defining forms without any details, indicating here a tree, there a bush; a black belt of forest far off. The day came rapidly, dismal and oppressed by the fog of the river and the heavy vapors of the sky—a day without color and without sunshine: incomplete, disappointing, sad.

原本柔和的黑暗渐渐褪色，斑驳的轮廓也随之显现，仿佛一个新的宇宙正从阴郁的混沌中演化而出。随后，轮廓浮现，勾勒出形状，却没有任何细节，这里是一棵树，那里是一丛灌木；远处是一片黑色的森林带。白昼迅速来临，河水的雾气和天空的浓重水汽笼罩着这阴沉压抑的一天——没有色彩，没有阳光：不完整，令人失望，令人悲伤。

When non-character awareness moves in the opposite direction and becomes intimate, imitative, and subjective, it adopts a stream of consciousness mode to invade the unsaid and unsayable realms and mirror a character’s inner life. This technique mixes the third-person narrator’s composure with the character’s emotional energies and word choices, melding into the role, replicating her thought processes, generating the impression of inner dialogue but without crossing the line to an in-character voice.
