当非角色视角转向更私密、更具模仿性和主观性时，它便会采用意识流模式，侵入那些未言明和不可言说的领域，映照出角色的内心世界。这种技巧将第三人称叙述者的沉稳与角色的情感能量和用词选择融合在一起，融入角色之中，复制其思维过程，营造出内心独白的氛围，却又不会越界成为角色的代言人。

Consider, for example, this passage from Virginia Woolf’s novel Mrs. Dalloway . Woolf’s non-character narrator uses words plucked from Clarissa Dalloway’s vocabulary (“lark,” “plunge,” “something awful”) to emulate the flow of memory:

例如，请看弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的小说《达洛维夫人》中的这段文字。伍尔夫笔下的非人物叙述者使用了从克拉丽莎·达洛维的词汇中摘取的词语（“云雀”、“纵身一跃”、“可怕的事情”）来模仿记忆的流动：

What a lark! What a plunge! For so it always seemed to her when, with a little squeak of the hinges, which she can hear now, she burst open the French windows and plunged into the open air. How fresh, how calm, stiller than this of course, the air was in the early morning; like the flap of a wave; the kiss of a wave; chill and sharp and yet (for a girl of eighteen as she then was) solemn, feeling as she did, standing there at the open window, that something awful was about to happen…

多么轻快！多么酣畅淋漓！每当她推开落地窗，窗户发出轻微的吱呀声（她现在还能听到），纵身跃入户外时，她总是这样觉得。清晨的空气多么清新，多么宁静，当然比现在更加静谧；如同海浪拍打；如同海浪轻吻；寒冷而凛冽，然而（对于当时十八岁的她来说）却又带着一丝庄严，因为她站在敞开的窗前，感觉有什么可怕的事情即将发生……

Not all stream of consciousness “streams” with Virginia Woolf’s breathless fluidity. Some interiorized passages zigzag or circle or pulse (see the Ken Kesey and David Means examples below). For that reason, some schools of writing use “stream of consciousness” and “inner dialogue” interchangeably as if the terms were synonyms. But for the purposes of this book, I give them distinct definitions. I draw the line with the answer to this question: Who is talking to whom? Stream of consciousness uses a third-person non-character voice to talk to the reader (as in the Woolf example above); inner dialogue uses a character’s voice in first or second person to talk to himself (as in the Nabokov example below).

并非所有意识流都像弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫那样流畅自如，令人屏息。有些内心独白段落曲折蜿蜒，或循环往复，或如脉动般律动（参见下文肯·凯西和戴维·米恩斯的例子）。正因如此，一些写作流派将“意识流”和“内心对话”混用，仿佛它们是同义词。但就本书而言，我为它们赋予了不同的定义。我的区分依据是这个问题：谁在和谁说话？意识流使用第三人称非人物视角与读者对话（如上文伍尔夫的例子）；而内心对话则使用人物的第一人称或第二人称视角与自己对话（如下文纳博科夫的例子）。

The In-Character Voice

角色配音

The in-character side of prose speaks with character-specific voices. Dialogue, as I previously defined the term, includes all purposeful character talk, whether spoken in duologues with other characters, said to the reader, or by the character talking to herself. As we noted in Chapter One, because prose does its acting in the reader’s imagination, it offers a far greater range of in-character techniques than stage or screen. In-character prose employs six tactics: 1) dramatized dialogue, 2) first-person direct address, 3) indirect dialogue, 4) inner dialogue, 5) paralanguage, and 6) mixed techniques (see Chapter Five for the last two tactics).

散文中的人物描写部分运用了角色特有的声音。正如我之前所定义的，对话涵盖了所有有目的的角色谈话，无论是与其他角色的对话、对读者的直接对话，还是角色的自言自语。正如我们在第一章中提到的，由于散文是在读者的想象中进行表演，因此它比舞台剧或电影提供了更丰富的人物描写技巧。人物描写散文运用了六种技巧：1）戏剧化的对话，2）第一人称直接对话，3）间接对话，4）内心独白，5）副语言，以及6）混合技巧（后两种技巧详见第五章）。

Dramatized Dialogue

戏剧化对话

In the novel, dramatized dialogue rarely reaches the intensity of a verse play. Nonetheless, within the limits of genre and characterizations set by the author, figurative language may enhance scenes, just as it does onstage and onscreen. First-person narrators often enact “I said”/“she said”/“he said” scenes, purely dramatized and without commentary.

在小说中，戏剧化的对话很少能达到诗剧的强度。然而，在作者设定的体裁和人物设定范围内，比喻性的语言可以增强场景效果，正如它在舞台和银幕上所做的那样。第一人称叙述者经常会表演“我说”/“她说”/“他说”之类的场景，纯粹是戏剧化的，没有任何评论。

Robert Penn Warren’s All the King’s Men is narrated by Jack Burden, an aide to a ruthless politician and the novel’s central character, Willie Stark, a.k.a. the Boss. Stark needs a secret piece of dirt to smear the reputation of a political foe, Judge Irwin. Note how Stark uses the decades that span from diapers to the coffin as a metaphor for life:

罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦的小说《国王的人马》由杰克·伯登叙述，他是冷酷无情的政客威利·斯塔克（又名“老板”）的助手，而斯塔克正是小说的主人公。斯塔克需要一些不可告人的秘密来抹黑他的政治对手欧文法官。请注意斯塔克是如何用从婴儿时期到死亡的几十年来比喻人生的：

It all began, as I have said, when the Boss, sitting in the black Cadillac which sped through the night, said to me… “There is always something.”

正如我之前所说，这一切都始于老板坐在疾驰在夜色中的黑色凯迪拉克里对我说……“总会有事发生的。”

And I said, “Maybe not on the Judge.”

我说：“也许法官不会同意。”

And he said, “Man is conceived in sin and born in corruption and he passeth from the stink of the didie to the stench of the shroud. There is always something.” 4

他说：“人生于罪孽，生于败坏，从衣衫褴褛的恶臭走向裹尸布的腐臭。总有一些东西在作祟。”

Direct Address

直接地址

First-person narration is first cousin to soliloquys onstage and in-character voice-overs onscreen. In all three cases a character speaks directly to the person consuming the story. More often than not, the protagonist narrates his or her story, but occasionally a supporting character does the talking. Direct address can be more or less emotional, more or less objective, the specific tone dependent on the personality of the narrator.

第一人称叙述与舞台上的独白和银幕上的角色旁白非常相似。在这三种情况下，角色都是直接与故事的听众对话。通常情况下，主角会叙述自己的故事，但有时也会由配角来讲述。直接对话的情感表达可以更强烈或更淡漠，客观程度也可以不同，具体的语气取决于叙述者的个性。

Here, a Rudyard Kipling protagonist recalls looking out to sea and describes the wide, calm, objective pleasure of his experience to the reader:

在这里，鲁德亚德·吉卜林笔下的主人公回忆起眺望大海的情景，并向读者描述了他所感受到的广阔、平静、客观的愉悦：

I remember the windjammer as she sailed toward me. The setting sun ablaze astern. Out flung water at her feet, her shadow slashed rope furled sails bulging sideways like insolent cheeks of angels.

我记得那艘帆船向我驶来。落日余晖在船尾熊熊燃烧。溅起的水花落在船脚，船的影子割破了卷起的绳索，船帆向两侧鼓起，像天使傲慢的脸颊。

Or, a first-person narrator’s view may contract, blinded by strong emotions or lesser degrees of sanity. In Ken Kesey’s One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest , a patient in a mental hospital, “Chief” Bromden, begins the novel with:

或者，第一人称叙述者的视角可能会因为强烈的情绪或精神状态的缺失而变得狭隘。在肯·凯西的《飞越疯人院》中，精神病院的病人“酋长”布罗姆登在小说开头写道：

They’re out there. Black boys in white suits up before me to commit sex acts in the hall and get it mopped up before I can catch them. They’re mopping when I come out of the dorm, all three of them sulky and hating everything, the time of day, the place they’re at here, the people they got to work around. When they hate like this, better if they don’t see me. I creep along the wall quiet as dust in my canvas shoes, but they got special sensitive equipment to detect my fear and they all look up, all three at once, eyes glittering out of the black faces like the hard glitter of radio tubes out of the back of an old radio. 5

他们就在那里。几个穿着白西装的黑人男孩在我之前就在走廊里做那种事，然后等我抓到他们才把现场清理干净。我走出宿舍时，他们正在拖地，三个都闷闷不乐，恨透了一切：讨厌现在的时间，讨厌这里，讨厌周围的人。他们这么恨我，最好别让他们看到我。我穿着帆布鞋，沿着墙悄无声息地蹑手蹑脚，但他们似乎有某种灵敏的设备能探测到我的恐惧，他们三个同时抬起头，黑色的脸上闪着寒光，就像老式收音机里电子管闪烁的光芒。

Bromden’s imaginings of unseen orgies and fear-detecting technology, enriched with his metaphors (quiet as dust) and similes (faces like the hard glitter of radio tubes) express his paranoid inner life, but at the same time, give the impression that despite the Chief’s constricted, insane thoughts, he is knowingly talking to us, the reader.

布罗姆登对看不见的狂欢和恐惧探测技术的想象，辅以他的比喻（像灰尘一样安静）和明喻（像无线电管坚硬的闪光一样的脸），表达了他偏执的内心世界，但同时也给人一种印象，尽管酋长思想狭隘、疯狂，但他却在有意地与我们读者对话。

Indirect Dialogue

间接对话

When a non-character third-person narrator uses indirect dialogue, subtext often becomes text. For example, in the David Means scene above, his third-person narrator tells the reader what was not said: “… nothing about dancing on the lip of volcanoes, or throwing themselves into one sacrificially, but a hint of it.”

当非角色扮演的第三人称叙述者使用间接对话时，潜台词往往会变成明文。例如，在上面提到的大卫·米恩斯的场景中，他的第三人称叙述者告诉读者那些未说出口的话：“……没有提到在火山口跳舞，也没有提到把自己献祭给火山，但暗示了一下。”

When in-character first-or second-person prose relates indirect dialogue, subtext can only be implied because a first-person narrator doesn’t have access to his own subconscious. For example, this scene from The Sense of an Ending by Julian Barnes: Webster, the protagonist, wants to take action against an ex-lover because she won’t give him a letter he believes is rightfully his, so he consults a lawyer:

当人物的第一人称或第二人称叙述间接对话时，潜台词只能通过暗示来表达，因为第一人称叙述者无法了解自己的潜意识。例如，朱利安·巴恩斯的小说《结局的感觉》中的这个场景：主人公韦伯斯特想对前女友采取行动，因为她不肯把一封他认为理应属于他的信给他，于是他咨询了律师：

Mr. Gunnell is a calm, gaunt man who doesn’t mind silence. After all, it costs his clients just as much as speech.

冈内尔先生是一位沉着冷静、面容清瘦的男人，他并不介意沉默。毕竟，沉默对他的客户来说，代价并不亚于滔滔不绝。

“Mr. Webster.”

“韦伯斯特先生。”

“Mr. Gunnell.”

“冈内尔先生。”

And so we mistered one another for the next forty-five minutes, in which he gave me the professional advice I was paying for. He told me that going to the police and trying to persuade them to lay a charge of theft against a woman of mature years who had recently lost her mother would, in his view, be foolish. I liked that. Not the advice, but the way he expressed it. “Foolish”: much better than “inadvisable” or “inappropriate.” 6

于是，接下来的四十五分钟里，我们互相倾诉，他给了我一些我付费请他提供的专业建议。他告诉我，去警察局试图说服他们以盗窃罪起诉一位刚刚失去母亲的中年妇女，在他看来是愚蠢的。我喜欢这个说法。不是喜欢他的建议，而是喜欢他表达的方式。“愚蠢”：比“不明智”或“不合适”好多了。

The reader senses that beneath his glib approval of Gunnell’s choice of words, Webster rages.

读者能感觉到，在韦伯斯特轻率地赞同冈内尔的用词之下，隐藏着愤怒。

Inner Dialogue

内心对话

Onstage and onscreen, the actor brings the unsaid to life within her performance, where it stays mute in the subtext. But when novelists and short-story writers wish, they can turn subtext into text and convert the unsaid directly into literature. The chief difference, therefore, between in-character direct address and inner dialogue is who’s listening. A first-person voice narrates to the reader; an inner dialogist talks to himself.

在舞台和银幕上，演员通过表演赋予未言之意以生命，而这些未言之意则以潜台词的形式保持沉默。但当小说家和短篇小说作家愿意时，他们可以将潜台词转化为文字，直接将未言之意转化为文学作品。因此，角色直接对话和内心独白的主要区别在于谁在倾听。第一人称叙述是面向读者；而内心独白则是与自己对话。

Lolita , for example, begins with Vladimir Nabokov’s protagonist, Humbert Humbert, in self-celebration:

例如，《洛丽塔》以弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫笔下的主人公亨伯特·亨伯特自我陶醉的开篇：

Lolita, light of my life, fire of my loins. My sin, my soul. Lo-lee-ta: the tip of the tongue taking a trip of three steps down the palate to tap, at three, on the teeth. Lo. Lee. Ta.

洛丽塔，我生命之光，我欲望之火。我的罪孽，我的灵魂。洛丽塔：舌尖沿着上颚向下移动三步，最后轻敲牙齿，三下。洛。丽。塔。

Humbert is not talking to us. Rather, we sit outside, listening as his inward-facing mind revels in memories. To capture this self-absorbed admixture of sex and worship, Nabokov opens with metaphors for passion as prayer, then focuses on Humbert’s tongue as it pounds “t” sounds in alliteration.

亨伯特并没有和我们说话。相反，我们坐在外面，聆听他沉浸在回忆中的内心世界。为了捕捉这种自我沉溺的性与崇拜的混合，纳博科夫开篇便以祈祷来比喻激情，然后着重描写亨伯特的舌头如何用头韵反复发出“t”音。

Compare Humbert’s masturbatory fantasy with a passage from “The Knocking,” a short story by David Means. Means’s protagonist talks directly to us as he reclines in his New York apartment, listening to the tenant above him hang pictures or do repairs. His in-character voice guides us through his hopscotching thoughts as they leap from now to then and back to now.

将亨伯特的自慰幻想与大卫·米恩斯短篇小说《敲门声》中的一段文字进行比较。米恩斯的主人公斜倚在纽约的公寓里，直接与我们对话，他一边听着楼上房客挂画或修理东西，一边用他自己的声音讲述着自己的故事。他那跳跃的思绪引领我们进入他那仿佛在跳房子般的思绪世界，这些思绪在现在和过去之间来回跳跃。

A piercingly sharp metallic tap, not too loud and not too soft, coming out from under the casual noise of summer afternoon—the roar of traffic on Fifth combined with high heel taps, taxi horns, and the murmur of voices—again, many of these knockings come late in the day when he knows, because he knows, that I’m in my deepest state of reverie, trying to ponder—what else can one do!—the nature of my sadness in relation to my past actions, throwing out, silently, wordlessly, my theorems: Love is a blank senseless vibration that, when picked up by another soul, brings form to something that feels eternal (like our marriage) and then tapers and thins and becomes wispy, barely audible (the final days in the house along the Hudson) and then, finally, nothing but air unable to move anything (the deep persistent silence of loss).

一阵尖锐的金属敲击声，不大也不小，从夏日午后随意的喧嚣中传来——第五大道上车水马龙的轰鸣声，高跟鞋的敲击声，出租车的喇叭声，以及人们的低语——这些敲击声大多在傍晚时分响起，因为他知道，因为他明白，我正沉浸在深深的沉思中，试图思考——还能做什么呢！——我的悲伤与我过去的行为之间的联系，默默地、无声地抛出我的理论：爱是一种空白的、无意义的振动，当它被另一个灵魂拾起时，便赋予了某种感觉永恒的东西以形式（比如我们的婚姻），然后逐渐变细，变得飘渺，几乎听不见（在哈德逊河畔的房子里的最后几天），最后，它只剩下空气，无法移动任何东西（失去的深沉而持久的沉默）。

Inner dialogue mimics free association to leapfrog through a character’s mind. When we glance in the cracks between the images, we glimpse the unsayable.

内心独白模仿自由联想，让我们得以快速穿梭于角色的内心世界。当我们透过画面间的缝隙瞥见那些难以言说的事物时，便能窥见其真谛。

To sum up: from stage to screen to page, the nature, need, and expressivity of dialogue vary considerably. Stage dialogue is the most embellished, screen dialogue the most concise, and prose dialogue the most mutable.

总而言之，从舞台到银幕再到书页，对话的性质、必要性和表现力差异显著。舞台对话最为华丽，银幕对话最为简洁，而散文对话则最为多变。

#↩

5

EXPRESSIVITY III: TECHNIQUE

表现力 III：技巧

FIGURATIVE LANGUAGE

比喻语言

Figurative devices range from metaphor, simile, synecdoche, and metonymy to alliteration, assonance, oxymoron, personification, and beyond. In fact, the list of all linguistic tropes and ploys numbers in the hundreds. These turns of phrase not only enrich what’s said, but also send connotations of meaning resonating into the subtexts of the unsaid and unsayable as well.

修辞手法种类繁多，从隐喻、明喻、提喻、转喻到头韵、谐音、矛盾修辞、拟人等等，不一而足。事实上，所有语言修辞手法和技巧加起来多达数百种。这些语言表达方式不仅丰富了言外之意，还能将意义的内涵传递到那些未言明或不可言说的潜台词中。

For example: In Scene Six of Tennessee Williams’s play A Streetcar Named Desire , Blanche DuBois, a desperately vulnerable, aging Southern belle on the edge of mental and emotional collapse, meets Mitch, a lonely, sensitive, working-class bachelor who lives with his dying mother. After an evening out, they confess to very different but equally pain-filled lives. Their attraction builds to this moment:

例如：在田纳西·威廉姆斯的戏剧《欲望号街车》第六幕中，布兰奇·杜波依斯，一位濒临精神和情感崩溃边缘、脆弱不堪的年迈南方美人，遇到了米奇，一位孤独、敏感、与病危母亲同住的工人阶级单身汉。一夜外出后，他们坦白了彼此截然不同却同样充满痛苦的生活。他们的吸引力逐渐发展到这一刻：

MITCH: (drawing Blanche slowly into his arms) You need somebody. And I need somebody, too. Could it be you and me, Blanche?

米奇：（慢慢地将布兰奇拥入怀中）你需要人陪伴。我也需要人陪伴。布兰奇，会是你和我吗？

She stares at him vacantly for a moment, then with a soft cry huddles in his embrace. She makes a sobbing effort to speak but the words won’t come. He kisses her forehead and her eyes and finally her lips. Her breath is drawn and released in long, grateful sobs.

她茫然地望着他片刻，然后轻轻啜泣着，依偎在他怀里。她抽泣着想要开口，却一个字也说不出来。他吻了吻她的额头、眼睛，最后吻了吻她的嘴唇。她长长地、充满感激地抽泣着，呼吸也随之缓缓吐出。

BLANCHE: Sometimes—there’s God—so quickly.

布兰奇：有时候——上帝——来得如此之快。

These five words condense tremendous meaning and emotion. The phrase “there’s God” is not a metaphor comparing Mitch to a deity, but rather hyperbole to express Blanche’s sense of an overwhelming, heaven-like salvation. We suspect, however, that this epiphany is not her first.

这五个字蕴含着巨大的意义和情感。“上帝存在”并非将米奇比作神明的比喻，而是夸张地表达了布兰奇内心那种如天堂般令人震撼的救赎感。然而，我们怀疑这并非她第一次顿悟。

The words “Sometimes” and “so quickly” suggest that Blanche has been rescued by men many times in the past. But the men who suddenly saved her must have abandoned her just as fast because here she is, still desperately alone, clinging to yet another stranger. In five words the audience instantly glimpses the implied pattern: When Blanche meets men, she plays the victim and inspires their inner white knight. They rescue her, but then, for reasons we are yet to discover, desert her. Will Mitch be any different?

“有时”和“如此迅速”这两个词暗示布兰奇过去曾多次被男人拯救。但那些突然救了她的男人肯定也很快就抛弃了她，因为如今她依然孤苦伶仃，孤苦伶仃，只能依偎在另一个陌生人身边。短短五个字，观众便能立刻领悟其中的模式：布兰奇遇到男人时，总是扮演受害者，激发他们内心深处的“白马王子”情结。他们救了她，但随后，出于我们尚未知晓的原因，又抛弃了她。米奇会例外吗？

In one ear-catching trope, Tennessee Williams exposes the tragic cadence of Blanche’s life and raises a dread-filled question in the audience’s mind.

田纳西·威廉姆斯用一个引人入胜的比喻，揭示了布兰奇悲惨人生的节奏，并在观众心中提出了一个令人恐惧的问题。

Language composed into dialogue offers a spectrum that runs from mental meanings at one end to sensual experiences at the other. For example, a character might call a singer’s voice either “lousy” or “sour.” Both terms make sense, but “lousy” is a dead metaphor that once meant “covered with lice.” “Sour” still has life. The moment the audience hears “sour,” their lips start to pucker. Which line stirs the most inner feeling: “She walks like a model” or “She moves like a slow, hot song”? Dialogue can express the same idea in countless ways, but, in general, the more sensory the trope, the deeper and more memorable its effect. 1

对话中语言的表达方式丰富多样，从理性的心理层面延伸到感性的体验层面。例如，一个角色可能会用“糟糕”或“酸涩”来形容歌手的声音。这两个词都说得通，但“糟糕”是一个过时的比喻，它曾经的意思是“浑身虱子”。而“酸涩”却依然鲜活。观众一听到“酸涩”这个词，嘴唇就会不由自主地撅起来。那么，哪一句台词更能触动人心：“她走路像个模特”还是“她舞动起来像一首缓慢而热烈的歌”？对话可以用无数种方式表达同一个意思，但总的来说，越是感官化的表达方式，其效果就越深刻、越令人难忘。

Tropes work within a single sentence, but because dialogue dramatizes conflict-filled talk speech after speech, temporal and counter-punctual techniques also come into play: rapid rhythms versus silent pauses, run-on sentences versus fragments, repartee versus argument, literate versus illiterate grammars, monosyllabic versus polysyllabic vocabularies, politeness versus profanity, verisimilitude versus verse, understatement versus overstatement, and countless other examples of stylistics and wordplay. Dialogue can dance to as many different tunes as life can sing.

修辞手法在单个句子中就能发挥作用，但由于对话将充满冲突的言语戏剧化，因此时间节奏和反标点技巧也随之发挥作用：快速的节奏与沉默的停顿、连贯的句子与片段式的句子、妙语连珠与争论、规范的语法与不规范的语法、单音节词汇与多音节词汇、礼貌与粗俗、写实与诗意、轻描淡写与夸张，以及其他无数的文体和文字游戏。对话可以像生活本身一样，谱写出丰富多彩的乐章。

I have emphasized the infinite array of creative possibilities that face the writer a few times already and will again. I repeat this point because I want writers to understand that form does not limit expression; it inspires it . This book explores the forms that underlie dialogue but never proposes formulae for writing it. Creativity is choice-making.

我已多次强调作家面临的无限创作可能性，以后还会再次强调。我之所以重申这一点，是因为我希望作家们明白，形式并非限制表达，而是激发表达。本书探讨了对话的各种形式，但从未提出任何对话写作的固定模式。创造力在于选择。

PARALANGUAGE

副语言

Actors provide their audiences with all forms of paralanguage, those nonlexical nuances of voice and body language that enhance the meanings and feelings of words—facial expression; gestures; posture; rate of words; pitch, volume, rhythm, intonation, stress; and even proxemics, the distances characters keep between themselves and others. An actor’s paralanguage speaks a gesticulate dialogue. The eye of the audience reads these microexpressions at up to one twenty-fifth of a second. 2 On page, however, paralanguage calls for description enhanced with figurative language.

演员通过各种形式的副语言向观众传递信息，这些非词汇性的语音和肢体语言细微差别能够增强词语的意义和情感——面部表情、手势、姿势、语速、音调、音量、节奏、语调、重音，甚至包括空间关系，即角色与他人之间的距离。演员的副语言就像一场手势对话。观众的目光能在1/25秒内捕捉到这些微表情。然而，在文字中，副语言需要借助比喻等修辞手法进行描述。

In this example from “Railroad Incident, August 1995,” a short story by David Means, four homeless men sit around a fire at night when a half-dressed man comes out of the shadows.

在大卫·米恩斯的短篇小说《1995 年 8 月的铁路事件》的这个例子中，四个无家可归的男人在夜里围坐在篝火旁，这时一个衣衫不整的男人从阴影中走了出来。

What they saw emerge was a man softening into middle age. In his limp was a slight residue of dignity and formality, the way he lifted his feet as if they were still shod and weighted by the expensive shoes; or maybe all of that wasn’t noticed until, coming up to them, he opened his mouth and spoke, saying hello softly, the vowels widening, the cup of his mouth over those words like an expensive shell… 3

他们看到的是一个逐渐步入中年的男人。他走路一瘸一拐，却仍保留着些许尊严和礼节，他抬起脚的方式，仿佛脚上还穿着昂贵的皮鞋，沉甸甸的；或许这一切直到他走到他们面前，开口说话，轻声说着“你好”时才被他们注意到，他的元音渐渐拉长，嘴唇像一只精致的贝壳，轻轻地包裹着这些字句…… 3

(David Means writes short stories, I suspect, because his arsenal of prose techniques is so diverse, he needs hundreds of tellings to explore them all.)

（我怀疑大卫·米恩斯之所以写短篇小说，是因为他的散文技巧非常丰富多样，需要数百个故事才能全部探索出来。）

MIXED TECHNIQUES

混合技法

Prose techniques can be used singularly or in concert. In this exchange from An American Dream , Norman Mailer weaves three: direct dialogue, first-person direct address, and paralanguage, both literal and figurative.

散文技巧可以单独使用，也可以组合使用。在《美国梦》的这段对话中，诺曼·梅勒巧妙地运用了三种技巧：直接对话、第一人称直接称呼以及字面意义和比喻意义的副语言。

“You want a divorce?” I said.

“你想离婚吗？”我问。

“I think so.”

“我也这么认为。”

“Like that?”

“像这样吗？”

“Not like that, darling. After all that.” She yawned prettily and looked for a moment like a fifteen-year-old Irish maid. “When you didn’t come by today to say goodbye to Deirdre—”

“不是那样的，亲爱的。毕竟……”她打了个漂亮的哈欠，一时间看起来像个十五岁的爱尔兰少女。“你今天竟然没来跟迪尔德丽道别——”

“—I didn’t know she was leaving.”

“——我不知道她要离开。”

“Of course you didn’t know. How could you know? You’ve been nuzzling and nipping with your little girls.” She did not know that at the moment I had no girl.

“你当然不知道。你怎么可能知道？你一直在跟你的小女儿们亲昵地玩闹。”她并不知道，此刻我根本没有女儿。

“They’re not so little any more.” A fire had begun to spread in me. It was burning now in my stomach and my lungs were dry as old leaves, my heart had a herded pressure which gave promise to explode.

“他们不再是小孩子了。”一股怒火开始在我体内蔓延。现在，它灼烧着我的胃，我的肺干涸如枯叶，我的心脏仿佛被一股强大的压力压制着，随时可能爆炸。

“Give us a bit of the rum,” I said. 4

“给我们来点朗姆酒，”我说。

A quick point about adaptation from medium to medium: If you wish to adapt a prose story to the screen, recognize that novelists and short-story writers tend to concentrate their finest language in the voices of their narrators and not in the dialogue of their dramatized scenes—just as Mailer did above.

关于从一种媒介改编到另一种媒介，这里有一个要点：如果你想把一个散文故事改编成电影，要知道小说家和短篇小说作家往往会把他们最精彩的语言集中在叙述者的声音中，而不是集中在戏剧化场景的对话中——就像梅勒在上面所做的那样。

Literature resists filmic adaptation for the obvious reason: The camera cannot photograph thought. Inner dialogues of concentrated prose cannot shift sideways from page to screen. Therefore, to adapt you must reinvent. You must re-envision the novel’s storytelling from the inside out, and transform its novelistic narratized dialogue into filmic dramatized dialogue. No small task.

文学作品难以改编成电影，原因显而易见：镜头无法捕捉思想。精炼的文字中蕴含的内心独白无法从书页跃然于银幕之上。因此，改编必须重塑。必须由内而外地重新构思小说的叙事结构，并将小说式的叙事对话转化为电影式的戏剧对话。这绝非易事。

LINE DESIGN

线条设计

A line’s design pivots around its key term—the word or phrase essential to its meaning. An author can place that key term first, last, or anywhere in the middle. That choice results in one of three fundamental line designs: suspenseful, cumulative, balanced.

一行文字的设计围绕着它的关键术语——即构成其意义的核心词语或短语。作者可以将关键术语放在句首、句末或中间的任何位置。这种选择造就了三种基本的线条设计：悬念式、累积式和平衡式。

The Suspense Sentence

悬念句

Curiosity drives the thirst for knowledge—our intellectual need to solve puzzles and answer questions. Empathy drives the hunger for connection—our emotional need to identify with others and root for their well-being. When the rational and emotional sides of life merge, they generate the phenomenon of suspense. Suspense, simply put, is curiosity charged with empathy.

好奇心驱使我们求知——我们出于智力需要去解谜、解答疑问。同理心驱使我们渴望联结——我们出于情感需要去理解他人、关心他人的福祉。当生活的理性与感性交融时，便产生了悬念。简而言之，悬念便是充满同理心的好奇心。

Suspense focuses the reader/audience by flooding the mind with emotionally tinged questions that hook and hold attention: “What’s going to happen next?” “What’ll happen after that?” “What will the protagonist do? Feel?” And the major dramatic question (MDQ) that hangs suspended over the entire telling: “How will this turn out?” These powerful questions so grip our concentration that time vanishes. As events build to story climax, suspense intensifies and peaks at the final and irreversible turning point that answers the MDQ and ends the telling.

悬念通过抛出一系列充满情感张力的问题来吸引读者/观众的注意力，这些问题紧紧抓住他们的心：“接下来会发生什么？”“之后又会发生什么？”“主人公会做什么？会有什么感受？”而贯穿整个故事的核心戏剧性问题（MDQ）则是：“结局会如何？”这些强有力的问题牢牢抓住我们的注意力，让我们感觉时间仿佛静止。随着剧情发展，悬念不断增强，并在最终不可逆转的转折点达到顶峰，解答了核心戏剧性问题，故事也随之结束。

This combination of curiosity and concern arcs the story’s overall suspense, but when we zoom in for a close-up, we see that inquisitive emotions permeate every story component, no matter its size. Each scene dramatizes a suspense-filled turning point; each speech within the scene grips interest from first line to last; even the smallest element of all, the line of dialogue, shapes itself into a miniature unit of suspense. A superbly told story holds unbroken intellectual and emotional involvement scene by scene, speech by speech, line by line. The reader never pauses and the audience never looks away, not for a moment.

这种好奇与担忧交织的情绪贯穿了整个故事，营造出紧张悬念。但当我们细细品味时，会发现这种探索的情感渗透到故事的每一个细节，无论大小。每一幕都戏剧化地展现了一个充满悬念的转折点；场景中的每一句台词都从头到尾紧紧抓住读者的注意力；即使是最小的元素——一句对话，也构成了一个微型的悬念单元。一个精彩绝伦的故事，能够让读者在每一幕、每一句台词、每一行文字中，都持续地投入到理智和情感的体验中。读者不会停顿，观众也不会移开视线，片刻也不行。

The key to composing dialogue that holds the eye to page and the ear to the stage and screen is the periodic sentence . A periodic sentence withholds its core idea until the final word. By front-loading the sentence with modifiers or subordinate ideas and thus delaying the meaning to last, the periodic sentence compels uninterrupted interest.

要想创作出引人入胜、扣人心弦的对话，关键在于运用周期句。周期句会将核心思想保留到最后一个词才揭示。通过在句首插入修饰语或从属信息，从而延缓意义的展开，周期句能够牢牢抓住读者的注意力。

For example: “If you didn’t want me to do it, why did you give me that________?” What word would give that line its specific meaning? “Look?” “Gun?” “Kiss?” “Nod?” “Photo?” “Money?” “Report?” “Smile?” “E-mail?” “Ice cream sundae?” Almost any noun imaginable could nail the meaning. To inspire intrigue, the periodic design makes meaning wait, and thus compels the reader/audience to listen in wonder from the first word to the last.

例如：“如果你不想让我做，为什么还要给我那个____？” 哪个词能准确表达这句话的意思？“看？”“枪？”“吻？”“点头？”“照片？”“钱？”“报告？”“微笑？”“电子邮件？”“冰淇淋圣代？” 几乎任何你能想到的名词都能恰如其分地表达这个意思。这种周期性的句式设计，让意义的呈现保持悬念，从而迫使读者/听众从第一个字到最后一个字都带着好奇心去聆听。

In other words, the periodic sentence is the suspense sentence.

换句话说，周期句就是悬念句。

For example, the opening scene from Art , a play by Yasmina Reza, translated by Christopher Hampton. I have put the core word or phrase in each sentence in bold.

例如，选自雅丝米娜·雷扎的戏剧《艺术》（Art），由克里斯托弗·汉普顿翻译。我已将每句话中的核心词或短语用粗体标出。

Marc, alone onstage.

马克独自一人在台上。

Marc: My friend Serge has bought a painting . It’s a canvas about five-foot by four: white . The background is white . If you screw up your eyes, you can make out some fine white diagonal lines .

马克：我的朋友塞尔吉买了一幅画。那是一幅大约五英尺乘四英尺的画布，白色的。背景是白色的。如果你眯起眼睛仔细看，可以看到一些细细的白色斜线。

Serge is one of my oldest friends . He’s done very well for himself, he’s a dermatologist and he’s keen on art .

塞尔吉是我最老的朋友之一。他事业有成，是一名皮肤科医生，而且热爱艺术。

On Monday, I went to see the painting ; Serge actually got hold of it on the Saturday, but he’s been lusting after it for several months . This white painting with white lines .

星期一，我去看了那幅画；塞尔日其实是星期六才拿到的，但他已经垂涎这幅画好几个月了。这是一幅白色底、白色线条的画。

At Serge’s.

在塞尔吉家。

At floor level, a white canvas with fine white diagonal scars. Serge looks at his painting, thrilled. Marc looks at the painting. Serge looks at Marc looking at the painting.

地上放着一幅白色画布，上面布满了细密的白色斜纹痕迹。塞尔日激动地看着自己的画。马克也看着这幅画。塞尔日看着马克看着画的样子。

Long silence: from both of them, a whole range of wordless emotions .

长时间的沉默：两人之间流露出各种无法言说的复杂情绪。

Marc: Expensive?

马克：贵吗？

Serge: Two hundred thousand.

塞尔吉：二十万。

Marc: Two hundred thousand?

马克：二十万？

Serge: Huntington would take it off my hands for two hundred and twenty .

Serge：亨廷顿公司愿意花220美元买下它。

Marc: Who’s that?

马克：那是谁？

Serge: Huntington?

塞尔吉：亨廷顿？

Marc: Never heard of him.

马克：我从没听说过他。

Serge: Huntington! The Huntington Gallery!

塞尔日：亨廷顿！亨廷顿画廊！

Marc: The Huntington Gallery would take it off your hands for two hundred and twenty ?

马克：亨廷顿美术馆愿意以220美元的价格收购它吗？

Serge: No, not the Gallery. Him. Huntington himself. For his own collection .

塞尔日：不，不是画廊。是他。亨廷顿本人。为了他自己的收藏。

Marc: Then why didn’t Huntington buy it ?

马克：那为什么亨廷顿银行没有买下它呢？

Serge: It’s important for them to sell to private clients . That’s how the market circulates .

塞尔吉：对他们来说，向私人客户销售产品很重要。市场就是这样流通的。

Marc: Mm hm…

马克：嗯……

Serge: Well?

塞尔吉：嗯？

Marc: …

马克：……

Serge: You’re not in the right place . Look at it from this angle . Can you see the lines ?

塞尔吉：你找错地方了。从这个角度看。你能看到线条吗？

Marc: What’s the name of the…?

马克：那个……叫什么名字？

Serge: Painter. Antrios .

塞尔日：画家。安提里奥斯。

Marc: Well-known?

马克：很有名吗？

Serge: Very . Very.

塞尔吉：非常。非常。

Pause.

暂停。

Marc: Serge, you haven’t bought this painting for two hundred thousand Euros ?

马克：塞尔吉，你没花二十万欧元买下这幅画吧？

Serge: You don’t understand, that’s what it costs. In an Antrios .

塞尔吉：你不明白，这就是它的价格。在安特里奥斯（Antrios）里。

Marc: You haven’t bought this painting for two hundred thousand Euros ?

马克：你没花二十万欧元买下这幅画吧？

Serge: I might have known you’d miss the point .

塞尔吉：我早就料到你会误解我的意思。

Marc: You paid two hundred thousand Euros for this shit ?

马克：你花了二十万欧元买了这玩意儿？

Serge, as if alone.

塞尔吉，仿佛独自一人。

Serge: My friend Marc’s an intelligent enough fellow, I’ve always valued our relationship, he has a good job , he’s an aeronautical engineer, but he’s one of those new-style intellectuals , who are not only enemies of modernism , but seem to take some sort of incomprehensible pride in running it down … 5

塞尔日：我的朋友马克是个相当聪明的人，我一直很珍惜我们的友谊。他有一份不错的工作，是一名航空工程师，但他属于那种新式知识分子，他们不仅反对现代主义，而且似乎还以贬低现代主义为荣…… 5

Of the forty-five ideas expressed in these two soliloquies of narratized dialogue and the scene of dramatized dialogue they bracket, forty are shaped for suspense. Even the brief description of paralanguage (the nonverbal facial expressions on Marc and Serge) delays its point until the phrase “wordless emotions.”

在这两段叙述性独白及其前后穿插的戏剧化对话场景中，共表达了45个观点，其中40个都旨在营造悬念。即使是对副语言（马克和塞尔日的非语言面部表情）的简短描述，也刻意拖延，直到“无言的情感”这一短语出现才揭示其真正含义。

The suspense sentence is not only the most dramatic design but the most comic as well. Almost all verbal jokes trigger laughter by ending on a suspense sentence that suddenly severs its rising tension with a final punch word. By saving the core word for last, Reza and Hampton energize their lines, hold the audience’s interest, and concentrate impact into a single, final, often comic punch.

悬念句不仅是最具戏剧性的设计，也是最具喜剧效果的。几乎所有语言笑话都以悬念句结尾，突然用一个重磅词打破层层递进的紧张感，从而引发笑声。雷扎和汉普顿通过将核心词留到最后，使他们的台词充满活力，牢牢抓住观众的注意力，并将冲击力集中于一个最终的、往往是喜剧性的重磅词中。

The Cumulative Sentence

累积刑期

How old is the cumulative technique? Aristotle advocated it over 2,300 years ago. In Book Three, Part Nine of On Rhetoric , he examined the differences between the tight, periodic suspense sentence and the loose, free-running cumulative sentence. The two designs reverse mirror each other: the suspense structure puts subordinate phrases first and ends on its core word; the cumulative design puts its core word up front, then follows with subordinate phrases that develop or modify the point.

累积句法结构有多久的历史了？早在2300多年前，亚里士多德就提倡使用这种结构。在《修辞学》第三卷第九部分中，他探讨了结构紧凑、周期性的悬念句和结构松散、自由延伸的累积句之间的区别。这两种句式互为镜像：悬念句将从句置于句首，以核心词结尾；而累积句则将核心词放在句首，然后用从句展开或修正论点。

Consider the line design of Character B’s dialogue:

请看角色B的对话线条设计：

Character A

角色A

Remember Jack?

还记得杰克吗？

Character B

角色 B

(nodding)

（点头）

Smoke circling his head like an angry halo, cigarette butt burning his lip, wrestling the spare, cursing the jack, trying to fix a flat…

烟雾在他头顶盘旋，像一圈愤怒的光环，烟头烫得他嘴唇生疼，他费力地摸索着备用轮胎，咒骂着千斤顶，试图补胎……

(with a sense of loss)

（带着一种失落感）

… last time I ever saw him.

……那是我最后一次见到他。

When we reverse the design, this suspense sentence turns into a cumulative sentence:

当我们反过来设计时，这个悬念句就变成了一个累积句：

Character A

角色A

Remember Jack?

还记得杰克吗？

Character B

角色 B

(with a sense of loss)

（带着一种失落感）

I saw him, last time ever, trying to fix a flat, cursing the jack, wrestling with the spare, cigarette butt burning his lip, smoke circling his head like an angry halo.

我最后一次见到他时，他正在修理轮胎，咒骂着千斤顶，费力地摆弄着备用轮胎，烟头烫伤了他的嘴唇，烟雾在他头顶盘旋，像一个愤怒的光环。

Although the free-running cumulative style may be less dramatic than a suspense sentence, it is not slapdash. When well crafted, it paints an ever-growing, more detailed picture of its subject. This snowballing quality gives dialogue a conversational spontaneity while its phrases roll out with a pleasing rhythm.

虽然自由奔放的累积式叙事风格可能不如悬念句那样引人入胜，但它绝非草率之作。精心构思的累积式叙事风格能够逐步展现主题的全貌，使其愈加细致入微。这种滚雪球式的特质赋予对话一种自然流畅的对话感，同时，其语句也以一种悦耳的节奏娓娓道来。

The suspense design offers many advantages but drawbacks as well. First, the meaning, constantly delayed, risks sounding contrived. Second, a long suspense sentence may force the reader/audience to remember too many pieces of a complex idea while waiting for the ending to pull the thoughts together. If overwritten, a suspense sentence takes on the same tedious feebleness of a badly built cumulative sentence.

悬念设计有很多优点，但也存在一些缺点。首先，意义的不断延迟可能会显得牵强附会。其次，冗长的悬念句可能会迫使读者/观众记住复杂概念的太多细节，同时还要等待结尾将所有信息串联起来。如果写得过长，悬念句就会变得像结构糟糕的累积句一样，令人感到乏味无力。

The suspense and cumulative designs sit at opposite ends of the spectrum. Between opening a line with its core word versus closing with it run countless variations.

悬念式和层层递进式的设计手法处于光谱的两端。以核心词开头还是以核心词结尾，这其中蕴含着无数种变化。

Parallel designs, for example, link phrases of similar length, meaning, and design for contrast and emphasis:

例如，平行设计将长度、含义和设计相似的短语联系起来，以达到对比和强调的效果：

When I walked into that church , I walked into a new life .

走进那座教堂的那一刻，我就走进了新的生活。

The Balanced Sentence

平衡句

The balanced sentence puts its core word(s) somewhere in the middle with subordinate phrases on either side:

平衡句的核心词语位于句首，从属短语则分布在句的两侧：

Jack’s sex and gambling obsessions are high risk enough, but I think the guy must be an adrenaline junkie when I add his rock climbing and skydiving.

杰克沉迷于性和赌博，这本身就够危险的了，但考虑到他还喜欢攀岩和跳伞，我觉得他肯定是个肾上腺素成瘾者。

The suspense sentence, straight or in parallel, is dialogue’s most compelling and dramatic design. So for tension, emphasis, flourish, and laughs, delay the core word. On the other hand, cumulative and balanced sentences are the most conversational and free-running designs. But the constant use of any single technique becomes as repetitious as wallpaper and artificial as a robot. Therefore, to compel involvement and build tension, while at the same time expressing a sense of characters living in the moment and making up whatever they say, dialogue calls for a mixture of designs.

悬念句，无论是直接的还是平行的，都是对话中最具吸引力和戏剧性的技巧。因此，为了营造紧张感、强调重点、增添趣味性或博人一笑，可以延迟核心词的出现。另一方面，递进式和平衡式的句型则最贴近对话，也最自然流畅。但任何单一技巧的反复使用都会变得像壁纸一样单调乏味，像机器人一样生硬做作。所以，为了吸引读者、营造紧张感，同时又能展现人物活在当下、即兴发挥的一面，对话需要多种技巧的融合运用。

Mixed Designs

混合设计

In Season 1, Episode 3 of TRUE DETECTIVE, the co-protagonist, Rustin Cohle, relates his worldview to Detectives Gilbough and Papania. Once again, I bolded the core words. Note where each is located within its sentence. (DB is cop-talk for dead body.)

在《真探》第一季第三集中，主角之一拉斯汀·科尔向吉尔博和帕帕尼亚两位警探讲述了他的世界观。我再次用粗体标出了关键词语。请注意每个词语在句子中的位置。（DB是警察术语，指尸体。）

RUSTIN COHLE

鲁斯汀·科尔

This… This is what I’m talking about. This is what I mean when I’m talkin’ about time and death and futility . All right there are broader ideas at work, mainly what is owed between us as a society for our mutual illusions . Fourteen straight hours of staring at DB’s , these are the things ya think of . You ever done that ? You look in their eyes , even in a picture, doesn’t matter if they’re dead or alive, you can still read ’em . You know what you see ? They welcomed it… not at first, but… right there in the last instant. It’s an unmistakable relief . See, ’cause they were afraid, and now they saw for the very first time how easy it was to just… let go . Yeah, they saw, in that last nanosecond, they saw… what they were . You, yourself, this whole big drama, it was never more than a jerry rig of presumption and dumb will , and you could just let go . To finally know that you didn’t have to hold on so tight. To realize that all your life, all your love, all your hate, all your memories, all your pain, it was all the same thing . It was all the same dream , a dream you had inside a locked room, a dream about being a person . And like a lot of dreams, there’s a monster at the end of it.

这……这就是我说的。这就是我谈论时间、死亡和虚无时所指的。好吧，这里面还有更深层次的思考，主要是我们作为一个社会，为了我们共同的幻觉而应该承担的责任。连续十四个小时盯着DB的照片，你会想到这些。你试过吗？你看着他们的眼睛，即使是在照片里，不管他们是死是活，你都能读懂他们的心思。你知道你看到了什么吗？他们欣然接受了……不是一开始，而是……就在最后一刻。那是一种无可置疑的解脱。你看，因为他们曾经害怕，而现在他们第一次意识到，放手是多么容易。是的，在那最后一纳秒，他们看到了……他们自己。你，你自己，这场闹剧，从来都不过是自以为是和愚蠢意志的拼凑，而你完全可以放手。终于明白，你不必抓得那么紧。你会意识到，你的一生，你所有的爱，你所有的恨，你所有的记忆，你所有的痛苦，都源于同一件事。它们都是同一个梦，一个你在密室里做的梦，一个关于成为人的梦。而就像很多梦一样，梦的尽头藏着一个怪物。

Of the twenty-plus ideas Rust expresses, a dozen use suspense sentences, and the rest are a mix of balanced, parallel, and cumulative structures. As a result, this long passage hooks, builds, and pays off interest, yet seems spontaneous, almost wandering. Note also how series creator and writer Nic Pizzolatto caps Rust’s speech with a metaphor: Life is a dream. Like a grace note that enhances a passage of music, a trope tagged on a suspense sentence can add a mind-catching ornament.

在Rust提出的二十多个观点中，有十几个使用了悬念句，其余的则采用了平衡、平行和递进式的结构。因此，这段长文既引人入胜、层层递进，又最终令人满意，同时又显得自然流畅，近乎漫无目的。还要注意的是，剧集创作人兼编剧Nic Pizzolatto是如何用一个比喻来结束Rust的演讲的：人生如梦。就像装饰音能为乐曲增添光彩一样，在悬念句上巧妙运用比喻也能起到画龙点睛的作用。

ECONOMY

经济

One final but critical quality of expressive dialogue is economy—saying the maximum in the fewest possible words. All fine writing, especially of dialogue, follows the principle of economy as laid down by William Strunk Jr. and E. B. White in The Elements of Style : “Vigorous writing is concise. A sentence should contain no unnecessary words, a paragraph no unnecessary sentences, for the same reason that a drawing should have no unnecessary lines and a machine no unnecessary parts. This requires not that the writer make all his sentences short, or that he avoid all detail and treat his subjects only in outline, but that he make every word tell.” 6

富有表现力的对话还有一个至关重要的特点，那就是简洁——用尽可能少的词语表达最多的信息。所有优秀的写作，尤其是对话，都遵循威廉·斯特伦克和E·B·怀特在《风格的要素》中提出的简洁原则：“简洁有力的写作是精炼的。一个句子不应该包含不必要的词语，一个段落不应该包含不必要的句子，正如一幅画不应该有多余的线条，一台机器不应该有多余的零件一样。这并非要求作者把所有句子都写得很短，或者完全忽略细节，只勾勒出主题的轮廓，而是要求他让每一个字都言之有物。”

Not vacuity, but economy.

不是空洞，而是节俭。

This principle became the Strunk and White imperative: “Omit needless words.” Do your writing a favor and tape that dictate to your computer screen, then do it. No speech, no matter its length, should ask the reader/audience to absorb one more word than necessary. Extraneous language annoys us. Omit it.

这条原则后来成为斯特伦克和怀特的准则：“省略不必要的词语。” 为了你的写作，不妨对着电脑屏幕录音，然后再进行写作。任何演讲，无论长短，都不应该让读者/听众多吸收一个字。多余的语言会让我们感到厌烦。请省略它。

(The dialogue in Sofia Coppola’s film LOST IN TRANSLATION executes the principle of economy with perfection. See Chapter Eighteen.)

（索菲亚·科波拉的电影《迷失东京》中的对话完美地运用了简洁的语言原则。参见第十八章。）

THE PAUSE

暂停

Inside the give-and-take of dialogue, the pause serves many uses. When used prior to a turning point, a moment of wordless hesitation tightens tension in the reader/audience, focuses their attention on what will happen next, and emphasizes the gravity of the event. A pause after a turning point allows the reader/audience time to absorb the meaning of the change and savor its aftermath.

在对话的互动中，停顿发挥着多种作用。在转折点之前，短暂的无言犹豫能增强读者/观众的紧张感，引导他们关注接下来的发展，并强调事件的重要性。转折点之后的停顿则能让读者/观众有时间消化变化的意义，并细细品味其带来的后续影响。

A pre-crisis pause dams emotion momentum. In a well-written scene, curiosity and concern flow toward the moment of critical change. The reader/audience asks itself, “What’s going to happen next? What’s she going to do when it does? How will this turn out?” As this impetus peaks, a pause holds it in check and compresses its power. When the turning point pivots, all that pent-up energy explodes into the scene’s climactic beat.

危机前的停顿抑制了情绪的涌动。在精心设计的场景中，好奇心和担忧会涌向关键转折点。读者/观众会问自己：“接下来会发生什么？她会怎么做？事情最终会如何发展？”当这种情绪达到顶峰时，停顿会抑制它，压缩它的力量。当转折点到来时，所有积蓄的能量都会爆发，最终汇聚成场景的高潮。

Overused, however, the pause—like talk—can wear out its welcome. The principle of economy applies as much to this tactic as any other. If dialogue halts again and again and again to signal emphasis, emphasis, emphasis, nothing gets emphasis. Like “The Boy Who Cried Wolf,” the more often an author repeats a technique, the less effect it has. Then when the scene arrives in which she wants the tactic to deliver its effect in full, she discovers that repetition has blunted its edge.

然而，停顿如果使用过度，就像说话一样，也会让人感到厌倦。节约原则同样适用于这种技巧。如果对话反复停顿以示强调，那么最终什么也强调不了。就像《狼来了》的故事一样，作者重复使用某种技巧的次数越多，其效果就越差。等到她想要充分发挥该技巧作用的场景出现时，她会发现重复已经削弱了它的威力。

Be judicious in the placement of pauses. Shape the rhythm of scenes without undo hesitation, so that when you put on the brakes, the standstill moment grips attention. There are no free rests: A pause must be earned.

要巧妙地安排停顿。塑造场景节奏，避免不必要的犹豫，这样，当你突然刹车时，这短暂的静止时刻才能真正抓住观众的注意力。没有免费的休息：停顿必须经过精心设计才能获得。

THE CASE FOR SILENCE

沉默的理由

Lean, pacey dialogue, more implicit than explicit, keeps readers and audiences hungry for more; stuffed, sluggish speeches, more explicit than implicit, discourage interest. As overwritten dialogue wears on and on, the reader skims, the audience stops listening. So, in the same way that tragic scenes often call for comic relief, surplus talk may call for silence.

简洁明了、节奏紧凑的对话，含蓄多于直白，能让读者和观众意犹未尽；冗长拖沓、直白多于含蓄的对话则会令人失去兴趣。随着对话的不断重复，读者会略读，观众也会停止聆听。因此，正如悲剧场景往往需要喜剧元素来缓和气氛一样，过多的对话也需要以沉默来化解。

From story to story, scene to scene, how much is too much is impossible to say. Your taste and judgment must guide that decision. But if you feel that your pages overtalk their scenes, switch gears and write for the eye rather than the ear, make image substitute for language.

从一个故事到另一个故事，从一个场景到另一个场景，究竟多少才算过量，这很难说。你的品味和判断必须指导你做出决定。但如果你觉得你的文字过多，场景描述过于冗杂，那就转换思路，用图像代替语言，让画面来表达。

Challenge yourself with this question: How could I write this scene in a purely visual way, doing all that needs to be done for character and story without resorting to a single line of dialogue? You can call upon the power of images in one of two ways:

挑战一下自己，思考这个问题：我该如何用纯粹的视觉方式来描写这个场景，在不使用任何一句对白的情况下，完成所有塑造角色和推进故事发展所需的工作？你可以通过以下两种方式之一来运用图像的力量：

One, paralanguage. Gestures and facial expressions are not, strictly speaking, linguistic. Nonetheless, they can speak with all the overtones and undertones of words. So rather than cluttering scenes with verbalized affirmations or disaffirmations such as “yes/no,” “I agree/I disagree,” or “I think you’re right/I think you’re wrong,” carry the moment with a nod, a glance, a wave of the hand.

第一，副语言。严格来说，手势和面部表情并非语言。然而，它们却能传递出语言的所有弦外之音和弦外之音。因此，与其在场景中堆砌“是/否”、“我同意/我不同意”或“我认为你是对的/我认为你是错的”之类的口头肯定或否定，不如用点头、眼神或挥手来表达当下。

This is especially true when writing for television and film. Whenever possible, leave room for the screen actor’s creativity. Because the camera can magnify a face many times larger than life, thoughts and emotions seem to flow behind the eyes and under the skin like swells across a sea. Silence invites the camera in. Use it.

这一点在为电视和电影创作剧本时尤为重要。尽可能地为演员的创作留出空间。因为镜头可以将面部放大数倍，所以思想和情感仿佛在眼底和皮肤下涌动，如同海浪翻滚。沉默会吸引镜头，所以要善加利用。

Two, physical action. At every opportunity ask yourself this question: What physical, rather than verbal, behavior would execute my characters’ actions and reactions? Let your imagination paint word-pictures of doing rather than saying.

第二，肢体动作。抓住每一个机会问自己这个问题：用肢体动作而非语言来表现人物的行动和反应会是什么？让你的想象力描绘出行动的画面，而不是用语言来表达。

Consider, for example, a scene from a film by Ingmar Bergman with an apt title in this context, THE SILENCE. In it, a woman in a hotel restaurant allows herself to be seduced by a waiter. How to write that?

例如，考虑一下英格玛·伯格曼的一部电影《沉默》中的一个场景，这部电影的片名在这个语境下非常贴切。在影片中，一位女士在酒店餐厅里被一位服务员诱惑。该如何描写这个场景呢？

Does the waiter offer her the menu, listing the specials of the day? Does he recommend his favorite dishes? Does he compliment her on how she’s dressed? Does he ask her if she’s staying at the hotel? Traveling far? Does he ask if she knows the city? Does he mention he’s getting off work in an hour and would love to show her the sights? Talk, talk, talk?

服务员会递给她菜单，列出当日特色菜吗？他会推荐他最喜欢的菜肴吗？他会称赞她的穿着吗？他会问她是否住在酒店吗？是远道而来吗？他会问她是否熟悉这座城市吗？他会提到自己一个小时后下班，很乐意带她游览景点吗？他们会聊个不停吗？

Here’s how Bergman played it: The waiter, accidently on purpose, drops a napkin on the floor next to her chair. As he slowly stoops and kneels to pick it up, he sniffs and smells the woman from head to crotch to foot. She, in reaction, inhales a deep, pleasure-filled sigh. Bergman then cuts to a hotel room where the customer and waiter writhe in passion. Their intensely erotic, visual, physical, wordless seduction in the restaurant executes its turning point on her inhale.

伯格曼是这样处理的：服务员故意将餐巾纸掉在她椅子旁的地板上。他缓缓弯腰跪下捡起餐巾纸时，从头到脚嗅遍了女人的全身。她闻到后，深深地吸了一口气，发出了一声充满愉悦的叹息。伯格曼随后切换到酒店房间，顾客和服务员激情缠绵。他们在餐厅里那场充满情欲、视觉冲击力十足、肢体交融、无声的诱惑，在她那声叹息中达到了转折点。

Silence is the ultimate economy of language.

沉默是语言最极致的简洁。

#↩

PART 2

第二部分

FLAWS AND FIXES

缺陷与修复

#↩

Introduction:

介绍：

SIX DIALOGUE TASKS

六项对话任务

Effective dialogue executes six tasks simultaneously:

有效的对话同时完成六项任务：

1. Each verbal expression takes an inner action.

1. 每个言语表达都伴随着一个内在的动作。

2. Each beat of action/reaction intensifies the scene, building to and around its turning point.

2. 每一次行动/反应都加剧了场景的紧张感，并逐渐推向转折点。

3. Statements and allusions within the lines convey exposition.

3. 诗句中的陈述和典故起到了阐述作用。

4. A unique verbal style characterizes each role.

4. 每个角色都有其独特的语言风格。

5. The flow of progressive beats captivates the reader/audience, carrying them on a wave of narrative drive, unaware of the passage of time.

5. 渐进式的节奏吸引着读者/观众，让他们沉浸在叙事的浪潮中，忘记了时间的流逝。

6. The language strikes the reader/audience as authentic in its setting and true to character, thus maintaining belief in the story’s fictional reality.

6. 语言风格与故事背景相符，符合人物性格，从而让读者/观众相信故事的虚构真实性。

Fine dialogue harmonizes all six of these objectives at once, so let’s look at the various faults that break the flow and cause discord.

良好的对话能够同时协调这六个目标，所以让我们来看看破坏对话流畅性和造成不和谐的各种缺陷。

#↩

6

CREDIBILITY FLAWS

信誉缺陷

INCREDIBILITY

不可思议

The standards of credibility we set for the physical behaviors of characters apply equally to what they say. Dialogue written for television, stage, or film must inspire believable performances in its actors. Scenes written for a novel or short story must inspire the reader to imagine credible behaviors in literary characters. So, no matter how complex and compelling the psychology of your characters, no matter how emotional and meaningful your story design, if your characters do not talk in a manner true to their natures, true to the setting and genre, the reader/audience loses faith. Unconvincing dialogue destroys interest faster than sour notes destroy a recital.

我们为角色肢体行为设定的可信度标准同样适用于他们的言语。为电视、舞台或电影创作的对话必须能够激发演员们做出令人信服的表演。为小说或短篇故事创作的场景必须能够激发读者想象出文学人物合情合理的行为。因此，无论你的角色心理多么复杂引人入胜，无论你的故事构思多么感人至深，如果你的角色说话的方式不符合他们的本性、不符合故事背景和类型，读者/观众就会失去信任。不令人信服的对话比走调的音符毁掉一场演出更能迅速地扼杀观众的兴趣。

Hollow, phony dialogue cannot be cured with naturalism. If you eavesdrop on the conversations of your fellow passengers on planes, trains, and buses, you realize in a flash that you would never put those gossipy bull sessions on stage, page, or screen. Actual chatter repeats like a dribbling basketball. Everyday talk lacks vividness, resonance, expressivity, and, most critically, significance. Business meetings, for example, often roll on and on, hour after hour, without metaphor, simile, trope, or imagery of the least expressivity.

空洞虚假的对话无法用自然主义来弥补。如果你在飞机、火车或公共汽车上偷听其他乘客的谈话，你会立刻意识到，你绝不会把那些闲聊搬上舞台、书页或银幕。日常对话就像篮球运球一样不断重复。它们缺乏生动性、共鸣、表现力，以及最关键的意义。例如，商务会议往往没完没了，一小时又一小时，却没有任何比喻、明喻、修辞手法或哪怕是最基本的意象。

The crucial difference between conversation and dialogue is not the number, choice, or arrangement of words. The difference is content. Dialogue concentrates meaning; conversation dilutes it. Therefore, even in the most realistic settings and genres, credible dialogue does not imitate actuality.

对话与交流的关键区别不在于词语的数量、选择或排列方式，而在于内容。交流强调意义，而对话则淡化意义。因此，即使在最写实的场景和类型中，可信的交流也并非模仿现实。

In fact, credibility has no necessary relationship to actuality whatsoever. Characters who live in impossible worlds, such as Alice’s Wonderland, deliver lines that would never be said by a living person but are true to themselves and true to the settings.

事实上，可信度与现实并无必然联系。生活在虚构世界中的角色，例如《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的角色，会说出一些真人绝不会说的话，但这却符合他们自身以及故事背景的设定。

In all settings from the most down-to-earth to the most magical, in all genres from war stories to musicals, in all styles of speech from inarticulate monosyllables to lyrical verse, dialogue should sound like the spontaneous talk of its characters. For that reason, we gauge dialogue against a standard of fictional authenticity, not factual accuracy. A character’s word choices and syntax should not be so true to life that they imitate the redundant banalities of the everyday. Rather, they must strike us as plausible and vernacular within the context of the story’s world and genre(s).

无论场景是朴实无华还是奇幻瑰丽，无论题材是战争故事还是音乐剧，无论语言风格是含糊不清的单音节词还是优美的诗句，对话都应该听起来像是角色自然流露的言语。因此，我们评判对话的标准是虚构的真实性，而非事实的准确性。角色的用词和句法不应过于贴近生活，以至于模仿日常生活中那些陈词滥调。相反，它们必须在故事的世界观和类型背景下显得合情合理、通俗易懂。

The reader/audience wants to believe that characters speak offstage, off-page, or offscreen exactly as they speak onstage, on the page, or onscreen, no matter how fantasized the story’s setting. Even in worlds as fantastic as Guillermo del Toro’s film PAN’S LABYRINTH, as absurd as Eugène Ionesco’s play Exit the King , as poetic as T. S. Eliot’s play Murder in the Cathedral , or as archaic as Robert Graves’s novel, I, Claudius , the cast’s talk need not be factual, but it must seem credible.

读者/观众希望相信，无论故事的背景设定多么奇幻，角色在舞台之外、书页之外或银幕之外的对话都与他们在舞台上、书页上或银幕上所说的一模一样。即使是在像吉尔莫·德尔·托罗的电影《潘神的迷宫》那样奇幻的世界，像尤金·尤内斯库的戏剧《国王之死》那样荒诞的世界，像T·S·艾略特的戏剧《大教堂谋杀案》那样充满诗意的世界，或是像罗伯特·格雷夫斯的小说《我，克劳狄乌斯》那样古老的世界，演员的对话不必完全符合事实，但必须听起来可信。

On the other hand, anyone might say anything at any time. So, how do we judge dialogue credibility? How do we know when a line is true to its character and true to the moment, or false on both counts?

另一方面，任何人都有可能在任何时候说出任何话。那么，我们如何判断对话的可信度？我们如何知道一句台词是否符合人物性格和当时的语境，还是两者都不成立？

Aesthetic judgment will never be a science. It is, by nature, as feeling as it is thoughtful. Instead, you must rely on skilled intuition, on your sense of rightness based on knowledge, experience, and inborn taste. Learn to judge your dialogue by listening past the words and sensing the harmony or disharmony between cause and effect. Dialogue rings true when a character’s verbal actions resonate with his motivations, when his inner desires and outer tactics seem to complement each other.

审美判断永远无法成为一门科学。它本质上既包含感觉也包含思考。因此，你必须依靠娴熟的直觉，依靠基于知识、经验和与生俱来的品味而产生的正确感。学会透过字面意思去聆听对话，感受因果关系中的和谐或不和谐，从而判断对话的真谛。当角色的言语行为与其动机相符，当他的内心渴望与外在策略相辅相成时，对话便会显得真实可信。

Exactly how you will master judgment in your own work is yours to discover, but to help guide you in that goal, below is a short list of faults that damage credibility: empty talk, overly emoted talk, overly knowing talk, overly perceptive talk, and excuses substituting for motivation.

如何在自己的工作中掌握判断力，这完全取决于你自己的探索。但为了帮助你实现这个目标，以下列出了一些会损害信誉的错误：空谈、情绪化的言论、自以为是的言论、过于敏锐的言论，以及用借口代替动机。

EMPTY TALK

空谈

When a character speaks, the reader/audience looks into the subtext for a motivation to make sense out of the lines, a cause to explain the effect. If they find none, the dialogue sounds phony and the scene with it. The most commonplace example: one character telling another character something they both already know to satisfy the author’s expositional exigencies.

当角色说话时，读者/观众会探究其言外之意，寻找话语背后的动机，以理解其含义，并解释其结果。如果找不到动机，对话就会显得虚假，整个场景也会因此而显得牵强。最常见的例子就是：一个角色为了满足作者的叙事需要，告诉另一个角色一些他们早已知晓的事情。

OVERLY EMOTIVE TALK

过于情绪化的谈话

When a character uses language that seems far more emotional than his actual feelings, again the reader/audience wonders why and checks the subtext for an explanation. If they find none, they may assume that either this hyper-dramatic character is a hysteric or that the author is desperately trying to make too much out of too little. At some social/psychological level, emotive dialogue and its context should complement each other.

当一个角色使用的语言听起来远比他实际的感受更加情绪化时，读者/观众会感到疑惑，并试图从文本的潜台词中寻找解释。如果找不到，他们可能会认为这个过度戏剧化的角色要么是个歇斯底里的人，要么是作者在用力过猛，试图将有限的信息过度解读。从某种社会/心理层面来看，情感化的对话及其语境应该相辅相成。

OVERLY KNOWING TALK

过于自以为是的谈话

Know what your characters know. Characters are an author’s creatures, born of exhaustive research into the story’s setting and cast, countless observations of human behavior, and ruthless self-awareness. A bold line, therefore, runs between creator and created. Or should. But if a writer crosses that line and injects his author’s knowledge into his character’s awareness, we sense a cheat. When a character onscreen or onstage talks about current events with a breadth and depth of understanding only his author could have, or when a novel’s first-person protagonist looks back on past events with factuality and clarity of insight beyond his experience, again, the reader may sense that the author is whispering into his character’s ear.

了解你笔下人物的认知。人物是作者的造物，源于对故事背景和人物的详尽研究、对人类行为的无数次观察以及毫不留情的自我认知。因此，创造者和被创造者之间应该有一条清晰的界限。或者说，应该是这样。但如果作者越过这条界限，将自己的知识注入到人物的认知中，我们就会感到一种欺骗。当银幕或舞台上的角色以只有作者才能拥有的广度和深度谈论时事，或者当小说的第一人称主人公以超越自身经验的事实性和洞察力回顾过去时，读者同样会感觉到作者在对角色耳语。

OVERLY PERCEPTIVE TALK

过于敏感的谈话

Similarly, beware characters who know themselves better than you know yourself. When a character describes himself with a depth of insight more profound than Freud, Jung, and Socrates combined, readers and audiences not only recoil at the implausibility; they lose faith in the writer. Authors set traps for themselves when they create characters with excessive, unconvincing self-awareness.

同样，要警惕那些比你更了解自己的角色。当一个角色对自己的描述比弗洛伊德、荣格和苏格拉底加起来还要深刻时，读者和观众不仅会因为这种不合情理而感到反感，还会对作者失去信任。作者塑造出过度且缺乏说服力的自我意识角色，无异于给自己设下陷阱。

It happens like this: Hardworking writers fill notebooks and files with character biographies and psychologies, generating ten or twenty times more material than they would directly use in the writing. They do this, as they must, to give themselves a surfeit of material in order to win the war on clichés with original, unexpected choices. Having amassed this knowledge, the desire to get all they know out into the world can become an irresistible temptation. Unwittingly, the author crosses the line between writer and character, turning his creation into a mouthpiece for his research.

事情是这样的：勤奋的作家们在笔记本和文件里记录着人物的生平、心理，积累的素材量是实际写作所需素材的十倍甚至二十倍。他们这样做是必须的，为了积累足够的素材，以便用原创且出人意料的选择战胜陈词滥调。然而，一旦积累了这些知识，想要把所有了解都公之于众的渴望就可能变成一种难以抗拒的诱惑。不知不觉中，作者越过了作家和人物之间的界限，将笔下的人物变成了自己研究成果的传声筒。

EXCUSES MISTAKEN FOR MOTIVATION

借口被误认为是动力

Create honest motivation for behavior. In an effort to match a character’s over-the-top action with a cause, writers often backtrack to the character’s childhood, insert a trauma, and pass it off as motivation. Over recent decades, episodes of sexual abuse became an overused, all-purpose, mono-explanation for virtually any extreme behavior. Writers who resort to this kind of psychological shorthand do not understand the difference between excuse and motivation.

为行为找到合理的动机。为了给角色的极端行为找到合理的解释，作家们常常会追溯角色的童年，插入一段创伤经历，并将其包装成行为的动机。近几十年来，性虐待事件几乎成了所有极端行为的万能解释，而且这种解释被过度使用。诉诸这种心理速成手法的作家们，并不理解借口和动机之间的区别。

Motivations (hunger, sleep, sex, power, shelter, love, self-love, etc.) are needs that drive human nature and compel behavior. 1 More often than not, these subconscious drives go unrecognized, and as often as not, cause more trouble than they cure. Unwilling to face the truth of why they do what they do, human beings invent excuses.

动机（饥饿、睡眠、性欲、权力、住所、爱、自爱等等）是驱动人类本性并驱使行为的需求。这些潜意识的驱动力往往不被察觉，而且常常弊大于利。人们不愿面对自身行为背后的真相，于是编造借口。

Suppose you were writing a pivotal scene for a political drama in which a national leader explains to his cabinet why he is taking the country to war. Throughout history, two primary motivations have driven one people to war against another. First, the drive for power abroad. Land, slaves, and wealth seized from the defeated empowers the victor. Second, the drive for power at home. When rulers fear losing strength, they provoke war to distract their citizens and regrip domestic power. (George Orwell dramatized both motivations in his masterpiece, 1984 .)

假设你正在为一部政治剧创作一个关键场景，剧中一位国家领导人向内阁解释他为何要发动战争。纵观历史，驱使一个民族向另一个民族发动战争的主要动机有两个。首先是对外扩张的野心。从战败国掠夺的土地、奴隶和财富能够增强战胜国的实力。其次是内政的欲望。当统治者担心失去权力时，他们会挑起战争，以此转移民众的注意力，重新掌控国内权力。（乔治·奥威尔在他的杰作《1984》中生动地展现了这两种动机。）

These two motivations compel the reality of war, but no ruler who declares war thinks like that. Or if he does, he would never say it. So, to write your scene, you would have to bury motivation in the subtext, create a leader with just the right quality of self-deception, and then write his dialogue to frame an excuse other characters believe and follow.

这两种动机促成了战争的现实，但没有哪个宣战的统治者会这样想。即便他真有这种想法，也绝不会说出口。所以，要写好你的场景，你必须把动机隐藏在言外之意中，塑造一个恰到好处地具有自欺欺人特质的领导者，然后编写他的台词，为他的战争行为构建一个其他角色相信并追随的借口。

Some of the excuses warring peoples have used throughout history include: “Saving souls for God” (Christian Crusades, Spanish Empire, Ottoman Empire), “Shining the light of civilization into the darkness of savagery” (British Empire), “Manifest Destiny” (genocide of Native Americans), “Purifying the race” (the holocaust), and “Transforming capitalist tyranny into Communist equality” (the Russian and Chinese revolutions). 2

历史上交战各方使用的借口包括：“为上帝拯救灵魂”（基督教十字军东征、西班牙帝国、奥斯曼帝国）、“将文明之光照进野蛮的黑暗”（大英帝国）、“昭昭天命”（对美洲原住民的种族灭绝）、“净化种族”（纳粹对犹太人的大屠杀）以及“将资本主义暴政转变为共产主义平等”（俄国革命和中国革命）。

For an example of an excuse masquerading as motivation, consider Shakespeare’s The Tragedy of Richard III . In Act 1, Scene 1, Richard, the hunchbacked Duke of Gloucester, says that because his deformity is repellent, he “cannot prove a lover.” So, instead he will “prove a villain” and murder everyone between himself and the throne.

莎士比亚的悲剧《理查三世》就是一个以借口伪装成动机的例子。在第一幕第一场中，驼背的格洛斯特公爵理查声称，因为他的畸形令人厌恶，所以他“无法成为一个爱人”。因此，他决定“成为一个恶人”，杀光所有挡在他和王位之间的人。

Then, in the very next scene, Richard meets Anne, the beautiful widow of a rival he recently assassinated. She hates Richard and curses him, calling him the devil. Nonetheless, Richard, ugly as he is, guilty as he is, mounts a campaign of brilliant psychological seduction. He claims that because Anne is so breathtakingly beautiful and he is so desperately in love with her, he had to kill her husband in the hopes of having her. He then kneels down and offers her his sword so she can kill him, if she wishes. She declines and by the end of the scene this blend of flattery and self-pity wins her heart.

紧接着，在接下来的场景中，理查德遇到了安妮，他不久前刺杀的一位竞争对手的遗孀，一位美丽的女子。安妮憎恨理查德，诅咒他，称他为魔鬼。然而，尽管理查德相貌丑陋，罪孽深重，他却精心策划了一场心理战，成功地诱惑了安妮。他声称，因为安妮美得令人窒息，而他又深深地爱着她，所以他不得不杀死她的丈夫，只为得到她。随后，他单膝跪地，将剑递给她，问她是否愿意，可以杀死他。安妮拒绝了，而到了场景的结尾，理查德这番谄媚与自怜交织的表演最终赢得了她的芳心。

With that seduction, Richard reveals himself as a masterful lover. So why does he say he is not? Because he needs an excuse to mask his lust for power.

凭借那番诱惑，理查德展现了他高超的情人技巧。那么，他为何否认这一点呢？因为他需要一个借口来掩盖他对权力的渴望。

To write intriguing, layered, credible dialogue, first study the difference between the two motors for human action—motivation and justification. Then see if masking your characters’ subconscious drives with their conscious efforts to excuse, or to at least make sense out of their unexplainable behaviors, adds depth to their words.

要写出引人入胜、层次丰富、令人信服的对话，首先要研究人类行为的两种驱动力——动机和辩解——之间的区别。然后，看看用角色有意识的努力来为他们无法解释的行为辩解，或者至少让他们为自己的行为找到合理的解释，是否能为他们的话语增添深度。

In most cases, false dialogue is not the signature of an overly confident, overly knowledgeable writer, but the opposite: a nervous, unschooled writer. Anxiety is the natural by-product of ignorance. If you don’t know your character beyond his name, if you cannot imagine how he reacts, if you cannot hear his voice, if you write in bewilderment, your hand will scratch out nothing but bogus dialogue. In the fog of not knowing, you have no other choice.

大多数情况下，虚假对话并非自信过头、知识渊博的作家的标志，恰恰相反：它往往出自紧张、缺乏经验的作家之手。焦虑是无知的必然产物。如果你对笔下的人物一无所知，只知道他的名字，无法想象他的反应，听不出他的声音，如果你在茫然中写作，那么你写出来的只会是虚假的对话。在无知的迷雾中，你别无选择。

Therefore, do the hard work. Surround your character with all the knowledge and imagining you can. Test his traits against the people around him and, most importantly, yourself. For at the end of the day, you are the touchstone of truth. Ask yourself: “If I were my character in this situation, what would I say?” Then listen with your most truth-sensitive ear for the honest, credible answer.

因此，要努力钻研。尽可能地运用知识和想象力来塑造你的角色。将他的特质与他周围的人，尤其是你自己进行比较。因为归根结底，你才是真理的试金石。问问自己：“如果我是这个角色，身处这种情况，我会说什么？”然后，用你最敏锐的耳朵去聆听那个真诚可信的答案。

MELODRAMA

情节剧

The adjective “melodramatic” indicts writing for excessiveness—shrill voices, lurid violence, tear-stained sentimentality, or sex scenes one shadow this side of pornography. On the other hand, Shakespeare’s The Tragedy of Othello rages with murderous jealousy; Sam Peckinpah’s THE WILD BUNCH turns violence into cinematic poetry; Stephen Sondheim’s A Little Night Music explores deep, painful sentiments; and Nagisa Oshima’s masterpiece IN THE REALM OF THE SENSES indulges explicit sex; and none of them is melodrama.

“情节剧式”这个形容词往往指责作品过于夸张——尖锐的嗓音、骇人的暴力、催人泪下的感伤，或是近乎色情的性爱场景。然而，莎士比亚的《奥赛罗》中充满了嫉妒的杀戮；萨姆·佩金帕的《野战群》将暴力转化为电影般的诗意；斯蒂芬·桑德海姆的《小夜曲》探索了深刻而痛苦的情感；大岛渚的杰作《感官世界》则展现了露骨的性爱；而这些作品都不是情节剧。

Long before Oedipus gouged out his eyes, great storytellers have sought the limits of human experience. Twenty-first-century artists continue this quest because they sense that the depths and breadths of human nature know no limits. Anything you can picture your characters doing, believe me, human beings have already done it and in ways beyond imagining.

早在俄狄浦斯挖出双眼之前，伟大的故事讲述者就已探寻人类经验的极限。二十一世纪的艺术家们延续着这一探索，因为他们深知人性的深度和广度是无穷无尽的。相信我，你笔下人物所能想象的任何行为，人类都早已做过，而且做得远超你的想象。

The problem of melodrama, therefore, is not over-expression but under-motivation.

因此，情节剧的问题不在于表现过度，而在于动机不足。

When a writer scores a scene with ping-ponging histrionics, trying to make a snit seem lethal; when he cascades tears down a character’s face, hoping to make a setback seem tragic; or when he forces behavior to exceed what’s actually at stake in a character’s life, we dismiss his work as melodrama.

当一位作家用夸张的戏剧化手法来渲染一个场景，试图将一次小小的抱怨描绘成致命的；当他让一个角色泪流满面，希望将一次挫折描绘成悲剧；或者当他强迫角色的行为超出其生活中实际面临的风险时，我们会将他的作品斥为情节剧。

Melodramatic dialogue, therefore, is not a matter of word choices. Human beings are capable of doing anything and saying anything while they do it. If you can imagine your character talking in a passionate, pleading, profane, or even violent way, then lift his motivation to match his action. Once you have behavior balanced with desire, take it a step further and ask yourself: “Would my character state or understate his action?”

因此，戏剧化的对话并非在于措辞的选择。人类在做任何事情的同时，都能说出任何事情。如果你能想象你的角色以充满激情、恳求、粗俗甚至暴力的方式说话，那么就提升他的动机，使之与他的行动相匹配。一旦你的行为与欲望达到了平衡，不妨更进一步，问问自己：“我的角色会明确表达他的行动，还是会含蓄地表达？”

Compare two versions of a “Cut off his head!” scene: Suppose GAME OF THRONES were to develop a plotline in which two kings fight each other in a long war to a blood-soaked end. Then comes the climax: The victorious king sprawls on his throne; his defeated enemy kneels at his feet, awaiting sentencing. A courtier asks the king, “What are your wishes, sire?” and the king screams his answer: “Smash every bone in his body! Burn his skin black, peel it off, and feed it to him! Rip his eyes from his head and his head from his neck.”

比较两个版本的“砍头！”场景：假设《权力的游戏》剧情发展成两位国王之间展开一场旷日持久的血腥战争。高潮来临：胜利的国王瘫坐在王座上；战败的敌人跪在他的脚下，等待判决。一位朝臣问国王：“陛下，您有何吩咐？”国王怒吼道：“打碎他身上的每一根骨头！把他的皮烧成焦黑，剥下来喂给他吃！挖出他的眼珠，把他的头颅从脖子上扯下来！”

Or, the courtier asks the king’s wishes, and as the victor examines his manicure, he whispers, “Crucify him.”

或者，朝臣询问国王的意愿，当胜利者检查自己的指甲时，他低声说道：“把他钉在十字架上。”

The subtext under “Crucify him” implies a death as hideous as the screamed answer, but which answer conveys greater personal power? The lurid, harsh, overstated rant, or the simple, understated “Crucify him”?

“把他钉在十字架上”这句话的潜台词暗示着一种与喊出的回答一样可怕的死法，但哪种回答更能传达个人的力量？是耸人听闻、严厉苛刻、夸张的咆哮，还是简单、低调的“把他钉在十字架上”？

Either answer could be perfectly in-character, but what kind of character? The first answer implies a weak king at the mercy of his emotions; the second suggests a powerful king in command of his emotions. In the matter of melodrama, motivation and character are never separate. What would drive one character over a cliff wouldn’t get another character off his sofa. Therefore, the balance of motivation versus action is unique to every role and has to be struck inside a character who first feels it and then does it.

两种答案都完全符合人物性格，但究竟是怎样的性格呢？第一个答案暗示着一位软弱无能、受情绪左右的君王；第二个答案则暗示着一位强大而能掌控自己情绪的君王。在通俗剧中，动机和性格从来都不是分开的。足以让一个角色坠入深渊的事件，对另一个角色来说却可能毫无作用。因此，动机与行动之间的平衡因角色而异，必须由角色自身去体会，并最终付诸行动。

#↩

7

LANGUAGE FLAWS

语言缺陷

CLICHÉS

陈词滥调

Clichés are scenes we’ve seen too many times before, acted with predictable behaviors, mouthed in dialogue we can recite before the actor says a word.

老套的场景是指我们已经看过太多遍的情节，演员的表演方式也千篇一律，台词我们甚至在演员开口之前就能背诵出来。

Like the weeds of repetition, clichés grow in the barren mind of the lazy writer. Many wannabes assume that writing is easy, or it should be, so they try to make it easy by rummaging through the trash of old stories, and pulling out the same tired phrases we’ve heard or read a hundred times in the same tired scenes we’ve heard or read a thousand times.

就像重复的杂草一样，陈词滥调在懒惰作家的贫瘠头脑中滋生蔓延。许多想成为作家的人认为写作很容易，或者应该很容易，所以他们试图通过翻找旧故事的垃圾来简化写作，把我们已经听过或读过上百遍的陈词滥调，以及我们已经听过或读过上千遍的陈词滥调，生搬硬套到同样的场景中。

Why lazy writers lack originality is no mystery, but why do diligent, professional authors, who should know better, also resort to clichés? Because they work. Once upon a time, today’s hackneyed expressions were inspired creative choices.

懒惰的作家缺乏原创性的原因并不难理解，但为什么勤奋的专业作家，明明应该更懂得如何运用陈词滥调，却也诉诸于此呢？因为陈词滥调确实有效。曾几何时，如今这些老生常谈的表达方式，却是充满灵感的创意之选。

In CASABLANCA (1942), Captain Renault’s gem-quality imperative “Round up the usual suspects” encapsulated political corruption in five smart words. Since then, the phrase “the usual suspects” has topped the list of the usual clichéd suspects in dozens of dictionaries devoted to clichés. 1

在1942年的电影《卡萨布兰卡》中，雷诺上尉那句精辟的命令“把那些惯犯抓起来”用五个字就概括了政治腐败。自此，“惯犯”这个短语便在数十部陈词滥调词典中位列最常见陈词滥调之首。

Somewhere in humanity’s past, a cave-dwelling storyteller first described a teardrop in a character’s eye to express sorrow, and everyone around the fire felt a wave of sadness. Once upon a time, a king’s raconteur first compared an enemy’s military trap to a spider’s web, and the whole palace felt a rush of fear. Although time has dulled the cliché’s edge, the original invention was so sharp it still cuts a sliver of truth.

在人类远古的某个时期，一位穴居说书人首次用人物眼中的泪珠来表达悲伤，围坐在篝火旁的人们都感受到了一股淡淡的哀愁。很久以前，一位国王的吟游诗人首次将敌人的军事陷阱比作蜘蛛网，整个宫殿顿时笼罩在恐惧之中。尽管时间冲淡了这句陈词滥调的锋芒，但最初的创造却如此犀利，至今仍能折射出一丝真理。

Here, for example, is a short list of clichés that frequently find their way into modern dialogue (to set a limit, I restricted the slate to phrases that begin with the letters “ba”): backseat driver, back to basics, back to square one, back to the drawing board, bad hair day, bag of tricks, ballpark figure, ball’s in your court, bang your head against a brick wall, barking up the wrong tree, battle royal… and the list goes on.

例如，以下是一些经常出现在现代对话中的陈词滥调（为了限制数量，我将列表限制在以字母“ba”开头的短语中）：后座司机、回归基本、回到原点、回到原点、糟糕的发型日、一招鲜、大致估算、球在你手里、撞墙、找错方向、大乱斗……等等。

Familiarity breeds comfort. People, on occasion, enjoy a cliché because it signals cultural continuity. The past is still present. What people loved in their childhood, they still love today. For that reason, clichés infect their everyday talk. People use them because, trite or not, they make immediate sense. As a result, the infrequent cliché adds verisimilitude.

熟悉感带来舒适感。人们有时会喜欢陈词滥调，因为它象征着文化的延续。过去依然存在。人们童年喜爱的事物，如今依然喜爱。正因如此，陈词滥调渗透到人们的日常对话中。人们使用它们，无论是否老套，它们都能立刻引起共鸣。因此，偶尔出现的陈词滥调反而增添了真实感。

Just remember this: Sooner or later, every cliché reaches its use-by date and becomes so odorous the world finally turns away in disgust.

记住这一点：任何陈词滥调迟早都会过时，变得令人作呕，最终让世人厌恶地避而远之。

To create fresh, original dialogue, set high standards and never settle for the obvious choice. Indeed, never settle for the first choice. Just write it down, then improvise, experiment, go a little crazy, pour out as many choices as your talent can create. Let your character say any off-the-wall thing that comes into her head. By playing with every wild thing you can imagine, you might discover that one of your lunatic choices is crazy but brilliant.

要想创作出新鲜原创的对话，就要设定高标准，绝不满足于显而易见的选择。事实上，永远不要满足于第一个念头。先把它写下来，然后即兴发挥，反复试验，尽情天马行空，把你的才华倾泻而出，创造出尽可能多的选择。让你的角色说出任何她脑海中浮现的奇思妙想。通过尝试各种天马行空的想法，你可能会发现，你那些看似疯狂的选择中，某个看似疯狂却又无比精彩。

At the end of the day make your best choice, then cut the rest. No one has to see your weak choices… unless you’re foolish enough to leave them on the page.

最终，做出你认为最好的选择，然后删掉其他的。没人需要看到你那些不太理想的选择……除非你傻到把它们留在纸上。

CHARACTER-NEUTRAL LANGUAGE

字符中立语言

Character-neutral dialogue substitutes generality for specificity.

不涉及特定角色的对话以概括性代替具体性。

When writers use the stale language of everyday talk, they defend their vapidities, once again, with appeals to verisimilitude. And again, they would be correct. For when you turn an objective ear to the talk around you, banalities and clichés do indeed echo and re-echo down the caverns of conversation. In states of surprise, for instance, people call upon their deities. “Oh my God!” naturally pops out of the startled. As dialogue, however, this ready-made phrase robs the actor of a chance to create a revealing, character-specific moment.

当作家使用陈腐的日常语言时，他们又一次以追求真实性来为自己的空洞辩护。而他们也确实没错。因为当你客观地倾听周围的谈话时，你会发现那些平庸之语和陈词滥调的确在对话的洞穴中不断回响。例如，在惊讶的状态下，人们会呼唤他们的神明。“我的天哪！”自然而然地脱口而出。然而，作为对话，这种现成的短语却剥夺了演员创造一个揭示人物内心、展现角色特质的瞬间的机会。

What to do?

该怎么办？

Ask yourself this question: If my character, in a state of shock, were to call upon God, how would she and she alone do it? If she were from Alabama, would she say, “Sweet, bleeding Jesus”? If she were from Detroit, would she look up to the sky and plead, “Lord have mercy”? If she were from New York, would she call upon the devil instead and curse, “Well, damn me to hell”? Whatever your choice, find words so true to your character, they wouldn’t quite fit in anyone else’s mouth.

问问自己这个问题：如果我的角色在极度震惊之下向上帝祈祷，她会如何祈祷？如果她来自阿拉巴马州，她会说“我的天哪”吗？如果她来自底特律，她会仰望天空祈求“主啊，怜悯我”吗？如果她来自纽约，她会转而呼唤魔鬼，诅咒“该死的，让我下地狱吧”吗？无论你选择哪种方式，都要找到最能体现你角色特质的词语，让它们只适合你一个人的口吻。

We’ll examine character-specific language in depth in Part Three.

我们将在第三部分深入探讨角色特有的语言。

OSTENTATIOUS LANGUAGE

炫耀性语言

In a dialogue scene near the end of James Joyce’s A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man , the novel’s protagonist, Stephen Dedalus, and Lynch, his friend, debate aesthetics. To clinch his argument, Stephen describes the ideal relationship between an author and his finished work in these words: “The artist, like the God of creation, remains within or behind or beyond or above his handiwork, invisible, refined out of existence, indifferent, paring his fingernails.”

在詹姆斯·乔伊斯的小说《青年艺术家画像》接近尾声的一段对话中，小说主人公斯蒂芬·迪达勒斯和他的朋友林奇就美学展开辩论。为了巩固自己的论点，斯蒂芬用这样一段话描述了作者与其完成作品之间的理想关系：“艺术家，如同造物主一般，存在于他的作品之中、背后、之外或之上，隐形于世，被提炼得无影无踪，漠然地修剪着指甲。”

Joyce’s analogy advocates a writing method that so harmonizes characters and events, the telling seems authorless. Applied to dialogue, the Joycean ideal becomes talk so true to the vocal personalities that any hint of string pulling vanishes. Rather, each spoken word draws us deeper and deeper into the storytelling, holding us spellbound to the end.

乔伊斯的比喻提倡一种写作方法，这种方法使人物与事件如此和谐，以至于叙述仿佛没有作者的痕迹。应用于对话时，乔伊斯的理想体现在对话中，对话真实地反映了人物的个性，任何刻意安排的痕迹都消失殆尽。相反，每一个字都引领我们更深入地进入故事，让我们着迷直至结尾。

Ostentatiousness breaks that spell. By ostentatious dialogue, I mean self-conscious displays of literariness, lines so unnecessarily expressive, so clearly out of character that they call attention to the writing as writing. The worst of these jumps out of the scene waving pompoms in celebration of its author’s victory, declaring, “Oh, what a clever line am I!”

矫揉造作会破坏这种氛围。我所说的矫揉造作的对话，指的是刻意炫耀文学技巧，那些过于夸张、明显不符合人物性格的台词，反而让人注意到作者的写作手法。最糟糕的例子莫过于作者跳出场景，挥舞着彩球庆祝自己的胜利，高声宣称：“哦，我写了一句多么精彩的台词啊！”

Like stand-up comics who laugh at their own jokes, like exhibitionistic athletes who dance in the end zone, literary swagger celebrates its success. But the instant a line of dialogue makes the reader or audience aware of art as art, the bond of belief fused between them and the character snaps.

就像脱口秀演员会自嘲一样，就像爱炫耀的运动员会在达阵区跳舞一样，文学作品中的傲慢自大也是为了庆祝成功。但一旦某句台词让读者或观众意识到艺术的本质，他们与角色之间建立起来的信任纽带就会断裂。

As we noted in the “as if” discussion in Chapter Five, when people open a book or sit down as an audience, they shift their mental gears from the factual to the fictional mode. They know that to take part in the ritual of story, they must willingly believe in imaginary characters as if they were real, and react to fictitious events as if they were actually happening. It’s a childlike state, so a bond of trust must run through the story, that ancient contract that conjoins a reader/audience to an author.

正如我们在第五章“仿佛”讨论中所提到的，当人们打开一本书或坐下来聆听故事时，他们的思维模式会从现实模式切换到虚构模式。他们知道，要参与到故事的仪式中，就必须心甘情愿地相信虚构的人物，如同他们真实存在一般，并对虚构的事件做出如同真实发生一般的反应。这是一种孩童般的状态，因此，信任的纽带必须贯穿整个故事，这种古老的契约将读者/观众与作者联系在一起。

That’s the deal, and no matter how realistic or fantasied the genre, the bond will hold so long as the reader/audience finds the dialogue true to the characters who speak it. The moment technique becomes visible, dialogue rings false, the reader/audience loses trust, the bond breaks, and the scene fails. Break belief often enough, the reader/audience tears up the contract and tosses your work in the trash.

这就是关键所在。无论题材多么写实或奇幻，只要读者/观众觉得对话符合角色性格，这种联系就能维系。一旦技巧显露出来，对话听起来不真实，读者/观众就会失去信任，联系就会断裂，场景也会失败。如果屡次打破读者/观众的信任，他们就会撕毁合约，把你的作品扔进垃圾桶。

Of all aspects of characterization—dress, gesture, age, sexuality, mood, facial expression—speech is by far the most susceptible to disbelief. Odd phrasings, eccentric word choices, even out-of-place pauses can betray the odor of bad acting—fake emotions, shallow mind, and hollow heart. That’s why every line of dialogue puts the writer under pressure to maintain the bond of credibility.

在所有人物塑造要素中——包括服饰、姿态、年龄、性取向、情绪和面部表情——语言无疑是最容易让人产生怀疑的。怪异的措辞、古怪的用词，甚至不合时宜的停顿，都可能暴露出拙劣演技的本质——虚假的情感、肤浅的思想和空洞的内心。正因如此，每一句台词都让编剧倍感压力，必须努力维持角色的可信度。

As an author, you must develop taste enough to sense the shift from expressivity to exhibitionism. To do so, first test the limits of language your medium imposes. What could be said with moving conviction on page may be embarrassingly unactable onstage. Because the marker dividing veracity from falsity is set as much by tradition as by authorship, first identify your story’s genre(s), and then study the conventions. Finally, bring your best judgment to bear by asking this question: If I were my character, in these circumstances, what would I say? The only curbs on garishness are your innate taste and schooled judgment. So let your inner acumen be your guide. When in doubt, tone it down.

作为一名作者，你必须培养足够的品味，才能察觉到表达与炫耀之间的微妙转变。为此，首先要测试你所用媒介对语言的局限性。在纸面上能饱含深情地表达的内容，在舞台上可能显得尴尬不堪。因为真假之间的界限既取决于传统也取决于作者的创作，所以首先要确定故事的类型，然后研究其惯例。最后，运用你最佳的判断力，问问自己：如果我是我笔下的人物，在这种情况下，我会说什么？唯一能抑制浮夸的，是你与生俱来的品味和后天习得的判断力。所以，让你的直觉指引你。如有疑问，就收敛一些。

ARID LANGUAGE

干旱语言

The opposite of ostentation is desert-dry, Latinate, polysyllabic language composed into long sentences strung out over long speeches. The suggestions below help avoid arid speech in favor of natural, unaffected, seemingly spontaneous dialogue. But always bear in mind that these points (like all else in this book) are guidelines, not imperatives. Every writer has to find her own way.

与炫耀截然相反的是枯燥乏味、拉丁语式的、多音节的语言，这种语言由冗长的句子构成，贯穿于冗长的演讲之中。以下建议有助于避免枯燥的语言，转而追求自然、不做作、看似即兴的对话。但请始终记住，这些要点（如同本书中的所有其他内容一样）只是指导原则，而非硬性规定。每位作家都必须找到属于自己的道路。

PREFER THE CONCRETE TO THE ABSTRACT

宁愿选择具体事物而非抽象事物

Would a twenty-first-century character call her home a “domicile” or her car a “vehicle”? Doubtful. On the other hand, there may be people who would. So if you have a character-specific reason for your role’s formality, then by all means, give her an abstract vocabulary. Otherwise, keep it real with specific names for objects and actions.

一个二十一世纪的人物会把家称为“住所”（domicile），把车称为“车辆”（vehicle）吗？恐怕不会。但另一方面，也许有人会这么做。所以，如果你的角色需要使用正式的语言表达方式，并且有特定的理由，那么当然可以给她一套抽象的词汇。否则，还是应该使用具体的名称来指代物品和动作，保持真实可信。

PREFER THE FAMILIAR TO THE EXOTIC

比起异域风情，我更喜欢熟悉的事物。

Would your character refer to his house as his palais or his apartment as his pied-à-terre ? Doubtful. Then again, he may be la-di-da by nature… or actually French.

你笔下的人物会把自己的房子称为“宫殿”（palais），把公寓称为“临时住所”（pied-à-terre）吗？不太可能。不过话说回来，他或许天生就有点儿矫揉造作……或者他其实是个法国人。

PREFER SHORT WORDS TO LONG WORDS

尽量使用短词而非长词

Would you write a line such as “His fabrications are falsifications of factuality”? Doubtful. “He stretches the truth,” or simply, “He lies,” or bluntly, “He bullshits,” would be more credible choices.

你会写“他的捏造事实就是歪曲事实”这样的句子吗？恐怕不会。“他夸大其词”、“他撒谎”或者更直白地说“他胡说八道”，会是更可信的选择。

And you always have at least two choices. English grew out of the merger of two languages, Anglo-Saxon, a dialect of Old German, and Old French, a dialect of Latin. As a result, the vocabulary of the language that became modern English immediately doubled (see the sidebar). English has at least two words for everything. In fact, with more than a million words, the English vocabulary offers near-inexhaustible choices.

而且你总是至少有两种选择。英语是由两种语言融合而成：盎格鲁-撒克逊语（古德语的一种方言）和古法语（拉丁语的一种方言）。因此，现代英语的词汇量立即翻了一番（参见侧边栏）。英语中几乎任何事物都有至少两个词来表达。事实上，英语词汇量超过一百万，提供了近乎无穷的选择。

HOW ENGLISH BECAME A DOUBLE LANGUAGE

英语如何成为双语

After the Romans conquered England in the first century AD, they hired German and Scandinavian mercenaries from Anglia and Saxony to help fend off pirates and put down rebellions by the native Picts and Celts. When the Roman Empire abandoned England in 410 AD, more Anglo-Saxons migrated to the island, marginalizing the Gallic-speaking Celts, wiping out the Latin of the Romans, and imposing their Germanic tongue throughout England.

公元1世纪罗马人征服英格兰后，他们从盎格利亚和萨克森雇佣了日耳曼人和斯堪的纳维亚雇佣兵，以抵御海盗并镇压当地皮克特人和凯尔特人的叛乱。公元410年罗马帝国放弃英格兰后，更多盎格鲁-撒克逊人迁徙到该岛，边缘化了讲高卢语的凯尔特人，抹杀了罗马人的拉丁语，并将他们的日耳曼语强加于整个英格兰。

But 600 years later Latin came back this roundabout way: In 911 AD Danish Vikings conquered territory along the north coast of France and named it after themselves, Normandy, land of the Norsemen. After 150 years of marriage to French women, these Danes spoke what their mothers spoke, a thousand-year-old French dialect of Latin. In 1066 King Wilhelm of Normandy (a.k.a. William the Conqueror) led his armies across the English Channel and defeated the English king. With that victory, French came to England.

但600年后，拉丁语以一种迂回的方式回归：公元911年，丹麦维京人征服了法国北部沿海地区，并以自己的名字将其命名为诺曼底，意为“北欧人的土地”。在与法国女子通婚150年后，这些丹麦人开始说他们母亲所说的语言——一种有着千年历史的法语拉丁语方言。1066年，诺曼底国王威廉（即征服者威廉）率领军队渡过英吉利海峡，击败了英国国王。随着这场胜利，法语传入了英格兰。

Throughout history, foreign conquests usually erase native languages. But England was the exception. For some mysterious reason, the Germanic language of the Anglo-Saxons and the Latinate French of the Normans merged. As a result, the vocabulary of what became modern English doubled. English has at least two words for everything. Compare, for example, the Germanic-rooted words “fire,” “hand,” “tip,” “ham,” and “flow” to the French-derived words “flame,” “palm,” “point,” “pork,” and “fluid.”

纵观历史，外来征服通常会抹杀本土语言。但英格兰是个例外。由于某种神秘的原因，盎格鲁-撒克逊人的日耳曼语和诺曼人的拉丁语融合在一起。结果，现代英语的词汇量翻了一番。英语中几乎每个事物都至少有两个词。例如，源自日耳曼语的“fire”（火）、“hand”（手）、“tip”（尖端）、“ham”（火腿）和“flow”（流动）与源自法语的“flame”（火焰）、“palm”（手掌）、“point”（点）、“pork”（猪肉）和“fluid”（液体）就截然不同。

Given the massive vocabulary of English, I offer this guiding principle: Shun polysyllabic words, especially those that end in Latinate suffixes such as “-ation,” “-uality,” and “-icity.” Instead, favor the punchy, vivid one-or two-syllable words that, more often than not, come from the ancient Anglo-Saxon heritage of English. But whether your phrasings follow from the Germanic or French traditions, consider these four observations in making word choices:

鉴于英语词汇量庞大，我提出以下指导原则：避免使用多音节词，尤其是以拉丁语后缀（如“-ation”、“-uality”和“-icity”）结尾的词。相反，应倾向于使用简洁有力、生动形象的一音节或双音节词，这些词通常源自古老的盎格鲁-撒克逊英语传统。但无论你的措辞遵循的是日耳曼语系还是法语系的传统，在选择词语时都应考虑以下四点：

1) The more emotional people become, the shorter the words and sentences they use; the more rational people become, the longer the words and sentences they use.

1) 情绪化的人说话越用词越简短；理性的人说话越理性。

2) The more active and direct people become, the shorter the words and sentences they use; the more passive and reflective people become, the longer the words and sentences they use.

2) 人越是积极主动、说话直接，使用的词语和句子就越短；人越是消极内省、说话含蓄，使用的词语和句子就越长。

3) The more intelligent the person, the more complex his sentences; the less intelligent, the briefer his sentences.

3）人的智力越高，句子越复杂；人的智力越低，句子越简短。

4) The more well read the person, the larger his vocabulary and the longer his words; the less read, the smaller his vocabulary and the shorter his words.

4) 一个人读书越多，词汇量就越大，用词就越长；读书越少，词汇量就越小，用词就越短。

Returning to an earlier example, consider the line “His fabrications are falsifications of factuality” as opposed to “The son of a bitch lies.” The former polysyllabic, alliterated, Latinized accusation might be said by a bemused wigged barrister in a litigation comedy that satirizes the formalities of royal high court. The six monosyllables of the latter, however, could be said in anger by almost anyone anywhere.

回到之前的例子，想想“他的捏造都是对事实的歪曲”和“这个混蛋在撒谎”这两句话。前者是一句多音节、押头韵、拉丁语化的指控，可能是在一部讽刺皇家高等法院繁文缛节的诉讼喜剧中，一位戴着假发、一脸茫然的律师会说的话。而后者只有六个单音节，几乎任何人都可以在任何地方愤怒地脱口而出。
