When conflict builds and risk soars, people get emotional, active, direct, monosyllabic, and dumb. As conflict peaks, people often say really stupid things they later regret. In all media and all structural shapes of story, conflict-rich scenes not only carry the telling, but as strife progresses, they also tend to shape talk in the four ways I’ve described above.

当冲突升级、风险飙升时，人们会变得情绪化、行动迅速、直言不讳、言辞简短，甚至愚蠢。冲突达到顶峰时，人们常常会说出一些事后后悔莫及的蠢话。在所有媒体和所有故事结构中，充满冲突的场景不仅推动着叙事发展，而且随着冲突的加剧，它们往往会以我上面描述的四种方式影响人们的谈话。

On the other hand, when composing a story in the past tense of prose, reflective passages with little or no conflict become fairly common. So once again, let me remind you that the guidelines in this book only describe tendencies. Somewhere, somehow, someone’s behavior turns every psychological doctrine ever formulated on its head. The same is true of writing. Every principle of craft sets up its creative contradiction.

另一方面，用过去时态创作散文故事时，几乎没有冲突的反思段落会变得相当常见。所以，我再次提醒各位，本书中的指导原则仅仅描述了一些趋势。在某个地方，以某种方式，总会有人做出颠覆所有既有心理学理论的行为。写作亦是如此。每一项写作原则本身就蕴含着创造性的矛盾。

Consider, for example, Boyd Crowder, the protagonist’s frenemy in the long-form series JUSTIFIED. Showrunner Graham Yost pitched the dialogue for the entire cast at a heightened timbre. But for Boyd, he reached centuries back into the show’s Appalachian setting and found a speech style fit for a Confederate politician. Here’s Boyd on going to bed:

例如，想想长篇剧集《火线警探》（JUSTIFIED）中主角的亦敌亦友博伊德·克劳德。剧集运作人格雷厄姆·约斯特为所有角色都设计了高亢的台词。但对于博伊德，他却追溯到几个世纪前该剧设定的阿巴拉契亚山区，找到了一种适合南方邦联政客的说话方式。以下是博伊德谈到睡觉时的一段话：

BOYD

博伊德

Be that as it may, I sense within me a growing, nagging torpor that seeks a temporary hibernation in a solitary area for comfort and slumber.

尽管如此，我内心却感到一种日益增长的、挥之不去的倦怠感，渴望在一个僻静的地方暂时蛰伏，以获得舒适和睡眠。

Over the centuries before the final merger of Latinate French and Old German into modern English, Latin and French were the languages of power in England. 2 Like many people in public life, politicians and corporate leaders alike, Boyd Crowder’s quest for power and prestige propels his life down a series-long spine of action. And like the power greedy, Boyd flaunts his polysyllabic vocabulary and puts as many words as possible between the capital letter that opens a sentence and the period that closes it, scoffing at the admonition below.

在拉丁语系法语和古德语最终融合为现代英语之前的几个世纪里，拉丁语和法语一直是英国的权力语言。 2 和许多身居要职的人一样，无论是政客还是企业领袖，博伊德·克劳德对权力和声望的追求都驱使着他的人生走上了一条充满行动的道路。而像那些权力欲熏心的人一样，博伊德炫耀着他那冗长的词汇，在句首大写字母和句末句号之间塞入尽可能多的词语，对句末的告诫嗤之以鼻。

PREFER DIRECT PHRASES TO CIRCUMLOCUTION

尽量使用直接的语句，避免拐弯抹角。

Would you write: “When I punched the guy, I suddenly realized that it hurt me a lot more than it hurt him, because after I took my hand out of my pocket and closed it as tight as I could, making sure that my thumb was on the outside and not the inside of my fingers, and then hit him in the face as hard as I could, I felt a sharp pain and couldn’t close my fist anymore”? Or: “Broke my fist on his jaw. Hurt like hell.”

你会这样写：“我打了那家伙一拳，突然意识到自己比他疼得多，因为我把手从口袋里掏出来，紧紧握拳，确保拇指在外面而不是里面，然后用尽全力打他脸的时候，突然感到一阵剧痛，拳头都握不住了”？还是会这样写：“我的拳头打在他的下巴上，疼得要命。”

Wording reflects the distinct qualities of a character played out against his once-in-a-lifetime conflicts. So if, for example, your character is a scientist, theologian, diplomat, professor, an intellectual of any persuasion, or simply pretentious, then he or she may very well use elaborate, academic locutions when calm and rational circumstances allow. But as a general principle, pace scenes with direct, unaffected speeches of crisp words.

措辞体现了人物的独特特质，并展现了他/她一生中可能遇到的种种冲突。例如，如果你的角色是科学家、神学家、外交官、教授、任何流派的知识分子，或者仅仅是自命不凡之人，那么在冷静理智的环境下，他/她完全可以使用华丽的学术辞藻。但总的来说，场景的节奏应该以简洁明了、自然流畅的对话来推进。

This principle holds true on page and stage, but particularly onscreen. The theatre audience listens intensely. The reader can reread a novel’s sentence if she doesn’t get it on the first pass. Television viewers can record and rewind, if necessary, to listen to dialogue a second time. Big-screen dialogue, however, is spoken, then gone. The cinema audience concentrates through its eyes, not its ears. If moviegoers don’t instantly understand, they turn to each other asking, “What did he say?”

这条原则在书页和舞台上都适用，但在银幕上尤其如此。剧院观众全神贯注地聆听。读者如果第一次没听懂，可以重读小说中的句子。电视观众可以录制并倒带，以便再次聆听对话。然而，大银幕上的对话一说完就消失了。电影观众的注意力是通过眼睛而不是耳朵。如果观众没能立即理解，他们会互相询问：“他说了什么？”

But no matter the medium, misunderstood dialogue annoys. What difference does it make how eloquent your language is if the reader/audience misses its meaning? Therefore, expressive inversions aside, let line structure flow from noun to verb to complement in that order. Clarity above all.

但无论在何种媒介中，对话被误解都会令人恼火。如果读者/观众无法理解你的意思，那么你的语言再优美又有什么用呢？因此，撇开华丽的倒装句不谈，让句子结构遵循名词-动词-补语的顺序。清晰明了至关重要。

PREFER AN ACTIVE TO A PASSIVE VOICE

尽量使用主动语态而非被动语态

Passive dialogue uses linking verbs such as “am,” “is,” “are,” “was,” “were,” “be,” and “been” to express static states (for example, “He isn’t very smart”); active dialogue uses action verbs to express dynamic change (for example, “He’ll figure it out for himself”).

被动对话使用系动词，如“am”、“is”、“are”、“was”、“were”、“be”和“been”来表达静态状态（例如，“他不太聪明”）；主动对话使用动作动词来表达动态变化（例如，“他会自己想办法解决”）。

When humans enter into conflicts, their minds become energized, their views of themselves and the world around them become active, and therefore, their language becomes charged with action verbs. When situations calm, human beings become more passive, their view of life more reflective, and their language tends to fill with state-of-being verbs. Again, this pattern is only a tendency, not a rule of human behavior. Nonetheless, in a storm of conflict, state-of-being verbs slow headway like a ship dragging anchor.

当人类陷入冲突时，他们的思维会变得活跃，他们对自身和周围世界的看法也会变得积极，因此，他们的语言中会充斥着行动动词。当局势平静下来时，人们会变得更加被动，他们对生活的看法也会更加反思，他们的语言中往往会充满状态动词。当然，这仅仅是一种倾向，而非人类行为的必然规律。然而，在冲突的风暴中，状态动词会像拖着锚的船一样，阻碍局势的进展。

The passivity that’s most difficult to spot hides inside gerund phrases. In these cases, a state-of-being verb connects to an “-ing” ending verb in phrases such as “She is playing around,” “They are working hard,” “They were coming home yesterday.” Gerunds give dialogue only slightly more energy. Before you commit to a gerund phrase, test the active case: “She plays around,” “They work hard,” “They came home yesterday,” and see whether a single, direct verb doesn’t better fit the moment.

最难察觉的被动语态隐藏在动名词短语中。在这种情况下，表示状态的动词与以“-ing”结尾的动词连接，例如“She is playing around”、“They are working hard”、“They were coming home yesterday”。动名词只能略微增强对话的语气。在决定使用动名词短语之前，不妨先试试主动语态：“She plays around”、“They work hard”、“They came home yesterday”，看看是否用一个直接的动词更能贴合语境。

PREFER SHORT SPEECHES TO LONG

比起冗长的演讲，我更喜欢简短的演讲。

When the pretentious wish to impress, they add syllables to words, words to sentences, sentences to paragraphs, paragraphs to speeches. They substitute quantity for quality, length for brevity, convolution for simplicity. The effect is often unintentionally comic.

当那些自命不凡的人想要给人留下深刻印象时，他们会在单词里增加音节，在句子里增加单词，在段落里增加句子，在演讲里增加段落。他们用数量代替质量，用冗长代替简洁，用繁复代替简单。其结果往往令人啼笑皆非。

For example, these three bites from the festooned language of Helen Sinclair (Dianne Wiest), the aging Broadway grande dame, in Woody Allen and Douglas McGrath’s screenplay BULLETS OVER BROADWAY.

例如，以下三段摘自伍迪·艾伦和道格拉斯·麦克格拉斯编剧的电影《百老汇的子弹》中，年迈的百老汇老牌女星海伦·辛克莱（黛安·韦斯特饰）华丽辞藻的片段。

When she arrives late for a rehearsal:

当她排练迟到时：

HELEN

海伦

My pedicurist had a stroke. She fell forward on the orange stick and plunged it into my toe. It required bandaging.

我的修脚师中风了。她向前摔倒，压在橘子棒上，橘子棒扎进了我的脚趾。需要包扎。

Staring into a dark theatre auditorium:

凝视着黑暗的剧院礼堂：

HELEN

海伦

This old theatre—this church—so replete with memories, so full of ghosts, Mrs. Alving, Uncle Vanya, here’s Ophelia, there’s Cordelia… Clytemnestra… every performance a birth, each curtain, a death…

这座古老的剧院——这座教堂——充满了回忆，充满了幽灵，阿尔文夫人，万尼亚舅舅，这里是奥菲莉娅，那里是科迪莉娅……克吕泰涅斯特拉……每一场演出都是一次新生，每一幕落幕都是一次死亡……

Walking through Central Park with her young playwright:

与她的年轻剧作家一起漫步中央公园：

HELEN

海伦

Everything is meaningful in some unexplainable form, more primordial than mere language.

万物都以某种无法解释的形式具有意义，这种意义比语言本身更为原始。

(as he tries to talk, she clamps her hand over his mouth)

（他试图说话，她却用手捂住了他的嘴）

Shh… shh… be silent… be silent… Let’s just walk holding our thoughts… not revealing them… be still… let the birds have their song but let ours, for now, remain unsung.

嘘……嘘……安静……安静……让我们各自走着，把思绪藏在心里……不要说出来……保持安静……让鸟儿歌唱，而我们，此刻，就让我们的心声保持沉默。

So unless, like Woody Allen, your intention is satirical, strive to express the maximum in the fewest, truest possible words.

所以，除非你像伍迪·艾伦那样，意图讽刺，否则就努力用最少、最真实的语言表达最多的意思。

PREFER EXPRESSIVE LANGUAGE TO MIMICRY

更喜欢富有表现力的语言而不是模仿

Dialogue should sound like character talk, but its content must be way above normal. Fine writers listen to the world but rarely copy what they hear, word for word, to the page. If you study documentaries and listen to what real people actually say in real life, or watch so-called reality shows and listen to the improvisations of untrained actors, you’ll soon realize that everyday talk on camera sounds awkward and amateurish. Fiction takes talk to a much higher level—far more economic, expressive, layered, and character-specific than back-fence chatter. Like marble carved by a Michelangelo, language is raw material chiseled by an author. Don’t copy life, express it.

对话听起来应该像人物的日常对话，但内容必须远超寻常。优秀的作家倾听世界，但很少逐字逐句地照搬所听到的内容。如果你研究纪录片，聆听真实人物在现实生活中的对话，或者观看所谓的真人秀，聆听未经训练的演员的即兴表演，你很快就会意识到，镜头前的日常对话听起来生硬而业余。小说将对话提升到一个更高的层次——比乡间闲聊更加精炼、富有表现力、层次丰富且更具人物特色。语言如同米开朗基罗雕刻的大理石，是作者雕琢的原材料。不要复制生活，要表达生活。

ELIMINATE CLUTTER

清除杂物

By clutter, I mean exchanges such as “Hi, how ya doing?” “Oh, I’m fine.” “And the kids?” “They’re fine, too.” “Isn’t it a beautiful day?” “Yes, finally. Last week was so rainy.” In the same way people decorate empty shelves with knickknacks, inept writers dress up vapid scenes with verbal bric-a-brac, thinking that small talk adds an air of realism. But chitchat makes characters no more authentic than dressing them in sweat pants makes them athletic. Worse yet, cluttered talk not only hollows out characters and scenes; it misleads the reader/audience.

所谓“冗余对话”，指的是诸如“嗨，你好吗？”“哦，我很好。”“孩子们呢？”“他们也很好。”“今天天气真好啊！”“是啊，终于好了。上周一直下雨。”就像人们用小摆设装饰空荡荡的架子一样，拙劣的作家也喜欢用冗长的闲聊来粉饰空洞的场景，以为这样就能增添真实感。但闲聊并不能让角色更真实，就像让他们穿上运动裤并不能让他们显得运动健将一样。更糟糕的是，冗长的对话不仅会掏空人物和场景，还会误导读者/观众。

Dialogue is more than talk in the same way dance is more than movement, music more than sound, and painting more than shapes. A work of art means more than the sum of its parts, and every part of the work means more than the part itself.

对话不仅仅是说话，正如舞蹈不仅仅是动作，音乐不仅仅是声音，绘画不仅仅是形状一样。一件艺术作品的意义远不止其各个部分的简单相加，而作品的每一个部分又都蕴含着更深远的意义。

Badly written dialogue tends to be literal; it means what it says and no more. Well-written dialogue, on the other hand, implies more than it says; it puts a subtext under every text. Readers and audiences schooled in the conventions of realism assume that every line has significance beyond its words or it wouldn’t have been written. For that reason, story-goers seek the hidden beneath the clutter, the connotation under every denotation. If they cannot find it, confused and annoyed, they lose interest.

糟糕的对话往往直白，字面意思就是字面意思，仅此而已。而好的对话则不然，它蕴含着更深层的意义，字里行间都暗藏着潜台词。受现实主义惯例熏陶的读者和观众会认为，每一句台词都蕴含着字面意义之外的含义，否则就不会被写出来。正因如此，故事的读者会试图在繁复的表象下寻找隐藏的意义，探寻字面意义背后的内涵。如果他们找不到这些，就会感到困惑和恼火，最终失去兴趣。

If your dialogue does not suggest unsaid thoughts and feelings below its surface, either enrich it or cut it.

如果你的对话没有暗示出表面之下未说出口的想法和感受，要么丰富它，要么删减它。

#↩

8

CONTENT FLAWS

内容缺陷

WRITING ON-THE-NOSE

直截了当地写出来

Writing on-the-nose means putting a character’s fullest thoughts and deepest emotions directly and fully into what she says out loud. Of the many varieties of inept dialogue, writing on-the-nose is by far the most common and most ruinous. It flattens characters into cardboard and trivializes scenes into melodrama and sentimentality. To understand the damaging effect of on-the-nose writing, let’s study this flaw in depth.

“直白”的写作方式是指将角色的全部想法和最深层的情感直接、完整地融入到她所说的话中。在众多拙劣的对话写法中，“直白”无疑是最常见也最具破坏性的。它使人物形象扁平化，使场景沦为矫揉造作的煽情剧。为了理解“直白”写作方式的危害，让我们深入探讨一下这种缺陷。

The axiom “Nothing is what it seems” bears witness to life’s duality: What seems is the surface of life—what strikes the eye and ear, the things people say and do… outwardly. What is is the actual life of thought and feeling that flows inwardly beneath the things said and done.

“眼见未必为实”这句格言印证了人生的二元性：表象是人生的表面——映照出我们眼耳所闻的，人们的言行举止……外在的。而内在的，则是隐藏在言行之下，思想与情感的真实生活。

As we noted in Chapter Three, a person’s life moves simultaneously through three levels corresponding to the said, the unsaid, and the unsayable: outwardly what people say and do, personally and socially, to get through their day (text); inwardly what they privately think and feel while they carry out these tasks (conscious subtext); and deepest yet, the massive realm of subconscious urges and primal miens that drive their inner energies (subconscious subtext).

正如我们在第三章中提到的，一个人的生活同时经历三个层面，分别对应于已说的、未说的和不可说的：外在层面，人们为了度过一天，在个人和社会层面上所说所做的事（文本）；内在层面，他们在执行这些任务时私下里所想所感（有意识的潜台词）；以及最深层的，驱动他们内在能量的庞大的潜意识冲动和原始气质领域（潜意识的潜台词）。

It is, therefore, categorically impossible for a human being to say and do what she is fully thinking and feeling for the obvious reason: The vast majority of her thoughts and feelings run below her awareness. These thoughts cannot, by their nature, rise to the surface of the said. No matter how hard we may try to be absolutely open and honest, how we try to put the subtext of truth into the text of our behavior, our subconscious self haunts every word and deed. As in life, so in story: Every text condenses a subtext.

因此，人不可能完全说出和做出自己内心所想所感，原因显而易见：绝大多数的思想和情感都潜藏在意识之外。这些思想本质上无法浮现到言语的表面。无论我们多么努力地想要做到绝对坦诚，多么努力地将潜意识中的真理融入到我们的行为之中，我们的潜意识仍然会影响我们的一言一行。正如生活一样，故事也一样：每个文本都蕴含着潜意识。

Suppose, for example, you were in mid-session with your psychiatrist, pouring out your darkest confession of the worst thing you’ve ever done to another human being. Tears filling your eyes, pain doubling you in two on the chaise, you choke out the words. And what’s your psychiatrist doing? Taking notes. And what’s in those notes? What you are not saying. What you cannot say.

例如，假设你正在和精神科医生进行咨询，倾诉你对他人做过的最黑暗、最伤人的秘密。泪水盈满眼眶，痛苦让你在躺椅上蜷缩成两截，你哽咽着说出那些话。而你的精神科医生在做什么？他在做笔记。而那些笔记里记录了什么？你没说出口的话。你无法说出口的话。

A psychiatrist is not a stenographer, there to take down your exposés. He is trained to see through the text of you to the unsayable subtext, to those things you cannot say because you cannot consciously think them.

精神科医生不是速记员，他们的职责是记录你的吐槽。他们受过专业训练，能够透过你的言辞，看到你难以言说的潜台词，那些你因为无法有意识地思考而无法说出口的话。

On-the-nose writing eliminates subtext by erasing conscious, unsaid thoughts and desires, along with subconscious, unsayable longings and energies, and leaving only spoken words, delivered in blatant, explicit, hollow-sounding speeches. Or, to put it another way, on-the-nose dialogue rewrites the subtext into a text, so that characters proclaim exactly and fully what they think and feel, and therefore, speak in ways no human being has ever spoken.

直白的写作方式抹杀了潜台词，抹去了意识层面未曾言明的想法和欲望，以及潜意识中难以言说的渴望和能量，只留下直白、空洞、直白的言语。换句话说，直白的对话将潜台词改写成文本，使角色能够完整而准确地表达他们的所思所想，因此，他们的说话方式是前所未有的。

For example, this scene: Two attractive people sit across from each other in a secluded corner of a graceful restaurant. The light glints off the crystal and the dewy eyes of the lovers. Beautiful music plays in the background; gentle breezes billow the curtains. The lovers reach across the table, touch fingertips, look longingly in each other’s eyes, simultaneously say, “I love you, I love you,” and actually mean it .

例如，这样的场景：两个俊男靓女在一家雅致餐厅的僻静角落里相对而坐。灯光映照在水晶杯和恋人湿润的眼眸中。优美的音乐在耳边萦绕；微风轻拂着窗帘。恋人们越过桌子，指尖相触，深情凝视着彼此，同时轻声说着“我爱你，我爱你”，而且是发自内心的。

This scene, if produced, would die like a squashed dog in the road. It is simply unactable.

这场戏如果拍出来，肯定会像被车碾死的狗一样彻底失败。它根本没法演。

By unactable I mean this: Actors are not marionettes hired to mouth your words and mime your actions. These artists give life to your cast by first discovering their character’s true desire hidden in the subtext. They then ignite this inner energy and with it build ineffable layers of complexity from the inside out that finally surface in the character’s actions, expressed in gestures, facial expressions, and words. But the scene, as I described it, is void of subtext and therefore, by definition, unactable.

所谓“无法表演”，我的意思是：演员不是傀儡，他们不是被雇佣来念台词、模仿动作的。这些艺术家赋予角色生命，首先要挖掘出角色隐藏在潜台词中的真实渴望。然后，他们点燃这种内在能量，并由此由内而外地构建出难以言喻的复杂性，最终通过角色的行动、手势、面部表情和言语展现出来。但是，正如我所描述的，场景缺乏潜台词，因此，从定义上讲，它是无法表演的。

The page, stage, and screen are not opaque surfaces. Each storytelling medium creates a transparency that allows us to glimpse the unsaid or unsayable in other human beings. When we watch a television series, a film, or play, or turn pages of prose, our eye does not stop at the words on the page or the actor onstage or onscreen. Our eye travels through the text to the subtext, to the deepest stirrings within the character. When you experience a quality story, don’t you have the constant impression that you are reading minds, reading emotions? Don’t you often think to yourself, “I know what that character’s really thinking, feeling, and doing. I can see what’s going on inside him better than he can, because he’s blinded by his immediate problem”? The combined creativity of writer and actor gives us what we want from any story: to be a fly on the wall of life and see through the surface to the truth.

书页、舞台和银幕并非不透明的表面。每一种叙事媒介都创造了一种透明性，让我们得以窥见他人未曾言说或难以言说的内心世界。当我们观看电视剧、电影或戏剧，或是翻阅散文时，我们的目光并非停留在纸上的文字或舞台/银幕上的演员身上。我们的目光会穿透文本，直达潜台词，触及角色内心深处的悸动。当你体验一个精彩的故事时，难道你不会始终感觉自己仿佛在读懂人心，解读情感吗？难道你不会经常想：“我知道那个角色真正的想法、感受和行为。我比他自己更了解他内心的挣扎，因为他被眼前的困境蒙蔽了双眼”吗？编剧和演员的共同创作赋予了我们从任何故事中都渴望的东西：成为生活的旁观者，透过表象看到真相。

If I were an actor forced to act this candlelit cliché, my first ambition would be to protect my career. I would not let a bad writer make me look like a bad actor. I would put a subtext under that scene, even if it had nothing to do with the story.

如果我是个演员，被迫出演这种烛光戏码，我的首要目标就是保住我的演艺生涯。我绝不会让一个糟糕的编剧让我看起来像个糟糕的演员。我会给这场戏赋予一些潜台词，即便它和故事本身毫无关系。

My approach might go like this: Why has this couple gone out of their way to create a movie scene for themselves? What’s with all the candlelight and soft music? Why don’t they take their pasta to the TV set like normal people? What’s wrong with this relationship?

我的想法可能是这样的：这对情侣为什么非要营造出电影般的氛围？为什么点上蜡烛，放上轻柔的音乐？为什么他们不和正常人一样，拿着意面去电视机前吃？他们的关系到底出了什么问题？

Isn’t that the truth? When do the candles come out in life? When things are fine? No. When things are fine, we take our pasta to the TV set like normal people. When there’s a problem, that’s when the candles come out.

难道不是这样吗？生活中什么时候才会点亮蜡烛呢？一切顺利的时候吗？不。一切顺利的时候，我们就像正常人一样，端着意大利面窝在电视机前。只有遇到问题的时候，蜡烛才会出现。

So, taking that insight to heart, I could act the scene in such a way that the audience would see to the truth: “Yes, he says he loves her. But look, he’s desperate he’s losing her.” That subtextual action adds substance as the scene deepens into a man’s desperate attempt to rekindle the romance. Or the audience might think, “Yes, he says he loves her, but look, he’s setting her up to dump her.” That implied action stirs our fascination as we watch a man let a woman down gently with a last romantic dinner because, in truth, he’s walking out.

所以，我把这个洞察铭记于心，并以此来演绎这场戏，让观众看清真相：“没错，他说他爱她。但你看，他多么绝望，他快要失去她了。”这种潜台词式的表演，随着剧情的深入，展现出一个男人拼命想要重燃旧情的挣扎，增添了戏份的深度。或者，观众可能会想：“没错，他说他爱她，但你看，他这是在设局甩掉她。”这种隐含的意图激起了我们的好奇心，我们看着一个男人用最后的浪漫晚餐温柔地拒绝一个女人，因为实际上，他已经准备离开了。

With rare exceptions, a scene should never be outwardly and entirely about what it seems to be about. Dialogue should imply, not explain, its subtext. In the two variations above, the subtextual motivations and tactics are conscious but unspoken. As the audience/reader perceives the unsaid tactic beneath the surface of behavior, the inner action gives the scene a depth that enriches the reader/audience with insight. An ever-present subtext is the guiding principle of realism.

除了极少数例外，场景的表象绝不应完全指向其表面含义。对话应当暗示而非直接解释其潜台词。在上述两种情况下，潜台词的动机和策略都是有意为之，却又未明言。当观众/读者感知到行为表象之下隐藏的策略时，内在的行动便赋予场景深度，从而丰富读者/观众的理解。始终存在的潜台词是现实主义的指导原则。

Nonrealism, on the other hand, is the great exception. Nonrealism employs on-the-nose dialogue in all its genres and subgenres: myth and fairy tale, science fiction and time travel, animation, the musical, the supernatural, Theatre of the Absurd, action/adventure, farce, horror, allegory, magical realism, postmodernism, dieselpunk retrofuturism, and the like.

另一方面，非现实主义是个例外。非现实主义在其所有类型和子类型中都采用直白的对话：神话和童话、科幻和时间旅行、动画、音乐剧、超自然、荒诞派戏剧、动作/冒险、闹剧、恐怖、寓言、魔幻现实主义、后现代主义、柴油朋克复古未来主义等等。

In nonrealism, characters become more archetypical and less dimensional. Stories set in imaginary or exaggerated worlds move toward allegorical event designs. Pixar’s INSIDE OUT, for example. As a result, subtext tends to atrophy as dialogue becomes less complex, more explanatory, more on-the-nose. In a work such as THE LORD OF THE RINGS, no hidden or double meaning plays under lines such as “Those who venture there never return.” If an actor were to layer that line with irony, it might prompt a laugh and kill the moment.

在非现实主义作品中，人物形象变得更加典型化，立体感也随之降低。故事发生在虚构或夸张的世界中，情节设计也趋向于寓言式的。例如，皮克斯的《头脑特工队》。因此，随着对话变得不那么复杂、更加直白、更加解释性，潜台词往往会逐渐消失。在《指环王》这样的作品中，像“那些冒险前往那里的人，一去不复返”这样的台词没有任何隐藏或双关的含义。如果演员用讽刺的语气来演绎这句台词，可能会引人发笑，破坏气氛。

At some point during the fiction-writing process, every writer must answer that troublesome question: Exactly what kind of story am I telling? Two grand visions define the storyteller’s approach to reality: the mimetic and the symbolic.

在小说创作过程中，每位作家都必须回答那个棘手的问题：我究竟在讲述什么样的故事？两种宏大的视角定义了故事讲述者看待现实的方式：模仿和象征。

Mimetic stories reflect or imitate life as lived and sort themselves into the various genres of realism. Symbolic stories exaggerate or abstract life as lived and fall into one of the many genres of nonrealism. Neither approach has a greater claim on faithfulness to the truth. All stories are metaphors for existence, and the degree of realism versus nonrealism is simply a writer’s choice in his strategy to persuade and involve the reader/audience while he expresses his vision.

模仿性故事反映或模仿真实生活，并归入各种现实主义类型。象征性故事则夸张或抽象真实生活，并归入众多非现实主义类型之一。这两种方法在忠实还原真相方面并无优劣之分。所有故事都是存在的隐喻，现实主义与非现实主义的程度仅仅是作者在表达其观点时，为了说服和吸引读者/观众而采取的策略选择。

Nonetheless, one of the key differences between nonrealism and realism is subtext. Nonrealism tends to diminish or eliminate it; realism can’t exist without it.

然而，非现实主义与现实主义的关键区别之一在于潜台词。非现实主义倾向于削弱或消除潜台词；而现实主义则离不开潜台词。

Why?

为什么？

Because to clarify and purify a character’s symbolic nature—virtue, villainy, love, greed, innocence, and such—nonrealistic genres eliminate the subconscious and with that, psychological complexity.

因为为了阐明和净化人物的象征本质——美德、邪恶、爱情、贪婪、纯真等等——非现实主义类型消除了潜意识，也因此消除了心理复杂性。

Whereas, the first premise of realism is that the majority of what a person thinks and feels is unconscious to her, and for that reason, the full content of her thoughts and feelings can never be expressed directly, literally, or completely. Therefore, to dimensionalize, complicate, and ironize the psychology of the role, mimetic genres clash desires arising from the subconscious against conscious willpower.

然而，现实主义的首要前提是，一个人的大部分思想和感受都是无意识的，因此，其思想和感受的全部内容永远无法直接、字面或完整地表达出来。所以，为了使角色的心理层面更加立体、复杂和讽刺，模仿性戏剧类型将源于潜意识的欲望与意识意志力进行冲突。

The psychological and social complexity of realism demands a subtext under virtually every line of dialogue. To avoid these distracting intricacies, nonrealism discourages subtext.

现实主义作品中复杂的心理和社会因素要求几乎每一句台词都暗含深意。为了避免这些令人分心的复杂细节，非现实主义作品则不鼓励使用潜台词。

THE MONOLOGUE FALLACY

独白谬误

Every consequential moment in life pivots around a dynamic of action/reaction. In the physical realm, reactions are equal, opposite, and predictable in obedience to Newton’s third law of motion; in the human sphere, the unforeseen rules. Whenever we take an important step, our world reacts—but almost never in the way we expect. From within us or around us come reactions we cannot and do not see coming. For no matter how much we rehearse life’s big moments, when they finally arrive, they never seem to work out quite the way we thought, hoped, or planned. The drama of life is an endless improvisation.

人生中的每一个重要时刻都围绕着行动与反作用的动态关系展开。在物理领域，反作用力大小相等、方向相反且可预测，遵循牛顿第三运动定律；而在人类世界，不可预见性才是主宰。每当我们迈出重要的一步，世界都会做出反应——但几乎从不会以我们预想的方式。来自我们内心或周遭的反应，是我们无法预料的。无论我们如何预演人生中的重要时刻，当它们真正到来时，似乎永远不会完全按照我们设想、希望或计划的那样发展。人生的戏剧性在于它永无止境的即兴发挥。

For this reason, when a character sits alone staring at a wall, his flow of thought is an inner dialogue, not a monologue. This inner flux often becomes the stuff and substance of the modern novel. Prose writers can take us inside their characters’ heads, bouncing inner actions back and forth between a thinking self and his doubting, applauding, criticizing, arguing, forgiving, listening, ever-reacting selves. This purpose-filled give-and-take is dialogue that takes the form of thought rather than talk.

因此，当一个角色独自坐着凝视墙壁时，他的思绪并非独白，而是内心的对话。这种内心的流动往往构成了现代小说的素材和实质。散文作家能够带领我们进入角色的内心世界，展现其思考的自我与那些怀疑、赞扬、批评、争论、宽恕、倾听、不断做出反应的自我之间的内心互动。这种充满目的性的互动，是一种以思想而非言语形式呈现的对话。

A true monologue would provoke no response as it pours out long, uninterrupted, inactive, unreactive passages to no one in particular, turning characters into mouthpieces for their author’s philosophy. Whether voiced aloud or thought from within, any speech that runs on for too long without change in value charge risks lifelessness, artificiality, and tedium.

真正的独白不会引发任何反应，因为它冗长、不间断、毫无生气地向空无一人地倾泻而出，将人物变成了作者哲学思想的传声筒。无论是口头表达还是内心独白，任何冗长且价值取向没有变化的言语都可能变得死气沉沉、矫揉造作，令人厌倦。

How long is too long? The average speaking rate ranges between two to three words per second. At that pace, a two-minute speech could contain three hundred words. Onstage or onscreen, that’s a lot of talk without someone or something reacting. In a novel, three hundred words is a full page. Pages of first-person musing or memory, unbroken by the crisscross of counterpointing inner reactions, would severely test the reader’s patience.

多久才算太长？平均语速在每秒两到三个单词之间。按这个速度，两分钟的演讲可以包含三百个单词。无论是在舞台上还是屏幕上，如果没有人或事物做出反应，这么长的篇幅就显得冗长乏味。在小说中，三百个单词相当于一整页。如果整页都是第一人称的沉思或回忆，没有穿插其中的各种内心独白，那将会严重考验读者的耐心。

On the other hand, suppose you were writing a two-character scene and feel that Character A talks throughout, while Character B sits in silence. In that case, long speeches become natural and necessary. As you write them, however, remember that even if Character A has rehearsed her confrontation with Character B, as she begins to tell him what’s on her mind, the scene will not play out the way she expected.

另一方面，假设你在写一个双人场景，觉得角色A一直在说话，而角色B则一直沉默不语。在这种情况下，冗长的独白就变得自然而必要。然而，在写作时，请记住，即使角色A已经预演过与角色B的对话，当她开始倾诉心声时，场景的走向也不会如她所愿。

Let’s say, for example, that Character A expected Character B to defend himself against her accusations and so she memorized a long list of stinging retorts. But instead of arguing, he sits there in dead silence. His stone-faced reaction destroys her prepared speech. This unexpected turn forces her to improvise, and as we noted earlier, life is always an improvisation, always action/reaction.

例如，假设角色A期望角色B反驳她的指责，所以她事先准备了一长串犀利的反驳话。然而，角色B并没有反驳，而是沉默不语。他面无表情的反应彻底打乱了角色A的计划。这种意想不到的转变迫使角色A即兴发挥，而正如我们之前提到的，生活本身就是一场即兴表演，永远是行动与反应的较量。

On the page, therefore, insert Character A’s nonverbal reactions to Character B’s enigma. Into her column of talk, interlace her looks, gestures, pauses, stumbling phrases, and the like. Break her scene-long speech into beats of action/reaction within her and between her and the silent Character B.

因此，请在页面上插入角色A对角色B谜团的非语言反应。在她的对话段落中，穿插她的眼神、手势、停顿、结巴等。将她冗长的台词分解成她内心以及她与沉默的角色B之间的一系列动作/反应。

Imagine another example: Let’s say your character is reading a well-prepared sermon to her church’s congregation. As her eyes move down the page, might she glance up, now and then, to check the congregation for expressions of interest or lack thereof? Suppose some people look bored, what would she do? Might not thoughts bounce through her mind, inspecting her voice, her gestures, the nervous energy in her belly, telling her to breathe, to relax, to smile, to make one adjustment after another as she performs her sermon? Her sermon may seem like a monologue, but her inner life is a dynamic dialogue.

再举个例子：假设你的角色正在向教堂的会众宣读一篇精心准备的讲道稿。当她的目光向下移动时，她会不会时不时地抬头看看会众的反应？假设有些人看起来很无聊，她会怎么做？她的脑海中会不会涌现出各种念头，审视着自己的声音、手势，以及腹部的紧张感，告诉她要深呼吸、放松、微笑，并在讲道过程中不断调整？她的讲道看似独白，但她的内心世界却是一场动态的对话。

Let’s take the action/reaction principle a step further: Suppose that your character talks at length by nature. Consider Meryl Streep’s Violet Weston in the film AUGUST: OSAGE COUNTY. Long speeches drive her behavior as she dominates all conversation and never reacts to what people think or feel. Such a character may bore other characters, but you can’t allow her to bore the audience. Therefore, like playwright Tracy Letts, create the impression of long-windedness without actually going on and on. Watch the film and notice how Letts propels Violet’s speeches, then builds each scene around the reactions of her word-weary relatives who have no choice but to suffer the talkaholic.

让我们进一步探讨行动/反应原则：假设你的角色天生话多。想想梅丽尔·斯特里普在电影《八月：奥塞奇郡》中饰演的维奥莱特·韦斯顿。冗长的演讲驱动着她的行为，她主导着所有的对话，从不回应别人的想法或感受。这样的角色可能会让其他角色感到厌烦，但你不能让她让观众也感到厌烦。因此，就像剧作家特雷西·莱茨那样，营造出滔滔不绝的印象，但实际上不必真的没完没了地讲个不停。观看这部电影，注意莱茨是如何推动维奥莱特的演讲，然后围绕着她那些不堪其扰的亲戚们的反应来构建每个场景，他们别无选择，只能忍受这个话痨。

In 1889, playwright August Strindberg wrote The Stronger . The play is set in a café and dramatizes an hour-long scene that pits Mrs. X, a wife, against her husband’s mistress, Miss Y. Mrs. X carries all the dialogue, but when performed, the silent Miss Y becomes the star role.

1889年，剧作家奥古斯特·斯特林堡创作了《强者》。该剧以一家咖啡馆为背景，戏剧化地展现了一个长达一小时的场景：妻子X夫人与丈夫的情妇Y小姐针锋相对。X夫人包揽了所有对白，但在演出中，沉默寡言的Y小姐却成为了主角。

THE DUELOGUE

决斗

Think of the thousands of hours of bad film, television, and theatre you have suffered through. I suspect that more often than not, the shallow, tinny acting was not the fault of the actors but of the unactable duelogues that writers and their directors forced them to recite. Duelogue is my term for face-to-face confrontations in which two characters talk directly, explicitly, and emotionally about their immediate problem. Duelogues have the resonance of a brick because every line is on-the-nose, nothing left unsaid.

想想你忍受过的成千上万小时的糟糕电影、电视剧和戏剧。我怀疑，很多时候，肤浅、生硬的表演并非演员的错，而是编剧和导演强迫他们念的那些根本无法表演的对白造成的。“对白”是我用来指代两个角色面对面直接、直白、充满情感地谈论他们眼前问题的术语。对白就像一块砖头一样沉重，因为每一句台词都直白得不能再直白，没有丝毫保留。

For example, this scene from the film GLADIATOR. The Emperor Commodus has imprisoned his rival Maximus Decimus Meridius. That night Maximus discovers Lucilla, Commodus’s sister, waiting in his cell.

例如，电影《角斗士》中的这个场景。皇帝康茂德囚禁了他的对手马克西姆斯·狄西姆斯·梅里迪乌斯。当晚，马克西姆斯发现康茂德的妹妹卢西拉在他的牢房里等着他。

INT. DUNGEON—NIGHT

内景 地牢—夜晚

Guards take Maximus to an empty cell and chain him to the wall. As they leave, Lucilla steps out of the shadows.

卫兵们把马克西姆斯带到一间空牢房，用铁链把他锁在墙上。他们离开时，露西拉从阴影中走了出来。

LUCILLA

露西拉

Rich matrons pay well to be pleasured by the bravest champions.

富有的贵妇们愿意花重金取悦最勇敢的勇士。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

I knew your brother would send assassins. I didn’t think he would send his best.

我知道你哥哥会派刺客，但我没想到他会派出最精锐的。

LUCILLA

露西拉

Maximus… he doesn’t know.

马克西姆斯……他不知道。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

My family was burned and crucified while they were still alive.

我的家人在还活着的时候就被烧死并钉死在十字架上。

LUCILLA

露西拉

I knew nothing—

我一无所知——

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

(shouting)

（喊叫）

—Don’t lie to me.

别骗我。

LUCILLA

露西拉

I wept for them.

我为他们哭泣。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

As you wept for your father?

你为父亲哭泣的时候，是吗？

(grabbing her by the throat)

（掐住她的喉咙）

As you wept for your father?

你为父亲哭泣的时候，是吗？

LUCILLA

露西拉

I have been living in a prison of fear since that day. To be unable to mourn your father for fear of your brother. To live in terror every moment of every day because your son is heir to the throne. Oh, I’ve wept.

从那天起，我就一直生活在恐惧的牢笼里。因为害怕哥哥，我无法为父亲哀悼。因为你的儿子是王位继承人，我每时每刻都生活在恐惧之中。哦，我哭过。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

My son… was innocent.

我的儿子……是无辜的。

LUCILLA

露西拉

So… is… mine.

所以……也是……我的。

(pause)

（暂停）

Must my son die too before you will trust me?

难道我的儿子也要死，你们才会相信我吗？

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

What does it matter whether I trust you or not?

我是否信任你又有什么关系呢？

LUCILLA

露西拉

The gods have spared you. Don’t you understand? Today I saw a slave become more powerful than the emperor of Rome.

神明饶恕了你，你难道还不明白吗？今天我亲眼目睹一个奴隶的权力超过了罗马皇帝。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

The gods spared me? I am at their mercy, with the power only to amuse the mob.

诸神饶恕了我？我如今只能任由他们摆布，唯一的力量就是取悦暴民。

LUCILLA

露西拉

That is power. The mob is Rome, and while Commodus controls them, he controls everything.

这就是权力。民众就是罗马，而康茂德控制了民众，也就控制了一切。

(pause)

（暂停）

Listen to me, my brother has enemies, most of all in the senate. But while the people follow him, no one would dare stand up to him until you.

听我说，我哥哥树敌众多，尤其是在参议院。但只要人民拥护他，就没人敢与他作对，直到你出现。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

They oppose him yet they do nothing.

他们反对他，却什么也不做。

LUCILLA

露西拉

There are some politicians who have dedicated their lives to Rome. One man above all. If I can arrange it, will you meet him?

有些政治家毕生致力于罗马的事业，其中有一位尤为突出。如果我能安排，你愿意见见他吗？

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

Do you not understand, I may die in this cell tonight, or in the arena tomorrow. I am a slave. What possible difference can I make?

你难道不明白吗？我今晚可能死在这间牢房里，也可能死在明天的竞技场上。我是个奴隶。我能改变什么呢？

LUCILLA

露西拉

This man wants what you want.

这个人想要的正是你想要的。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

(shouting)

（喊叫）

Then have him kill Commodus.

然后让他杀了康茂德。

LUCILLA

露西拉

I knew a man once, a noble man, a man of principle who loved my father and my father loved him. This man served Rome well.

我曾认识一个人，一位高尚的人，一位有原则的人，他爱我的父亲，我的父亲也爱他。这个人为罗马做出了卓越的贡献。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

That man is gone. Your brother did his work well.

那个人已经走了。你哥哥做得很好。

LUCILLA

露西拉

Let me help you.

让我来帮你。

MAXIMUS

马克西姆斯

Yes, you can help me. Forget you ever knew me and never come here again.

是的，你可以帮帮我。忘了你曾经认识我，永远不要再来这里。

(calling out)

（喊叫）

Guard. The lady is finished with me.

警卫。那女人已经不理我了。

Lucilla, in tears, leaves.

卢西拉含泪离开了。

In Chapter Four of The Poetics , Aristotle argues that the deepest pleasure of theatregoing is learning, the sensation of seeing through the surface of behavior to the human truth beneath. Therefore, if you use dialogue to turn your characters’ unspoken needs and emotions into conscious pronouncements as in the scene above, if, in other words, you write the scene about what the scene is actually about, you block that insight and deprive the reader/audience of their rightful pleasure. Worse yet, you falsify life.

在《诗学》第四章中，亚里士多德论证说，观剧最深层的乐趣在于学习，在于透过行为的表象，洞察其下隐藏的人性真谛。因此，如果你像上文场景那样，用对话将人物未曾言明的需求和情感转化为有意识的表达，换句话说，如果你把场景本身的内容写出来，你就阻碍了这种洞察，剥夺了读者/观众应有的乐趣。更糟糕的是，你歪曲了生活。

In the give-and-take of life, we circle around problems, instinctively employing pretexts and tactics that skirt the painful, unspeakable truths that lurk in our subconscious. We rarely talk face-to-face, openly and directly, about our truest needs or desires. Instead, we try to get what we want from another person by navigating our way through a third thing.

在人生的讨价还价中，我们总是绕着问题打转，本能地使用各种借口和策略来回避潜意识中那些痛苦而难以启齿的真相。我们很少会面对面、坦诚直接地谈论自己最真实的需要或渴望。相反，我们总是试图通过某种中间环节来从他人那里得到自己想要的东西。

Therefore, you will find the fix for on-the-nose writing in something outside the immediate conflict, a third thing that diverts a duelogue into a trialogue.

因此，要解决直白的写作问题，你需要在直接冲突之外寻找解决办法，也就是引入第三种因素，将二重奏变成三重奏。

THE TRIALOGUE

三部曲

Trialogue , as I redefine the term, names the triangular relationship between two characters in conflict and the third thing through which they funnel their struggle.

我重新定义了“三部曲”这个术语，它指的是两个冲突人物之间的三角关系，以及他们通过第三种事物来表达斗争的三角关系。

Four examples:

四个例子：

In his novel Legs , William Kennedy tells the story of the gangster, Jack “Legs” Diamond. In Chapter Three, as Jack comes into his house, his wife Alice confronts him. Jack’s men, Oxie and Fogarty, have told her that Jack nicknamed one of their canaries Marion because the bird reminds him of his mistress. In the scene that follows, two canaries act as the third thing. The narrator is Jack’s lawyer:

在威廉·肯尼迪的小说《腿》中，他讲述了黑帮分子杰克·“腿”·戴蒙德的故事。在第三章中，杰克回到家，妻子爱丽丝与他对峙。杰克的手下奥克西和福格蒂告诉她，杰克给他们的一只金丝雀取名为玛丽昂，因为这只鸟让他想起他的情妇。在接下来的场景中，两只金丝雀扮演了“第三者”的角色。叙述者是杰克的律师。

We were hardly inside the house when Alice called out to Jack, “Will you come here please?” She was on the front porch, with Oxie and Fogarty still on the sofa. They were not moving, not speaking, not looking at Alice or at Jack or at me either when we got there. They both stared out toward the road.

我们刚进屋不久，爱丽丝就喊杰克：“你过来一下好吗？”她站在前廊上，奥克西和福格蒂还坐在沙发上。我们走到他们跟前时，他们一动不动，一句话也没说，既没看爱丽丝，也没看杰克，更没看我。他们俩都直勾勾地盯着马路。

Alice opened the canary cage and said to Jack, “Which one do you call Marion?”

爱丽丝打开金丝雀笼子，问杰克：“你管哪只叫玛丽昂？”

Jack quickly turned to Fogarty and Oxie.

杰克迅速转向福格蒂和奥克西。

“Don’t look at them, they didn’t tell me,” Alice said. “I just heard them talking. Is it the one with the black spot on its head?”

“别看它们，它们没告诉我，”爱丽丝说。“我只是听到它们在说话。是那只头上有黑点的吗？”

Jack didn’t answer, didn’t move. Alice grabbed the bird with the black spot and held it in her fist.

杰克没有回答，也没有动。爱丽丝抓住那只身上有黑点的鸟，攥在拳头里。

“You don’t have to tell me—the black spot’s for her black hair. Isn’t it? Isn’t it?”

“不用你告诉我——那块黑点代表的是她的黑头发，对吧？对吧？”

When Jack said nothing, Alice wrung the bird’s neck and threw it back in the cage. “That’s how much I love you,” she said and started past Jack, toward the living room, but he grabbed her and pulled her back. He reached for the second bird and squeezed it to death with one hand, then shoved the twitching, eye-bleeding corpse down the crevice of Alice’s breasts. “I love you too,” he said.

杰克一言不发，爱丽丝便扭断了鸟的脖子，把它扔回笼子里。“我就是这么爱你，”她说着，转身越过杰克，朝客厅走去，但杰克一把抓住她，把她拉了回来。他伸手抓起第二只鸟，用一只手把它捏死，然后把那只抽搐着、眼睛流血的尸体塞进爱丽丝的胸口。“我也爱你，”他说。

That solved everything for the canaries.

这解决了金丝雀的所有问题。

When Vince Gilligan pitched his long-form series BREAKING BAD to the network, his logline was “Mr. Chips goes Scarface.” The protagonist, Walter White, faces multiple conflicts on all levels of life in dozens of directions, surrounded by a large cast of antagonists. Although building a drug empire seems to be Walter’s super-intention, Gilligan casts the shadow of Heisenberg, Walter’s doppelgänger, over all his scenes. From the very first episode, Walter’s desires and dreads, his actions and reactions, are simply manifestations of Heisenberg’s struggle to take over Walter and achieve the ultimate triumph of his genius. Heisenberg is BREAKING BAD’s third thing.

当文斯·吉利根向电视台推介他的长篇剧集《绝命毒师》时，他的剧情梗概是“《绝命毒师》版的《疤面煞星》”。主人公沃尔特·怀特在人生的各个层面都面临着多重冲突，周旋于数十个不同的方向，身边围绕着一大群反派角色。虽然建立毒品帝国似乎是沃尔特的终极目标，但吉利根却在沃尔特的所有场景中都投射了海森堡——沃尔特的分身——的阴影。从第一集开始，沃尔特的欲望和恐惧、他的行动和反应，都不过是海森堡试图控制沃尔特并最终实现其天才的体现。海森堡是《绝命毒师》的第三个要素。

Salman Rushdie’s Midnight’s Children is an allegorical novel whose protagonist, Saleem Sinai, is telepathic. But the third thing that modulates the novel’s conflicts is not paranormal. Rather, Rushdie runs Sinai’s every conflict through the cultural gap between India and Europe. By foregrounding what would normally be a background desire and painting every scene with a shade of East versus West, Rushdie colors his novel with an all-constant third thing.

萨尔曼·鲁西迪的《午夜之子》是一部寓言小说，主人公萨利姆·西奈拥有心灵感应能力。然而，贯穿小说冲突的第三个因素并非超自然力量。鲁西迪将西奈的每一个冲突都置于印度与欧洲的文化鸿沟之中。他凸显了通常被置于背景之下的欲望，并在每个场景中都融入了东西方文化的色彩，从而为小说赋予了一个始终存在的第三要素。

For many readers and theatregoers, Samuel Beckett was the greatest writer of the twentieth century and his masterpiece is Waiting for Godot . The play shuttles a massive trialogue between Estragon and Vladimir (two homeless tramps) and Godot (the eponymous character named after the French slang for God). As the title implies, the two men spend the entire play waiting, hoping, arguing about, and preparing for “he who will never appear.” The waiting seems futile, but it gives the tramps a reason, as they put it, “for going on.”

对许多读者和观众而言，塞缪尔·贝克特是二十世纪最伟大的作家，而他的代表作便是《等待戈多》。这部剧以埃斯特拉贡和弗拉基米尔（两个无家可归的流浪汉）与戈多（剧名取自法语俚语“上帝”）之间展开了一场冗长的三重对话。正如剧名所示，这两个男人在整部剧中都在等待、期盼、争论和准备迎接“那个永远不会出现的人”。等待看似徒劳，却给了这两个流浪汉一个理由，正如他们所说，“继续活下去的理由”。

In other words, Godot, Beckett’s third thing, symbolizes the persistent belief that life will ultimately make beautiful and meaningful sense, once we find that transcendent, mysterious something that awaits us somewhere… somehow… out there…

换句话说，戈多，贝克特的第三件事物，象征着一种根深蒂固的信念：一旦我们找到那超越尘世、神秘莫测的东西，生命最终将变得美好而有意义，而那东西就在那里……以某种方式……在某个地方等待着我们……

#↩

9

DESIGN FLAWS

设计缺陷

REPETITION

重复

What makes otherwise vigorous language lie lifeless on the page? What makes scenes turn antiprogressive and their dialogue fall flat? I can think of many reasons, but the most common fault is the writer’s dread enemy—repetitiousness.

是什么让原本生动有力的语言在纸上显得毫无生气？是什么让场景变得消极被动，对话变得平淡无奇？我能想到很多原因，但最常见的错误是作家最害怕的敌人——重复。

Two kinds of repetition may infect a scene’s dialogue.

两种重复可能会影响场景对话。

1) Accidental echoes. When your eye skims down a page, lines like “They’re moving their car over there” may speed by unnoticed. To avoid these verbal mishaps, record your dialogue after every draft, and then play it back. When you act your dialogue aloud or hear it acted to you, accidental echoes pop out, and you’ll instantly know what to cut or rewrite.

1）无意间的重复。当你的目光快速掠过页面时，像“他们正把车挪到那边去”这样的句子可能一闪而过，你却浑然不觉。为了避免这些语言上的失误，每次写完一稿后都要录下对话，然后再回放。当你大声朗读或听别人朗读时，那些无意间的重复就会立刻显现出来，让你立刻知道哪些地方需要删减或重写。

2) Repetitious beats. Beyond echoing words, the greater danger is repetition of feeling: the same charge of value, positive-positive-positive-positive-positive, or negative-negative-negative-negative-negative, running on, beat after beat.

2）重复的节奏。除了重复的词语之外，更大的危险是重复的情感：同样的价值感受，积极-积极-积极-积极-积极，或者消极-消极-消极-消极-消极，一节一节地重复下去。

Repetitious feelings can be insidiously hard to spot because they hide behind variations in wording. So although the scene reads well, it feels, for some mysterious reason, dead.

重复的情感往往难以察觉，因为它们隐藏在措辞的变化背后。所以，尽管这段描写读起来很流畅，但不知为何却给人一种死气沉沉的感觉。

Whenever a character takes an action in the pursuit of his or her scene intention, someone or something somewhere in the scene reacts. This pattern of action/reaction in character behavior is called a beat . For example, Character A pleads with Character B to listen to him, but Character B rejects what he has to say. Using gerunds to express action, that beat becomes begging/rejecting. (See Chapter Twelve for the complete definition of a beat.)

每当一个角色为了实现其场景意图而采取行动时，场景中的某个人或事物都会做出反应。这种角色行为中的行动/反应模式被称为“节奏”。例如，角色A恳求角色B听他说话，但角色B拒绝了他。用动名词来表达动作，这个节奏就变成了“恳求/拒绝”。（节奏的完整定义请参见第十二章。）

Beats propel scenes by advancing the action/reaction dynamic of character behaviors, each beat topping the previous beat, until the value at stake in the scene changes its charge at the turning point. (See the scene breakdowns in Chapters Thirteen through Eighteen.) But when the same beat repeats itself, the scene flattens out and boredom sets in. Repetitious behavior is far more common than accidental alliterations, more damaging to a scene, and insidiously difficult to spot. Consider this passage:

节奏通过推进人物行为的行动/反应动态来推动场景发展，每个节奏都比前一个节奏更精彩，直到场景中的关键价值在转折点发生转变。（参见第十三章至第十八章的场景分析。）但当同样的节奏重复出现时，场景就会变得平淡乏味，令人感到厌倦。重复性行为远比偶然的头韵更为常见，对场景的损害更大，而且更难察觉。请看以下段落：

CHARACTER A

角色A

I have to talk to you.

我必须跟你谈谈。

CHARACTER B

角色 B

No, leave me alone.

不，别烦我。

CHARACTER A

角色A

It’s really important you listen to me.

你一定要听我说。

CHARACTER B

角色 B

Just let me be.

就让我一个人待着吧。

CHARACTER A

角色A

You’ve got to hear what I’ve got to say.

你一定要听听我说的话。

CHARACTER B

角色 B

Shut up and go away.

闭嘴，滚开。

Character A begs Character B three times to listen to him, and three times over she rejects his plea in virtually the same language: “talk, listen, hear; alone, let, go away.” Some writers try to solve this problem by using synonyms or switching the action/reaction beat around in the belief that textual rephrasing changes the beat. In this rewrite, for example, rejecting becomes the action and begging the reaction.

角色A三次恳求角色B听他说话，而角色B三次都用几乎相同的措辞拒绝了他：“说，听，听着；独自一人，放手，走开。”有些作家试图通过使用同义词或颠倒动作/反应的节奏来解决这个问题，他们认为文本的改写可以改变节奏。例如，在这个改写版本中，“拒绝”变成了动作，“恳求”变成了反应。

CHARACTER B

角色 B

Just standing there you bother me.

你站在那里就让我觉得烦。

CHARACTER A

角色A

I’m not bothering you, I’m trying to talk to you.

我不是在打扰你，我只是想跟你谈谈。

CHARACTER B

角色 B

I’ve heard enough.

我听够了。

CHARACTER A

角色A

You haven’t heard a single word I’ve said.

我说的话你一个字都没听进去。

CHARACTER B

角色 B

Because I’m fed up with your BS.

因为我受够了你的胡说八道。

CHARACTER A

角色A

Believe me, it’s not BS. It’s the truth.

相信我，这不是胡说八道，这是事实。

And on it goes. The identical beat of rejecting/begging, whether in the same words or different words, never changes, never progresses.

就这样，一遍又一遍地重复着。拒绝/乞求的节奏始终如一，无论用词相同还是不同，都从未改变，从未进展。

Some writers defend redundancies by claiming they’re lifelike. And it’s true. People do repeat themselves. Monotony is lifelike… and lifeless. My aesthetic calls for life-filled tellings. Stories, after all, are metaphors, not photocopies. Verisimilitude, the so-called “telling detail,” is a stylistic strategy to enhance credibility, not a substitute for creative insight.

有些作家辩称重复的描写更贴近生活，以此为借口。这没错，人们的确会重复自己说过的话。单调乏味既贴近生活，又死气沉沉。我的审美追求的是充满生命力的叙述。毕竟，故事是隐喻，而非复印件。所谓“逼真细节”，是一种增强可信度的文体策略，而非创造性洞察力的替代品。

The ultimate storytelling sin is boredom—a villainous violation of the law of diminishing returns. This law states: The more often an experience repeats, the less effect it has. The first ice cream cone tastes great; the second one loses flavor; the third makes you sick. In fact, the same cause repeated back-to-back not only loses its impact, but in time also causes an opposite effect.

讲故事最大的罪过就是让人感到乏味——这是对边际效益递减规律的严重违背。这条规律指出：经历重复的次数越多，效果就越差。第一个冰淇淋甜筒味道鲜美；第二个就没味了；第三个会让你感到恶心。事实上，同样的事情反复发生，不仅会失去冲击力，而且随着时间的推移，还会产生相反的效果。

Repetitiousness follows a three-step pattern: The first time an artist skillfully uses a technique, it has its intended effect. If he immediately repeats that technique, it has less than half of the intended effect. If he’s foolish enough to try it a third time, it will not only lack the effect he wants, but swing around from behind and inflict the reverse effect.

重复性遵循三步模式：艺术家第一次巧妙运用某种技巧时，能达到预期效果。如果他立即重复该技巧，效果会减半。如果他愚蠢地尝试第三次，不仅达不到预期效果，反而会适得其反，产生相反的效果。

Suppose, for example, you were to write three scenes in a row, all tragic, expecting the audience to cry in all three. What would be the aftereffect of that composition? In the first scene, the audience members may cry; in the second scene they might sniffle; and in the third scene they will laugh their heads off. Not because the third scene isn’t sad; it may be the most tragic of all. But because you have drained them of their tears, they feel it’s ludicrous and insensitive of you to think they’ll cry a third time, so they flip tragedy into comedy. The law of diminishing returns (true in life as it is in art) applies to all storytelling forms and contents—desires and conflicts, moods and emotions, images and actions, words and phrases.

例如，假设你连续写三个场景，每个场景都是悲剧，并期望观众在三个场景中都哭泣。这样的作品会产生什么效果呢？在第一幕中，观众可能会哭；在第二幕中，他们可能会抽泣；而在第三幕中，他们会捧腹大笑。这并非因为第三幕不悲伤；它或许是所有场景中最悲惨的。而是因为你已经榨干了他们的眼泪，他们觉得你指望他们第三次哭泣是荒谬且不体贴的，所以他们把悲剧转化成了喜剧。边际效益递减规律（在生活中和艺术中都适用）适用于所有叙事形式和内容——欲望和冲突、情绪和情感、意象和行动、词语和短语。

Repetitious beats notoriously plague first drafts. Why? Because in the early going, the writer is still searching for the succinct, character-specific language that would nail each action/reaction with a single stroke of speech/reply. Instead, he repeats the same beat in different words, thinking he can substitute quantity for quality, deceiving himself with the belief that repetition reinforces meaning. In fact, it does the opposite. Repetition trivializes meaning.

重复的句式是初稿中常见的弊病。为什么呢？因为在写作初期，作者仍在苦苦寻找简洁精炼、贴合人物性格的语言，力求用寥寥数语便能精准地表达每一个动作或反应。然而，他们却用不同的词语重复同样的句式，以为数量可以代替质量，自欺欺人地认为重复能够强化意义。事实上，重复恰恰相反。它会使意义变得肤浅。

So, what to do?

那么，该怎么办？

Never compromise. Fine writers scour their knowledge and imagination until they find the perfect choice. They write draft after draft, constantly improvising, playing one line against another, tossing lines around in their imagination, mouthing them out, and then, writing them down.

绝不妥协。优秀的作家会竭尽所能，挖掘自身的知识和想象力，直到找到最完美的表达。他们一遍又一遍地修改，不断即兴发挥，反复推敲每一句台词，在脑海中反复琢磨，反复练习，最后才将它们记录下来。

Gazing out the window daydreaming is not creativity. Aesthetic choices only come alive on paper. No matter how banal a line may be, write it down. Write down every choice that passes through your imagination. Do not wait for the moment your genius decides to wake up and give you a gift. Make the perfect choice by continuously moving your thoughts out of your brain and into the real world of the page. That’s writing.

望着窗外发呆并非创造力。唯有在纸上，美的选择才能鲜活起来。无论多么平庸的句子，都要写下来。写下你脑海中闪过的每一个念头。不要等待灵感乍现，才肯给你一份礼物。要不断地将思绪从大脑转移到纸上，做出完美的选择。这才是写作。

But even the most experienced writers will hit a wall as they stare at a beat and realize that for this particular action/reaction in this particular scene, no perfect choice exists. They do what they must. They stop banging their head against the keyboard and make a decision.

但即使是最有经验的编剧，也会遇到瓶颈，盯着某个情节，意识到在这个特定的场景中，对于这个特定的动作/反应，并不存在完美的选择。他们只能尽力而为。他们不再敲击键盘，而是做出决定。

They go back and look through all the imperfect choices they wrote down. They ask, “Which of all of these possible choices is the best? Could there be a combination of imperfect choices that’s better than any one choice?”

他们会回过头来，仔细查看之前写下的所有不完美的选择。他们会问：“在所有这些可能的选项中，哪个才是最好的？是否存在某种不完美选项的组合，比任何一个单独的选项都更好？”

The final choice may not be ideal, but it is the one that comes closest to perfection. They will live with it today and hope that in some future draft, they will find an even better choice. But for the moment, at least, they’ve pruned their repetitious bramble.

最终的选择或许并非完美，但却是最接近完美的。他们目前只能接受这个结果，并希望在未来的选秀中能找到更好的选择。但至少就目前而言，他们已经修剪掉了那些重复的枝节。

MISSHAPEN LINES

意外事故

Ideally, every line of dialogue is so perfectly worded, it fits its character in the moment and makes the immediate sense its author intended. Misshapen lines are like trip wires strung across a scene’s path. They force confused readers and audiences to reread, rewind, or ask the person in the next seat, “What did he say?” I can think of three primary reasons that the wording of a line fails to instantly express itself: blurred meaning, mistimed meaning, and mistimed cues.

理想情况下，每一句台词都措辞完美，既贴合人物当时的语境，又能立刻传达作者想要表达的意思。而那些措辞不当的台词就像是横亘在场景中的绊线，迫使读者和观众反复阅读、倒带，或者询问邻座：“他刚才说了什么？” 我认为台词表达不清晰主要有三个原因：含义模糊、时机不当以及与上下文不符。

Blurred Meaning

模糊的含义

Nouns name objects; verbs name actions. The amplitude of nouns and verbs ranges from the universal to the concrete, from the generic to the specific. As a general rule, specific nouns and verbs tend to sharpen meaning, while generic nouns and verbs modified by adjectives and adverbs tend to blur meaning.

名词指称物体；动词指称动作。名词和动词的表达范围从普遍到具体，从通用到特指。一般来说，特指的名词和动词往往能使意义更加明确，而由形容词和副词修饰的通用名词和动词则往往会使意义变得模糊。

Imagine writing a scene set in a shipyard. As a deckhand struggles to repair a sailboat’s mast step, a boatsmith looks over his shoulder and offers advice. Which of these two lines conveys its meaning with instant clarity: “Forcefully utilize a big nail” or “Hammer a spike”?

想象一下，你正在写一个以造船厂为背景的场景。一名水手正费力地修理帆船的桅杆底座，一位船匠从他身后探过头来，给了他一些建议。以下哪句话能更清晰地表达其含义：“用力钉入一根大钉子”还是“用锤子敲入一根尖钉”？

The second, of course. The first not only seems unnaturally formal, but it also forces the reader/audience to rethink the meaning because the word “nail” covers many dozens of sharp-pointed fasteners, the adjective “big” could be anything over a couple of inches, “utilize” is as vague a verb as any in the language, and the adverb “forcefully” seems unnecessary. As a result, the first line needs two or three mental passes to make sense.

当然是第二个。第一个不仅显得过于正式，而且迫使读者/听众重新思考其含义，因为“nail”一词涵盖了数十种尖锐的紧固件，“big”这个形容词可以指任何超过几英寸的东西，“utilize”是语言中最模糊的动词之一，“forcefully”这个副词似乎没有必要。因此，第一行需要反复思考两三遍才能理解其含义。

The lesson is this: Lines of dialogue that name specific objects and actions tend to express immediate understanding in clear, vivid images. Therefore, unless you intend ambiguous or mysterious qualities, avoid generic nouns and verbs strung with adjectives and adverbs.

由此可见，使用具体事物和动作的对话往往能以清晰生动的画面迅速传达含义。因此，除非你想表达含糊不清或神秘莫测的意味，否则应避免使用泛指的名词和动词，并搭配形容词和副词。

Mistimed Meaning

时机不当的含义

The instant a speech makes sense, its reader or audience absorbs the line’s action and leaps ahead to witness the reaction from the other side of the scene. Lines that mistime their meaning disrupt this action/reaction rhythm. Break interest frequently enough, and readers will toss your book; TV viewers will change channels, theatre audiences will leave at intermission. Therefore, before you send your writing into the world, reread the dialogue carefully, act out speeches if necessary, study each line, and listen for the precise moment of meaning.

当一段台词恰到好处时，读者或听众便能领会其背后的意义，并迅速跳到场景另一侧，观察其后续反应。如果台词的时机把握不当，就会破坏这种行动/反应的节奏。如果频繁出现令人分心的情况，读者会扔掉你的书；电视观众会换台；剧院观众会在中场休息时离场。因此，在将你的作品公之于众之前，务必仔细重读对话，必要时甚至要表演台词，仔细推敲每一句，并聆听其意义的精准表达。

Too late: When a speech drones on word after word without getting to its point, the reader/audience has one of two reactions: Either they lose patience and skip over the point, or they guess the point long before it arrives, and then sit in boredom as the speech stumbles to an anticlimax.

为时已晚：当演讲冗长乏味，一言不发却始终没有切入主题时，读者/听众有两种反应：要么失去耐心，直接跳过主题；要么在主题出现之前就猜到，然后无聊地坐着，看着演讲草草收场，最终以虎头蛇尾的结局告终。

Too soon: When a speech begins with its meaning and then rattles on, interest quickly wanes. Readers skim over the words that follow; audiences tune out.

为时过早：如果演讲一开始就阐述意义，然后喋喋不休，听众的兴趣很快就会消退。读者会略读后面的内容；听众也会走神。

To skillfully time the meaning of each line, follow the guiding principles we previously covered: economy and design. 1) Say the maximum in the fewest words. 2) Master the three basic sentence designs—cumulative, balanced, suspense—so you can place meaning wherever you think best: beginning, middle, or end.

为了巧妙地把握每句话的含义，请遵循我们之前讨论过的指导原则：简洁和结构化。1）用最少的文字表达最多的信息。2）掌握三种基本的句式结构——递进式、平衡式和悬念式——这样你就可以根据自己的判断，将含义放在最合适的位置：开头、中间或结尾。

Mistimed Cues

时机把握不当

A scene finds its natural rhythm of action/reaction in the give-and-take of meaning. Until a character has some sense of what was just said, of what just happened, he waits in limbo. But the instant Character A senses (or thinks he senses) what Character B is saying or doing, he reacts. Although most reactions seem instinctive, spontaneous, and instantaneous, they are in fact triggered by a glimpse of meaning. Character A may completely misinterpret the moment and overreact, underreact, or react off-the-wall. Nonetheless, his reaction, indeed every reaction, needs an action to prompt it.

场景的自然节奏源于意义的互动与传递。在角色理解刚才所说的话、刚才发生的事情之前，他会处于一种悬而未决的状态。但一旦角色A感知到（或自认为感知到）角色B的言行，他就会立即做出反应。虽然大多数反应看似本能、自发且瞬间发生，但实际上它们是由对意义的顿悟触发的。角色A可能完全误解了当下，做出过激反应、反应不足，或者做出匪夷所思的反应。然而，他的反应，实际上每一个反应，都需要一个行动作为触发因素。

Therefore, ideally, the last word or phrase of each speech is the core word that seals meaning and cues a reaction from the other side of the scene. On page, mistiming the core word is a relatively minor problem, but in the theatre or on a soundstage, it can break scenic rhythm and ruin performances.

因此，理想情况下，每段台词的最后一个词或短语应该是核心词，它能概括台词的含义，并引发场景另一侧的反应。在剧本中，核心词的时机把握不当问题相对较小，但在剧院或录音棚里，这会破坏舞台节奏，毁掉演出。

A miscue happens when a core word is placed too early in Character A’s line and prompts a reaction from Character B, but because Character A has more words to recite, Actor B must swallow her response and wait while Actor A finishes performing his speech.

当角色 A 的台词中一个核心词出现得太早，导致角色 B 做出反应，但由于角色 A 还有更多台词要念，演员 B 不得不忍住不回应，等待演员 A 完成他的台词时，就会发生失误。

To make cueing technique clear, let’s work with this passage adapted from Act 1, Scene 5 of John Pielmeier’s play Agnes of God .

为了使提示技巧清晰明了，让我们来看一下改编自约翰·皮尔迈尔戏剧《上帝的羔羊》第一幕第五场的这段文字。

Sister Agnes, a young nun, has given birth inside a convent. The newborn’s dead body was found in a wastepaper basket next to Agnes’s blood-soaked bed. Agnes claims to be a virgin. Some weeks prior to Agnes’s giving birth, a hole appeared in the palm of Agnes’s hand. The convent’s Mother Superior wants to believe that these events are the work of God.

年轻的修女艾格尼丝在修道院里生下了一个孩子。新生儿的尸体在艾格尼丝血迹斑斑的床边的废纸篓里被发现。艾格尼丝自称是处女。在她分娩前几周，她的手掌上出现了一个洞。修道院院长希望这一切都是上帝的旨意。

The police suspect that Agnes committed neonaticide, and so the court has appointed Dr. Martha Livingston, a psychiatrist, to determine Agnes’s sanity. After examining Agnes, the doctor and Mother Superior talk.

警方怀疑艾格尼丝犯有杀害新生儿罪，因此法院指派精神病学家玛莎·利文斯顿博士鉴定艾格尼丝的精神状态。医生检查完艾格尼丝后，与修女院长进行了交谈。

As you read this passage, notice how the line structure places the core word or phrase at or near the end of speeches. This technique creates crisp cueing and a well-paced rhythm of action/reaction:

阅读这段文字时，请注意其句式结构是如何将核心词语或短语置于句末或接近句末的。这种技巧能够营造清晰的提示和流畅的节奏感：

MOTHER SUPERIOR: Look, I know what you’re thinking. She’s an hysteric, pure and simple .

院长：我知道你在想什么。她就是个歇斯底里的人，彻头彻尾的歇斯底里症患者。

DOCTOR LIVINGSTON: Not simple, no .

利文斯顿医生：没那么简单。

MOTHER: I saw the hole. Clean through the palm of her hand. Do you think hysteria did that?

母亲：我看到了那个洞。直接穿透了她的手掌。你觉得是歇斯底里造成的吗？

DOCTOR: It’s been doing it for centuries—she’s not unique, you know. She’s just another victim .

医生：这种情况已经持续了几个世纪——她并不特殊，你知道吗？她只是另一个受害者。

MOTHER: Yes, God’s victim. That’s her innocence. She belongs to God .

母亲：是的，她是上帝的受害者。这就是她的清白。她属于上帝。

DOCTOR: And I mean to take her away from Him. Isn’t that what you fear ?

医生：我的意思是把她从他身边带走。这不正是你所担心的吗？

MOTHER: You bet I do .

母亲：当然愿意。

DOCTOR: Well, I prefer to look upon it as opening her mind, so she can begin to heal .

医生：嗯，我更愿意把它看作是打开她的心扉，这样她就可以开始康复了。

MOTHER: But that’s not your job, is it? You’re here to diagnose, not to heal .

母亲：但那不是你的工作，对吧？你是来诊断的，不是来治病的。

DOCTOR: I’m here to help her in whatever way I see fit. That’s my duty as a doctor .

医生：我来这里是为了尽我所能帮助她。这是我作为医生的职责。

MOTHER: But not as an employee of the court. You’re here to make a decision on her sanity as quickly as possible .

母亲：但你不是以法院雇员的身份来做这件事的。你来这里是为了尽快对她的精神状态做出判断。

DOCTOR: Not as possible. As quickly as I see fit .

医生：并非越快越好。我会尽快安排。

MOTHER: The kindest thing you can do for Agnes is to make that decision and let her go .

母亲：你能为艾格尼丝做的最仁慈的事就是做出那个决定，让她走吧。

DOCTOR: And what then? If I say she’s crazy, she goes to an institution. If I say she’s sane, she goes to prison .

医生：那又怎样？如果我说她疯了，她就被送进精神病院。如果我说她神志清醒，她就被送进监狱。

Now, I’ll rephrase the lines and move their core words back into the middle of each speech. Notice how the overall meanings stay more or less the same, but the cueing stumbles, the actions/reactions seem to spasm, and the scene staggers along.

现在，我会重新组织这些台词，并将它们的核心词语移回每段独白的中间部分。请注意，整体含义基本保持不变，但提示语却显得生硬，动作/反应似乎有些痉挛，整个场景也显得步履蹒跚。

MOTHER: Look, she’s an hysteric, pure and simple . I know what you’re thinking.

母亲：你看，她就是个歇斯底里的人，就这么简单。我知道你在想什么。

DOCTOR: No , not simple.

医生：不，没那么简单。

MOTHER: Clean through the palm of her hand. Do you think hysteria did that? I saw the hole.

母亲：她手掌上全是洞。你觉得是歇斯底里造成的吗？我看到了那个洞。

DOCTOR: It’s been doing it for centuries. She’s just another victim. She’s not unique, you know.

医生：这种情况已经持续了几个世纪。她只是另一个受害者。她并不特殊，你知道吗？

MOTHER: Yes, she belongs to God . God’s victim. That’s her innocence.

母亲：是的，她属于上帝。上帝的受害者。这就是她的清白。

DOCTOR: Is that what you fear ? That I mean to take her away from Him?

医生：你害怕的就是这个吗？害怕我会把她从他身边带走？

MOTHER: I do , you bet.

母亲：当然愿意。

DOCTOR: Well, opening her mind, so she can begin to heal , is how I prefer to look upon it.

医生：嗯，我更倾向于这样看待这件事：打开她的心扉，让她开始康复。

MOTHER: You’re not here to heal but to diagnose. That’s your job, isn’t it?

母亲：你来这里不是为了治病，而是为了诊断。那是你的工作，不是吗？

DOCTOR: My duty as a doctor is to help her in whatever way I see fit.

医生：作为一名医生，我的职责就是尽我所能帮助她。

MOTHER: You’re here to make a decision on her sanity as quickly as possible as an employee of the court.

母亲：作为法院工作人员，你的任务是尽快对她的精神状态做出决定。

DOCTOR: As quickly as I see fit . Not as possible.

医生：我会尽快处理，但不是最快。

MOTHER: Make that decision and let her go . That’s the kindest thing you can do for Agnes.

母亲：做决定吧，放她走。这是你能为艾格尼丝做的最仁慈的事。

DOCTOR: And what then? She goes to prison if I say she’s sane. She goes to an institution if I say she’s crazy.

医生：那又怎样？如果我说她精神正常，她就去坐牢；如果我说她精神失常，她就去精神病院。

When actors encounter scenes of this kind, one of three things will happen: Actors will cut off each other’s lines, talk over each other, or phony up their performance by politely and unnaturally waiting for each speech to end. None of these options solves the problem of mistimed cues.

当演员遇到这类场景时，通常会出现以下三种情况之一：演员会打断对方的台词，互相抢话，或者为了表演效果而装腔作势，礼貌而又不自然地等待对方说完。但这些方法都无法解决提示时机不准的问题。

Generally, speeches that end with cumulative sentences cause miscues. Before your scenes reach performance, act them aloud into a recorder and listen for the core words. Then go through the lines again, this time with a highlighter, and mark the core words, paying special attention to the last sentence of each speech. You will see that some phrases, especially prepositional phrases, tend to float to the ends of lines (just as they did in my last sentence). If so, cut or rephrase so that each speech ends on its cue.

一般来说，以累积句结尾的台词容易导致失误。在正式演出前，对着录音机大声朗读一遍，并仔细聆听关键词。然后再次通读台词，这次用荧光笔标记关键词，尤其要注意每段台词的最后一句。你会发现有些短语，特别是介词短语，往往会拖到句末（就像我最后一句那样）。如果是这样，就删减或改写，确保每段台词都能在提示点结束。

MISSHAPEN SCENES

意外事故场景

Faulty designs may also infect scenes. Like a misshapen line that mistimes its core word, a misshapen scene can mistime its turning point, bringing it in too soon or too late or not at all. A well-shaped scene pivots around its turning point in just the right way at just the right moment. From story to story, the “right” moment for any scene’s turning point is unpredictable and idiosyncratic. Nonetheless, when timing misfires, the reader/audience feels it.

糟糕的设计也会影响场景。就像一条变形的线条错位了核心词语的表达一样，一个结构糟糕的场景也会错失转折点，要么过早出现，要么过晚出现，甚至根本没有转折点。一个结构精良的场景，会在恰当的时机，以恰当的方式围绕转折点展开。每个故事中，场景转折点的“恰当”时机都是不可预测且因故事而异的。然而，一旦时机把握不当，读者/观众都会有所察觉。

Too soon:

为时尚早：

The first beat powerfully jolts the scene around its turning point. But from that moment on, the scene runs anticlimactically downhill as characters pour out exposition.

第一个音符强劲有力地将剧情推向转折点。但从那一刻起，随着角色们喋喋不休地讲述背景信息，剧情便开始虎头蛇尾地下滑。

Example: A scene we’ll call “The Lovers Break Up.”

例如：我们称之为“恋人分手”的场景。

Version 1: In the first beat one lover declares the relationship over; the other agrees. The action/reaction of this immediate turning point swings the value charge of love from positive to negative. A beat of resolution may need to follow, but if the scene goes on and on as the lovers pour out their history, reminiscing about the good times and lamenting the bad, the reader/audience may turn against the scene and its characters, thinking, “You guys are done. Get over it.”

版本一：在第一个转折点，其中一位恋人宣布分手；另一位表示同意。这一突如其来的转折点将爱情的价值从正面转变为负面。之后可能需要一个解决的转折点，但如果场景持续下去，恋人们倾诉过往，回忆美好时光，哀叹痛苦，读者/观众可能会对场景和人物产生反感，心想：“你们俩完了，别再纠缠了。”

Too late:

为时已晚：

Repetitious beats of dialogue prattle on far too long until, sometime after the audience has lost interest, the turning point finally arrives.

重复的对话喋喋不休地持续了太长时间，直到观众失去兴趣之后，转折点才终于到来。

Version 2: Lovers whose relationship has run its course reminisce about the good times and lament the bad until the audience sees the turning point coming long before it arrives. When the lovers finally agree to break up, the unsurprised audience sits there, thinking, “I saw this coming ten minutes ago.”

版本二：一对感情走到尽头的恋人回忆着美好的时光，哀叹着糟糕的过往，直到观众在转折点到来之前很久就预见到了。当这对恋人最终同意分手时，毫无意外的观众坐在那里，心想：“我十分钟前就预料到了。”

Not at all:

一点也不：

Version 3: A couple floating in the doldrums of their relationship reminisce about the good times and lament the bad. They never take an action to either break up or recommit. The value of love is at the same tepid temperature it was when the scene opened. None of the scene’s beats executes a turning point. The beats may zigzag in conflict, but the scene still has no shape, no arc, because the charge of its core value at the end of the scene is exactly what it was at the beginning of the scene. If nothing changes, nothing happens. The scene is a repetitious nonevent, leaving the audience to sit in wonder, asking, “What was the point of all that talk?”

版本三：一对情侣陷入了感情的低谷，他们回忆着美好的时光，哀叹着糟糕的过往。他们既没有分手，也没有重新开始。爱情的价值依然如场景开始时那般温吞。场景的任何转折点都没有出现。尽管情节可能在冲突中起伏，但整个场景仍然没有结构，没有弧线，因为场景结尾的核心价值与开头时完全一样。如果什么都不改变，那就什么都不会发生。这个场景就像一场重复的闹剧，让观众百思不得其解，不禁问道：“这一切到底有什么意义？”

As you compose beats of dialogue, give thought to the scene’s shape. Build it beat by beat, line by line, progressively to and around the turning point, timing that pivotal beat for the perfect moment. You must decide how sharply or gradually a scene progresses. Your judgment guides what’s too soon or too late. Every scene has a life of its own, and you have to feel your way to its ideal shape.

在构思对话节奏时，要考虑场景的整体结构。逐句、逐拍地构建场景，逐步推进，直至转折点，并精准把握关键时刻。你必须决定场景推进的节奏是迅猛还是缓慢。你的判断决定了哪些情节过早或过晚。每个场景都有其独特的生命力，你需要用心去感受，才能找到它最理想的形态。

SPLINTERED SCENES

碎片化的场景

Scenes flow with life when the reader/audience senses a unity between the characters’ inner motivations and outer tactics. No matter how subtle, indirect, or disguised their maneuvers may be, somehow what the characters say and do links back to their underlying desires. Scenes splinter and die for the converse reason: We sense a breakdown between what drives the scene from the subtext and what is said and done on the text, a disconnect between inner intentions and outer behaviors. As a result, the scene strikes us as false.

当读者/观众感受到角色内在动机与外在策略的一致性时，场景便会生动流畅。无论他们的手段多么微妙、间接或隐晦，他们的言行最终都与他们内心深处的渴望息息相关。场景之所以支离破碎、索然无味，恰恰相反：我们感受到场景的潜台词驱动力与文本表述的言行之间存在脱节，内在意图与外在行为脱节。结果，场景便会显得虚假做作。

I can think of four reasons that an otherwise promising scene rambles out of joint, and the dialogue seems phony or lifeless: 1) The inner desires are fully motivated, but the dialogue is too bland, and so the scene falls flat. 2) The inner wishes are weakly motivated, but the dialogue is overwrought, and so the scene feels melodramatic. 3) The inner intentions and outer actions seem irrelevant to one another, and so the scene makes no sense and dialogue ricochets into non sequitur. 4) The characters’ desires run side by side, never crossing in conflict. Without conflict, the scene has no turning point and so nothing changes; without change, dialogue thickens with exposition, the scene flattens into a nonevent, and we sit bored at best, confused at worst.

我认为有四种原因会导致原本很有潜力的场景变得支离破碎，对话显得虚假或缺乏生气：1）人物的内心欲望动机充分，但对话过于平淡，导致场景乏味。2）人物的内心愿望动机薄弱，但对话过于矫揉造作，导致场景显得过于戏剧化。3）人物的内心意图和外在行为似乎毫无关联，导致场景逻辑混乱，对话也显得莫名其妙。4）人物的欲望并存，从未发生冲突。没有冲突，场景就没有转折点，也就没有任何变化；没有变化，对话就会变得冗长乏味，场景变得毫无生气，观众充其量感到无聊，最坏的情况则是感到困惑。

The writers of nonevents often try to conceal their ineptitude behind excessive language. Profanity is the common choice. They think that by inserting expletives into tepid dialogue, they raise the dramatic temperature. They would be wrong.

那些写出平庸之作的作家常常试图用冗长的语言掩盖自己的拙劣。粗俗的语言是他们的常用手段。他们认为，在平淡无奇的对话中插入脏话就能提升戏剧张力。但他们错了。

Not, as Seinfeld would remind us, that there’s anything wrong with profanity per se. Certain settings demand profanity. In long-form crime series like DEADWOOD, THE WIRE, or THE SOPRANOS, profanity fits the characters like a silk suit. In fact, when criminals stop swearing, we know they mean business: A silent gangster is a lethal gangster.

正如塞恩菲尔德会提醒我们的那样，脏话本身并没有什么错。某些场景需要脏话。在像《死木》、《火线》或《黑道家族》这样的长篇犯罪剧集中，脏话就像丝绸西装一样与角色完美契合。事实上，当罪犯不再说脏话时，我们就知道他们是来真的了：沉默的黑帮分子才是真正的狠角色。

To reshape a faulty scene, start at either level, subtext or text. You could work from the outside of it by rewriting the line and then backtracking to create an inner action to fit. Or you could work from the inside out by going down into the inner life of your characters and layer by layer rebuild their deep psychologies and desires from the subtext outward into the scene’s actions and reactions, sayings and doings. This process demands hard work and time, but because the inside-out method is more difficult, its successes are more powerful.

要重塑一个有缺陷的场景，可以从两个层面入手：潜台词或文本层面。你可以从外部着手，重写台词，然后回溯并创造一个与之相符的内在动作。或者，你也可以从内部着手，深入角色的内心世界，从潜台词开始，一层层地重建他们深层的心理和欲望，最终将其融入到场景中的动作、反应、言语和行为中。这个过程需要付出艰辛的努力和时间，但正因为这种由内而外的方法更难，所以它带来的成功也更加震撼人心。

THE PARAPHRASING TRAP

释义陷阱

Novice writers want to believe that writing problems are word problems, so when they sense the need to rewrite, they start by paraphrasing faulty dialogue, over and over. The more they rephrase, the more on-the-nose their language becomes, until subtext vanishes and the scene is irredeemably dull and false.

新手写作者往往认为写作问题只是文字问题，所以当他们意识到需要修改时，便开始反复改写错误的对话。他们改写的次数越多，语言就越直白，直到潜台词消失殆尽，场景变得无可救药地乏味虚假。

When scenes fail, the fault is rarely in the words; the solution will be found deep within event and character design. Dialogue problems are story problems.

场景失败时，问题很少出在台词上；解决方法往往深藏于事件和人物设计之中。对话问题就是故事问题。

Parts One and Two mapped out the complexities of dialogue. Part Three takes on the task of imagining and refining dialogue to serve your characters and their story.

第一部分和第二部分阐述了对话的复杂性。第三部分则着重于构思和润色对话，使其更好地服务于你的角色及其故事。

#↩

PART 3

第三部分

CREATING DIALOGUE

创建对话

#↩

10

CHARACTER-SPECIFIC DIALOGUE

角色专属对话

THE TWO TALENTS

两位天才

Creative writing calls on two sources of creativity: story talent and literary talent. Story talent converts daily existence into meaningful, emotionally moving events and characters, then sculpts a work’s inner design—what happens and to whom—to create metaphors for life. Literary talent converts everyday talk into expressive dialogue, then sculpts verbal designs—what’s said and to whom—to create metaphors for talk. These two talents combine to shape scenes.

创意写作依赖于两种创造力来源：故事天赋和文学天赋。故事天赋将日常生活转化为意义深远、感人至深的事件和人物，并精心雕琢作品的内在结构——事件的发生和对象——以此构建人生隐喻。文学天赋则将日常对话转化为富有表现力的对白，并精心雕琢语言结构——话语的内容和对象——以此构建对话的隐喻。这两种天赋相辅相成，共同塑造场景。

Drawing on both talents, fine writers employ an iceberg technique: To drive their story, they submerge the massive content of unspoken thoughts, feelings, desires, and actions out of sight in the subtext of scenes; to tell their story, they create a text of words on the visible tip of character behavior. Let’s step back to the time those voices first spoke.

优秀的作家们巧妙地运用这两种才能，采用冰山叙事技巧：为了推动故事发展，他们将大量未言明的思想、情感、欲望和行为隐藏在场景的潜台词之中；为了讲述故事，他们则在人物行为的表层文字之上，构建出清晰可见的文本。让我们回到这些声音最初响起的那一刻。

Homer, the earliest storyteller we know by name, recited the more than 250,000 words of description and dialogue in the Iliad and the Odyssey from memory. With the invention of the alphabet around 800 BC, his epics were written down and the first dialogue appeared on page. Homer’s characters argue and accuse each other, they recount the past and predict the future, but despite the blind poet’s image-rich rhyming couplets, their speeches tend toward declamations rather than conversations. As a result, although the choices and actions of his characters express their individuality, in dialogue they sound remarkably alike.

荷马，我们所知的最早的著名故事讲述者，凭记忆背诵了《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》中超过25万字的描写和对话。大约公元前800年，随着字母的发明，他的史诗被记录下来，最早的对话也出现在纸面上。荷马笔下的人物争论不休，互相指责，回顾过去，展望未来。尽管这位盲诗人运用了意象丰富的押韵对句，但他们的言辞更倾向于朗诵而非对话。因此，尽管人物的选择和行为展现了各自的个性，但他们的对话听起来却惊人地相似。

In this same period, the first onstage performances were sacred rituals in which choruses sang, danced, and chanted verse stories of gods and heroes. Religious ritual slowly evolved into theatre as the chorus leader stepped forward to become an actor with a distinguishable character. The playwright Aeschylus introduced a second actor and invented the technique of rapid face-to-face exchanges of short speeches known as stichomythia, literally line-talk (from stikho , meaning “line,” and muthos , meaning “talk”). The rhythmic intensity of characters alternating single lines or phrases, combined with quick, biting language, unleashed great dramatic power, as in Aeschylus’s play Agamemnon .

在同一时期，最早的舞台表演是神圣的仪式，合唱队在其中歌唱、舞蹈，吟诵关于神祇和英雄的诗歌故事。随着合唱队领队逐渐成为拥有鲜明角色的演员，宗教仪式也慢慢演变为戏剧。剧作家埃斯库罗斯引入了第二位演员，并发明了一种名为“stichomythia”（字面意思是“逐句对话”，源自希腊语“stikho”，意为“线条”，以及“muthos”，意为“对话”）的快速面对面短句对话技巧。角色们交替说出单句或短语，这种节奏鲜明的密集对话，结合快速而犀利的语言，释放出强大的戏剧力量，正如埃斯库罗斯的戏剧《阿伽门农》中所展现的那样。

But it was the introduction of the third actor by Sophocles in plays such as Oedipus Rex , Antigone , and Electra that gave rise to character complexity. Sophocles transformed ancient archetypes such as king, queen, princess, warrior, and messenger into characters with personality, dimensionality, and singular voices. What these first playwrights sensed—and what writers of all story media have understood since—is that the more complex the psychology of a character, the more distinctive his dialogue must become. In other words, originality in character design finds its final expression in character-specific dialogue.

但正是索福克勒斯在《俄狄浦斯王》、《安提戈涅》和《厄勒克特拉》等剧作中引入的第三位演员，才真正带来了人物的复杂性。索福克勒斯将国王、王后、公主、战士和信使等古代原型人物，转化为具有鲜明个性、立体感和独特声音的角色。这些早期剧作家敏锐地意识到——而此后所有叙事媒介的作家都深谙此道——人物的心理越复杂，其对话就必须越独特。换言之，人物设计的独创性最终体现在人物专属的对话之中。

Consider, for example, this exchange between Matthew McConaughey’s Detective Rustin Spencer “Rust” Cohle and Woody Harrelson’s Detective Martin Eric “Marty” Hart from the television series TRUE DETECTIVE. As they watch an old-fashioned tent revival in rural Louisiana, Rust turns to Marty and says:

例如，想想电视剧《真探》中马修·麦康纳饰演的侦探拉斯汀·斯宾塞·“拉斯特”·科尔和伍迪·哈里森饰演的侦探马丁·埃里克·“马蒂”·哈特之间的这段对话。当他们在路易斯安那州乡村观看一场老式的帐篷复兴布道会时，拉斯特转向马蒂说道：

RUST

锈

What do you think is the average IQ of this group, huh?

你觉得这群人的平均智商是多少？

MARTY

马蒂

What do you see up there on your high horse? What do you know about these people?

你高高在上，看到了什么？你对这些人了解多少？

RUST

锈

Just observations and deduction: I see a propensity for obesity, poverty, a yen for fairy tales. Folks putting what few bucks they do have in a little wicker basket that’s being passed around. I think it’s safe to say nobody here’s gonna be splitting the atom, Marty.

只是观察和推断：我发现这里肥胖、贫困的倾向比较明显，人们还喜欢童话故事。大家把仅有的几个小钱放进一个柳条篮子里，然后挨个传递。我想可以肯定地说，这里没人能做出原子裂变之类的壮举，马蒂。

MARTY

马蒂

You see that? Your fucking attitude. Not everybody wants to sit alone in an empty room beating off to murder manuals. Some folks enjoy community, the common good.

你看到了吗？你这该死的态度。不是每个人都想独自一人待在空荡荡的房间里对着杀人手册撸管。有些人喜欢群体生活，喜欢共同利益。

RUST

锈

If the common good’s got to make up fairy tales, then it’s not good for anybody.

如果为了公共利益而编造童话故事，那对谁都没有好处。

The scene focuses the Rust/Marty conflict through a trialogue. In this scene the revivalist congregation becomes the third thing, allowing word choices to distinguish Rust from Marty in two ways: First, their conflicting attitudes toward the congregation. Rust feels contempt, Marty compassion. Rust criticizes them; Marty forgives. Second, Rust’s logical intellectualizations versus Marty’s emotional personalizations. Rust keeps his cool; Marty loses his. As a result, Rust’s phrasings run noticeably slower and longer than Marty’s.

这一幕通过三方对话聚焦于拉斯特和马蒂之间的冲突。在这个场景中，复兴运动的信众成为了第三个因素，使得拉斯特和马蒂的用词在两个方面得以区分：首先，他们对信众的态度截然不同。拉斯特感到鄙夷，而马蒂则充满同情。拉斯特批评他们，马蒂则选择原谅。其次，拉斯特的理性分析与马蒂的情感表达形成鲜明对比。拉斯特保持冷静，而马蒂则情绪失控。因此，拉斯特的语速明显比马蒂慢，语调也更长。

Compare these two lines:

比较这两行：

Rust: “Just observations and deduction: I see a propensity for obesity, poverty, a yen for fairy tales.”

拉斯特：“只是观察和推断：我发现人们有肥胖、贫困的倾向，并且喜欢童话故事。”

Marty: “Not everybody wants to sit alone in an empty room beating off to murder manuals.”

马蒂：“不是每个人都想独自坐在空房间里对着谋杀手册撸管。”

Note Rust’s abstract, polysyllabic terms with Latinate suffixes of “-ion” and “-ity” versus Marty’s concrete images in iambs and trochees: “alone,” “empty,” “murder.” Showrunner Nic Pizzolatto’s precise word choices contrast the loner Rust and his need for justice against the gregarious Marty and his need for intimacy.

注意Rust使用的抽象、多音节词汇，以及拉丁语后缀“-ion”和“-ity”，与Marty使用抑扬格和扬抑格的具体意象形成对比，例如“孤独”、“空虚”、“谋杀”。剧集运作人Nic Pizzolatto精准的用词，将孤僻的Rust及其对正义的渴望，与外向的Marty及其对亲密关系的渴求，形成了鲜明的对比。

Crafting idiosyncratic speech, however, does not mean tricking up a role with vocal quirks. A self-conscious stylishness can be like bad acting, the literary equivalent of hamming it up and hogging the spotlight. Panache may impress us, but a true voice affects us. The former calls attention to itself; the latter calls us to life.

然而，塑造独特的语言风格并非指用一些怪癖的嗓音来装点角色。刻意追求华丽的风格就像拙劣的演技，相当于文学界的用力过猛、抢尽风头。华丽的辞藻或许能给我们留下深刻印象，但真正触动人心的声音才能打动我们。前者引人注目，后者则赋予我们生命。

Contemporary writing workshops often stress development of an inimitable presence in language known as “a voice.” To me, this talk seems pointless. A writer’s style or so-called voice cannot be found or created self-consciously. Voice is not a choice; it’s a result.

当代写作工作坊常常强调培养一种独一无二的语言风格，即所谓的“声音”。在我看来，这种说法毫无意义。作家的风格或所谓的“声音”并非刻意寻找或创造的。声音不是一种选择，而是一种结果。

A distinctive writing style pays off when a creative personality embraces a broad and deep knowledge of the human condition. When talent wraps its arms around content, the tumultuous coupling that follows breeds a singular manner of expression. Voice is the instinctive, spontaneous consequence of genius working up a sweat.

当创作者拥有广博而深刻的人性洞察时，独特的写作风格便会脱颖而出。当才华与内容交融，随之而来的碰撞与碰撞，便会孕育出一种独一无二的表达方式。声音，是天才辛勤耕耘后，自然而然、浑然天成的产物。

In other words, as you explore your story’s content of role, meaning, emotion, and action, as you do the hard work that brings life to your characters, you will write as only you would. That, for better or worse, like it or not, will be your voice. And like a painter covering canvas after canvas through decades of toil in search of his vision, your evolution toward a true voice will take time.

换句话说，当你探索故事中的角色、意义、情感和行动等内容，当你辛勤耕耘，赋予角色生命时，你就会用你独有的方式写作。无论好坏，无论你是否喜欢，这都将成为你的声音。就像一位画家历经数十年，在画布上反复涂抹，最终才找到自己的创作方向一样，你逐渐形成真正属于自己的声音也需要时间。

In writing dialogue, the same principle applies. When an original character reaches inside for expression, her voice will be the second-nature consequence of her one-of-a-kind personality, experience, knowledge, locution, and accent. Ideally, a character’s language is so plausible, so seemingly natural, so idiosyncratic that every line in every scene seems to be an improvisation that no one but that specific character in that specific moment would invent.

在对话写作中，同样的原则也适用。当一个原创角色需要表达内心想法时，她的声音会自然而然地流露出她独一无二的个性、经历、知识、措辞和口音。理想情况下，角色的语言应该如此真实可信、如此自然流畅、如此独具特色，以至于每场戏里的每一句台词都像是即兴发挥，只有这个角色在那个特定的时刻才会说出这样的话。

In saying this, I am not advocating difference for the sake of difference. Quirkiness is not originality, and it takes taste to know the difference. The ability to tell a true phrase from a clever phrase does not come easy; if it’s not innate, it must be learned over years of reading and rereading quality novels, while watching and rewatching exceptional television, films, and theatre. As you hone your judgment of story and character, one insight shifts into sharp focus: The foremost facet of dialogue is vocabulary.

我这么说，并非为了标新立异而标新立异。古怪并不等同于原创，而辨别二者的区别需要一定的鉴赏力。区分真词和巧语并非易事；即便不是与生俱来，也需要通过多年反复阅读优秀小说，以及反复观看杰出的电视、电影和戏剧作品来习得。随着你对故事和人物的鉴赏能力不断提升，一个重要的洞见会逐渐清晰：对话最重要的要素是词汇。

Dramatized storytelling is not about words but characters using words as they struggle through life. All components of speech from grammar to phrasing to pace are therefore vital to dialogue. But nothing conveys or betrays personality as much as a character’s choice of words, the names of the things that live within him.

戏剧化的叙事并非仅仅关乎文字本身，而是关乎角色在人生旅途中如何运用文字。因此，从语法、措辞到语速，语言的各个组成部分对对话都至关重要。然而，没有什么比角色对文字的选择，以及他们如何称呼内心世界更能传达或暴露人物性格了。

VOCABULARY AND CHARACTERIZATION

词汇和人物刻画

As noted in previous chapters, nouns name objects and verbs name actions. A character’s vocabulary names what he knows, what he sees, and what he feels. His choice of words is all-important because a character’s façade of talk should be a doorway to his depths. Passive, blurry, generic phrases flatten a character and numb the audience; active, concrete, sensory language arouses insights that weave dimension and complexity into a character.

如前几章所述，名词指代物体，动词指代动作。人物的词汇表达了他所知、所见、所感。他选择用词至关重要，因为人物的言谈举止应当是通往其内心世界的窗口。被动、模糊、泛泛的表达会使人物形象扁平化，令观众麻木；而主动、具体、富有感官体验的语言则能激发观众的洞察力，赋予人物立体感和复杂性。

To create a brilliant surface of talk that leads the audience into a character’s depths, your method must move in the reverse direction: Start within your character, and then work outward from content to form to effect.

要创造出引人入胜的对话，引导观众深入了解角色的内心世界，你的方法必须反其道而行之：从角色内部入手，然后从内容到形式再到效果，逐步展开。

First, draw on your sensory and visual powers to imagine content (what your character sees and feels on the inscape, the unsaid and unsayable), then craft his dialogue (the said) into a form that slips his words into the reader’s or audience’s ear with effect. In essence, you must transform the images in your character’s inner life into the verbiage of his outer talk.

首先，运用你的感官和视觉能力来想象内容（你的角色在内心世界中看到和感受到的东西，那些未说出口和不可言说的），然后精心构思他的对话（已说出口的内容），使之能够有效地将他的话语传递到读者或观众的耳中。本质上，你必须将角色内心世界的意象转化为他外在言语中的表达。

THE PRINCIPLE OF CREATIVE LIMITATION

创造力限制原则
