The tougher the technique, the more brilliant the feat.

技术难度越高，成就就越辉煌。

Constraint, discipline, and limitation inspire stunning creative achievement; unrestrained freedom, on the other hand, usually ends in a sprawl. If you take an easy, undisciplined path that makes little claim on your talent, the results smudge with paint-by-numbers banality. But if, contrarily, you choose an arduous technique that demands a master’s proficiency, then talent builds muscle until your imagination, strained to the tearing point, explodes with power.

约束、纪律和限制能激发惊人的创造力；相反，不受约束的自由往往会导致作品杂乱无章。如果你选择一条轻松、缺乏纪律的道路，这条路无法充分发挥你的才能，那么最终的结果只会沦为平庸乏味的填色游戏。但相反，如果你选择一种需要大师级技艺的艰辛方法，那么你的才能就会不断积累，直到你的想象力被推向极限，迸发出惊人的力量。

The great difficulties imposed by creative limitations are why a Beethoven symphony transcends whistling. Why Whistler’s Mother surpasses a doodle. Why a high school prom is not the Bolshoi.

正是由于创作上的局限，贝多芬的交响曲才超越了口哨，惠斯勒的《母亲》才超越了涂鸦，高中毕业舞会才不是莫斯科大剧院的演出。

The strategy of surrounding yourself with aesthetic obstacles to compel creative excellence begins by pitting language against image. Language is the medium of conscious thought; image is the medium of subconscious thought. Therefore, writing the first banal phrases that pop to mind is far easier than expressing character in lucid, three-dimensional imagery found in the far reaches of your imagination. When you write off the top of your head, all characters sound alike and the sounds they make irritate like fingernails on a blackboard. Their grating voices fake life and then fill the sham with irredeemably false dialogue—out of character, out of scene, void of feeling, void of truth.

用审美障碍来激发卓越创造力的策略，始于语言与图像的对抗。语言是意识思维的媒介，图像是潜意识思维的媒介。因此，写下脑海中浮现的第一个平庸词句，远比用清晰、立体的意象来描绘人物形象容易得多，而这些意象往往来自你想象力的深处。当你凭空想象写作时，所有人物听起来都千篇一律，他们发出的声音如同指甲刮黑板般刺耳难听。他们生硬的声音虚假地塑造着生命，然后用无可救药的虚假对话填充这虚假的世界——脱离人物性格，脱离场景，缺乏情感，缺乏真实感。

Dialogue takes work. Compare the effort to bring someone to mind with words (“my cousin Judy”) to the task of first conjuring up a glowing image of your cousin—her Alice-blue eyes, and the almost Asian shape they take when she smiles—then holding her living picture before your mind while you rummage through your vocabulary, searching for the perfect words to make your vision of Judy shine in the minds of your readers. Writing vividly for the outer eye and ear of a spectator or for the inner eye and ear of a reader demands fierce concentration.

对话的写作需要花费心思。试想一下，用文字勾勒出某人的形象（“我的表妹朱迪”）和先在脑海中勾勒出她鲜活的形象——她那双如爱丽丝般湛蓝的眼睛，以及她微笑时那略带亚洲风情的眼型——然后一边努力回忆，一边在脑海中反复斟酌词汇，寻找最恰当的词语，让读者也能感受到朱迪的神韵。无论是为旁观者生动地描绘画面，还是为读者营造身临其境的感受，都需要高度集中精力。

The language-bound art of writing aims its effects at the mental cortex that deciphers words. To tell a story in pure image runs contrary to writing’s psycholinguistic nature. Therefore, the masters of page, stage, and screen dedicate their lives to doing exactly that. They choose the strenuous, indeed, next-to-impossible technique. To inspire excellence, to create an insightful, original telling, the dedicated writer condemns himself to chain-gang labor, a long dig down the back roads of the unconscious in search of vigorous, deep-image language.

写作这门语言艺术，其作用直指解读文字的大脑皮层。纯粹用图像来讲述故事，与写作的心理语言学本质背道而驰。因此，文字、舞台和银幕上的大师们毕生致力于此。他们选择了艰辛的、近乎不可能的技法。为了激发卓越，创造出深刻而独到的叙事，执着的作家甘愿苦读，在潜意识深处的幽暗小径上进行漫长的挖掘，以寻找充满活力、意蕴深远的语言。

Sensory dialogue resonates with the speaker’s inner life. Specific, vivid, image-rich language leads the reader/audience to the character’s subtext of hidden, unconscious thoughts and feelings. As a result, when such characters take verbal actions in pursuit of their desires, they become transparent and we can know them in depth. But when characters sound like a business report—generic, literal, Latinate, polysyllabic—their language flattens the action and diminishes the scene’s inner life. The more opaque the characters become, the more we lose interest. Therefore, even if a character is in fact a bore, his dialogue must express his lifeless soul with vivid dreariness.

感官对话与说话者的内心世界产生共鸣。具体、生动、意象丰富的语言引导读者/观众深入角色隐藏的、无意识的想法和感受。因此，当这样的角色通过言语行动来追求自己的欲望时，他们便变得透明，我们可以深入了解他们。但如果角色的语言听起来像商业报告——空泛、生硬、拉丁化、多音节——那么他们的语言就会使情节变得平淡，削弱场景的内在生命力。角色越是晦涩难懂，我们就越容易失去兴趣。因此，即使一个角色本身乏味无趣，他的对话也必须生动地展现出他死气沉沉的灵魂。

LOCUTION AND CHARACTERIZATION

措辞与人物刻画

Character-specific locutions depend on both sides of a sentence, subject and predicate. Subject (what or whom the sentence is about) and predicate (something about the subject) combine to create a line of dialogue that helps express two primary dimensions of characterization: knowledge and personality. One aspect of the line tends to convey the former, and the other, the latter.

人物特有的言辞取决于句子的主体和谓语。主体（句子描述的对象或人物）和谓语（关于主体的信息）共同构成一句对话，有助于展现人物性格的两个主要维度：知识和个性。对话的某一部分侧重于传达前者，另一部分则侧重于传达后者。

Although characterization can be expressed through dialogue in a variety of ways, a character’s knowledge tends to be expressed in the names of things, nouns and verbs, while a character’s personality tends to be expressed in the modifiers that color those nouns and verbs.

虽然人物刻画可以通过对话以多种方式表达，但人物的知识往往通过事物的名称、名词和动词来表达，而人物的个性则往往通过修饰这些名词和动词的修饰语来表达。

Knowledge. If a character uses a vague phrase such as “a big nail,” we sense that his knowledge of carpentry is limited. Generic nouns suggest ignorance. But if he names the thing—“shank,” “clout,” “spike,” “corker,” “sinker”—we sense a much fuller knowledge.

知识。如果一个角色使用像“大钉子”这样模糊的短语，我们会觉得他对木工的了解有限。泛指的名词暗示着无知。但如果他能具体指出钉子的名称——“柄”、“杆”、“尖头”、“软木塞”、“沉子”——我们就能感受到他掌握了更全面的知识。

The same principle applies to verbs. Core verbs (as opposed to modal verbs) span from generic to specific. If a character remembers that someone “moved slowly across the room,” we sense that his recall is dull. Generic verbs also suggest ignorance. But if his dialogue sharpens and he says that another man “sauntered,” “waltzed,” “padded,” “slouched,” “moseyed,” “pranced,” or “dragged himself” across the room, his choice of verb suggests a vivid memory and insight into the other man. Specific names of objects and actions convey a superior mentality.

同样的原则也适用于动词。核心动词（与情态动词相对）涵盖了从泛指到特指的各个层面。如果一个角色记得某人“慢慢地穿过房间”，我们会觉得他的记忆力很差。泛指动词也暗示着无知。但如果他的对话变得生动起来，他说另一个人“闲庭信步”、“轻快地走”、“踱步”、“懒散地走”、“踱步”、“轻快地走”或“拖着身子”穿过房间，那么他选择的动词就表明他对那个人有着清晰的记忆和深刻的洞察力。对物体和动作进行具体的描述，则体现了一种更胜一筹的思维方式。

Personality. The idiosyncratic by-products of a character’s life experience—his beliefs, his attitudes, his individuality—are chiefly expressed through modifiers.

个性。人物生活经历的独特副产品——他的信仰、态度、个性——主要通过修饰语来表达。

First, adjectives. Two characters look at a fireworks display. One describes it as “big” and the other as “stupendous.” These are two very different personalities.

首先，我们来看形容词。两个人在看烟花表演。一个形容它“盛大”，另一个形容它“壮观”。这两个人的性格截然不同。

Second, adverbs. Two characters watch a motorcycle go by. One says it was going “ferociously” and the other says it was moving “quickly.” Again, two very different people.

其次，是副词。两个人看着一辆摩托车驶过。一个人说它“飞驰而过”，另一个人说它“快速地”行驶着。这又是两个人截然不同的感受。

Third, voice. Core verbs also span the spectrum that runs from active to passive. In active sentences, the thing doing the action is the subject, and the thing receiving the action is the object. Passive sentences reverse this so that the object becomes the subject. As a result, someone who tends to use phrases such as “The family planned the wedding” (active) versus someone who would remember the event as “The wedding was planned by the family” (passive) have two very different feelings about how things work in life, two very different temperaments.

第三，语态。核心动词也涵盖了从主动到被动的整个语态谱系。在主动句中，执行动作的是主语，接受动作的是宾语。被动句则相反，宾语变成了主语。因此，倾向于使用“家人策划了婚礼”（主动语态）这类表达的人，与会记住“婚礼是由家人策划的”（被动语态）这类表达的人，对生活运作方式有着截然不同的感受，也体现了两种截然不同的性格。

Fourth, modals. Modal verbs (could, can, may, might, must, ought, shall, should, will, would) attach to core verbs to add qualities of modality: ability, possibility, obligation, permission, and the like. Modal phrases convey:

第四，情态动词。情态动词（could、can、may、might、must、ought、shall、should、will、would）附加在动词上，表示情态含义：能力、可能性、义务、许可等等。情态短语表达：

1. A character’s sense of self and the world around him.

1. 人物的自我认知和对周围世界的认知。

2. His feelings for his place in society and the interplay of relationships.

2. 他对自己在社会中的地位以及人际关系的感受。

3. His view to the past, present, and future.

3. 他对过去、现在和未来的看法。

4. His attitudes toward what is possible, what is permitted, and what is necessary.

4. 他对什么是可能的、什么是允许的、什么是必要的态度。

Someone who says “The family could plan the wedding” versus someone who insists “All weddings must be planned by families” are probably two very different personalities.

认为“婚礼可以由家人来筹办”的人和坚持“所有婚礼都必须由家人来筹办”的人，很可能是两种截然不同的性格。

PRINCIPLE OF CHARACTER-SPECIFIC DIALOGUE

角色特定对话原则

Nouns and verbs express a character’s intellectual life and range of knowledge. Modifiers (adjectives, adverbs, voice, modalities) express his emotional life and personality.

名词和动词表达人物的智力生活和知识广度。修饰语（形容词、副词、语态、情态）表达人物的情感生活和个性。

To figure out how your character’s personality expresses itself, ask: “How does my character see life? Passive? Active? How does my character modify subjects and especially predicates?” Before your fingers hit the keys, constantly ask: “What words, phrases, and images would make my character’s dialogue his alone? What in the psyche, life experience, and education of my character will express the content of his knowledge (names of nouns and verbs) and the one-of-a-kind mannerisms of his personality (modifiers and modalities)?”

为了弄清楚你的角色是如何展现个性的，问问自己：“我的角色是如何看待生活的？被动的？主动的？我的角色是如何修饰主语，尤其是谓语的？” 在你敲击键盘之前，不断问自己：“哪些词语、短语和意象能使我的角色的对话独具特色？我的角色的心理、生活经历和教育背景中，哪些因素能够表达他所掌握的知识（名词和动词的名称）以及他独一无二的个性特征（修饰语和情态动词）？”

CULTURE AND CHARACTERIZATION

文化与特征

To answer these questions, consider this: Through the totality of your character’s living hours, awake and sleeping, his or her mind, conscious and unconscious, has absorbed an immense and character-specific volume of culture: a combination of language, family, society, art, sport, religion, and the like.

要回答这些问题，请考虑以下情况：在你的角色所有清醒和睡眠的时间里，他或她的思想，有意识的和无意识的，都吸收了大量与角色相关的文化：语言、家庭、社会、艺术、体育、宗教等等的组合。

Year after year, life’s events have hurt, rewarded, and influenced your character in countless ways. Into this sea of customs and encounters, the character has mixed the dispositions and physical givens he or she was handed at birth: attractive/plain, healthy/ailing, aggressive/shy, high IQ/low IQ, and so on. The result is a specific admixture of genes and life experience that makes each character unlike any other character and gives him or her a singular voice.

年复一年，生活中的种种经历以无数种方式塑造着你的性格，或伤人，或收获，或影响着你。在这纷繁的习俗和际遇中，你与生俱来的性格特质和生理特征——例如容貌姣好或相貌平平、健康或体弱多病、性格外向或内向、智商高或低等等——交织融合。最终，基因与人生阅历的独特组合，造就了每个人独一无二的个性，赋予其独特的生命力。

In the four case studies that follow, notice what their authors found when they entered into their characters’ psyches: popular culture. In The Tragedy of Julius Caesar , Shakespeare references the Colossus of Rhodes, which was the most famous, and certainly the largest, bronze statue of the classical era, which in turn means that the well-traveled Cassius and Brutus must have sailed past it in awe. In Out of Sight Elmore Leonard weaves images from THREE DAYS OF THE CONDOR, a hit film in the Watergate era. His characters probably saw it in their impressionable teens. Passages from 30 ROCK feature upper-class obsessions like yachts and mergers. Fine wine, on the other hand, is no longer the province of the rich; schoolteachers are as expert as sommeliers, which plays crucially in SIDEWAYS.

在接下来的四个案例研究中，请注意作者们在深入刻画人物内心世界时发现了什么：流行文化。在莎士比亚的《尤利乌斯·凯撒》中，他提到了罗德岛巨像，这是古典时代最著名、也是最大的青铜雕像，这意味着见多识广的卡西乌斯和布鲁图斯一定曾满怀敬畏地乘船经过它。在埃尔莫·伦纳德的《战略高手》中，他巧妙地融入了水门事件时期的热门电影《秃鹰七十二小时》的画面。他笔下的人物很可能在青少年时期就看过这部电影。《我为喜剧狂》中的一些片段展现了上流社会痴迷的事物，例如游艇和并购。另一方面，美酒不再是富人的专属；教师们也像侍酒师一样精通葡萄酒，这在《杯酒人生》中起到了至关重要的作用。

To write each scene, the author has gone inside to see what his character has seen. He then discovered a cultural icon to enrich the scene as the character draws an analogy between his immediate life and a work of art or cuisine. Once again, using a third thing to create a trialogue.

为了创作每一幕，作者都深入角色内心，体验他们所见所闻。然后，他找到一个文化符号来丰富场景，让角色将自己的生活与一件艺术品或美食进行类比。再一次，作者运用了第三者，构建了三方对话。

Think about it: How in fact do people express themselves in words? How do they explain what they’re thinking and feeling, say what needs to be said, and, most importantly, do what needs to be done? Answer: They use the bits and pieces of everything they know. And what, first and foremost, do they know? Culture. Whether popular or esoteric, whether acquired from formal education or overheard on a street corner, culture is our dominant source of knowledge. To that we add all the imagery rooted in characters’ encounters with nature, cityscapes, workscapes, and religious ritual. Plus images from dreams, from fantasies about the future, from the totality of the day and night musings that weave these familiarities together. This mass of experience creates a treasure chest of images that will inspire distinctive dialogue in the mouths of your characters.

仔细想想：人们究竟是如何用语言表达自己的？他们如何解释自己的想法和感受，说出需要说的话，以及最重要的，完成需要做的事情？答案是：他们运用自己所知的一切。那么，他们首先知道的是什么呢？是文化。无论是通俗的还是深奥的，无论是通过正规教育获得的还是在街头巷尾偶然听到的，文化都是我们知识的主要来源。除此之外，我们还要加上所有源于角色与自然、城市景观、工作场所和宗教仪式的邂逅的意象。还有来自梦境、对未来的幻想，以及日夜思绪交织而成的种种意象，这些都将这些熟悉的事物编织在一起。如此丰富的经验构成了一个意象宝库，能够激发你笔下人物说出独具特色的对话。

The next four case studies illustrate these principles.

接下来的四个案例研究将阐述这些原则。

#↩

11

FOUR CASE STUDIES

四个案例研究

THE TRAGEDY OF JULIUS CAESAR

《尤利乌斯·凯撒》的悲剧

Consider this setup: Senator A is powerful and popular. The envious Senator B wants the respected Senator C to join forces against Senator A. So Senator B pulls Senator C aside to persuade him:

设想以下情景：参议员A权势显赫，深受民众爱戴。心怀嫉妒的参议员B想让德高望重的参议员C联手对抗参议员A。于是，参议员B把参议员C拉到一边，试图说服他：

SENATOR B

参议员B

Senator A is so popular and so powerful that compared to him, we’re nobodies.

A 参议员非常受欢迎，也很有影响力，和他相比，我们简直就是无足轻重的小人物。

Senator B states the obvious in passive and opaque language. His dialogue couldn’t be less persuasive, less imaginative, less interesting. The comparison he makes might irritate Senator C, but Senator B’s words have no imagery to give them life; no subtext to give them depth. His complaint is so bland, Senator C could easily shrug it aside.

B参议员用平淡晦涩的语言陈述显而易见的事实。他的言辞毫无说服力，缺乏想象力，也乏味至极。他所做的比较或许会激怒C参议员，但B参议员的言辞缺乏生动形象的描绘，也没有任何弦外之音，使其缺乏深度。他的抱怨如此平淡无奇，C参议员很容易就能不予理会。

Here’s how history’s greatest dialogue artist rendered the moment in The Tragedy of Julius Caesar , Act 1, Scene 2:

以下是历史上最伟大的对话艺术家在《尤利乌斯·凯撒》第一幕第二场中对这一场景的演绎：

CASSIUS

卡西乌斯

(to Brutus)

（对布鲁图斯说）

Why, man, he doth bestride the narrow world like a Colossus, and we petty men walk under his huge legs and peep about to find ourselves dishonorable graves.

老天，他像巨人一样横跨狭小的世界，而我们这些渺小的人却在他的巨腿下行走，四处窥视，最终发现自己只能落得个耻辱的坟墓。

Shakespeare’s Cassius hugely overstates the case, which, of course, is what people do when trying to wheedle their way inside someone else’s head. They use the techniques of rhetoric to distort, exaggerate, or manipulate.

莎士比亚笔下的卡西乌斯极度夸大其词，这当然是人们试图左右他人想法时惯用的伎俩。他们运用修辞技巧来歪曲事实、夸大其词或操纵舆论。

The Colossus was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. More than one hundred feet tall, this bronze statue of the sun god Helios stood astride the harbor at Rhodes with ships sailing in and out of port under its legs. Cassius compares Caesar to an awesome, imaginary colossus that would have one foot in Spain, the other in Syria, and the whole Mediterranean world between its legs.

罗德岛巨像曾是古代世界七大奇迹之一。这座太阳神赫利俄斯的青铜雕像高达百余英尺，矗立在罗德岛港口，船只在其双腿下往来穿梭。卡西乌斯将凯撒比作一座令人敬畏的虚构巨像，一只脚踏在西班牙，另一只脚踏在叙利亚，整个地中海世界都夹在其双腿之间。

And yet, note that Shakespeare gives Cassius this phrase: “the narrow world.” The instinctive, off-the-top-of-the-head phrase would be “the wide world.” So, why “narrow”?

然而，请注意莎士比亚对卡西乌斯说的这句话：“狭小的世界”。人们下意识会脱口而出的短语应该是“广阔的世界”。那么，为什么是“狭小的”呢？

Because Shakespeare (I suspect) wrote in-character. He slipped his imagination into the mind of Cassius, so he could work from Cassius’s subjective point of view. He was then able to see the world the way Cassius saw it and write imagistic dialogue for the eye: “the narrow world.”

因为莎士比亚（我怀疑）是以人物视角进行写作的。他将自己的想象力融入卡西乌斯的内心世界，从而能够从卡西乌斯的主观视角进行创作。这样，他就能以卡西乌斯的视角看待世界，并创作出富有画面感的对话，展现“狭隘的世界”。

As Roman senators, Cassius and Brutus would have imperial maps spread across their desks. Every week they receive strategic reports from all corners of the empire. These men know exactly how wide the world is: the width of all things Roman. To the naive, the world may seem wide, but to these urbane politicos, it’s narrow. So slender, in fact, a single man—the ambitious Caesar—could seize it and rule it alone.

作为罗马元老，卡西乌斯和布鲁图斯的办公桌上总是摊着帝国地图。他们每周都会收到来自帝国各地的战略报告。这些人对世界的广袤了如指掌：这里指的是罗马世界的广袤。在天真的人眼中，世界或许广阔无垠，但在这些见多识广的政治家看来，它却十分狭窄。事实上，它如此狭小，以至于一个野心勃勃的人——凯撒——就能攫取并独揽大权。

While immersing himself in his characters, Shakespeare must have imagined, even researched, their childhoods, for it was in their educations that he found his inspiration for crafting the play’s unique dialogue.

莎士比亚在刻画人物的过程中，一定想象过，甚至研究过他们的童年，因为他正是从他们的教育经历中找到了创作该剧独特对话的灵感。

Aristocratic Roman schoolchildren were rigorously trained as orators, as future politicians skilled in the arts of declamation, persuasion, and rhetoric. And the guiding tenet of public speaking is, “Think as a wise man but speak as a common man.” Speak, in other words, in the plain, monosyllabic manner of the street.

罗马贵族学校的学童从小就接受严格的演说训练，成为精通演讲、说服和修辞技巧的未来政治家。公共演讲的指导原则是：“要像智者一样思考，像普通人一样说话。”换句话说，就是用街头巷尾那种朴实无华、简洁明了的语言说话。

So note that of the twenty-eight words in Cassius’s sentence, only two have more than two syllables.

所以请注意，卡西乌斯这句话中的二十八个单词中，只有两个单词的音节超过两个。

Shakespeare knew that seasoned orators string short words together to create the effect of casual, artless, sincere ease while at the same time showing off their verbal ingenuity. For it takes skill to deliver monosyllables in a natural, pleasing rhythm. And Cassius is very clever. In fact, all of the play’s characters have a way with simple words. The dialogue style throughout The Tragedy of Julius Caesar is almost exclusively monosyllabic, with some of Shakespeare’s passages stringing thirty or more monosyllables in a row. 1

莎士比亚深知，经验丰富的演说家会巧妙地将短词串联起来，营造出一种轻松自然、毫不矫揉造作、真诚坦率的效果，同时又能展现其语言的精妙之处。因为要以自然流畅、悦耳动听的节奏说出单音节词，需要相当的技巧。而卡西乌斯正是如此。事实上，剧中的所有角色都擅长运用简单的词语。《尤利乌斯·凯撒》的对话几乎完全由单音节词构成，莎士比亚的一些段落甚至连续使用了三十个或更多的单音节词。

What’s more, as patrician senators, Cassius and Brutus have immense pride in their aristocratic heritage. The notion of seeming “petty,” of “peeping about” in search of a “dishonorable” grave repels the noble Brutus. With these biting images, Cassius seduces him to assassinate Caesar.

此外，作为贵族出身的元老，卡西乌斯和布鲁图斯对自己的贵族血统无比自豪。一想到自己会显得“卑鄙”，会“四处窥探”，寻找“不光彩”的坟墓，就令高贵的布鲁图斯感到厌恶。卡西乌斯正是用这些尖刻的比喻，诱使他刺杀凯撒。

In terms of the modal side of dialogue, because Cassius is a bold, hard-thinking man on a mission, he uses direct action verbs: bestride, walk, peep. He does not modify his predicates. If he did, it might read like this:

就对话的语态而言，由于卡西乌斯是一位勇敢、思维缜密且肩负使命的人，他使用了直接动作动词：跨骑、行走、窥视。他没有修饰谓语。如果他修饰了谓语，句子可能会是这样：

CASSIUS

卡西乌斯

It seems to me as if mighty Caesar could bestride the narrow world like some kind of gigantic Colossus, so we poor men would have to walk carefully around under his huge legs, and try to peep about to maybe, should we get really lucky, someday find ourselves disgusting, dishonorable graves.

在我看来，强大的凯撒就像一个巨大的巨人，可以横跨狭窄的世界，所以我们这些可怜的人只能小心翼翼地从他巨大的腿下走过，四处窥视，也许，如果我们真的走运的话，有一天会发现自己躺在令人作呕、耻辱的坟墓里。

This Cassius, as I’ve rewritten him, becomes weak and nervous. He’s so preoccupied with what’s possible and not possible, what’s permitted and not permitted, what’s sure and unsure, that he surrounds his verbs with “could,” “would,” “should,” and other cautious supplementary phrases.

我改写的这个卡西乌斯变得虚弱而焦虑。他过于纠结于什么可能什么不可能，什么允许什么不允许，什么确定什么不确定，以至于他的动词周围总是加上“可能”、“会”、“应该”和其他谨慎的补充短语。

Lastly, very importantly, consider the background desires that surround Cassius and the gentlemanly restraints that shape his behavior. He knows that Brutus is a very private man, taciturn yet perceptive. Both men have been raised in an elite society in which cultured men do not bare their souls to each other. Therefore, to write in-character, Shakespeare must have given thought and feeling to what his character would not say. For example, the refined Cassius would not speak on-the-nose:

最后，非常重要的一点是，要考虑卡西乌斯内心深处的欲望以及塑造他行为的绅士风度。他知道布鲁图斯是个非常注重隐私的人，沉默寡言却又洞察力敏锐。两人都成长于一个精英社会，在这个社会里，有教养的男人们不会轻易向彼此袒露心扉。因此，为了写出符合人物性格的作品，莎士比亚必须认真思考并体会到他笔下人物不会说出口的话。例如，举止优雅的卡西乌斯绝不会直言不讳：

CASSIUS

卡西乌斯

I loathe that power-grabbing Caesar, and I know you hate the bastard, too. So before we end up begging on our knees, kissing his tyrant’s ass, let’s murder the son of a bitch.

我憎恨那个贪婪的凯撒，我知道你也恨透了这个混蛋。所以，在我们最终跪地求饶、舔他暴君屁股之前，让我们先干掉这个狗娘养的。

With the exception of hip-hop lyrics, the twenty-first century seems poetry-lite. Shakespearean iambic pentameter may feel out of reach; nonetheless, we want our scenes to play with an intensity that matches the emotional lives of our characters and, in turn, moves the reader/audience. To achieve this, we take inspiration from Shakespeare to enrich our dialogue with imagery. First, we visualize the scene from our character’s subjective point of view, and then find language from within his nature and experience to create his character-specific dialogue.

除了嘻哈歌词，二十一世纪似乎诗歌创作都显得单薄。莎士比亚式的抑扬格五音步或许遥不可及；然而，我们仍然希望场景的张力能够与人物的情感生活相契合，进而打动读者/观众。为了实现这一目标，我们从莎士比亚的作品中汲取灵感，用丰富的意象来充实对话。首先，我们从人物的主观视角出发，构想场景，然后从人物的性格和经历中寻找合适的语言，创作出符合其人物性格的对话。

OUT OF SIGHT

消失不见

Consider this setup: During a prison break, a criminal forces a federal agent into the trunk of her car and climbs in with her. His partner takes the wheel and drives off. While sardined in the pitch-dark trunk, crook and cop are irresistibly attracted. After the getaway, neither can stop thinking about the other. Eventually she tracks him to a hotel where, despite their antagonistic roles, their mutual passion moves them to declare a truce and spend a romantic evening together.

设想一下这样的场景：越狱期间，一名罪犯强迫一名联邦探员钻进她汽车的后备箱，自己也钻了进去。他的同伙则开车逃走。在漆黑的后备箱里，两人像沙丁鱼罐头一样挤在一起，却也产生了无法抗拒的吸引力。逃亡结束后，两人都对对方念念不忘。最终，她追踪他到了一家酒店。尽管两人原本是敌对关系，但彼此的激情促使他们达成和解，共度了一个浪漫的夜晚。

INT. LUXURY HOTEL ROOM—NIGHT

豪华酒店客房—夜晚

Candlelight glints off the dewy eyes of the handsome Criminal and beautiful Federal Agent as they gaze longingly at each other.

烛光映照着英俊的罪犯和美丽的联邦探员湿润的双眼，他们深情地凝视着彼此。

FEDERAL AGENT

联邦特工

I’m confused and scared.

我感到困惑和害怕。

CRIMINAL

刑事

Same here, but I’m trying to be cool.

我也是，但我努力装作很酷。

FEDERAL AGENT

联邦特工

Me, too, but I’m afraid that you might rape me.

我也是，但我害怕你会强奸我。

CRIMINAL

刑事

Never. My only hope is to have a nice romantic night together.

绝不。我只希望我们能共度一个美好的浪漫夜晚。

FEDERAL AGENT

联邦特工

Good. Because underneath your tough exterior I suspect there’s a really loving guy. But still I can’t be certain. Maybe you’re trying to seduce me so I’ll help you escape the law.

很好。因为我怀疑你坚硬的外表下藏着一颗温柔的心。但我也不能完全确定。也许你是想勾引我，好让我帮你逃脱法律的制裁。

CRIMINAL

刑事

No, I understand you’re still a federal agent and I’m still a bank robber and you have your job to do. It’s just that you’re so beautiful, I can’t stop thinking about how it was when we met.

不，我知道你仍然是联邦探员，我仍然是银行劫匪，你也有你的工作要做。只是你太美了，我总是忍不住想起我们初次相遇的情景。

They sigh and take a sad sip of champagne.

他们叹了口气，悲伤地抿了一口香槟。

I’ve written this scene in the paralytic language of people saying exactly and completely what they think and feel. The result? A flattened wreck no actor could salvage. Explicit dialogue that turns a character’s inner life into words turns an actor to wood.

我用那种让人麻木的语言写了这场戏，要求人们直白地、完整地表达自己的想法和感受。结果呢？一场彻底失败的表演，任何演员都无力回天。直白的对话把角色的内心世界用文字表达出来，只会让演员变成木头人。

In contrast to the scene I sketched above, here is how Elmore Leonard, one of the finest writers of dialogue in the modern novel, rendered the cop/criminal tryst:

与我上面描绘的场景相反，以下是现代小说中最优秀的对话作家之一埃尔莫·伦纳德对警察/罪犯幽会的描写：

In Chapter Twenty of Out of Sight , escaped bank robber Jack Foley invites US Marshal Karen Sisco to a hotel suite overlooking the Detroit waterfront. They drink and reminisce about the prison break and their dangerous, yet erotic encounter in the trunk of her car:

在《视线之外》第二十章中，越狱的银行劫匪杰克·弗利邀请美国法警凯伦·西斯科到一家可以俯瞰底特律海滨的酒店套房。他们喝酒，回忆起越狱事件以及在她汽车后备箱里那次危险却又充满情欲的邂逅：

She said, “Remember how talkative you were?”

她说：“你还记得你以前有多爱说话吗？”

He said, “I was nervous,” lighting her cigarette and then his own.

他说：“我很紧张，”说着，他点燃了她的香烟，然后又点燃了自己的香烟。

“Yeah, but you didn’t show it. You were a pretty cool guy. But then when you got in the trunk… I thought you’d try to tear my clothes off.”

“是啊，但你没表现出来。你人挺好的。可是当你钻进后备箱的时候……我还以为你会扒光我的衣服呢。”

“It never entered my mind. Well, not until—remember we were talking about Faye Dunaway?… I told you I liked that movie Three Days of the Condor , and you said yeah, you loved the lines? Like the next morning, after they’d slept together, he says he’ll need her help and she says…”

“我从没想过这个问题。嗯，直到——还记得我们聊到费·唐纳薇吗？……我跟你说过我喜欢那部电影《秃鹰七十二小时》，你说是啊，你也喜欢里面的台词？比如第二天早上，他们睡过之后，他说他需要她的帮助，然后她说……”

“Have I ever denied you anything?”

“我什么时候拒绝过你什么？”

“I thought for a couple of seconds there, the way you said it, you were coming on to me.”

“我刚才那几秒钟，听你说话的方式，以为你在勾引我。”

“Maybe I was and didn’t know it… Before they ever go to bed she accused him of getting rough. He says, ‘What? Have I raped you?’ And she says, ‘The night is young.’ I thought, Come on—what is she doing, giving him ideas?”

“也许我当时就是那样，只是自己不知道……在他们上床睡觉之前，她指责他动作粗暴。他说：‘什么？我强奸你了吗？’她说：‘夜还很长。’我心想，拜托——她这是在干什么，给他出主意吗？”

“You know you kept touching me, feeling my thigh.”

“你知道你一直在摸我，摸我的大腿。”

“Yeah, but in a nice way.”

“是啊，不过是褒义的。”

“You called me your zoo-zoo.”

你叫我你的动物园。

“That’s candy, inside, something sweet.”

“里面是糖果，是甜的。”

In this deceptively simple but complex scene, Leonard’s dialogue creates multiple layers of textual imagery over a double layer of implied images. The first two layers are set up in the previous pages:

在这个看似简单实则复杂的场景中，莱昂纳德的对话在两层隐含意象之上构建了多层文字意象。前两层意象在前几页中已经铺垫完毕：

Layer 1. The image of the setting: For his long-fantasized rendezvous with Karen, Foley chooses a posh hotel suite that commands a panorama of the city at night under a gentle snowfall. Soft lights, soft music. They’re posed like a chic couple on a Crown Royal whisky billboard. Leonard delights in setting up this glitzy cliché so that he can ironize and undercut it again and again.

第一层：场景意象：为了与凯伦进行他梦寐以求的约会，弗利选择了一间豪华酒店套房，可以俯瞰夜晚的城市全景，雪花轻柔飘落。柔和的灯光，舒缓的音乐。他们摆出的姿势就像皇冠威士忌广告牌上的时尚情侣。伦纳德乐于营造这种浮华的陈词滥调，以便反复地对其进行讽刺和解构。

Layer 2. The all-too-familiar image of the situation: Their romance is “illegal.” Foley is a felon on the run; Sisco is the law. But this has been done many times before: McQueen and Dunaway in THE THOMAS CROWN AFFAIR, Bogie and Bacall in DARK PASSAGE, Grant and Hepburn in CHARADE. It’s not just any cliché; it’s a movie cliché.

第二层：似曾相识的场景：他们的恋情是“非法的”。弗利是逃犯，西斯科是执法者。但这种情节早已屡见不鲜：麦奎因和邓纳薇在《托马斯·克朗事件》中，博吉和贝考尔在《黑暗通道》中，格兰特和赫本在《谜中谜》中。这并非普通的陈词滥调，而是电影史上的经典桥段。

And then the dialogue takes over to add more facets.

然后对话开始，增添了更多层次。

Layer 3. Escape from “reality”: Over their movie scene Foley and Sisco superimpose yet another movie—THREE DAYS OF THE CONDOR. They chat about their favorite moments from the film because they’re fully aware that they’re living in a virtual film. As a result, the reader blends the famous faces of Robert Redford and Faye Dunaway with the fictional faces of Foley and Sisco, coating the whole episode with Hollywood gloss.

第三层：逃离“现实”：在弗利和西斯科的电影场景之上，叠加了另一部电影——《秃鹰七十二小时》。他们聊着电影中最喜欢的片段，因为他们完全意识到自己正生活在一部虚拟电影中。因此，读者会将罗伯特·雷德福和费·唐纳薇的明星面孔与弗利和西斯科的虚构面孔融合在一起，为整个事件蒙上了一层好莱坞的光鲜亮丽。

Layer 4. The memory: The lovers replay their intimate adventure in her car trunk. This takes us back to the mini-movie that ran through our head when we read the prison break scene in the opening chapters.

第四层：记忆：这对恋人在她的汽车后备箱里重温了他们的亲密冒险。这让我们回想起在阅读开篇章节中越狱场景时，脑海中浮现的那段微电影。

Now four layers of images are superimposed on the reader’s mind: The hotel setting, the cop/criminal situation, the Hollywood version, and the burnished nostalgia of how they met. But that’s only the surface.

现在，读者的脑海中叠加了四层画面：酒店场景、警察/罪犯的情境、好莱坞版本，以及两人相遇时那种被美化的怀旧之情。但这仅仅是表面现象。

Beneath this, Leonard creates his characters’ inner lives of unspoken needs and dreams.

在此之下，伦纳德塑造了人物内心深处那些未曾言明的需求和梦想。

Leonard uses a pair of third things: THREE DAYS OF THE CONDOR and the memory of their first adventure. These play back-to-back to create interlocking trialogues. As I laid out in Part Two, working a scene through a third thing helps keep dialogue off-the-nose.

伦纳德运用了两个“第三元素”：《秃鹰七十二小时》和他们第一次冒险的回忆。这两个元素交替出现，形成环环相扣的三段对话。正如我在第二部分中所述，通过“第三元素”来推进剧情有助于避免对话显得生硬突兀。

Layer 5. The subtext: Under the lines, we sense Jack and Karen’s desire to put aside their cop/criminal roles, to take time out from life, so they can indulge this rush of romance. We can well imagine their sexual fantasies clashing with the realization that their intimacy is tabooed. This in turn makes their sensual desires dangerous, even lethal, and so all the more erotic. Could either of them name what they’re feeling? No. No one could and still feel it. To name a feeling is to kill it.

第五层含义：字里行间，我们能感受到杰克和凯伦渴望放下警察/罪犯的身份，暂时逃离现实生活，沉浸于这激情澎湃的浪漫之中。我们可以想象，他们的性幻想与禁忌的现实之间存在着强烈的冲突。这反过来又使他们的感官欲望变得危险，甚至致命，也因此更加令人着迷。他们之中有人能说出自己的感受吗？不能。没有人能说出，却仍然能感受到。说出感受就等于扼杀它。

The present is so razor sharp, Leonard has them sidestep it by reminiscing about how they met. But as they do, everything they say about the past betrays a subtext of what they’re feeling in the now.

当下的一切都如此尖锐，莱纳德只好让他们回忆相遇的往事来回避。但随着回忆的展开，他们口中关于过去的每一句话都暗含着此刻的感受。

They kid about the heart-pounding jailbreak and how they played it cool, but for all Karen knows she’s sitting on a sofa with a smooth-talking rapist, and for all Jack knows there’s a SWAT team with a battering ram outside the door. They tease offhandedly about the sexy tension they felt in the trunk of her car, while the heat of the moment blisters the hotel room. And, very importantly, they hide all this behind witty quotes from THREE DAYS OF THE CONDOR.

他们开玩笑说起那场惊心动魄的越狱，以及他们当时是如何装作若无其事的，但凯伦可能不知道自己正和一个油嘴滑舌的强奸犯坐在沙发上，而杰克可能不知道门外正站着一支带着破门锤的特警队。他们漫不经心地调侃着在她车后备箱里感受到的那种暧昧情愫，而此时此刻，酒店房间里的气氛却已如火如荼。更重要的是，他们还用《秃鹰七十二小时》里的妙语连珠来掩盖这一切。

It’s at this fifth layer of the unspoken that Leonard unites Karen and Jack. We realize that although they’re on opposite sides of the law, at heart they’re a matched pair of die-hard romantics hooked on old movies.

正是在这第五层未言明的层面，莱纳德将凯伦和杰克联系在了一起。我们意识到，尽管他们站在法律的对立面，但本质上，他们是一对痴迷老电影的死忠浪漫主义者。

Layer 6. Dreams: This subtextual insight leads us to imagine the wistful daydreams of Foley and Sisco. While he hopes that she will play Faye Dunaway to his Robert Redford and somehow rescue him, he knows that in fact that will never happen. Sisco can see herself as Dunaway acting out that scenario; it’s her wish, too. But like Foley, she knows it’s an impossible fantasy.

第六层：梦境：这一潜台词引导我们想象弗利和西斯科那些充满憧憬的白日梦。弗利希望西斯科能像费·唐纳薇一样，成为他的罗伯特·雷德福，拯救他于水火之中，但他心里明白，这根本不可能。西斯科也幻想自己是唐纳薇，演绎着那个场景；这也是她的愿望。但和弗利一样，她也明白这只是一个遥不可及的幻想。

Leonard must have loved dialogue or he couldn’t have written it with such skill. So note that his characters also love dialogue. When he has them remember THREE DAYS OF THE CONDOR, they don’t recall looks or gestures; they quote lines verbatim—lines that must have struck Leonard’s ear when he saw the film.

莱昂纳德一定非常热爱对话，否则他不可能写出如此精妙的对白。所以请注意，他笔下的人物也同样热爱对话。当他让他们回忆《秃鹰七十二小时》时，他们回忆的不是表情或手势，而是逐字逐句地背诵台词——这些台词想必是莱昂纳德在观看这部电影时印象深刻的。

What is the payoff to the deep insight this scene gives the reader?

这一幕给读者带来的深刻启示是什么？

Enormous suspense: Will they make love? Will she forget she’s a cop and let him escape? Will she arrest him? Will she have to shoot him? Will he be forced to kill her? This seemingly casual talk between forbidden lovers expresses all of the above and more.

悬念迭起：他们会发生关系吗？她会忘记自己是警察而让他逃脱吗？她会逮捕他吗？她会不得不开枪打死他吗？他会被迫杀死她吗？这段看似随意的禁忌恋人对话，其实包含了以上所有以及更多内容。

30 ROCK

30 Rock

Season 5, Episode 1, “The Fabian Strategy”

第五季第一集，“费边战略”

This half-hour comedy series takes place in the offices and studios of NBC in New York’s Rockefeller Center.

这部半小时的喜剧系列剧以纽约洛克菲勒中心的NBC办公室和演播室为背景。

John Francis “Jack” Donaghy (Alec Baldwin) serves as vice president of East Coast television and microwave oven programming for General Electric. Liz Lemon (Tina Fey) works for Jack as producer and head writer of a prime-time variety show. Avery (Elizabeth Banks) is Jack’s fiancée.

约翰·弗朗西斯·“杰克”·多纳吉（亚历克·鲍德温饰）是通用电气公司东海岸电视和微波炉节目制作副总裁。莉兹·莱蒙（蒂娜·菲饰）是杰克的下属，担任黄金时段综艺节目的制片人和首席编剧。艾弗里（伊丽莎白·班克斯饰）是杰克的未婚妻。

The passages below sample Jack’s verbal style. The phrases and words in bold signal his unique characterization and hint at his true character.

以下段落展现了杰克的语言风格。粗体字的词句体现了他独特的性格特征，并暗示了他的真实性格。

On his first morning back from summer vacation, Jack calls Liz on the phone:

暑假结束后的第一个早晨，杰克打电话给莉兹：

JACK

杰克

Oh, Lemon, Avery and I just got back from the most amazing vacation on Paul Allen’s yacht . Sheer bliss . Avery is the most perfect woman ever created. Like a young Bo Derek stuffed with a Barry Goldwater . (pause) But it’s back to reality. No more making love on the beach surrounded by a privacy circle of English-trained butlers .

哦，莱蒙，我和艾弗里刚从保罗·艾伦的游艇上度过了一个美妙绝伦的假期回来。简直太幸福了。艾弗里是世上最完美的女人。就像年轻版的波·德里克，又像巴里·戈德华特。（停顿）但现实是，再也不能回到过去了。再也不能在沙滩上，被一群受过英式训练的管家簇拥着，享受私密的二人世界了。

(Note: Paul Allen co-founded Microsoft.)

（注：保罗·艾伦是微软的联合创始人。）

In a meeting later that day with Liz and her show’s producers, Jack fears that the network’s weak performance will jeopardize an all-important merger:

当天晚些时候，杰克与莉兹和她节目的制片人开会，担心电视台糟糕的业绩会危及一项至关重要的合并：

JACK

杰克

In order for our merger to stay attractive to our friends at Kabletown, we have to seem like a sexy, profitable company , and we’re almost pulling it off. The Harry Potter Theme Park is a huge hit with both anglophiles and pedophiles. The movie division has a James Cameron movie the whole world will see whether they like it or not. Only NBC continues to be the engorged whitehead on the otherwise flawless face of Universal Media.

为了让我们的合并案继续吸引卡布尔镇的朋友们，我们必须看起来像一家性感又盈利的公司，而我们几乎做到了。哈利·波特主题公园深受英国文化爱好者和恋童癖者的喜爱。电影部门有一部詹姆斯·卡梅隆的电影，无论人们喜欢与否，全世界都会看到。只有NBC仍然是环球媒体这完美无瑕的脸上那颗碍眼的白头。

As their workday ends, Liz confesses that she suffers relationship problems, so Jack gives her this advice:

一天工作结束后，莉兹坦白自己遇到了感情问题，杰克于是给了她以下建议：

JACK

杰克

You can’t just do the vacation part. At some point you have to go home to the same house, unpack your dirty laundry, and have a life together . And one of you says, “We should redecorate.” And the other says, “Please, Avery, I’m using the commode right now.”

你不能只享受度假的乐趣。总有一天，你们要回到同一个家，整理脏衣服，一起生活。然后你们其中一个人说：“我们应该重新装修一下。”另一个人说：“拜托，艾弗里，我现在正在用马桶呢。”

LIZ

莉兹

Oh, she wants to redecorate? She just moved in.

哦，她想重新装修？她才刚搬进来。

JACK

杰克

Avery has opinions. I love her for that. Unfortunately, she wants to repaint the upstairs hallway in a striae faux finish called “ Husk .” I prefer the color that’s already there, a reddish brown shade called “ Elk Tongue .”

艾弗里很有主见，我喜欢她这一点。可惜的是，她想把楼上的走廊重新粉刷成一种叫做“Husk”的仿旧条纹漆。我更喜欢现在的颜色，一种叫做“Elk Tongue”的红棕色。

LIZ

莉兹

So tell her “No.” It’s your house.

所以就告诉她“不”。这是你的房子。

JACK

杰克

This is how I know you’ve never had an adult relationship. If I say “No,” then I will be required to say “Yes” to something else in the future and the stakes in the future might be higher.

这就是我判断你从未有过成年人恋爱关系的原因。如果我说“不”，那么将来我就不得不对其他事情说“是”，而且将来的风险可能会更大。

LIZ

莉兹

Then say “Yes.”

那就说“是”。

JACK

杰克

If I give in, then I’m no longer the alpha in my house . Before you know it, she’ll have me wearing jeans and reading fiction .

如果我屈服，我就不再是家里的老大。说不定过不了多久，她就会让我穿上牛仔裤，读小说。

LIZ

莉兹

Yeah, well, “Yes” and “No” are kind of your only two choices.

是啊，其实你只有“是”和“否”这两个选择。

JACK

杰克

For most men, sure , but there is a third option—the Fabian Strategy … The Fabian Strategy derives its name from the Roman general Quintus Fabius Maximus . He ran away, Lemon. Rather than engage in battle, he would retreat and retreat until the enemy grew fatigued and eventually made a mistake . Although I abhor it as a military strategy, it is the basis for all my personal relationships .

对大多数男人来说，当然是这样，但还有第三种选择——费边战略……费边战略得名于罗马将军昆图斯·费边·马克西姆斯。他逃跑了，莱蒙。他不去正面交锋，而是不断撤退，直到敌人疲惫不堪，最终犯下错误。虽然我厌恶这种军事策略，但它却是我所有人际关系的基础。

Jack’s handsome face, tailored suits, and $150 haircuts suggest who he might be, but beyond his physical appearance, the writers draw on terms such as “sheer bliss,” “flawless,” “Bo Derek,” “a sexy, profitable company,” “privacy circle,” “commode,” “Husk,” “Elk Tongue,” “prefer,” and “abhor” to nail his characterization. Modal phrases such as “no more,” “like it or not,” “you can’t,” “you have to,” and “if/then” signal Jack’s sense of power over others. The word and phrase choices in these speeches attest to Jack’s command of popular culture, his excellent education, his identification with the upper class, his capitalist ethos, his controlling executive leadership style, and, most of all, his supercilious, egoistic snobbery. Together, these traits etch the outer self he shows the world—his characterization.

杰克英俊的脸庞、剪裁合身的西装和150美元的理发，暗示着他的身份，但除了外表之外，作者还运用了“纯粹的幸福”、“完美无瑕”、“波·德里克”、“一家性感且盈利的公司”、“隐私圈”、“马桶”、“外壳”、“麋鹿舌”、“偏爱”和“厌恶”等词语，精准地刻画了他的性格。诸如“不再”、“不管你喜不喜欢”、“你不能”、“你必须”和“如果/那么”之类的情态动词短语，则暗示了杰克对他人拥有的权力感。这些演讲中的用词和短语选择，体现了杰克对流行文化的驾驭能力、他所受的良好教育、他对上流社会的认同、他的资本主义精神、他控制欲极强的领导风格，以及最重要的，他傲慢自大、自私自利的势利眼。所有这些特质共同塑造了他展现给世人的外在形象——他的人物形象。

But vocabulary and syntax also throw light on character dimension.

但词汇和句法也能反映人物性格。

A dimension is a contradiction that underpins a character’s nature. These psychological stanchions come in two kinds: 1) Contradictions that play characterization against true character. Namely, conflicts between a character’s outer traits and his inner truths, between the persona of his visible behavior and the person he hides behind the mask. 2) Contradictions that play self against self. These dimensions link the warring forces within true, deep character—most often desires from the conscious self at odds with opposite impulses from the subconscious self. 2

维度是构成角色本质的矛盾。这些心理支柱分为两类：1）角色塑造与真实性格之间的矛盾。具体而言，就是角色外在特征与内在真相之间的冲突，即角色外在行为所展现的形象与面具背后隐藏的真实自我之间的冲突。2）自我与自我之间的矛盾。这类维度连接着真实、深层性格中相互冲突的力量——通常是来自意识自我的欲望与来自潜意识自我的相反冲动之间的冲突。

Jack’s speech style reveals seven such dimensions: He’s 1) socially sophisticated (Paul Allen’s yacht/English-trained butlers) yet privately primal (the alpha in my house/engorged whitehead), 2) unscrupulous (The movie division has a James Cameron movie the whole world will see whether they like it or not) yet guilt-ridden (I will be required to say “Yes”), 3) fiscally conservative (Barry Goldwater) yet risk taking (The Harry Potter Theme Park is a huge hit with both anglophiles and pedophiles), 4) well educated (General Quintus Fabius Maximus invented his guerrilla strategy during the Second Punic War in 218 BC) yet self-deceived (the basis for all my personal relationships), and 5) intellectually pompous (a striae faux finish) yet factually informed (a striae faux finish). Jack 6) uses devious tactics to navigate his personal life (retreat until the enemy grows fatigued and eventually makes a mistake), yet idealizes his relationships with women (most perfect woman ever created). He 7) is a realist (You can’t just do the vacation part), yet a dreamer (a life together). The show’s directors constantly posed Jack in a close-up, staring into space, imagining his idealized future.

杰克的言谈举止揭示了七个这样的维度：1）他社交老练（保罗·艾伦的游艇/受过英国训练的管家），但私下里却很原始（我家里的阿尔法/满脸白头），2）肆无忌惮（电影部门有一部詹姆斯·卡梅隆的电影，不管全世界的人喜欢与否，他们都会去看），但又充满内疚（我将被要求说“是”），3）财政保守（巴里·戈德华特），但又敢于冒险（哈利·波特主题公园深受英国文化爱好者和恋童癖者的欢迎），4）受过良好教育（昆图斯·法比乌斯·马克西姆斯将军在公元前218年的第二次布匿战争期间发明了他的游击战术），但又自欺欺人（我所有人际关系的基础），以及5）知识分子自负（一种仿旧的纹路），但又掌握事实（一种仿旧的纹路）。杰克（6）在处理个人生活时惯用阴险手段（伺机退缩，直到敌人疲惫不堪，最终犯错），却又将与女性的关系理想化（他心目中最完美的女人）。他（7）既是现实主义者（度假可不是儿戏），又是梦想家（憧憬着共度一生）。剧集的导演经常让杰克以特写镜头凝视远方，想象着他理想化的未来。

Multidimensional as he is, Jack Donaghy is not, however, a dramatic character; he is, at heart, a comic character, driven by a blind obsession.

尽管杰克·唐纳吉是一个多面人物，但他并不是一个戏剧性人物；从本质上讲，他是一个喜剧人物，被一种盲目的痴迷所驱使。

Both dramatic and comic characters seek an object of desire. In that they are the same. Their core difference, however, is awareness. As a dramatic character pursues his quest, he has sense enough to step back and realize that his struggle could get him killed. Not the comic character: His core desire blinds him. His self-deluded mind fixates on his desire and pursues it, wildly unaware. This lifelong mania influences, if not controls, his every choice. 3

戏剧人物和喜剧人物都追求欲望的对象，这一点他们相同。然而，他们最根本的区别在于意识。戏剧人物在追求的过程中，会保持清醒的头脑，意识到自己的挣扎可能会害死自己。而喜剧人物则不然：他内心深处的欲望蒙蔽了他的双眼。他自欺欺人的头脑执着于欲望，疯狂地追逐它，浑然不觉。这种终生的执念影响着，甚至控制着他的每一个选择。

Jack Donaghy blithely obsesses on an aristocratic lifestyle more suited to the 1920s than today. “Made love on a beach surrounded by a privacy circle of English-trained butlers” sounds like a diary entry by Wallis Simpson before she became Duchess of Windsor. Vacationing on yachts recalls scenes from F. Scott Fitzgerald novels. The love of his life, a fellow aristocrat named Avery, graduated from Choate and Yale. Jack, like the Princeton alumnus he is, disdains jeans and only reads nonfiction.

杰克·唐纳吉痴迷于一种更适合20世纪20年代而非当今的贵族生活方式。“在沙滩上，被一群受过英式训练的管家环绕着，享受私密的性爱”听起来像是沃利斯·辛普森在成为温莎公爵夫人之前的日记。在游艇上度假让人想起菲茨杰拉德小说中的场景。他一生挚爱，一位名叫艾弗里的贵族同胞，毕业于乔特中学和耶鲁大学。杰克，就像他作为普林斯顿大学校友的身份一样，鄙视牛仔裤，只读非虚构类书籍。

His syntactically balanced sentences roll out rounded with relative clauses: “In order for our merger to stay attractive to our friends at Kabletown, we have to seem like a sexy, profitable company, and we’re almost pulling it off,” and “If I say ‘No,’ then I will be required to say ‘Yes’ to something else in the future, and the stakes in the future might be higher.” His dialogue sounds like a tuxedoed businessman talking shop in a penthouse cocktail party. The tuxedo, in fact, is Jack’s eveningwear of choice. In Season 1, Liz asks him why he’s wearing a tux in his office and he explains, “It’s after six. What am I, a farmer?”

他那句句结构严谨、用关系从句修饰的句子流畅自然：“为了让我们的合并案继续吸引卡布尔镇的朋友们，我们必须看起来像一家性感又盈利的公司，而且我们几乎做到了。”以及“如果我说‘不’，那么将来我就不得不对其他事情说‘是’，而且未来的风险可能会更大。”他的对话听起来就像一个穿着燕尾服的商人，在顶层公寓的鸡尾酒会上谈论生意。事实上，燕尾服正是杰克最喜欢的晚礼服。在第一季中，莉兹问他为什么在办公室里穿着燕尾服，他解释说：“现在都六点多了。我难道是农民吗？”

Like the clothes they wear, vocabulary and syntax dress characters inside and out.

就像衣服一样，词汇和句法从内到外地塑造着人物。

SIDEWAYS

侧身

Rex Pickett writes both novels and films. In addition to his first novel Sideways , and a second novel, La Purisima , he wrote the screenplay for the 2000 Oscar-winning short film MY MOTHER DREAMS THE SATAN’S DISCIPLES IN NEW YORK.

雷克斯·皮克特既创作小说，也参与电影剧本创作。除了他的第一部小说《杯酒人生》（Sideways）和第二部小说《圣洁的圣母》（La Purisima）之外，他还为2000年奥斯卡最佳短片奖获奖作品《我母亲梦见撒旦的门徒在纽约》（MY MOTHER DREAMS THE SATAN’S DISCIPLES IN NEW YORK）撰写了剧本。

Screenwriters Jim Taylor and Alexander Payne earned writers’ credit on the best-written episode of the Jurassic Park franchise, JURASSIC PARK III. In addition, they have collaborated with great success on CITIZEN RUTH, ELECTION, ABOUT SCHMIDT, and SIDEWAYS. More recently, Payne wrote and directed THE DESCENDANTS (2011) and directed NEBRASKA (2013).

编剧吉姆·泰勒和亚历山大·佩恩凭借《侏罗纪公园3》中剧本最佳的一集而获得编剧署名。此外，他们还成功合作创作了《公民露丝》、《选举》、《关于施密特》和《杯酒人生》。近年来，佩恩自编自导了《后裔》（2011），并执导了《内布拉斯加》（2013）。

SIDEWAYS, which Payne directed from their adaptation of Pickett’s novel, has won a long list of international nominations and awards, including an Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay. As their choice of subject matter suggests, these writers are attracted to life’s losers and their futile, often comic struggles to win.

佩恩执导、改编自皮克特小说的电影《杯酒人生》（SIDEWAYS）斩获众多国际奖项及提名，其中包括奥斯卡最佳改编剧本奖。正如他们选择的题材所示，这些编剧似乎对人生中的失败者以及他们徒劳无功、却又常常充满喜剧色彩的求胜之路情有独钟。

SIDEWAYS is, by genre, an education plot. Four simple conventions define this very difficult genre:

从类型上看，《杯酒人生》是一部教育题材的影片。这个非常复杂的题材由四个简单的惯例定义：

1. The protagonist begins the story with a life-denying mindset. He finds no meaning in the world around him or himself in it.

1. 故事开始时，主人公抱持着否定生命的心态。他觉得周围的世界毫无意义，他自己也感觉不到生命的意义。

2. The story will arc the protagonist’s downbeat point of view to a positive, life-affirming stance.

2. 故事将主人公从悲观消极的态度转变为积极乐观、充满生活态度的态度。

3. A “teacher” character will help guide the protagonist’s revolution in attitude.

3. “老师”角色将帮助引导主人公发生态度上的变革。

4. The story’s greatest source of conflict will come from the protagonist’s beliefs, emotions, habits, and attitudes—in other words, from an inner conflict with his own self-destructive nature.

4. 故事中最大的冲突来源将来自主人公的信仰、情感、习惯和态度——换句话说，来自他与自身自我毁灭本性的内心冲突。

The education plot is a natural genre for a novel because prose allows the writer to directly invade a character’s deepest thoughts and feelings. In Pickett’s first-person novel, for example, his protagonist whispers his secret fears and doubts directly into the reader’s ear. Onscreen, however, this literary form becomes extremely difficult, requiring superb dialogue to imply within a character what the novelist can explicitly state on page.

教育题材的故事自然而然地适合改编成小说，因为散文允许作者直接深入角色的内心世界，触及他们最深层的思想和情感。例如，在皮克特的第一人称小说中，主人公会直接在读者耳边低语他内心深处的恐惧和疑虑。然而，在银幕上，这种文学形式却变得极其困难，需要精妙的对话来暗示角色内心的想法，而这些想法小说家只能在纸面上明确表达。

The screenplay’s protagonist, Miles, is a pudgy, divorced, failed novelist who teaches junior high school English. Although no one makes the accusation onscreen, he’s clearly an alcoholic who hides his dependency behind the mask of (in Miles’s words from the novel) a wine cognoscente. The title SIDEWAYS is never explained in the film, but in the novel “sideways” is slang for drunk. To “go sideways” means to get very, very drunk.

剧本的主人公迈尔斯是个身材矮胖、离异、写作失败的小说家，在初中教英语。虽然电影里没人直接指责他，但他显然是个酒鬼，把自己的酗酒问题伪装成（用迈尔斯在小说里的话来说）一个葡萄酒鉴赏家。电影里并没有解释片名“SIDEWAYS”的含义，但在小说里，“sideways”是“醉酒”的俚语。“go sideways”的意思是喝得酩酊大醉。

The “teacher” role is filled by the intelligent and beautiful Maya, who’s also divorced, also a wine lover. Midway through the film, Miles and Maya spend an evening with Miles’s pal, Jack, and Maya’s friend, Stephanie. They all end up at Stephanie’s house. When Jack and Stephanie retire to the bedroom, Miles and Maya sit in the living room sipping a wine from Stephanie’s excellent collection. At first they chat about how they met (he was a customer in a restaurant where she waits tables), then the subject turns first to Miles (his novel), then to Maya (her MA in agrology), and, finally, to their mutual love of wine.

“老师”的角色由聪明美丽的玛雅扮演，她也离异，同样热爱葡萄酒。影片中段，迈尔斯和玛雅与迈尔斯的朋友杰克以及玛雅的朋友斯蒂芬妮共度良宵。他们最终都去了斯蒂芬妮家。杰克和斯蒂芬妮回卧室后，迈尔斯和玛雅坐在客厅里，品尝着斯蒂芬妮珍藏的美酒。起初，他们聊起了相识的经过（迈尔斯是玛雅打工的餐厅的顾客），然后话题先是转向迈尔斯（他的小说），接着是玛雅（她的农学硕士学位），最后，又回到了他们共同的爱好——葡萄酒。

MAYA

玛雅

Why are you so obsessed with Pinot? That’s all you ever order.

你为什么这么迷恋黑皮诺？你每次都只点这个牌子的酒。

Miles smiles wistfully at the question. He searches for the answer in his glass and begins slowly.

迈尔斯对这个问题露出了怅然的微笑。他从酒杯中寻找答案，然后缓缓地开始品尝。

MILES

迈尔斯

I don’t know. It’s a hard grape to grow. As you know. It’s thin-skinned, temperamental. It’s not a survivor like Cabernet that can grow and thrive anywhere… and withstand neglect. Pinot’s only happy in specific little corners of the world, and it needs a lot of doting. Only the patient and faithful and caring growers can do it, can access Pinot’s fragile, achingly beautiful qualities. It doesn’t come to you. You have to come to it, see? It takes the right combination of soil and sun… and love to coax it into its fullest expression. Then, and only then, its flavors are the most thrilling and brilliant and haunting on the planet.

我不知道。黑皮诺葡萄很难种，你也知道。它皮薄，娇气。它不像赤霞珠那样生命力顽强，能在任何地方生长繁茂，也能经受住疏于照料。黑皮诺只在世界上的特定角落才能茁壮成长，需要悉心呵护。只有耐心、忠诚、细心的种植者才能做到，才能领略黑皮诺脆弱而又令人心碎的美丽。它不会主动找上门来，你必须主动去寻找它，明白吗？它需要合适的土壤和阳光……以及爱，才能充分展现其魅力。只有这样，它的味道才能成为地球上最令人兴奋、最璀璨、最令人难忘的佳酿。

Maya has found this answer revealing and moving.

玛雅觉得这个答案既发人深省又令人感动。

MILES

迈尔斯

(CONT’D)

（续）

I mean, Cabernets can be powerful and exalting, but they seem prosaic to me for some reason. By comparison. How about you, why do you like wine so much?

我的意思是，赤霞珠葡萄酒固然浓郁醇厚，令人陶醉，但不知为何，相比之下，它们在我看来却显得平淡无奇。你呢，你为什么这么喜欢葡萄酒？

MAYA

玛雅

I suppose I got really into wine originally through my ex-husband. He had a big, kind of show-off cellar. But then I found out that I have a really sharp palate, and the more I drank, the more I liked what it made me think about.

我最初迷上葡萄酒大概是因为我的前夫。他有个很大的、有点炫耀性质的酒窖。但后来我发现自己味觉很灵敏，而且喝得越多，就越喜欢它带给我的思考。

MILES

迈尔斯

Yeah? Like what?

是吗？比如什么？

MAYA

玛雅

I started to appreciate the life of wine, that it’s a living thing, that it connects you more to life. I like to think about what was going on the year the grapes were growing. I like to think about how the sun was shining that summer and what the weather was like. I think about all those people who tended and picked the grapes. And if it’s an old wine, how many of them must be dead by now. I love how wine continues to evolve, how every time I open a bottle the wine will taste different than if I had uncorked it on any other day, or at any other moment. A bottle of wine is like life itself—it grows up, evolves and gains complexity. Then it peaks—like your ’61—and begins its steady, inexorable decline. And it tastes so fucking good.

我开始欣赏葡萄酒的生命，它有生命，它能让你与生活更紧密地联系在一起。我喜欢想象葡萄生长的那一年发生了什么。我喜欢想象那个夏天阳光的照射情况，以及当时的天气。我会想到所有那些照料和采摘葡萄的人们。如果这是一瓶陈年佳酿，那么他们当中又有多少人如今已不在人世了呢？我喜欢葡萄酒不断演变的过程，每次开瓶，它的味道都会与以往任何一天、任何时刻开瓶时的味道有所不同。一瓶葡萄酒就像生命本身——它成长、演变，变得复杂。然后，它会达到巅峰——就像你那瓶1961年的酒——然后开始稳步、不可阻挡地衰落。而它的味道真是他妈的棒极了。

Now it’s Miles’s turn to be swept away. Maya’s face tells us the moment is right, but Miles remains frozen. He needs another sign, and Maya is bold enough to offer it: she reaches out and places one hand atop his.

现在轮到迈尔斯被玛雅的魅力所俘虏了。玛雅的表情告诉我们时机已到，但迈尔斯却依然僵立不动。他还需要另一个信号，而玛雅大胆地给了他：她伸出手，将一只手放在他的手上。

MILES

迈尔斯

But I like a lot of wines besides Pinot too. Lately I’ve really been into Rieslings. Do you like Rieslings?

但我除了黑皮诺之外，也喜欢很多其他葡萄酒。最近我特别喜欢雷司令。你喜欢雷司令吗？

She nods, a Mona Lisa smile on her lips.

她点点头，嘴角挂着蒙娜丽莎般的微笑。

MILES

迈尔斯

(pointing)

（指着）

Bathroom over there?

那边是洗手间吗？

MAYA

玛雅

Yeah.

是的。

Miles gets up and walks out. Maya sighs and gets an American Spirit out of her purse.

迈尔斯起身走了出去。玛雅叹了口气，从钱包里掏出一支美国精神香烟。

Like the scene from Leonard’s Out of Sight , this is a seduction, but in this case between two very sensitive people—the sage earth mother, Maya, and the emotional wallflower, Miles. Like the scene from LOST IN TRANSLATION below, it’s an exchange of revelations. But they are not confessing personal failures; rather, the underlying actions of both characters are bragging and promising. Miles and Maya try hard to sell their virtues to each other.

如同伦纳德的《战略高手》中的场景，这也是一场诱惑，只不过这次是在两个非常敏感的人之间——睿智的“大地母亲”玛雅和情感内敛的“壁花”迈尔斯。如同下文《迷失东京》中的场景，这是一场自我剖析。但他们并非在坦白个人的失败；相反，两人的行为背后都隐藏着炫耀和承诺。迈尔斯和玛雅竭力向对方推销自己的优点。

In the subtext of Miles’s big speech, he invites Maya to come to him, and in the subtext of her reply she does, and brilliantly. So that she leaves no doubt about her desire for him, she even touches his hand and smiles a “Mona Lisa” come-on. But Miles chickens out, bolts for the toilet, and leaves her in frustration.

在迈尔斯那番慷慨激昂的演讲中，他暗含着邀请玛雅来见他的意思；而玛雅的回应也暗含着邀请，而且做得非常出色。为了让迈尔斯毫不掩饰自己的爱慕之情，她甚至轻轻触碰了他的手，露出了蒙娜丽莎般妩媚的微笑。然而，迈尔斯却临阵退缩，匆匆跑进洗手间，留下玛雅独自一人，倍感失望。

Once again, note how the scene is designed around a trialogue. Wine becomes the third thing under which the subtext pulses.

再次注意，这一幕的设计围绕着三方对话展开。葡萄酒成为了贯穿始终的第三要素，其背后蕴含着更深层次的含义。

Now I’ll rewrite their speeches on-the-nose, pulling the bragging and promising from the subtext and putting it directly into the text by eliminating the third thing.

现在我要彻底改写他们的演讲稿，把潜台词里的吹嘘和承诺去掉，直接放到正文里，删除第三点。

MILES

迈尔斯

I’m a hard guy to get to know. I’m thin-skinned and temperamental. I’m not tough, not a hard-hearted survivor. I need a cozy, safe little world and a woman who will dote on me. But if you are patient and faithful and caring, you will bring out my beautiful qualities. I cannot come to you. You must come to me. Do you understand? With the right kind of coaxing love I will turn into the most thrilling and brilliant man you could ever have the luck to know.

我这个人不太容易了解。我心思细腻，喜怒无常。我不是个坚强的人，也不是个冷酷无情的幸存者。我需要一个温馨安全的小世界，需要一个会宠爱我的女人。但如果你耐心、忠诚、体贴，你就能激发我身上美好的品质。我不能去找你，你必须来找我。你明白吗？只要你用正确的方式去引导我，我就会变成你此生有幸遇到的最迷人、最耀眼的男人。

MAYA

玛雅

I am a woman with a passion for life. Hour after hour, day after day, season after season, I thrive in the golden light of time, savoring its every precious spell. I am in my prime—old enough to have learned from mistakes, young enough to grow and evolve, so that with every passing day I will become ever more complex, ever more amazing. When I peak, and believe me, I am peaking at this very moment with you, I will taste good, oh so very, very good. Please fuck me.

我是一个热爱生活的女人。日复一日，时时刻刻，我沐浴在时光的金色光芒中，细细品味它每一个珍贵的瞬间。我正值盛年——既有足够的阅历从错误中吸取教训，又足够年轻去成长蜕变，因此，每一天，我都会变得更加复杂，更加迷人。当我达到巅峰之时——相信我，此刻与你在一起，我正处于巅峰——我会变得无比美味，哦，真的，真的非常美味。请与我缠绵。

A person might feel such feelings, might even think such thoughts in some vague way, but no one would ever say these embarrassingly painful things aloud. This bald language becomes impossibly corny when put directly into a living room chat about ideas and yearnings. Fine actors would choke on it.

一个人或许会有这样的感受，甚至可能在脑海中隐约闪过这样的念头，但没人会把这些令人尴尬痛苦的事情说出口。这种直白的语言，如果直接用在客厅里闲聊想法和渴望的时候，会显得极其矫揉造作。就连演技精湛的演员也会被它噎住。

Yet these are exactly the actions that Taylor and Payne want their characters to take: To put themselves in the very best light and to promise the moon in an effort to win the love of the other with seductive boasts and promises. So, how to write these beats of action into dialogue? Let them converse.

然而，这恰恰是泰勒和佩恩想要笔下人物采取的行动：竭尽全力展现自己最好的一面，并许下种种美好的承诺，试图用诱人的吹嘘和承诺赢得对方的芳心。那么，如何将这些行动融入对话呢？让他们直接对话。

How do people converse? By using what they know as a third thing. And what do these characters know? Miles and Maya are experts on two subjects: wine and themselves. They have extensive, practical knowledge of the former and romanticized, idealized knowledge of the latter. So using the nature of wine and its cultivation as metaphor for their own natures, they each campaign to win the esteem of the other.

人们如何交流？他们会运用已知的知识作为第三要素。那么，这些人物又了解什么呢？迈尔斯和玛雅都是两方面的专家：葡萄酒和他们自己。他们对前者拥有丰富的实践经验，而对后者则有着浪漫化、理想化的认知。因此，他们以葡萄酒的特性及其酿造工艺为隐喻，分别代表各自的性格，并以此来赢得对方的尊重。

As I laid out in the beginning of this section, the key is vocabulary. Character-specific dialogue originates in a character’s unspoken desires and the actions he takes to satisfy those desires. Actions become talk that translates the character’s implicit thoughts and feelings into explicit words—the precise words that only that specific character would use at that specific moment taking that specific action.

正如我在本节开头所述，关键在于词汇。人物特有的对话源于人物未曾言明的欲望以及他为满足这些欲望而采取的行动。行动转化为语言，将人物隐含的想法和感受转化为明确的词语——只有特定的人物在特定的时刻采取特定的行动时才会使用的精准词汇。

Drawing on Pickett’s novel, Payne and Taylor have added their knowledge and insight to Miles and Maya and given each a character-specific voice and vocabulary. In order to seduce, Miles and Maya describe themselves in the language of wine. Compare, for example, Miles’s modal language, his sensitive adjectives and adverbs, to Maya’s bold naming, her nouns and verbs.

佩恩和泰勒借鉴了皮克特的小说，将他们的知识和见解融入到迈尔斯和玛雅这两个角色中，赋予他们各自独特的嗓音和词汇。为了吸引异性，迈尔斯和玛雅都用葡萄酒的语言来描述自己。例如，比较一下迈尔斯的情态动词、他细腻的形容词和副词，以及玛雅大胆的命名、她的名词和动词。

Miles: “Thin-skinned,” “temperamental,” “doting,” “faithful,” “caring,” “fragile,” “have to come to,” “achingly beautiful,” “thrilling,” “brilliant,” “haunting,” “really been into…”

迈尔斯：“敏感的”、“喜怒无常的”、“溺爱的”、“忠诚的”、“体贴的”、“脆弱的”、“需要慢慢接受”、“美得令人心碎的”、“激动人心的”、“才华横溢的”、“令人难忘的”、“真的非常着迷……”

Maya: “Life,” “living thing,” “connects to life,” “life itself,” “sun,” “shining,” “summer,” “evolves,” “gains,” “peaks,” “tastes so fucking good…”

玛雅语：“生命”、“生物”、“与生命相连”、“生命本身”、“太阳”、“闪耀”、“夏天”、“进化”、“获得”、“高峰”、“味道真他妈好……”

These writers have an ear for their characters.

这些作家对笔下的人物有着敏锐的洞察力。

#↩

PART 4

第四部分

DIALOGUE DESIGN

对话设计

#↩

12

STORY/SCENE/DIALOGUE

故事/场景/对话

Now and then, we experience a flawed story that squandered surprisingly good dialogue. We have all waded through badly told stories with dreadful dialogue, but we rarely encounter a superbly told story ruined by lousy dialogue. And the reason is simple: Quality storytelling inspires quality dialogue.

我们偶尔会遇到一些故事本身存在缺陷，却浪费了原本精彩的对话。我们都曾读过一些叙事糟糕、对话拙劣的故事，但很少会遇到因为糟糕的对话而毁掉一个精彩绝伦的故事。原因很简单：好的故事才能孕育出好的对话。

Like a hectic fever, bad dialogue warns of a festering infection deep within a story. But because struggling writers often mistake the symptom for the disease, they try to bandage scenes by obsessively rewriting their dialogue, thinking that once the talk is right, the telling will heal. But maladies of character and event cannot be cured by scratching dialogue raw with draft after draft of paraphrases.

糟糕的对话就像高烧一样，预示着故事深处潜藏着一场正在恶化的疾病。但由于写作新手常常把症状误认为病根，他们试图通过反复修改对话来掩盖问题，以为只要对话本身没问题，叙述就能迎刃而解。然而，人物和情节的缺陷是无法通过一遍又一遍地修改对话来治愈的。

To put it as clearly as I can: Until you know what you are talking about, you cannot know how your characters go about talking. The order in which you create your story’s components and how you bring all these pieces together is unique to you. But no matter how helter-skelter the process, an author ultimately gathers godlike knowledge of form (event and cast design) and content (cultural, historical, and psychological substance) to support the telling from the bottom up, to create dialogue from the inside out. Dialogue is the final step, the frosting of text atop layers and layers of subtext.

说得越清楚越好：在你真正了解自己要写什么之前，你无法知道你的角色会如何对话。你创作故事各个组成部分的顺序，以及如何将它们组合在一起，都是你独有的。但无论创作过程多么混乱，作者最终都会积累起对形式（事件和人物设计）和内容（文化、历史和心理层面）的深刻理解，从而自下而上地构建故事，由内而外地创造对话。对话是最后一步，是层层叠叠的潜台词之上的点睛之笔。

So, before we examine dialogue design, let’s review the basic components of story design.

因此，在探讨对话设计之前，让我们先回顾一下故事设计的基本组成部分。

INCITING INCIDENT

诱发事件

At the opening of a story, the central character’s life rests in a state of relative balance. She has her ups and downs. Who doesn’t? Nonetheless, the protagonist holds reasonable sovereignty over her existence—until something happens that radically upsets that equilibrium. We call this event the inciting incident .

故事伊始，主人公的生活处于相对平衡的状态。她也有起起伏伏，谁又不是如此呢？尽管如此，主人公对自己的生活仍拥有相当的掌控权——直到发生某件事，彻底打破了这种平衡。我们称这个事件为诱发事件。

To incite means to start; “incident” means “event.” This first major event starts the story by throwing the protagonist’s life out of kilter. The inciting incident could happen by decision (she decides to quit her job and open her own business) or by coincidence (lightning strikes her store and she loses her business). The inciting incident could move her life powerfully to the positive (she invents a brilliant new product) or to the negative (a business rival steals her invention). The inciting incident could be a massive social event (her corporation goes bankrupt) or a quiet inner event (she comes to realize in her heart of hearts that she hates her career). 1

“incite”意为“开始”；“incident”意为“事件”。第一个重大事件打破了主人公生活的平衡，从而开启了故事。这个引发事件可能是主人公的决定（例如，她决定辞职创业），也可能是偶然事件（例如，她的店铺被闪电击中，导致生意失败）。这个引发事件可能使她的生活发生巨大的积极转变（例如，她发明了一种绝妙的新产品），也可能使她的生活走向消极（例如，她的商业竞争对手窃取了她的发明）。这个引发事件可能是一场巨大的社会事件（例如，她的公司破产），也可能是一场悄无声息的内心事件（例如，她终于从内心深处意识到自己厌恶这份工作）。

STORY VALUES

故事价值观

The impact of the inciting incident decisively changes the charge of the value at stake in the character’s life. Story values are binaries of positive/negative charge such as life/death, courage/cowardice, truth/lie, meaningfulness/meaninglessness, maturity/immaturity, hope/despair, justice/injustice, to name but a few. A story may incorporate any number, variety, and possible combinations of story values, but it anchors its content in an irreplaceable core value.

引发事件的影响决定性地改变了角色生命中价值的走向。故事价值是二元对立的，具有正负两面性，例如生/死、勇气/怯懦、真/假、意义/虚无、成熟/不成熟、希望/绝望、正义/不义等等。一个故事可以包含任意数量、种类和组合的各种价值，但其内容始终根植于一个不可替代的核心价值。

A core value is irreplaceable because it determines the story’s fundamental nature. Change core value, change the genre. For example, if a writer were to extract love/hate from her characters’ lives and substitute morality/immorality, this switch in core values would pivot her genre from love story to redemption plot.

核心价值观不可替代，因为它决定了故事的根本性质。改变核心价值观，就会改变故事类型。例如，如果一位作家从人物生活中剔除爱恨情仇，代之以道德与不道德，那么这种核心价值观的转变就会使故事类型从爱情故事转变为救赎故事。

The values in scenes can be very complex, but at minimum, every scene contains at least one story value at stake in the character’s life. This value either relates to or matches the story’s core value. Scenes dramatize change in the charge of this value. A scene may begin with its value(s) at either a purely positive charge, purely negative charge, or an admixture of both. Through conflicts and/or revelations, the opening charge of value(s) changes. It could reverse (positive to negative, negative to positive), intensify (positive to doubly positive, negative to doubly negative), or wane (purely positive to a weaker positive, purely negative to a weaker negative). The precise moment in which the charge of one or more values changes is a scene’s turning point. Therefore, a story event occurs the instant a value at stake in a scene changes charge. 2

场景中的价值观可能非常复杂，但至少每个场景都包含至少一个与角色生活息息相关的故事价值观。这个价值观要么与故事的核心价值观相关，要么与之相符。场景通过戏剧化的方式展现了这些价值观的强度变化。一个场景开始时，其价值观可能处于纯粹的正面状态、纯粹的负面状态，或者两者兼而有之。通过冲突和/或揭示，这些价值观的初始强度会发生变化。它可能逆转（由正面变为负面，由负面变为正面）、增强（由正面变为双重正面，由负面变为双重负面），或者减弱（由纯粹的正面变为较弱的正面，由纯粹的负面变为较弱的负面）。一个或多个价值观强度发生变化的确切时刻，就是场景的转折点。因此，当场景中某个关键价值观的强度发生变化时，就会发生一个故事事件。

THE COMPLEX OF DESIRE

欲望情结

Everyone wants reasonable sovereignty over existence. By throwing life out of balance, the inciting incident arouses the natural human desire to restore balance. Essentially, therefore, all stories dramatize the human struggle to move life from chaos to order, from imbalance to equilibrium.

每个人都渴望对自身生存拥有合理的自主权。打破生活平衡的事件会激发人类恢复平衡的本能欲望。因此，从本质上讲，所有故事都戏剧化地展现了人类努力使生活从混乱走向秩序、从失衡走向平衡的过程。

Characters act because needs demand deeds, but the complexity of life swirls through a labyrinth of desires. Ultimately the art of storytelling merges and organizes many streams of desire into a flow of events. The storyteller picks and chooses only those desires he wishes to express in the specific scenes that progress his story from beginning to end. To understand this process, we need to examine the components of desire and how they propel storytelling.

人物行动源于需求，但生活的复杂性却交织于错综复杂的欲望迷宫之中。最终，叙事艺术将众多欲望汇聚并组织成一股事件流。叙事者精心挑选并呈现他想要表达的欲望，并将其融入推动故事从始至终发展的特定场景。为了理解这一过程，我们需要探究欲望的构成要素及其如何驱动叙事发展。

Desire is a figure in five dimensions:

欲望是一个五维概念：

1. Object of desire

1. 欲望对象

2. Super-intention

2. 超意图

3. Motivation

3. 动机

4. Scene intention

4. 场景意图

5. Background desires

5. 背景愿望

1. Object of Desire

1. 欲望对象

In the wake of the inciting incident, the protagonist conceives of an object of desire, that which he feels he must have in order to put his life back on an even keel. This object could be something physical, like a stash of money; or situational, like revenge for an injustice; or ideational, like a faith to live by. Example: A humiliation on the job (inciting incident) has damaged the protagonist’s reputation, radically upsetting the balance of his life, so he seeks a victory in the workplace (object of desire) to restore balance.

在引发事件发生后，主人公会构想出一个渴望之物，他觉得必须拥有它才能让生活重回正轨。这个渴望之物可以是物质的，比如一笔积蓄；也可以是情境性的，比如对不公的报复；还可以是观念性的，比如一种赖以生存的信仰。例如：工作中的羞辱（引发事件）损害了主人公的名誉，彻底打破了他生活的平衡，因此他渴望在工作中取得胜利（渴望之物）来恢复平衡。

2. Super-Intention

2. 超意图

The super-intention motivates a character to pursue the object of desire. This phrase restates the protagonist’s conscious desire in terms of his deepest need. For example, the object of desire above (victory in the workplace) rephrased as the super-intention becomes: to gain inner peace through a public triumph.

超意图促使人物追求欲望对象。这句话用主人公最深层的需求来重述他意识层面的欲望。例如，上文提到的欲望对象（职场上的胜利）用超意图重新表述为：通过公开的胜利获得内心的平静。

In other words, the object of desire is objective, whereas the super-intention is subjective: what the protagonist wants versus the emotional hunger that drives him. The former term gives the writer a clear view of the crisis scene that waits at the end of the story when the protagonist will get or fail to get his object of desire. The latter term connects the writer to the feelings within the protagonist, the inner need that drives the telling.

换句话说，欲望的对象是客观的，而超意图则是主观的：主人公想要什么，以及驱使他行动的情感渴望。前者使作者能够清晰地看到故事结尾的危机场景——主人公能否得到他所渴望的对象。后者则将作者与主人公的内心感受联系起来，即驱动故事叙述的内在需求。

In every story, the protagonist’s super-intention is somewhat generic (for example, to win justice through revenge, to find happiness in intimate love, to live a meaningful life), but the exact object of desire (for example, a dead villain, the ideal mate, a reason not to commit suicide) gives a story originality. Whatever the object of desire may be, the protagonist wants it because he must satisfy his super-intention, his profound longing for a life in balance.

在每个故事中，主人公的终极目标都有些千篇一律（例如，通过复仇伸张正义，在爱情中找到幸福，过上有意义的生活），但具体的渴望对象（例如，死去的恶棍，理想的伴侣，放弃自杀的理由）却赋予了故事独特的个性。无论渴望的对象是什么，主人公想要得到它，是因为他必须满足自己的终极目标，满足他对平衡生活的深切渴望。

3. Motivation

3. 动机

Do not confuse either object of desire or super-intention with motivation. The first two answer “what” questions: What does the character consciously want? What does he subconsciously need? Motivation answers “why.” Why does a character need what he feels he needs? Why does he want his particular object of desire? And if he gets what he wants, will this success actually satisfy his need?

不要将欲望对象或超意图与动机混淆。前两者回答的是“是什么”的问题：角色有意识地想要什么？他潜意识里需要什么？而动机回答的是“为什么”。角色为什么需要他感觉自己需要的东西？他为什么想要他特定的欲望对象？如果他得到了他想要的东西，这种成功真的能满足他的需求吗？

The roots of motivation reach deep into childhood and, for that reason, are often irrational. How much you understand the whys of your character’s needs and wants is up to you. Some writers, like Tennessee Williams, obsess on motivation; some writers, like Shakespeare, ignore it. Either way, what’s essential to the writing of scenes and their dialogue is an understanding of the characters’ conscious and subconscious desires. 3

动机的根源可以追溯到童年时期，因此，它们往往是非理性的。你对笔下人物的需求和欲望背后的原因理解多少，取决于你自己。有些作家，比如田纳西·威廉姆斯，非常注重动机的刻画；有些作家，比如莎士比亚，则对此视而不见。无论如何，对于场景和对话的写作而言，理解人物的意识和潜意识欲望至关重要。

4. Scene Intention

4. 场景意图

A scene shapes a character’s moment-by-moment struggle toward his ultimate life goal. Scene intention names what a character immediately wants as a step in the long-term effort of the super-intention. As a result, the actions he takes and the reactions he gets in each scene will either take him closer to or bend him farther away from his object of desire.

场景塑造了角色在实现最终人生目标过程中每时每刻的挣扎。场景意图指明了角色在实现其长期目标（即超意图）的过程中，当下想要达成的目标。因此，他在每个场景中的行动和得到的反馈，要么会让他更接近目标，要么会让他离目标更远。

If the writer were to grant the character his scene intention, the scene would stop. For example, in a police interrogation scene, Character A wants Character B to stop questioning him. A’s scene intention is to stop the interrogation. If B were to give up and leave the room, the scene would end. B, on the other hand, wants A to reveal a secret. From B’s point of view, his scene intention is to discover the secret. If A were to confess, that too would end the scene. Scene intention names the character’s imminent, conscious desire—what he wants right now. 4

如果作者满足了角色的场景意图，场景就会停止。例如，在警察审讯的场景中，角色A希望角色B停止审问他。A的场景意图是停止审讯。如果B放弃并离开房间，场景就会结束。另一方面，B希望A透露一个秘密。从B的角度来看，他的场景意图是发现这个秘密。如果A坦白了，场景也会结束。场景意图表达的是角色即将产生的、有意识的欲望——他此刻想要什么。

5. Background Desires

5. 背景愿望

A character’s background desires limit his choices of action. Each of us is constantly aware of the state of the relationship between ourselves and every person and every object we encounter in life—our safety in traffic, which table the maître d’ gives us, our place in the hierarchy of coworkers, to name only three public examples. We are acutely aware of our private rapport with friends, family, and lovers. We’re also attuned to our innermost self, our relative state of physical, mental, emotional, and moral well-being. What’s more, we’re aware of our place in the flow of time, of our experiences in the past, the knife-edge of the present, and what we hope for the future. These complex interwoven relationships create our background desires.

人物的背景欲望限制了他的行动选择。我们每个人都时刻关注着自己与生活中遇到的每个人和每件事物之间的关系——例如，我们在交通中的安全、餐厅领班给我们安排的座位、我们在同事等级制度中的地位等等，这些只是三个公共领域的例子。我们敏锐地感知着与朋友、家人和爱人的私人关系。我们也关注着自己的内心世界，关注着我们身体、心理、情感和道德的相对状态。此外，我们还意识到自己在时间长河中的位置，意识到过去的经历、当下的紧张感以及对未来的期许。这些错综复杂的关系构成了我们的背景欲望。

Relationships become desires in this way: Once created, relationships form the foundation of our existence; they create the system that gives us our sense of identity and security in life. Our well-being depends on them. We try to eliminate relationships of negative value, while at the same time maintaining, if not improving, positive relationships. At the very least, we want relationships of either kind kept within reasonable control.

人际关系由此演变为欲望：一旦建立，人际关系便构成我们存在的基石；它们构建起赋予我们身份认同感和安全感的系统。我们的幸福感依赖于它们。我们试图消除负面关系，同时维护甚至改善积极的人际关系。至少，我们希望将各种关系都控制在合理的范围内。

Background desires, therefore, not only cement the status quo of a character’s life; they temper his behavior. Background desires form the web of restraints that follows every character into every scene. These fixed desires for stability limit and temper the character’s actions. They influence what the character will or will not say to get what he wants.

因此，背景欲望不仅巩固了人物生活的现状，也制约着他们的行为。背景欲望构成了一张束缚之网，如影随形地伴随着每个人物进入每一个场景。这些对稳定的固定渴望限制并约束着人物的行动。它们影响着人物为了达成目标而选择说什么或不说什么。

In principle, the more relationships of positive value a character accumulates in life, the more restrained, the more “civilized” his behavior. The reverse is also true: When a character has nothing to lose… he’s capable of anything.

原则上，一个人一生中积累的积极人际关系越多，他的行为就越克制、越“文明”。反之亦然：当一个人一无所有时……他什么都做得出来。

In some cultures, because of social mores, you can speak your mind; in other cultures, for the same reason, you must obey unspoken codes of address and keep your thoughts to yourself. Humanity’s enormous range of cultures creates a spectrum of polar extremes that spans from cultures that are all subtext with hardly any text versus cultures that are all text and very little subtext. In the social sciences, these polar extremes are known as high-context versus low-context cultures. 5 In fiction, they determine the relative quantity of text versus subtext.

在某些文化中，由于社会习俗，你可以畅所欲言；而在另一些文化中，出于同样的原因，你必须遵守不成文的礼仪规范，并将自己的想法藏在心底。人类文化的丰富多样性造就了一个极端的光谱，从几乎没有明文、只有潜台词的文化，到只有明文、只有极少潜台词的文化，两者之间形成了鲜明的对比。在社会科学领域，这些极端文化被称为高语境文化和低语境文化。在小说创作中，它们决定了明文和潜台词的相对比例。

High-context cultures have a strong sense of tradition and history. They change very slowly over time, and so from generation to generation their members hold many beliefs and experiences in common. A high-context culture will be relational, collectivistic, intuitive, and contemplative. It places high value on interpersonal relationships within a close-knit community (Native Americans, for example).

高语境文化具有强烈的传统和历史意识。它们随时间推移变化缓慢，因此其成员世世代代都拥有许多共同的信仰和经历。高语境文化注重关系、集体主义、直觉和沉思。它高度重视紧密社群内的人际关系（例如美洲原住民文化）。

As a result, within these in-groups many things can be left unsaid because their members can easily draw inferences from their shared culture and experiences. The Italian Mafia is such an in-group. In THE GODFATHER, when Michael Corleone says, “My father made him an offer he couldn’t refuse,” an entire episode of extortion becomes violently clear. Michael then goes on to make the event explicit to Kay Adams because she’s not in the in-group.

因此，在这些内部群体中，许多事情可以保持沉默，因为成员们可以轻易地从共同的文化和经历中推断出彼此的想法。意大利黑手党就是这样一个内部群体。在《教父》中，当迈克尔·柯里昂说“我父亲给了他一个无法拒绝的条件”时，一整段敲诈勒索的真相便昭然若揭。之后，迈克尔又向凯·亚当斯详细讲述了这件事，因为她并非这个群体的一员。

High-context cultures, such as those in the Middle East and Asia, have low ethnic and social diversity. They value community over the individual. In-group members rely on their common background, rather than words, to explain situations. Consequently, dialogue within high-context cultures calls for extreme economy and precise word choices because within such settings a few subtle words can implicitly express a complex message.

高语境文化，例如中东和亚洲的文化，种族和社会多样性较低。它们重视社群而非个人。群体成员依靠共同的背景而非语言来解释情况。因此，在高语境文化中进行对话需要极其简洁和精准的用词，因为在这种语境下，寥寥数语便可隐含地表达复杂的含义。

Conversely, characters in low-context cultures, such as North America, tend to explain things at greater length because the people around them come from a wide variety of racial, religious, class, and nationalistic backgrounds. Even within the same general cultures these differences appear. Compare, for example, two American stereotypes: a Louisianan (a high-context culture) and a New Yorker (a low-context culture). The former uses a few tacit words and prolonged silences, while the latter talks frankly and at length.

相反，在北美等低语境文化中，人物往往会更详细地解释事情，因为他们周围的人来自不同的种族、宗教、阶级和民族背景。即使在同一种文化中，这些差异也依然存在。例如，比较一下两种典型的美国人：路易斯安那州人（高语境文化）和纽约人（低语境文化）。前者说话含蓄，沉默寡言，而后者则直言不讳，滔滔不绝。

What’s more, in low-context cultures, shared experiences change constantly and drastically, thus creating communication gaps from one generation to the next. In immigrant societies, such as the United States, parents and children have notoriously difficult communication problems that result in long, loud arguments. Characters become more verbose and explicit as subtext shallows out.

此外，在低语境文化中，共同经历不断发生剧烈变化，从而造成代际沟通障碍。在像美国这样的移民社会中，父母与子女之间存在着众所周知的沟通难题，导致长时间的激烈争吵。随着潜台词的淡化，人物的言辞也变得更加冗长和直白。

FORCES OF ANTAGONISM

对立力量

As a character pursues her object of desire, she consciously or instinctively designs actions that she hopes will cause helpful, enabling reactions from her world, reactions that she expects will move her closer to a balanced life. But instead of getting cooperation, her actions arouse forces of antagonism that thwart her efforts. Her world reacts differently, more powerfully, in contrast or contradiction to what she reckoned. This surprising violation of expectation may move her further from or closer to her object of desire, but whether positive or negative, the turn will not happen in the way she imagined.

当一个角色追求她渴望的对象时，她会自觉或本能地设计一些行动，希望这些行动能引发周围环境的积极反应，使她更接近平衡的生活。然而，她的行动非但没有得到配合，反而激起了对抗的力量，阻碍了她的努力。她所处的环境做出了截然不同、更为强烈的反应，与她预想的完全相反。这种出乎意料的违背预期可能会让她离渴望的对象更远或更近，但无论结果如何，都不会如她所愿。

The term forces of antagonism does not necessarily refer to an antagonist or villain. Villains inhabit certain genres, and in his proper place an arch-villain, such as the Terminator, can be a fascinating antagonist. But by forces of antagonism I mean opposing forces from any or all of the four levels of conflict:

“对抗力量”一词并不一定指反派或恶棍。恶棍通常出现在某些类型作品中，而像终结者这样的超级反派，在合适的语境下，的确可以成为一个引人入胜的反派角色。但我所说的对抗力量，指的是来自冲突的四个层次中的任何一个或全部的对立力量：

1. Physical conflict: The titanic forces of time, space, and every object in the manmade and natural universe. Not enough time to get something done, too far to go to get something, nature’s tumult from tornadoes to viruses. To these natural forces, fantasy genres add supernatural and magical forces of amazing variety and unlimited imaginings.

1. 物理冲突：时间、空间以及人造和自然宇宙中一切物体的巨大力量。时间不够用，无法完成某件事；路途遥远，无法到达目的地；自然界的种种动荡，从龙卷风到病毒，无所不包。除了这些自然力量之外，奇幻题材还加入了种类繁多、想象力无限的超自然和魔法力量。

2. Social conflict: The powerful forces of institutions and the people who run them. All levels of government and the legal systems they enforce, all religions, the military, corporations, schools, hospitals, even charities. Every institution shapes itself into a pyramid of power. How do you gain it? Lose it? How do you move up and down the power pyramid?

2. 社会冲突：机构及其管理者所拥有的强大力量。各级政府及其执行的法律体系、所有宗教、军队、企业、学校、医院，甚至慈善机构，都构成了这种冲突。每个机构都构建了一个权力金字塔。如何获得权力？如何失去权力？如何在权力金字塔中上下移动？

3. Personal conflict: The problematic relationships of intimacy between friends, family, and lovers that range from infidelity to divorce to petty squabbles over money.

3. 个人冲突：朋友、家人和恋人之间亲密关系中出现的问题，包括不忠、离婚以及因金钱而起的琐碎争吵。

4. Inner conflict: Contradictory forces within a character’s mind, body, and emotions. How to cope when your memory betrays you, your body breaks down, or your feelings overwhelm your common sense?

4. 内心冲突：角色内心、身体和情感中存在的矛盾力量。当记忆背叛你、身体崩溃或情感压倒理智时，该如何应对？

Over the progressive dynamics of a story, forces from these various levels build in power and focus, deepening and widening the story. As these complications build, the protagonist reacts by digging deeper and deeper into her willpower as well as her mental, emotional, and physical capacities in an ever-escalating effort to restore life’s balance. 6

随着故事的推进，来自不同层面的力量不断增强，汇聚成一股强大的力量，深化并拓展了故事的内涵。随着这些复杂因素的累积，主人公不断挖掘自身的意志力以及精神、情感和身体潜能，竭尽全力地恢复生活的平衡。

SPINE OF ACTION

行动的脊梁

A story’s spine of action traces the protagonist’s constant quest for his object of desire. His persistent pursuit, driven by his super-intention, struggling against the story’s forces of antagonism, propels the entire telling from the inciting incident through the story’s progressions to the protagonist’s eventual crisis decision and climactic action, ending in a moment of resolution.

故事的脊梁贯穿始终，主人公不断追寻着他渴望的对象。他执着的追求，源于他强烈的愿望，与故事中各种对抗力量的抗争，推动着整个故事从最初的导火索，经过情节发展，最终到达主人公面临危机抉择和高潮行动的阶段，并以圆满的结局告终。

What the protagonist (or any character) does from scene to scene or says from line to line is simply a behavioral tactic. For no matter what happens on the surface, no matter what outer activity catches our eye and ear, the protagonist’s grand, unrelenting spine of action runs under every scene.

主人公（或任何角色）在场景间的一举一动，或台词间的一言一行，都不过是一种行为策略。因为无论表面发生什么，无论什么外在活动吸引了我们的眼球和耳畔，主人公宏大而坚定的行动主线始终贯穿于每一个场景之中。

Because other people are the most common source of life’s complications, the most common activity taken along the spine of action is talk. And like the five major movements of story (inciting incident, progressive complications, crisis, climax, resolution), talk has its own five stages—desire, sense of antagonism, choice of action, action/reaction, expression.

因为人际关系是生活中各种复杂情况最常见的来源，所以贯穿整个行动过程的最常见活动就是交谈。就像故事的五大情节（诱发事件、渐进式复杂情况、危机、高潮、结局）一样，交谈也有其自身的五个阶段——欲望、对抗感、行动选择、行动/反应、表达。

Of these stages, expression is the activity that carries the character’s action into his world. It’s most often speech, but it may be clenching a fist or planting a kiss, hurling a plate across a room or smiling deceitfully—all the nonverbal activities that may accompany or substitute for dialogue.

在这些阶段中，表达是将角色的行为带入其所处世界的一种活动。它通常是言语，但也可能是握紧拳头或献上一个吻，把盘子扔过房间或露出虚伪的笑容——所有这些非语言活动都可能伴随对话或替代对话。

Imagine this story: You are a first-time writer trying to break into the profession. In that secret place where you hide from the world, you feel incomplete as you teeter through life. You dream of a creative triumph that would give you wholeness and balance: a novel, play, or script of surpassing quality (object of desire). Your need to achieve artistic success (super-intention) drives your writing life (spine of action).

想象一下这样的故事：你是一位初出茅庐的作家，正努力在这个行业闯出一片天地。在你躲避尘世喧嚣的秘密角落里，你感到人生不完整，步履蹒跚。你梦想着创作上的成功，它能让你获得完整和平衡：一部卓越的小说、戏剧或剧本（渴望的对象）。你对艺术成功的渴望（超乎寻常的意图）驱动着你的写作生涯（行动的脊梁）。

You sit down (scene) and pursue your desire by attempting to write a page of dialogue (choice of action) because you hope it will unlock insight into your characters and story events to come (scene intention). But before you begin, you know that a pernicious horde of forces will oppose your efforts—your mother will call, the baby will wake up, fears of failure will churn your belly, the temptation to quit will whisper in your ear (sources of antagonism). In the face of these forces, you choose to stay at your desk and persevere (choice of action). And so you write and rewrite the same passage over and over (action). But with each pass your dialogue stumbles, sputters, and only gets worse (force of antagonism). You spew a chain of hyphenated profanity, “Stupid damn… mother… son of a…” (expression). Suddenly, from out of nowhere, a new angle of attack springs to mind (reaction). You pound out dialogue that reshapes the scene with surprising power (action). You lean back and mutter, “Wow, where did that come from?” (expression).

你坐下来（场景），试图写一页对话（行动选择），因为你希望它能帮助你更好地理解人物和即将发生的故事情节（场景意图）。但在动笔之前，你知道会有一大堆阻力阻挠你的努力——母亲会打电话来，婴儿会醒来，对失败的恐惧会让你心烦意乱，放弃的念头会在耳边低语（阻力来源）。面对这些阻力，你选择留在书桌前坚持下去（行动选择）。于是你一遍又一遍地修改同一段对话（行动）。但每一次修改，你的对话都磕磕绊绊，磕磕绊绊，而且越来越糟糕（阻力来源）。你忍不住爆出一连串带连字符的脏话：“该死的……妈的……狗娘养的……”（表达）。突然，一个全新的思路从脑海中浮现（反应）。你铿锵有力地吐出一句台词，以惊人的力量重塑了场景（动作）。你向后靠去，喃喃自语道：“哇，这台词是从哪儿来的？”（表情）。

Every immediate desire and action, no matter how seemingly trivial, even a thing as infinitesimal as taking a thought-filled sip of coffee, is somehow affixed to your future desire and your pursuit of literary achievement. Moment by moment, your life moves along a spine of action from desire to sense of antagonism to choice of action to action/reaction to expression.
