每一个当下的欲望和行动，无论多么看似微不足道，哪怕是像若有所思地啜饮一口咖啡这样微不足道的小事，都以某种方式与你未来的渴望和对文学成就的追求息息相关。你的生命分分秒秒都沿着一条行动的脊梁推进：从欲望到对抗感，再到行动的选择，再到行动/反应，最终到表达。

As for you, so for your characters. As for your life, so for your stories. 7

你如此，你的角色亦如此。你的人生如此，你的故事亦如此。

STORY PROGRESSION

故事进程

The scenes along the spine of action not only move dynamically across the positive/negative charges of the story’s values, but they arc along a progression of conflict. As a character struggles toward his object of desire, the forces of antagonism build, calling on greater and greater capacities from within him, generating greater and greater jeopardy in his life, demanding greater and greater willpower to make more and more risk-taking decisions.

贯穿故事主线的场景不仅动态地展现了故事价值观的正反两面，而且沿着冲突的推进不断演进。随着角色努力追求心仪之物，反抗的力量也随之增强，激发出他内在越来越强大的潜能，使他的生活面临越来越大的危险，需要他拥有越来越强大的意志力去做出越来越冒险的决定。

Finally, there comes a moment when the protagonist has exhausted all possible actions, save one. Faced with the most powerful and focused conflict of his life, the protagonist must choose one final action in a last effort to put his life back in balance. He makes his crisis decision, chooses a climactic action, and takes it. Out of the climax he either gets what he wants or fails to get it. End of story. A last resolution scene may be needed to tie up any loose ends and let the reader/audience gather their thoughts and recoup their emotions. 8

最后，主人公会面临一个时刻，他已经用尽了所有可能的行动，只剩下一个选择。面对人生中最强大、最紧迫的冲突，主人公必须做出最后的抉择，以期重回生活的平衡。他做出危机抉择，选择了一个决定性的行动，并付诸实施。在高潮之后，他要么如愿以偿，要么一无所获。故事结束。或许还需要一个最终的结局场景来收束所有未解之谜，让读者/观众整理思绪，平复情绪。

TURNING POINTS

转折点

Ideally, every scene contains a turning point. A turning point pivots the instant the value at stake in the scene dynamically changes from positive to negative or negative to positive. This change moves the character either farther from (negative) or closer to (positive) his object of desire than the previous scene’s turning point. Turning points progress the story along its spine of action toward the final satisfaction or dissatisfaction of the protagonist’s desire at story climax.

理想情况下，每个场景都包含一个转折点。转折点发生在场景中关键价值发生动态变化的那一刻，即从正面变为负面，或从负面变为正面。这种变化使角色与他渴望的对象之间，要么比前一个场景的转折点更远（负面），要么更近（正面）。转折点推动故事沿着其主线发展，最终在故事高潮中，主人公的欲望得到满足或落空。

A turning point can be created in only one of two ways: by action or revelation. An event turns either by an immediate, direct action, or by the disclosure or discovery of a secret or previously unknown fact. Because dialogue can express both deeds (“I’m leaving for good”) and information (“I married you for your money”), it can turn a scene’s value charge by action, revelation, or both at once. If a scene has no turning point, if the value charge does not change in any kind or degree, then the scene is merely an exposition-filled nonevent. Too many nonevents in a row and a story collapses into tedium. 9

转折点只能通过两种方式产生：行动或揭示。事件的转折要么源于直接的行动，要么源于对秘密或先前未知事实的披露或发现。由于对话既可以表达行为（“我要永远离开”），也可以表达信息（“我嫁给你是为了你的钱”），因此它可以通过行动、揭示或两者兼而有之的方式改变场景的价值。如果一个场景没有转折点，如果其价值没有任何改变，那么这个场景就只是一个充满背景介绍的空洞场景。连续出现太多这样的空洞场景，故事就会变得乏味无趣。

SCENE PROGRESSION

场景推进

“Progression” means the continuous topping of previous actions or events. A scene creates a turning point that progresses the storyline by topping the turning point in the previous scene. Each sequence of events causes a moderate change that surpasses the previous in terms of its impact, for better or worse, on the lives of the characters. Each act climax delivers a major impact.

“推进”指的是不断超越先前的行动或事件。场景创造了一个转折点，通过超越前一场景的转折点来推动故事情节的发展。每一系列事件都会带来适度的变化，其影响（无论好坏）都超过前一次。每一幕的高潮都带来重大影响。

But no matter whether a scene creates a minor, moderate, or major change in the story, the scene progresses within itself by building beats of behavior, so that each action/reaction tops the previous beat to and around the scene’s turning point. 10

但无论一个场景对故事的影响是轻微的、中等的还是重大的，它都是通过构建一系列行为节奏来推动剧情发展的，使得每一个动作/反应都超越了前一个节奏，直至场景的转折点。

THE BEAT

节拍

Like the physical objects governed by Newton’s third law of motion, every verbal action causes a reaction. The beat is a unit of scene design that contains both an action and a reaction from someone or something somewhere in the setting. Generally, the response comes from another character, but it could come from within the acting character himself.

就像受牛顿第三运动定律支配的物理物体一样，每一个语言动作都会产生相应的反应。节奏是场景设计的一个基本单元，它包含一个动作以及来自场景中某处某人或某物的反应。通常，这种反应来自另一个角色，但也可能来自表演角色自身。

Suppose Character A were to insult Character B. Character B could react in myriad ways, perhaps with an insult of his own or by laughing at Character A. Or Character A could react to his own action and apologize. Or Character A could regret what he said, feel remorse, but say nothing. Or Character B, who doesn’t speak English, greets the insult with a smile. These moment-to-moment exchanges of action/reaction build a scene. Ideally, each beat tops the previous beat and leads to the next. This continuous surpassing of previous beats within a scene generates dialogue progression, shaping the scene’s beats to and around its turning point. 11

假设角色A侮辱了角色B。角色B可能会有多种反应，比如回敬侮辱，或者嘲笑角色A。角色A也可能为自己的行为道歉。或者角色A可能后悔自己说过的话，感到懊悔，但什么也不说。又或者，不懂英语的角色B会面带微笑地回应侮辱。这些瞬息万变的行动/反应构成了场景。理想情况下，每个节奏都超越前一个节奏，并引出下一个节奏。场景中这种不断超越前一个节奏的循环推动了对话的发展，塑造了场景的节奏，使其围绕转折点展开。

Beats are best identified by gerunds. A gerund is a noun that names an action by adding “-ing” to a verb. The four possible beats above, for example, could be labeled insulting/ridiculing, insulting/apologizing, insulting/regretting, insulting/greeting. The use of gerunds to name the actions beneath exchanges of dialogue is the best way I know to stop yourself from writing on-the-nose.

用动名词来描述语气语调最为有效。动名词是一种通过在动词后加“-ing”来表示动作的名词。例如，上面提到的四个语气语调可以分别标记为侮辱/嘲笑、侮辱/道歉、侮辱/后悔、侮辱/问候。用动名词来描述对话中的动作，是我所知的避免直白表达的最佳方法。

FIVE STEPS OF BEHAVIOR

行为的五个步骤

When characters use what they say to pursue what they want, the rambling activity of conversation turns into the focused action of dialogue. Verbal action, indeed all behavior, moves through five distinct steps from desire to antagonism to choice to action to expression. Because people often act and react in a flash, these steps seem fused together because they fly from first to last in a blur. But that’s life, not writing. No matter how quickly and instinctively things might happen, the five steps are always there. To make the flow of character behavior as clear as possible, let’s examine these five steps in slow-motion detail:

当角色运用言语追求自身目标时，漫无目的的对话便转化为目标明确的行动。言语行为，乃至所有行为，都遵循五个截然不同的步骤：从欲望到对抗，再到选择、行动和表达。由于人们常常在瞬间做出反应，这些步骤看似交织在一起，如同疾驰而过。但那是生活，而非写作。无论事情发生得多么迅速和本能，这五个步骤始终存在。为了尽可能清晰地展现角色行为的流程，让我们以慢镜头的方式细致地审视这五个步骤：

1. Desire: The moment a character’s life is thrown out of balance (inciting incident), he, in reaction, conceives of (or at least senses) what he must achieve in order to restore life’s balance (object of desire). His overarching purpose to reach the object of desire (super-intention) motivates his active pursuit (spine of action). As he moves along the story’s spine, at each specific moment (scene) he must satisfy an immediate want (scene intention) in order to progress toward his object of desire. The foreground desire of scene intention and underlying pull of the super-intention influence each choice of action he makes and takes. But his background desires limit his choices because they influence what he cannot or will not do.

1. 欲望：当一个角色的生活失去平衡（诱发事件）时，他会本能地构想（或至少感知到）自己必须达成的目标，才能恢复生活的平衡（欲望对象）。他达成欲望对象的总体目标（超意图）驱动着他积极的追求（行动主线）。随着故事沿着主线推进，在每个特定的时刻（场景），他都必须满足一个迫切的需求（场景意图），才能朝着欲望对象迈进。场景意图所代表的前景欲望和超意图的潜在牵引力影响着他做出的每一个行动选择。但他的次要欲望限制了他的选择，因为它们决定了他不能或不愿做什么。

2. Sense of Antagonism: Before the character can act, however, he must sense or recognize the immediate forces of antagonism that block his way. How much of his understanding is conscious or subconscious, realistic or mistaken, depends on the psychology of the character, the nature of his situation, and the story the author is telling.

2. 对抗感：然而，在角色采取行动之前，他必须感知或认识到阻碍他前进的直接对抗力量。他对这种对抗的理解有多少是意识层面的，有多少是潜意识层面的；有多少是现实的，又有多少是错误的，取决于角色的心理、他所处情境的性质以及作者所讲述的故事。

3. Choice of Action : The character then chooses to take a specific action in an effort to cause a reaction from his world that will move him toward his scene intention. Again, how deliberate or instantaneous this choice may be is relative to the nature of the character and his situation.

3. 行动选择：角色选择采取特定行动，试图引发周围环境的反应，从而推动剧情朝着他预期的方向发展。同样，这种选择是深思熟虑还是瞬间做出，取决于角色的性格和所处情境。

4. Action: The activity the character chooses to carry out his action may be physical or verbal or both. Desire is the source of action, and action is the source of dialogue.

4. 行动：角色选择执行其行动的方式可以是肢体上的，也可以是语言上的，或者两者兼而有之。欲望是行动的源泉，而行动又是对话的源泉。

5. Expression: To the extent that the character’s action needs words to carry it out, the writer composes dialogue.

5. 表达：当人物的行动需要用语言来表达时，作者就会创作对话。

To create a scene, an author must separate the links in this chain of behavior and give consideration to each. (How conscious or subconscious this “consideration” may be varies from writer to writer. Oscar Wilde once noted that an author spends a whole morning putting in a comma and a whole afternoon taking it out. But that’s Wilde. For some writers, commas just get in the way.) Finally, in however long it may take to pen one perfect speech, the writer pieces the links back together so they happen in the breath of time it takes an actor to act or a reader to read.

为了创作一个场景，作者必须将这一系列行为拆解开来，并对每一个环节都进行仔细斟酌。（这种“斟酌”是有意识的还是无意识的，因人而异。奥斯卡·王尔德曾说过，有的作者会花一上午的时间添加一个逗号，然后又花一下午的时间把它删掉。但那是王尔德的情况。对某些作家来说，逗号只是碍事而已。）最后，无论写出一段完美的台词需要花费多少时间，作者都会将这些环节重新串联起来，使之在演员表演或读者阅读所需的时间里自然流畅地呈现出来。

It is impossible to know exactly what a character will say in this fifth step until we answer these questions: What does the character want? What stops him from getting it? What will he choose to do in an effort to achieve it?

在回答以下问题之前，我们不可能确切地知道角色在第五步中会说什么：角色想要什么？是什么阻止他得到它？为了实现它，他会选择做什么？

A scene lives, not in the activity of talking, but in the action the character takes by talking. So before we write dialogue, we must ask questions and find answers that guide us down the stream from desire to antagonism to choice to action, ending in expression—the dialogue that helps shape and turn the scene.

场景的生命力不在于对话本身，而在于角色通过对话所采取的行动。因此，在撰写对话之前，我们必须提出问题并找到答案，引导我们从欲望出发，最终走向对抗，再到选择和行动，最终形成表达——也就是塑造和推动场景发展的对话。

INTRODUCTION TO SEVEN CASE STUDIES

七个案例研究简介

The five stages of character behavior blend in concert to create a progressive subtext that ultimately finds expression in dialogue. To demonstrate how this works, we’ll examine five dramatized scenes—two from teleplays, one each from a play, a novel, a screenplay—plus two passages of narratized dialogue in prose. Each author employs a distinctively different balance, type, and intensity of conflict. The quality of conflict determines the quality of action, and the quality of action determines the quality of talk. As a result, the behaviors of characters, the dynamic of beats, and, above all, the tonality of each scene’s dialogue play out in seven distinctively different ways over the next six chapters.

人物行为的五个阶段相互交织，共同构建出一个渐进的潜台词，最终在对话中得以展现。为了阐释这一机制，我们将分析五个戏剧化的场景——两个选自电视剧本，一个选自话剧，一个选自小说，一个选自电影剧本——以及两段散文叙述对话。每位作者都运用了截然不同的冲突平衡、类型和强度。冲突的质量决定了行动的质量，而行动的质量又决定了对话的质量。因此，在接下来的六章中，人物的行为、节奏的动态，以及最重要的，每个场景对话的语气，都将以七种截然不同的方式呈现出来。

Balanced conflict: In the “Two Tonys” episode from THE SOPRANOS, series creator David Chase and cowriter Terence Winter turn their characters loose in a hard-fought duelogue of equals.

平衡的冲突：在《黑道家族》的“两个托尼”一集中，剧集创作者大卫·蔡斯和联合编剧特伦斯·温特让他们的角色展开了一场势均力敌的激烈对决。

Comic conflict: The “Author, Author” episode from FRASIER, written by Don Seigel and Jerry Perzigian, exaggerates balanced conflict to its lunatic limits.

喜剧冲突：《欢乐一家亲》中的“作者，作者”一集，由唐·西格尔和杰瑞·佩尔齐吉安编剧，将平衡冲突夸张到了疯狂的程度。

Asymmetric conflict: In A Raisin in the Sun , playwright Lorraine Hansberry sets one character’s aggressive verbal action against another’s quiet resistance.

不对称冲突：在《阳光下的葡萄干》中，剧作家洛兰·汉斯贝里将一个角色咄咄逼人的言语行为与另一个角色的默默抵抗进行对比。

Indirect conflict: In The Great Gatsby , F. Scott Fitzgerald’s characters manipulate each other with words of covert antagonism.

间接冲突：在《了不起的盖茨比》中，F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德笔下的人物通过隐晦的敌对言语相互操纵。

Reflexive conflict: Chapter Seventeen compares the uses of narratized dialogue in two novels: In Fräulein Else , Arthur Schnitzler uses this technique to wage inner conflict within his protagonist, self against self; whereas in The Museum of Innocence , Orhan Pamuk’s protagonist confesses his inner wars directly to the reader.

反思性冲突：第十七章比较了两部小说中叙述性对话的运用：在《艾尔莎小姐》中，阿图尔·施尼茨勒运用这种技巧来挑起主人公内心的冲突，即自我与自我的斗争；而在《纯真博物馆》中，奥尔罕·帕慕克的主人公则直接向读者坦白了他内心的战争。

Implied conflict: In LOST IN TRANSLATION, screenwriter Sofia Coppola suspends her characters in depths of inner tension, self versus self, played out in the shadows of conflicts from the past.

隐含冲突：在《迷失东京》中，编剧索菲亚·科波拉将她的角色置于深深的内心冲突之中，自我与自我的较量，在过去冲突的阴影下上演。

The following chapters demonstrate a working method for scene analysis that separates a scene into its components, pulls out their subtextual actions, labels them with gerunds, and then discovers how these actions express themselves in dialogue. The technique begins with breaking a scene into its beats.

以下章节将展示一种场景分析的工作方法，该方法将场景分解为各个组成部分，提取出其中的潜台词，用动名词标记它们，然后探究这些潜台词如何在对话中表达出来。该技巧首先将场景分解成各个节奏节拍。

Over the decades, writers have evolved three different meanings for the term “beat.” In the outlining stages of a screenplay, some filmmakers use the word to name a story’s key turning points: “In the story’s first beat they meet; in the second beat they fall in love.” Playwrights and screenwriters often place the term between parentheses in a column of dialogue, e.g., (beat), to signal a short pause. But for the purposes of exploring how a scene’s inner life inspires its dialogue, I use “beat” in its original sense: a unit of action/reaction. An action starts a beat; a corresponding reaction ends it.

几十年来，作家们对“beat”（节奏）一词衍生出了三种不同的含义。在剧本的构思阶段，一些电影制作人用这个词来指代故事的关键转折点：“故事的第一个节奏是他们相遇；第二个节奏是他们坠入爱河。”剧作家和编剧经常在对话中用括号将“beat”括起来，例如“(beat)”，表示短暂的停顿。但为了探讨场景的内在内涵如何激发对话，我使用“beat”的原始含义：一个动作/反应单元。一个动作开启一个节奏；相应的反应结束一个节奏。

When scenes feel lifeless or false, the cause is rarely found in the language of the dialogue. Rather, flaws fester in the subtext. For that reason, we break a scene into its beats in order to uncover the misshapen subtextual actions and reactions that cause these faults. A skillful analysis then guides the redesign of the scene’s beats and, with that, the re-creation of its dialogue.

当场景显得死气沉沉或虚假做作时，原因很少在于对话的语言本身，而是潜台词中存在缺陷。因此，我们会将场景拆解成各个节奏点，以揭示导致这些缺陷的、扭曲的潜台词行为和反应。通过巧妙的分析，我们可以重新设计场景的节奏点，并据此重新创作对话。

No matter how many times a pattern of action/reaction repeats, it constitutes one, and only one, beat. A scene cannot progress unless its beats change, and beats cannot change until the characters change their tactics. Indeed, the most common early warning sign of an ailing scene is repetitious beats—characters using the same tactic to take essentially the same action, again and again, but using different words, speech after speech, to do it. These duplicating beats hide beneath a scene’s verbiage, and it often takes an insightful, beat-by-beat analysis to bring this flaw to light.

无论某种行为/反应模式重复多少次，它都只构成一个节拍。场景的推进离不开节拍的变化，而节拍的变化又离不开角色策略的改变。事实上，场景缺陷最常见的早期预警信号就是节拍重复——角色反复使用相同的策略，做出本质上相同的动作，却每次都换一种说法，用不同的语言来表达。这些重复的节拍隐藏在场景的语言表述之下，往往需要逐节拍进行深入的分析才能发现这一缺陷。

Before we move on, however, a note of caution: No one can teach you how to write. I can only define the shape and function of a scene, lay out its components, and demonstrate their inner workings. Although the principles of scene design illuminate creativity, they are not the creative process itself. The following six chapters are logical, after-the-fact analyses of finished work. My breakdowns do not presume to know the artist’s process or follow his or her actual writing experience.

不过，在继续之前，有一点需要注意：没有人能教会你如何写作。我只能定义场景的结构和功能，梳理其组成部分，并展示其内在运作机制。虽然场景设计的原则能够启发创造力，但它们并非创作过程本身。接下来的六章是对已完成作品的逻辑分析。我的分析并不假定自己了解艺术家的创作过程，也不试图模拟他或她的实际写作体验。

Of this, however, I am certain: Writing rarely flows in a straight line. Creativity likes to zigzag—trial/error, elation/depression, this way and that, draft after draft after draft. Knowledge of story and scene design strengthens the work, provokes ideas, and guides rewrites, but an author must discover through her personal creative process exactly how to use her talent and expertise to move from inspiration to last draft.

然而，有一点我可以肯定：写作很少一帆风顺。创作过程往往曲折蜿蜒——反复尝试、欣喜与沮丧，不断修改润色。对故事和场景设计的了解固然能增强作品的质量，激发灵感，指导修改，但作者必须通过自身的创作过程，才能真正领悟如何运用自身的天赋和经验，将灵感转化为最终定稿。

#↩

13

BALANCED CONFLICT

平衡冲突

THE SOPRANOS

黑道家族

THE SOPRANOS ran on HBO from January 1999 to June 2007. Its eighty-six episodes tell the story of Tony Soprano, a New Jersey Mafia don, portrayed by James Gandolfini. David Chase, the series creator, built this complex, multidimensional character around a core contradiction: On one hand, Tony commits violent, tyrannical, murderous acts; on the other, he falls victim to paralyzing nightmares and sudden, unexplained panic attacks.

《黑道家族》于1999年1月至2007年6月在HBO播出。这部共86集的剧集讲述了新泽西黑手党教父托尼·索普拉诺（詹姆斯·甘多菲尼饰）的故事。该剧的创作人大卫·蔡斯围绕着一个核心矛盾塑造了这个复杂而多面的角色：一方面，托尼犯下了暴力、暴虐、谋杀的罪行；另一方面，他又饱受噩梦和突发性、无法解释的恐慌症的折磨。

Realizing that his panic disorder could cost him his life, Tony seeks the help of a psychiatrist, Dr. Jennifer Melfi (Lorraine Bracco). Over the next four seasons, their therapy sessions struggle through moral dilemmas, sexual tensions, and bouts of Tony’s raging temper, until Tony finally breaks off his therapy.

意识到自己的恐慌症可能会危及生命，托尼寻求精神科医生詹妮弗·梅尔菲（洛雷恩·布拉科饰）的帮助。在接下来的四季中，他们的治疗过程中充满了道德困境、性张力以及托尼暴躁的脾气，直到托尼最终中断了治疗。

In Episode 1 of Season 5, he convinces himself that he’s deeply in love with Melfi and goes on a romantic quest. He has often flirted with her, but now he puts on his best courting behavior and asks her out for dinner twice. Twice she declines, but he persists until he finally confronts her in her office.

在第五季第一集中，他认定自己深深爱上了梅尔菲，并展开了一场浪漫的追求。他之前就经常和她调情，但现在他使出浑身解数，两次邀请她共进晚餐。她两次都拒绝了他，但他锲而不舍，最终在她的办公室里当面质问她。

I will work through their confrontation with an eye to the scene’s four essential modes: 1) how the five steps of behavior (desire, antagonism, choice, action, expression) translate into the characters’ scene intentions and tactics, 2) how their beats of action/reaction shape progression, 3) how the values at stake arc their changing charges, and 4) how these foundational layers impel and inspire the scene’s character-specific dialogue.

我将着眼于场景的四个基本模式来分析他们的对抗：1）行为的五个步骤（欲望、对抗、选择、行动、表达）如何转化为角色的场景意图和策略；2）他们的行动/反应节奏如何塑造情节发展；3）所涉价值观如何影响他们不断变化的立场；以及4）这些基础层面如何推动和启发场景中特定角色的对话。

I will take you through this inside-out analysis to remind you once again that character talk is the final result of everything that went before, a surface manifestation of the layers of life beneath the words. The stronger the inner scene, the more powerful the dialogue.

我将带你进行一次由内而外的分析，再次提醒你，人物对话是之前一切的最终结果，是隐藏在言语之下的生活层次的表面体现。内心世界越深刻，对话就越有力。

To begin: If we were to ask Tony what he wants (desire) and what’s stopping him from getting it (antagonism), he would tell us that he wants to win Jennifer Melfi’s love, but she resists because she doesn’t see the other Tony, the nice-guy Tony. Tony’s scene intention is to seduce Melfi, and his tactic (action) is to prove that he’s a nice guy.

首先：如果我们问托尼他想要什么（欲望）以及是什么阻碍了他得到它（敌意），他会告诉我们他想赢得詹妮弗·梅尔菲的芳心，但她拒绝是因为她看不到另一个托尼，那个善良的托尼。托尼在这场戏中的意图是诱惑梅尔菲，而他的策略（行动）是证明他是个好人。

If we were to ask Dr. Melfi the same questions, she would tell us that she wants to help Tony overcome his emotional problems (desire), but his impulse to take their relationship from professional to personal makes that impossible (antagonism). Melfi’s scene intention is to help Tony change for the better, and her tactic (action) is to confront him with the truth.

如果我们问梅尔菲医生同样的问题，她会告诉我们，她想帮助托尼克服他的情感问题（愿望），但他急于将两人的关系从职业发展到私人关系，这使得一切努力都无法实现（对抗）。梅尔菲的意图是帮助托尼改过自新，而她的策略（行动）是让他直面真相。

However, if we look past Tony’s romantic gestures, we sense that the ruling value of his life is power. His Romeo persona masks his subconscious lust, not for sex, but for ownership. He needs to dominate the only person who has ever wielded power over him—Dr. Melfi.

然而，如果我们抛开托尼的浪漫举动，就会发现他生命中最看重的其实是权力。他扮演的罗密欧式人物掩盖了他潜意识里的欲望，并非性欲，而是占有欲。他需要支配唯一一个曾经对他拥有过权力的人——梅尔菲医生。

But Melfi packs double-fisted punches of truth and morality. She knows the truth of Tony’s immature, sociopathic nature. In the face of her high moral standards and courage (antagonism), Tony flinches and withers. So his dark self, hungry to regain the upper hand, silently urges him to get her into bed and give her the orgasmic thrill of a lifetime. With that, he thinks, her moral shell will crack and she will fall into his arms, enthralled and subservient. His subconscious desire (super-intention), therefore, is to subjugate Melfi.

但梅尔菲的言辞犀利而有力，她深知托尼不成熟、反社会的本性。面对她高尚的道德标准和勇气（或称对抗），托尼畏缩不前，意志消沉。于是，他内心深处渴望重新掌控局面的阴暗面，驱使他把她弄上床，让她体验毕生难忘的性高潮。他心想，这样一来，她坚守的道德防线就会崩溃，她就会臣服于他，对他百依百顺。因此，他潜意识里的欲望（或称超意识的意图）是征服梅尔菲。

Dr. Melfi tells Tony she wants to help him, therapeutically; and consciously, of course, she means what she says. But if we look beneath her prudent, professional personality, we sense the very opposite of discretion and objectivity. We see a high-risk adventurer.

梅尔菲医生告诉托尼，她想在治疗方面帮助他；当然，从意识层面来说，她是真心实意的。但如果我们透过她谨慎专业的外表，就会感受到与谨慎和客观截然相反的一面。我们看到的是一个敢于冒险的人。

Consider this: During her university years, Melfi could have taken any number of career paths, but she chose clinical psychiatry. Now, picture a psychiatrist’s day.

想想看：梅尔菲在大学期间有很多职业选择，但她选择了临床精神病学。现在，想象一下精神科医生的一天。

Imagine the enormous mental stamina and emotional courage it must take to burrow into the dark unknown of life-wrecked souls. Think of the damage done to the therapist as she listens with empathy to the wretched, tortured, heartbreaking confessions of neurotic after psychotic, hour by hour, day by day. Almost no one, it seems to me, would devote herself to that profession unless, deep inside, she found exploring the danger-filled jungles of other people’s minds fascinating, even exhilarating.

想象一下，要深入那些饱受生活摧残的灵魂深处，需要多么巨大的精神耐力和情感勇气。想想看，当治疗师日复一日、时时刻刻倾听一个又一个神经质患者痛苦、折磨、令人心碎的忏悔时，她自身会承受怎样的创伤。在我看来，几乎没有人会甘愿投身于这份职业，除非她内心深处真的对探索他人充满危险的心灵丛林充满兴趣，甚至感到兴奋。

Dr. Melfi’s core dimension sends her risk-averse characterization up against her risk-enticed true character. To express her contradictory nature, the writers propel her through a series-long, dynamic, on-again, off-again relationship with Tony Soprano.

梅尔菲博士的核心特质在于她规避风险的性格与她内心深处冒险的本性之间的冲突。为了展现她矛盾的性格，编剧安排她与托尼·索普拉诺之间展开了一段贯穿全剧、跌宕起伏、分分合合的复杂关系。

Soon after Dr. Melfi takes Tony Soprano as a patient, she discovers he’s a murderous Mafia don. At first, ending the relationship seems her only option, but in time she overcomes her disgust and continues treating him. Her probing questions about his parents often provoke his rage and a break in therapy. But once time quiets his rage, she always takes Tony back, even though she knows that someday he may turn his violence against her.

梅尔菲医生接手托尼·索普拉诺的治疗后不久，便发现他竟然是位杀人如麻的黑手党老大。起初，她觉得结束这段关系是唯一的选择，但随着时间的推移，她克服了内心的厌恶，继续为他治疗。她对托尼父母的探究性提问常常激怒他，导致治疗中断。但一旦时间平息了他的怒火，她总是会重新接纳他，即使她知道，总有一天他可能会将暴力转向她。

Near the end of Season 1, Tony tells her that rival mobsters plan to kill her because they fear he may have revealed Mafia secrets during therapy. Melfi goes into hiding while Tony hunts down and kills the assassins. Once the danger lifts, Melfi resumes Tony’s sessions.

第一季接近尾声时，托尼告诉梅尔菲，敌对的黑帮分子计划杀掉她，因为他们担心托尼在治疗过程中可能泄露了黑手党的秘密。梅尔菲躲藏起来，而托尼则负责追捕并击毙这些刺客。危险解除后，梅尔菲继续接受托尼的治疗。

Dr. Melfi’s pattern of on-again, off-again psychotherapy raises this question: Why would a psychiatrist put her life at risk to treat a manifestly impulsive, sociopathic criminal? One possible answer:

梅尔菲医生断断续续的心理治疗模式引发了一个问题：为什么一位精神科医生会冒着生命危险去治疗一个明显冲动、反社会的罪犯？一个可能的答案是：

While her conscious concern for a secure doctor/patient relationship masks her true desire, subconsciously she actually wants the very contradiction of security; she longs for risk, life-and-death risk. Her super-intention seeks the heart-pounding rush that can only be found along the fuse burning of danger.

她表面上重视建立稳固的医患关系，但这掩盖了她内心深处的真实渴望。实际上，她潜意识里追求的恰恰是与安全感截然相反的东西：她渴望冒险，渴望生死攸关的冒险。她内心深处渴望的是那种只有在危险边缘才能体验到的、令人心跳加速的刺激感。

Three values arc over the course of the scene: together/apart in the doctor/patient relationship; self-deception/self-awareness in Tony’s mind; and the core value, jeopardy/security for Dr. Melfi’s life. As the scene opens, these values begin with the two characters together on speaking terms (positive), Tony blind to his moral identity (negative), and, most importantly, Dr. Melfi in life-and-death jeopardy as she confronts her dangerous patient (negative).

贯穿整个场景的有三个价值维度：医患关系中的“在一起/分开”；托尼内心的“自欺欺人/自我认知”；以及梅尔菲医生生命安全的核心价值——“危险/安全”。场景伊始，这两个角色能够交谈（积极），托尼对自己的道德认知盲区（消极），而最重要的是，梅尔菲医生正面临着生死攸关的境地，她要面对的是危险的病人（消极）。

The scene matches two powerful personalities in a balanced conflict, told over thirteen beats. The first twelve beats match Tony’s actions against Dr. Melfi’s reactions, but the last beat reverses that pattern and sends Tony out the door.

这一幕巧妙地展现了两个性格鲜明的人物之间势均力敌的冲突，整个过程分为十三个阶段。前十二个阶段是托尼的行动与梅尔菲医生的反应相对应，但最后一个阶段却颠覆了这种模式，托尼愤然离去。

A transcription of the scene as televised follows, printed in bold. First read the bold passages straight through, skipping over my analysis. As you do, listen to the dialogue in your mind, or better yet, act it out aloud and feel what it would be like emotionally to live through this conflict, first from Tony’s point of view, and then from Dr. Melfi’s.

以下是电视播出场景的文字稿，以粗体字标出。请先通读粗体字部分，跳过我的分析。阅读时，请在脑海中默念对话，或者更好的是，大声朗读出来，感受一下经历这场冲突的情感体验，先从托尼的角度，再从梅尔菲医生的角度。

Once you have a sense for how the scene arcs, reread it against my analysis of the beats, their subtext, and the shaping of the action.

一旦你对场景的走向有了大致的了解，就对照我对节奏、其潜台词和动作塑造的分析重新阅读它。

INT. DR. MELFI’S OFFICE—EARLY EVENING

内景：梅尔菲医生办公室——傍晚

As PATIENTS from a group session file out, Tony enters like a lost little boy.

小组治疗结束后，患者们鱼贯而出，托尼像个迷路的小男孩一样走了进来。

BEAT 1

节拍 1

Dr. Melfi looks up, surprised to see him.

梅尔菲博士抬起头，惊讶地看着他。

MELFI

梅尔菲

Anthony.

安东尼。

As Tony glances down, embarrassed, Dr. Melfi strides up to him.

托尼尴尬地低下头，梅尔菲医生大步走到他面前。

MELFI

梅尔菲

Hello.

你好。

TONY

托尼

(with a shy smile)

（带着腼腆的微笑）

Hi.

你好。

ACTION: Tony turning on the charm.

行动：托尼使出浑身解数讨好。

REACTION: Melfi gearing up for trouble.

反应：梅尔菲准备惹麻烦了。

SUBTEXT: Twice that day Tony asked Dr. Melfi out for dinner, and twice she turned him down. Tony senses he’s out on a limb, so as he enters, he plays sensitive and shy, hoping to win her sympathy. Beneath her cheerful welcome, she puzzles over why he’s back yet again and readies herself for a third confrontation.

潜台词：那天托尼两次邀请梅尔菲医生共进晚餐，都被她拒绝了。托尼意识到自己处境艰难，于是进门时装出一副敏感腼腆的样子，希望能博得她的同情。梅尔菲医生热情地欢迎他，但内心却在疑惑他为何又来了，并做好了迎接第三次冲突的准备。

BEAT 2

节拍 2

TONY

托尼

(handing her an envelope)

（递给她一个信封）

A friend of mine had these and couldn’t use them. And I figure, well, maybe we could.

我的一个朋友有这些东西，但他用不了。我想，或许我们可以用得上。

(explaining)

（解释）

Tickets… Bermuda…

门票……百慕大……

(doing a little dance)

（跳了一小段舞）

… lodging at the Elbow Beach Hotel.

…入住肘滩酒店。

MELFI

梅尔菲

(amazed)

（惊讶地）

I turn down a wonderful dinner invitation and you think I’ll go away with you?

我拒绝了你盛情邀请的晚餐，你觉得我会跟你走吗？

ACTION: Tony propositioning her.

行动：托尼向她求爱。

REACTION: Melfi calling him an idiot.

反应：梅尔菲骂他是白痴。

SUBTEXT: Tony bought the tickets himself. He not only lies about that, but far worse, his underlying action treats Dr. Melfi like a whore. Dinner for two might cost $200; a weekend at the five-star Elbow Beach Hotel would run into the thousands. Tony ups the ante, thinking she turned down his previous offers because they were too cheap.

言外之意：托尼自己买了票。他不仅撒谎，更糟糕的是，他这种行为实际上是把梅尔菲医生当妓女一样对待。两人晚餐可能要200美元；在五星级的肘形海滩酒店度过一个周末则要花费数千美元。托尼提高了价码，因为他认为梅尔菲医生拒绝他之前的提议是因为他出价太低。

Tony’s disrespect and delusions offend Dr. Melfi, but because she knows he’s prone to violence, she avoids direct confrontation by repaying his insult with a rhetorical question. This ancient verbal tactic asks a question but not to get an answer; it assumes the answer in the question. So if we were to rewrite Melfi’s dialogue on-the-nose, it might read: “What kind of man thinks I’ll sleep with him just because he takes me to Bermuda? An idiot.”

托尼的无礼和妄想激怒了梅尔菲医生，但她知道他有暴力倾向，所以避免正面冲突，而是用反问句回击他的侮辱。这种古老的语言技巧提出问题，但并不寻求答案；它预设了答案就在问题之中。因此，如果我们直白地改写梅尔菲的台词，它可能是：“什么样的男人会以为我带他去百慕大就会跟他上床？真是个白痴。”

BEAT 3

节拍 3

TONY

托尼

Well, the guy couldn’t use ’em and, you know, he gave ’em to me and what’d you want me to do, throw ’em away?

嗯，那家伙用不了那些东西，你知道，他就把它们给了我，你觉得我应该怎么做，把它们扔掉吗？

Dr. Melfi stands in silence.

梅尔菲博士沉默地站在那里。

ACTION: Tony claiming his innocence.

行动：托尼声称自己无罪。

REACTION: Melfi avoiding conflict.

反应：梅尔菲试图避免冲突。

SUBTEXT: Tony tries to shrug off her criticism by pretending his proposition wasn’t manipulative, just practical—he’s the innocent victim of a friend’s generosity.

言外之意：托尼试图对她的批评不予理睬，假装他的提议并非出于操纵，而只是出于实际考虑——他是朋友慷慨的无辜受害者。

Dr. Melfi knows he bought the tickets as a sexual bribe, but rather than call out his canard, she turns silence into a weapon. In the right context, refusing to speak can be more powerful than anything said.

梅尔菲医生知道他买票是为了行贿，但她没有揭穿他的谎言，而是将沉默化作武器。在合适的语境下，拒绝说话的力量胜过任何言语。

梅尔菲

听着，安东尼。我不会和你出去，好吗？这并非因为你不吸引人，也不是因为我觉得和你在一起不会开心。我只是不想这么做。我希望你能尊重我的决定，也希望你能理解我知道什么才是最适合我的。好吗？

言外之意：他指责她贬低他，再次扮演受害者，并利用愧疚感来博取她的同情。

Instead, she begins with the “It’s not you, it’s me” tactic, seeming to put the blame on herself. But the phrase “I know what’s right for me” alerts Tony. Despite her opening ploy, it implies that he is not right for her because there’s something wrong, something broken inside him.

相反，她一开始就摆出一副“不是你的错，是我的错”的姿态，似乎在自责。但“我知道什么对我是正确的”这句话却让托尼警觉起来。尽管她一开始耍了这套伎俩，但这句话暗示着他并不适合她，因为他内心深处出了问题，某种破碎的东西。

Tony came to her in hopes of getting laid, but when she hints at his flawed nature, the subconscious need that has driven Tony through the entire series takes hold. He desperately longs for an answer to the core question of his life, a question only his psychiatrist can answer: What is wrong with me?

托尼来找她是为了和她上床，但当她暗示他性格中的缺陷时，贯穿整部剧集的潜意识需求再次涌上心头。他迫切地想要找到人生核心问题的答案，而这个问题只有他的精神科医生才能解答：我到底怎么了？

潜台词：托尼苦苦哀求真相，但梅尔菲医生深知真相会对他造成多么巨大的冲击，所以她故意拖延。然而，他坚持要知道真相，于是梅尔菲医生含糊其辞地回避了六秒钟后，终于越过了职业界限，谈及了私人关系，而这一举动也让她自己陷入了极大的危险之中。

Tony can read subtext with the best. When she says that the values separating them are “just very different,” he knows that that’s PC for “My values are clearly better than yours, but let’s not fight about it.”

托尼很擅长察言观色。当她说他们之间的价值观“非常不同”时，他知道这其实是委婉地表达“我的价值观显然比你的好，但我们还是别争论这个了”。

The word “values” startles Tony, and its insinuations anger him, but he manages to hold his rage in check.

“价值观”这个词让托尼大吃一惊，它所暗示的含义也让他愤怒，但他还是设法克制住了自己的怒火。

潜台词：我们衡量一个人的价值，取决于他的价值观及其所驱动的行为。她否定托尼的个人价值观，就等于否定了他作为一个人应有的价值。

When Tony confronts Dr. Melfi, she does not flinch. Instead, she states her disdain for him with such sudden, unexpected power that he drops his bullying tone.

当托尼质问梅尔菲医生时，她毫不畏惧。相反，她以一种出人意料的强势表达了对他的蔑视，以至于托尼收起了欺凌的语气。

Notice that when Dr. Melfi hits Tony with the bitter facts, her language softens the blow. She could have called him a liar, abuser, or worse. Instead, she keeps her cool control—“not a truthful person,” “not really respectful.”

注意，当梅尔菲医生用残酷的现实打击托尼时，她的措辞有所缓和。她本可以骂他是骗子、虐待者，甚至更难听的话。但她却保持了冷静——“他不是个诚实的人”，“他不太尊重人”。

节拍 12

TONY

托尼

梅尔菲

Maybe you love them, I don’t know. You take what you want from them by force, or the threat of force.

也许你爱他们，我不知道。你用武力或武力威胁从他们那里得到你想要的东西。

ACTION: Tony doubting himself.

行动：托尼开始怀疑自己。

REACTION: Melfi firing the first barrel.

SUBTEXT: Tony has never for a moment doubted his love for his family, friends, and lovers. But the instant Dr. Melfi shows him his essential tyrannical nature, he cannot argue back. Instead, he phrases his denial as a question, a question he seems to ask himself as much as her.

潜台词：托尼从未怀疑过自己对家人、朋友和爱人的爱。但当梅尔菲医生向他展现出其专横跋扈的本性时，他却无力反驳。于是，他用疑问句来表达自己的否认，这个问题似乎既在问她，也在问自己。

Line by line, fact by fact, Dr. Melfi has destroyed Tony’s self-worth. She knows full well that, humiliated and emasculated, he might lash out in violence. She faces a dilemma between speaking the final full truth and the violence it might bring versus keeping silent and staying secure. She makes her choice of action and dares to launch the final beat.

梅尔菲医生逐字逐句、一一列举事实，摧毁了托尼的自尊。她深知，托尼在遭受羞辱和丧失男子气概后，可能会诉诸暴力。她面临着两难的抉择：是说出最终的真相，承受可能带来的暴力，还是保持沉默，保全自身。她最终做出了选择，勇敢地发起了最后的反击。

节拍 13

MELFI

梅尔菲

(continuing)

（续）

I couldn’t live like that. I couldn’t bear witness to violence or—

我无法忍受那样的生活。我无法目睹暴力或——

TONY

托尼

—Fuck you…

-去你的…

Tony runs out, slams the door, and shouts from the lobby:

托尼跑了出去，砰地一声关上门，从大厅里大喊：

TONY

托尼

… you fucking cunt.

你这个混蛋。

ACTION: Melfi firing the second barrel.

行动：梅尔菲开火第二枪。

REACTION: Tony killing her with words.

反应：托尼用言语杀死了她。

SUBTEXT: In Beat 12 she impugns Tony’s morals, but in Beat 13 she denigrates the whole gangster life and, with that, everyone close to him.

潜台词：在第 12 行中，她质疑托尼的道德，但在第 13 行中，她贬低了整个黑帮生活，也贬低了所有与他亲近的人。

He could kill her for those insults; he has killed others for as much. But he runs out instead because of the way the writers staged the opening. As Tony entered Dr. Melfi’s office, a dozen members of a group session filed out past him. She saw Tony standing in the crowd and called out to him. In other words, there were witnesses. If he were to attack her now, those people could put him at the scene by name. Tony’s too savvy to make that mistake, so he fires off the most lethal words he knows.

他完全可以因为这些侮辱杀了她；他以前就因为同样的事情杀过别人。但他却逃走了，这都怪编剧的开场安排。托尼走进梅尔菲医生的办公室时，一群参加小组治疗的人从他身边鱼贯而出。梅尔菲医生看到托尼站在人群中，便喊住了他。换句话说，有目击者。如果他现在攻击她，这些人就能指认出他。托尼太精明了，不会犯这种错误，所以他脱口而出他所知道的最致命的话语。

This final beat turns with a sharp irony. Dr. Melfi tells Tony that she cannot witness violence, but we suspect that subconsciously she relishes face-to-face brushes with violence and the adrenaline rush they bring.

结尾处充满了讽刺意味。梅尔菲医生告诉托尼她无法忍受暴力，但我们怀疑，在潜意识里，她其实很享受与暴力正面交锋以及由此带来的肾上腺素飙升的感觉。

So even though Tony starts every beat but the last, it’s Dr. Melfi’s passive aggression that carries the scene to its climax. At first, she deflects his sexual moves, then in Beat 4 she provokes his desire to know why, and finally, she leads him to the self-discovery he dreads. On balance, Dr. Melfi owns the more powerful personality; she controls the conflict from open to close.

所以，尽管托尼几乎主导了除最后一个环节外的所有冲突，但真正将这场戏推向高潮的却是梅尔菲医生的被动攻击。起初，她拒绝了他的性暗示，然后在第四个环节中，她激起了他想要探究原因的渴望，最终，她引导他走向了他所恐惧的自我发现。总的来说，梅尔菲医生占据了更强大的主导地位；她掌控着冲突的始末。

Subtextual Progression

潜台词发展

Scan the list of subtextual actions below. Note how they progress the scene: Conflict builds through the first four beats, backs off for a moment in Beat 5, then progresses to the climax of Beat 13. Next note how this progression arcs the three values at stake in the scene: 1) Friendship/hatred in the doctor/patient relationship swings from positive to negative. 2) Tony’s comfortable self-deception (positive irony) turns to painful self-awareness (negative irony). 3) Peril/survival for Dr. Melfi pivots from negative to positive.

浏览下方列出的潜台词动作。注意它们如何推动场景发展：冲突在前四个节拍中逐渐增强，在第五个节拍中稍作缓和，然后在第十三个节拍中达到高潮。接下来，注意这种发展如何体现场景中三个关键价值的转变：1）医患关系中的友情/仇恨由积极转为消极。2）托尼安然的自我欺骗（积极反讽）转变为痛苦的自我认知（消极反讽）。3）梅尔菲医生的危险/生存状况由消极转为积极。

BEAT 1: Turning on the charm/Gearing up for trouble.

第一拍：展现魅力/准备惹麻烦。

BEAT 2: Propositioning her/Calling him an idiot.

第二拍：向她求爱/骂他是白痴。

BEAT 3: Claiming his innocence/Avoiding conflict.

第三步：声称自己无罪/避免冲突。

BEAT 4: Playing for pity/Blaming him.

第四拍：博取同情/责怪他。

BEAT 5: Looking for a way out/Giving him a way out.

节拍 5：寻找出路/给他一条出路。

BEAT 6: Laying it on the line/Buying time.

节拍 6：孤注一掷/争取时间。

BEAT 7: Asking for trouble/Crossing the line.

第七拍：自找麻烦/越界。

BEAT 8: Cornering her/Belittling him.

第 8 拍：将她逼到角落/贬低他。

BEAT 9: Daring her to cross him/Denying his worth.

节拍 9：挑衅她与他作对/否认他的价值。

BEAT 10: Asking nice/Giving him a last way out.

第 10 拍：好好请求/给他最后一次机会。

BEAT 11: Inviting the worst/Pulling her punch.

第 11 节：引诱最糟糕的情况/手下留情。

BEAT 12: Doubting himself/Firing her first barrel.

第 12 拍：怀疑自己/开出第一枪。

BEAT 13: Firing her second barrel/Killing her with words.

第 13 拍：发射第二枪/用言语杀死她。

To see how inner actions manifest in outer speech, let’s compare the dialogue for these two characters on three points: content, length, and pace.

为了了解内心行为如何体现在外在言语中，让我们从三个方面比较这两个角色的对话：内容、长度和节奏。

CONTENT: Tony comes into the scene feeling unloved and empty, suffering from an existential crisis. The reasons he used to give himself for living his high-risk life no longer make sense. In such a state, people naturally ask questions, the two biggest being: “Who am I?” and “What’s the point?”

内容：托尼出场时感到不被爱，内心空虚，正经历着一场存在主义危机。他过去为自己过着高风险生活找的理由如今都站不住脚了。在这种状态下，人们自然会提出各种问题，其中最关键的两个问题是：“我是谁？”和“这一切的意义何在？”

Note that half of Tony’s lines are questions. The rest are either lies or pleas, told and asked in the hope that Dr. Melfi will give him the insight into himself he craves. The only line in which he does not beg for an answer is the last, and it may be his weakest, most desperate call for help.

注意，托尼一半的台词都是疑问句。其余的要么是谎言，要么是恳求，他提出这些话或发出这些请求，都是希望梅尔菲医生能让他获得渴望已久的自我认知。他唯一一句没有乞求答案的话是最后一句，这或许是他最无力、最绝望的求助。

Dr. Melfi enters the scene at the height of her profession, sated with confident knowledge. Her therapeutic skill gives her what she wants: the power to lighten the darkness in her patients’ psyches. As a result, her lines make statements, the answers to Tony’s questions that she slowly, at times evasively, doles out.

梅尔菲医生在事业巅峰时期登场，自信满满，知识渊博。她的治疗技巧让她如愿以偿：拥有驱散病人心灵阴霾的力量。因此，她的话语本身就蕴含着深意，她缓慢而有时闪烁其词地回答着托尼的问题。

LENGTH: As noted in Chapter Seven, when people lose control of their emotions, their words, phrases, and sentences tend to shorten. Conversely, people in control often lengthen all three.

长度：正如第七章所述，当人们情绪失控时，他们的词语、短语和句子往往会变短。相反，情绪稳定的人通常会延长这三者。

Tony talks in monosyllables, and his longest sentence is ten words; Dr. Melfi frequently uses three-and four-syllable terms, and her sentences run as long as twenty-five words. Each of Dr. Melfi’s sentences includes a noun, verb, and object; Tony often abbreviates meaning into phrases such as “tickets,” “Bermuda,” “Go, go.”

托尼说话只用单音节词，最长的句子也只有十个词；梅尔菲医生经常使用三音节或四音节的词语，她的句子最长可达二十五个词。梅尔菲医生的每个句子都包含名词、动词和宾语；托尼则经常把意思简化成“票”、“百慕大”、“走，走”之类的短语。

PACE: In an athletic event, the player who controls the pace of the game tends to win. Much the same is true in life. First note how Tony’s staccato cadence and Dr. Melfi’s languid rhythms mirror their contradictory emotional states. Then compare Tony’s frantic phrases (“Then, what is it, okay? What is it?) to Dr. Melfi’s long, slow sentences. Tony tries to bulldoze through the opening beats, but ultimately, her moral power controls the pace of the scene. She takes her time; he stumbles from moment to moment, lurching out in defeat.

节奏：在体育比赛中，掌控比赛节奏的选手往往能获胜。人生亦是如此。首先，请注意托尼断断续续的语调和梅尔菲医生慵懒的节奏是如何反映出他们截然相反的情感状态的。然后，比较托尼焦急的语句（“到底是什么，好吗？到底是什么？”）和梅尔菲医生冗长而缓慢的句子。托尼试图强行推进，但最终，梅尔菲医生的道德力量掌控了整个场景的节奏。她从容不迫；而他则步履蹒跚，最终败下阵来。

Lastly, Chapter Nine argued that repetitiousness is the enemy of fine writing, and generally that’s true, but, as always, the antithesis has its uses, too. Like waves pounding a shore, the writers use repetition to swell Tony’s rising tide of anger and frustration. He repeats, for example, the word “okay” five times, the last two as a promise not to hurt her—which, by climax, if he could, he would (“Fuck you, you fucking cunt”).

最后，第九章论述了重复是优秀写作的敌人，这通常没错，但正如常言所说，反面也有其用处。就像海浪拍打海岸一样，作者运用重复来加剧托尼不断涌起的愤怒和挫败感。例如，他重复了五遍“好的”，最后两次是承诺不会伤害她——但到了高潮部分，如果可以的话，他真的会这么做（“去你妈的，你这个贱人”）。

If you haven’t already, watch the scene online to study how the dialogue’s contrasting qualities of content, length, and pace help channel the actors’ performances.

如果你还没有看过，请在线观看该场景，研究对话在内容、长度和节奏方面的对比特点是如何引导演员表演的。

In life, emotions seem to surge from the belly and then spread through the body. For this reason, acting coaches teach their students to think, not in their heads, but in their guts. Bad actors tend to be self-puppeteers who work from the head down to pull their own strings; fine actors let conflict hit below the waist as they surrender to their character.

生活中，情绪似乎总是从内心深处涌起，然后蔓延至全身。正因如此，表演教练教导学生不要用头脑思考，而要用心感受。糟糕的演员往往是自我操控的傀儡，他们从头脑出发，用心控制自己的表演；而优秀的演员则让冲突直击内心深处，全身心地投入到角色之中。

An instinct-driven performance is only possible if the writing, text and subtext, allows the actor to feel the meaning of the words in his guts, so that idea and emotion merge into immediate, vivid, seemingly spontaneous dialogue. Because the writing of THE SOPRANOS was the best of its day, James Gandolfini could create the from-the-guts tour de force that carried him to multiple Emmy, Screen Actors Guild, and Golden Globe Awards.

只有当剧本、文本和潜台词让演员能够从内心深处感受到文字的含义，并将想法和情感融为一体，形成即刻、生动、看似自然流露的对话时，才能实现凭直觉发挥的表演。正因为《黑道家族》的剧本堪称当时最佳，詹姆斯·甘多菲尼才能奉献出如此震撼人心的表演，并凭借此片斩获多项艾美奖、美国演员工会奖和金球奖。

#↩

14

COMIC CONFLICT

漫画冲突

All characters pursue secondary desires per scene (scene intention) in pursuit of a primary, overall desire per story (super-intention). If, however, we were to place all stories ever told along a spectrum ranging from tragedy to farce, we would see that dramatic characters and comic characters go about these pursuits with distinctively different dialogue styles.

所有角色在每个场景中都会追求次要的欲望（场景意图），而这些次要欲望都服务于故事中的主要、总体的欲望（超意图）。然而，如果我们把所有故事放在一个从悲剧到闹剧的连续谱系中，就会发现戏剧角色和喜剧角色在追求这些欲望时，会使用截然不同的对话风格。

The reason is simple: These two basic character types possess two fundamentally different mentalities. They do not think the same, and so they do not speak the same. Writing dialogue for one versus the other, therefore, demands two decidedly different techniques.

原因很简单：这两种基本人物类型拥有截然不同的思维模式。他们的思考方式不同，因此说话方式也不同。所以，为这两种人物撰写对话需要两种截然不同的技巧。

The dramatic character pursues what life demands with some degree of awareness. He has a mental flexibility that lets him step back from the fray and think the thought, “Wow, this could get me killed.” This realization doesn’t necessarily stop his quest, but he’s aware of its irony and risk. Tony Soprano, for instance, in the midst of rage, has enough mindfulness not to commit murder in public.

这个戏剧性人物在追求人生所需时，会保持一定的清醒意识。他拥有灵活的思维，能够从纷争中抽身而出，思考“哇，这可能会要了我的命”。这种认知未必会阻止他的追求，但他意识到其中的讽刺意味和风险。例如，托尼·索普拉诺即便在盛怒之下，也足够清醒地避免在公共场合杀人。

What makes a comic character comic is mental rigidity. He pursues his all-absorbing desire as if myopic to any choice beyond it. In the scene I’ll analyze below, for example, two psychiatrists (e.g., professionals who ought to know better) are so consumed by sibling rivalry they regress to infanticide.

喜剧人物之所以滑稽，在于其思维僵化。他一心追求自己的欲望，仿佛对其他任何选择都视而不见。例如，在我将要分析的场景中，两位精神科医生（理应更懂事的专业人士）被手足之争所吞噬，最终竟犯下了杀婴罪。

In centuries past, the monomania of the comic character was known as his “humor.” In 1612, playwright Ben Jonson wrote a verse prologue to his comedy Every Man out of His Humour . In it, he drew upon theories from medieval physiology that allege that every person’s body has a unique balance of four humors (fluids)—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—and their one-of-a-kind concoction determines each person’s specific temperament. (Why the ancients didn’t add sexual fluids to their list of humors, I cannot say, but they sure seem influential to me.)

在过去的几个世纪里，喜剧人物的偏执被称为他的“体质”。1612年，剧作家本·琼森为他的喜剧《人皆有性情》（Every Man out of His Humour）创作了一首诗歌序言。序言中，他借鉴了中世纪生理学的理论，认为每个人体内都有四种体液（血液、黏液、黄胆汁和黑胆汁）独特的平衡，而这四种体液的混合比例决定了每个人的具体气质。（至于为什么古人没有将性液也纳入体液的范畴，我不得而知，但性液在我看来确实影响深远。）

Jonson seized upon this theory as a metaphor for the comic character. In his definition, a humor arises

琼森抓住这一理论，将其作为喜剧人物的隐喻。在他的定义中，幽默由此产生。

… when some one peculiar quality

……当某种独特的品质

Doth so possesse a man, that it doth draw

它如此占据一个人，以至于它吸引

All his affects, his spirits, and his powers

他所有的情感、精神和力量

In their confluctions, all to runne one way. 1

它们汇聚在一起，最终都将奔向同一个方向。

In my comedy lectures, I call Jonson’s “one peculiar quality” the blind obsession. As noted in Chapter Eleven, desire intensifies in the comic character to the point of obsession. This fixation holds the character so tightly in its grip he cannot deviate from it. All aspects of his identity are bound to it; without it, he is no longer comic. What’s more, this obsession blinds him. He is driven to pursue it but cannot see the mania in himself. To us, he’s a crazed neurotic; to him, his obsession is normalcy.

在我的喜剧讲座中，我把琼森的“一个独特特质”称为盲目的执念。正如第十一章所述，喜剧人物的欲望会不断强化，直至达到痴迷的程度。这种执念牢牢地控制着人物，使他无法摆脱。他身份的方方面面都与此紧密相连；没有它，他就失去了喜剧的特质。更重要的是，这种执念蒙蔽了他的双眼。他被驱使着去追求它，却看不到自己内心的疯狂。在我们看来，他是一个神经质的疯子；而对他自己来说，他的执念却是正常。

Consider, for example, Inspector Jacques Clouseau (Peter Sellers and others), the protagonist of no less than eleven Pink Panther films. Deaf, dumb, and blind to his incompetence, Clouseau obsesses on perfection. He devotes every compulsive waking hour to becoming the world’s ultimate detective.

例如，想想雅克·克鲁索探长（彼得·塞勒斯等人饰演），他是至少十一部《粉红豹》电影的主角。克鲁索又聋又哑，对自己能力的不足视而不见，却执着于追求完美。他把所有清醒的时间都用来强迫自己成为世界上最伟大的侦探。

A few comic protagonists, such as Woody Allen’s Alvy Singer in ANNIE HALL and Larry David’s Larry David in CURB YOUR ENTHUSIASM, constantly dissect their obsession, phobically alert to any sign of neuroses. But what they do not grasp is that addictive self-analysis is itself a blind obsession. The more seriously and persistently these two guys self-psychoanalyze, the more hysterical they become—in both senses of the word.

一些喜剧主角，比如伍迪·艾伦在《安妮·霍尔》中饰演的艾维·辛格和拉里·大卫在《抑制热情》中饰演的拉里·大卫，总是不断地剖析自己的执念，对任何神经质的迹象都异常警惕。但他们没有意识到的是，沉迷于自我分析本身就是一种盲目的执念。这两个人越是认真、越是执着地进行自我心理分析，就越是歇斯底里——无论从哪个角度来看都是如此。

The comic protagonist’s blind obsession usually comes nested inside otherwise normal traits that anoint him with believability, dimensionalize his personality, and make him one of a kind. The art of comedy, however, imposes certain limitations on dimensionality, for this reason: Jokes require objectivity. Laughter explodes the moment two incongruous ideas suddenly clash in the mind. If their illogicality is not instantly recognized, the gag sputters in confusion. Therefore, the mind of the reader/audience must be kept sharply focused and uncluttered by compassion.

喜剧主角的盲目执念通常隐藏在其他正常的性格特征之中，这些特征赋予他可信度，丰富了他的个性，使他独一无二。然而，喜剧艺术对这种丰富性施加了一定的限制，原因如下：笑话需要客观性。当两个不相干的想法在脑海中突然碰撞时，笑声便会爆发。如果这种不合逻辑性没有被立即识别出来，笑话就会在混乱中哑口无言。因此，读者/观众的思维必须保持高度集中，不受同情心的干扰。

In Chapter Eleven’s 30 ROCK case study, I defined a dimension as a consistent contradiction within a character’s nature: either a contradiction between an outer trait of characterization versus an inner quality of true character (e.g., Jack Foley’s romantic charm versus his bank robber’s ethics in Out of Sight ), or a deep contradiction within the inner self (e.g., Macbeth’s blood-soaked ambition to be king versus his guilt-ridden conscience over the actions he takes to be king).

在第十一章的《我为喜剧狂》案例研究中，我将维度定义为角色性格中持续存在的矛盾：要么是角色外在特征与真实性格内在品质之间的矛盾（例如，《战略高手》中杰克·弗利的浪漫魅力与他作为银行劫匪的道德），要么是内心深处的矛盾（例如，麦克白嗜血成性的野心与他为成为国王而采取的行动所带来的罪恶感）。

A profound self-contradiction (such as those we saw previously within Dr. Melfi and Tony Soprano) draws a reader/audience into an empathic identification with a fellow human being and a compassionate concern for that character’s well-being. We welcome feelings in drama, but in comedy, empathy and compassion kill the laughs.

深刻的自我矛盾（例如我们之前在梅尔菲医生和托尼·索普拉诺身上看到的）能让读者/观众对某个角色产生共情，并对其福祉产生同情和关怀。我们欢迎戏剧中的情感，但在喜剧中，共情和同情会扼杀笑点。

For this reason, comic protagonists, almost without exception, have fewer dimensions than their dramatic counterparts and virtually none at the subconscious level of conflicted inner selves. Instead, comic dimensions pit appearance against reality, the man the character thinks he is versus the fool we know him in fact to be.

因此，几乎所有喜剧主角都比戏剧主角的性格维度少，几乎没有潜意识层面的内心冲突。喜剧的维度在于表象与现实的对比，在于角色自认为的自我与我们所了解的他实际上的愚蠢之间的冲突。

Bit parts in comedy—geek, diva, jock, valley girl, fop, braggart, nag, nerd, etc.—chase their blind obsession with glaring clarity because monomania is their only trait. As you might imagine, writing fresh, innovative dialogue for these nondimensional roles can break your brain. Indeed, many comedies fail at this. Too often, when supporting characters speak, their blind obsession funnels what they say into trite lingo and clichéd reactions.

喜剧中的小角色——书呆子、歌剧女主角、运动健将、拜金女、纨绔子弟、吹牛大王、唠叨鬼、宅男等等——都执迷不悟，因为他们唯一的特征就是偏执。可想而知，为这些缺乏立体感的角色创作新颖独特的台词有多么费脑筋。事实上，很多喜剧在这方面都失败了。很多时候，当配角开口说话时，他们那盲目的执念让他们说的话变成了陈词滥调和老套的反应。

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Peter Casey, David Lee, and David Angell spun FRASIER off from the sitcom CHEERS and filled it with a cast of unique obsessives. The show ran on NBC from 1993 to 2004, winning a record thirty-seven Emmy Awards. It tells the story of radio talk show psychiatrist Frasier Crane (Kelsey Grammer), his brother Niles (David Hyde Pierce), and the people in their lives.

彼得·凯西、大卫·李和大卫·安吉尔从情景喜剧《欢乐酒店》（Cheers）中衍生出《欢乐一家亲》（Frasier），并为其打造了一群性格迥异、各有怪癖的角色。该剧于1993年至2004年在NBC电视台播出，并创纪录地斩获了37项艾美奖。故事围绕着电台脱口秀主持人、心理医生弗雷泽·克莱恩（凯尔西·格拉默饰）、他的弟弟奈尔斯（大卫·海德·皮尔斯饰）以及他们生活中形形色色的人们展开。

Frasier and Niles share a number of blind obsessions. These become super-intentions that weave in and out of storylines, arcing through 264 episodes in eleven seasons, unifying the series: Both Frasier and Niles have a mortal fear of embarrassment; both crave social, intellectual, and cultural status—all leading to their supreme, often snobbish, pretentiousness; and, like all self-respecting comic characters, they obsess on sex.

弗雷泽和奈尔斯有很多共同的执念。这些执念逐渐演变成贯穿剧情的“超级意图”，在十一季共264集中交织出现，将整部剧集串联起来：弗雷泽和奈尔斯都极度害怕尴尬；他们都渴望获得社会、知识和文化地位——所有这些都导致了他们极度自负，甚至常常显得势利眼；而且，像所有自尊自爱的漫画人物一样，他们都对性着迷。

In a first season episode entitled “Author, Author,” Frasier and Niles have contracted with a publisher to write a book on the psychology of sibling rivalry. As fellow psychiatrists and siblings, this book, they feel, should be a snap. Unfortunately, they procrastinate the actual writing to the last day before the contract’s deadline.

在第一季名为“作家，作家”的一集中，弗雷泽和奈尔斯与出版社签订了一份合同，撰写一本关于手足竞争心理学的书。作为同行精神科医生和亲兄弟，他们觉得这本书应该轻而易举就能完成。然而不幸的是，他们却把实际写作拖到了合同截止日期前的最后一天才开始。

Desperate, they isolate themselves in a hotel room where they manage, after great difficulty, to compose a lead sentence. But then the fear of embarrassment grabs them by the throat: “What will people say if we fail as writers?” This fear paralyzes them with writer’s block, and they spend the rest of the day and the whole of the night eating and drinking their way through the minibar, writing nothing.

绝望之下，他们把自己关在酒店房间里，费尽周折才勉强写出一个开头句。但随即，对尴尬的恐惧攫住了他们的喉咙：“如果我们写作失败了，人们会怎么说？”这种恐惧让他们陷入了写作瓶颈，他们整天整夜都在吃喝玩乐，把迷你吧里的东西都吃光，却什么也没写出来。

The opening four beats turn on the value of humiliation/pride, but that dread quickly segues into yet another grand, series-long obsession: their mutual envy and constant competition, a.k.a. sibling rivalry, the very subject of the book they struggle to write. Onscreen, the scene runs for three minutes and fourteen seconds, igniting direct conflict between Frasier and Niles, two equally imbalanced personalities.

开篇的四个片段围绕着羞辱与骄傲的价值展开，但这种恐惧很快过渡到贯穿全剧的另一个宏大主题：他们彼此的嫉妒和持续不断的竞争，也就是所谓的兄弟阋墙，而这正是他们苦苦追寻的那本书的主题。在屏幕上，这一幕持续了三分十四秒，直接点燃了弗雷泽和奈尔斯这两个性格同样不平衡的人之间的冲突。

As in the previous chapter, I will work with the scene from two angles: Viewing it from the outside in, I will look at the beats of action/reaction that shape the scene’s progression as well as the changing charge of its values. Reversing the angle to the inside out, I will trace the steps of behavior—desire, antagonism, choice, action—that translate the intentions and tactics of Frasier and Niles into comically expressive dialogue.

与上一章一样，我将从两个角度分析这个场景：首先，从外向内观察，我会分析塑造场景进程的行动/反应节奏，以及其中价值观的转变；其次，从内向外分析，我会追溯行为的各个步骤——欲望、对抗、选择、行动——这些步骤将弗雷泽和奈尔斯的意图和策略转化为富有喜剧表现力的对话。

Once again, the scene is printed in bold. Read it through without break and then review it in light of my notes.

这段文字再次以粗体字标出。请一口气读完，然后结合我的笔记进行复习。

INT. HOTEL ROOM—EARLY MORNING

酒店房间内景——清晨

As Niles nods off in front of the computer keyboard, Frasier pulls open the drapes.

奈尔斯在电脑键盘前打起了瞌睡，弗雷泽拉开了窗帘。

BEAT 1

节拍 1

FRASIER

弗雷泽

(looking out at the day)

（望着窗外）

Oh, dear God! It’s dawn! It’s Friday!

我的天哪！天亮了！今天是星期五！

(turning to his brother)

（转向他的兄弟）

Niles, why don’t we just admit it? We can’t work together. There’s never going to be any book.

奈尔斯，我们为什么不承认呢？我们根本无法合作。这本书永远也写不出来。

NILES

奈尔斯

No, not with that attitude, there isn’t.

不，抱着这种态度，是不可能实现的。

ACTION: Frasier urging Niles to accept failure.

行动：弗雷泽敦促奈尔斯接受失败。

REACTION: Niles blaming their failure on Frasier.

反应：奈尔斯将他们的失败归咎于弗雷泽。

SUBTEXT: Niles and Frasier begin with the same scene intention: the desire to fix blame. To Frasier’s credit, he’s willing to share blame, but Niles, to preserve his pride, places the fault squarely on his brother. They instantly become each other’s antagonist, and for the next four beats choose name-calling as their underlying tactic. At first, their spiraling insults masquerade as accusations, but by Beat 6 the masks fall.

潜台词：奈尔斯和弗雷泽的开场意图相同：都想找出责任归属。值得称赞的是，弗雷泽愿意分担责任，但奈尔斯为了维护自尊，把所有错都推给了哥哥。他们立刻成了彼此的敌人，接下来的四个音节里，他们选择互相谩骂作为对抗的手段。起初，他们不断升级的侮辱还伪装成指责，但到了第六个音节，伪装就被揭穿了。

TECHNIQUE: Comedy writing calls for artful exaggeration. Over-the-top distortion itself often prompts laughs, but its primary work is to promote enough distance between the characters and the reader/audience that we can judge behaviors against what society considers normal and find them ridiculously out of step.

技巧：喜剧写作需要巧妙的夸张手法。过火的扭曲本身往往能引人发笑，但其主要作用在于拉开角色与读者/观众之间的距离，使我们能够用社会公认的正常标准来评判他们的行为，并发现这些行为荒谬可笑，与常人格格不入。

Note Frasier’s first line: He could have simply said, “It’s morning.” Instead, he calls upon the deity. Comic dialogue thrives on overstatement (although understatement is also an exaggeration).

注意弗雷泽的第一句话：他本来可以简单地说“早上好”，但他却祈求神灵保佑。喜剧对话的魅力在于夸张（尽管轻描淡写也是一种夸张）。

BEAT 2

节拍 2

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Will you get off it? Come on. The fat lady has sung. The curtain has been rung down. Let’s just go home.

你能不能别闹了？快点儿。大势已去，帷幕已经落下，咱们回家吧。

NILES

奈尔斯

Well, I guess I shouldn’t be surprised you’d give up so easily. It’s not your dream after all. Why should it be, mister big shot radio host.

嗯，我想我也不该对你这么轻易放弃感到惊讶。毕竟，这不是你的梦想。为什么非得是呢，这位自以为是的电台主持人先生。

ACTION: Frasier calling Niles an idiot.

行动：弗雷泽骂奈尔斯是白痴。

REACTION: Niles calling Frasier a snob.

反应：奈尔斯称弗雷泽是势利眼。

SUBTEXT: Frasier accuses Niles of being oblivious to the obvious. We have a name for those people: idiots. Niles, in turn, accuses Frasier of being arrogantly self-important and looking down on lesser souls. We have a name for those people: snobs. Their accusations become humiliations with a literary touch.

潜台词：弗雷泽指责奈尔斯对显而易见的事实视而不见。我们有个词可以形容这种人：白痴。奈尔斯反过来指责弗雷泽傲慢自大，瞧不起不如自己的人。我们有个词可以形容这种人：势利眼。他们的指责最终都变成了带有文学意味的羞辱。

Both Niles and Frasier are culture vultures, so notice that when Frasier declares that their work is done, he references opera and theatre.

奈尔斯和弗雷泽都是文化爱好者，所以请注意，当弗雷泽宣布他们的工作完成时，他提到了歌剧和戏剧。

BEAT 3

节拍 3

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Is that what this little tantrum is all about, huh? You’re jealous of my celebrity?

原来你耍小脾气是因为这个啊？你嫉妒我的名人身份？

NILES

奈尔斯

It’s not a tantrum and I’m not jealous. I’m just FED UP! I’m fed up with being second all the time. You know, I wanted to be a psychiatrist, just like mom, way before you did, but because you were older, you got there first. You were first to get married; you were first to give Dad the grandchild he always wanted. By the time I get around to doing anything, it’s all chewed meat.

这不是耍脾气，我也不是嫉妒。我只是受够了！我受够了总是屈居第二。你知道吗，我比你早得多就想当精神科医生，就像妈妈一样，但因为你比我大，所以你先实现了这个梦想。你先结婚；你先让爸爸抱上他一直想要的孙子。等我终于有机会去做某件事的时候，一切都已经被别人吃光了。

ACTION: Frasier calling Niles a petulant child.

行动：弗雷泽称奈尔斯是个任性的孩子。

REACTION: Niles calling Frasier an upstaging ham.

反应：奈尔斯称弗雷泽是个抢戏的演技派。

SUBTEXT: Frasier’s accusation is on point. Niles lapses into an adolescent snit as he accuses Frasier of deliberately hogging life’s spotlight and thus ruining his dreams. To save his pride Niles conflates coincidence with malevolence—a massive exaggeration.

潜台词：弗雷泽的指责一针见血。奈尔斯像个孩子一样耍脾气，指责弗雷泽故意抢走他人生的风头，毁了他的梦想。为了维护自己的尊严，奈尔斯把巧合和恶意混为一谈——这完全是夸大其词。

TECHNIQUE: Note the phrase “chewed meat.” Its incongruity pops a smart laugh, but more to the point, the allusion fits hand and glove with the rest of the scene. Mothers around the world pre-chew meat so their infants can swallow it. The whole scene plays as an elaborate Benjamin Button–like metaphor, regressing the brothers to their diapered days, so that at climax Frasier can reenact his failed infanticide of Niles.

技巧：注意“嚼过的肉”这个短语。它的不协调感引人发笑，但更重要的是，这个典故与场景的其他部分完美契合。世界各地的母亲都会提前嚼碎肉，以便婴儿能够吞咽。整个场景就像一个精心设计的、类似《本杰明·巴顿奇事》的隐喻，让兄弟俩倒退回他们还在穿尿布的年代，这样在高潮部分，弗雷泽就可以重演他之前试图杀死奈尔斯的失败之举。

BEAT 4

节拍 4

FRASIER

弗雷泽

You’re crying about something we can’t change.

你哭的是一些我们无法改变的事情。

NILES

奈尔斯

You wouldn’t change it if you could. You love it.

即使可以，你也不会改变它。你喜欢它。

ACTION: Frasier calling Niles a masochist.

行动：弗雷泽称奈尔斯是受虐狂。

REACTION: Niles calling Frasier a sadist.

反应：奈尔斯称弗雷泽是虐待狂。

SUBTEXT: Frasier accuses Niles of crying for no reason. We have a name for people who indulge needless suffering: masochists. Niles, in turn, accuses Frasier of reveling in his misery. We have a name for people who enjoy watching others suffer: sadists. These brothers are psychiatrists; they punch the secret places below the belt.

潜台词：弗雷泽指责奈尔斯无缘无故地哭泣。我们有一个词来形容那些沉溺于无谓痛苦的人：受虐狂。奈尔斯反过来指责弗雷泽以他的痛苦为乐。我们有一个词来形容那些喜欢看别人受苦的人：施虐狂。这两兄弟都是精神科医生；他们攻击的是别人的下体。

TECHNIQUE: A joke is a design in two parts: setup/payoff. The setup arouses energy; the payoff explodes it into laughter. Comic energy comes from three primary sources: defensive emotions, aggressive emotions, and sex. For this reason, when we look deeply into comic subtext, things can get scary, angry, and wild. But then, the more powerful the setup, the bigger the laugh.

技巧：笑话的设计分为两部分：铺垫和高潮。铺垫激发能量；高潮则将能量爆发为笑声。喜剧能量主要来源于三个方面：防御性情绪、攻击性情绪和性。因此，当我们深入探究喜剧的潜台词时，可能会发现其中蕴含着恐惧、愤怒和狂野的意味。但是，铺垫越精彩，笑声就越响亮。

You may or may not agree with the darkness of my interpretation, but when we reach the climax, look back and ask if it doesn’t fit.

你或许认同我这种阴暗的解读，或许不认同，但当故事发展到高潮时，回过头来问问自己，这种解读是否合理。

BEAT 5

节拍 5

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Oh, let it go, Niles.

哦，放手吧，奈尔斯。

NILES

奈尔斯

I can’t let it go. My nose is rubbed in it every day. I’M the one on the board of the Psychiatric Association; MY research is well respected in academic circles; four of MY patients have been elected to political office, but it’s YOUR big fat face they put on the side of buses.

我无法释怀。每天都有人拿这件事来羞辱我。我是精神病学会的理事；我的研究在学术界备受推崇；我的四个病人当选了公职，但他们却把你的脸印在公交车身上。

ACTION: Frasier calling Niles a crybaby.

行动：弗雷泽骂奈尔斯是爱哭鬼。

REACTION: Niles calling Frasier a show-off.

反应：奈尔斯称弗雷泽是个爱炫耀的人。

TECHNIQUE: Note how the writers build the joke in Beat 5. They use a technique known as trivializing the exalted.

技巧：注意编剧们是如何在第 5 段中构建笑点的。他们运用了一种称为“将崇高之事庸俗化”的技巧。

Niles’s anger over injustice infuses his setup, but he contains the energy inside a list of institutions of respect: “Psychiatric Association,” “academic circles,” and “political office.” Then his punch line throws a bomb of banality: “big fat face they put on the side of buses.”

奈尔斯对不公正的愤怒贯穿了他的整部作品，但他将这种能量控制在一系列受人尊敬的机构之中：“精神病学会”、“学术界”和“政治机构”。然后，他的妙语却抛出了一个平庸的炸弹：“公交车侧面印着的那张大脸。”

SUBTEXT: Niles immediately senses that Frasier actually takes pride in his public transportation portrait. With that, he suffers his final humiliation. The value of humiliation/pride has run its course, and now a deeper value rooted in sibling rivalry comes to the fore: winning/losing.

潜台词：奈尔斯立刻察觉到弗雷泽其实很自豪于他那幅公共交通工具上的肖像画。由此，他遭受了最后的羞辱。羞辱/自豪的价值已经消逝，如今，一种源于兄弟竞争的更深层次的价值——输赢——开始凸显。

节拍 6

FRASIER

弗雷泽

(indignant)

（愤怒）

I do not have a fat face.

我的脸并不胖。

NILES

奈尔斯

Oh, please, I keep wondering how long you’re going to store those nuts for winter.

哦，拜托，我一直在想你打算把那些坚果储存多久过冬。

ACTION: Frasier defending his face.

动作：弗雷泽保护自己的脸。

REACTION: Niles attacking his face.

反应：奈尔斯攻击他的脸。

SUBTEXT: By Beat 6 their subtext has risen to the text, and so the beats that follow are all more or less on-the-nose.

潜台词：到了第 6 拍，他们的潜台词已经上升到了正文，因此接下来的几拍或多或少都直白明了。

节拍 7

FRASIER

Well, at least I’m not spindly.

NILES

奈尔斯

Who are you calling spindly, fat face?

你叫谁瘦骨嶙峋、脸蛋肥嘟嘟的？

FRASIER

弗雷泽

You, spindly!

NILES

奈尔斯

Fat face!

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Spindly!

NILES

奈尔斯

Fat face!

胖脸！

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Spindly!

细长的！

NILES

奈尔斯

Fat face!

胖脸！

ACTION: Frasier calling Niles ugly.

行动：弗雷泽说奈尔斯长得丑。

REACTION: Niles calling Frasier ugly.

反应：奈尔斯说弗雷泽长得丑。

TECHNIQUE: “Spindly,” a unique vocabulary choice, characterizes Frasier perfectly. Nonetheless, he loses the name-calling contest because he is in fact more fat-faced than Niles is spindly. Back to the wall, he escalates from verbal to physical.

技巧：“瘦弱”这个词用得恰到好处，完美地刻画了弗雷泽的形象。然而，他却在互相辱骂的较量中败下阵来，因为事实上，他的脸比奈尔斯瘦弱的程度要胖得多。被逼到墙角后，他开始从言语冲突升级为肢体冲突。

BEAT 8

节拍 8

FRASIER

弗雷泽

You take that back!

你收回这句话！

NILES

奈尔斯

You make me!

你让我……

ACTION: Frasier making a fist.

REACTION: Niles making a fist.

反应：奈尔斯握紧了拳头。

SUBTEXT: By “making a fist,” I mean they take a moment to mentally and emotionally prepare for a fight.

言外之意：我所说的“握紧拳头”，是指他们花点时间在精神和情感上为战斗做好准备。

BEAT 9

节拍 9

FRASIER

弗雷泽

I will make you.

我会让你成功的。

NILES

奈尔斯

I don’t see you making me.

ACTION: Frasier deciding where to punch.

REACTION: Niles daring him to punch.

SUBTEXT: Under this brief beat, the brothers make decisions about how far to take the fight. Frasier chooses to start light.

潜台词：在这短暂的停顿中，兄弟俩决定这场争斗要进行到什么程度。弗雷泽选择先从小处着手。

FRASIER

弗雷泽

Oh yeah, well…

(ripping hairs out of his brother’s chest)

Niles winces in pain.

奈尔斯疼得龇牙咧嘴。

ACTION: Frasier attacking Niles.

REACTION: Niles gathering his counterattack.

SUBTEXT: Under his wince and yelp, Niles chooses all-out war.

潜台词：在痛苦的呻吟和哀嚎声中，奈尔斯选择了全面战争。

TECHNIQUE: After all of their threatening bluster, pulling out chest hairs makes a superb comic understatement. Note how the repetition of make/make/making/making gives the actors staccato, pace-building rhythm.

技巧：在他们一番咄咄逼人的虚张声势之后，拔胸毛这种举动反而成了绝妙的喜剧式轻描淡写。注意“拔/拔/拔/拔”的重复如何赋予演员一种断断续续、节奏递增的韵律。

Frasier turns to leave, but Niles races across the room, jumps on Frasier’s back, and wrestles him into a violent headlock.

FRASIER

弗雷泽

(shouting)

（喊叫）

Ow! Ow! Niles, stop it! We’re psychiatrists, not pugilists!

ACTION: Niles attacking Frasier.

行动：奈尔斯攻击弗雷泽。

REACTION: Frasier deceiving Niles.

反应：弗雷泽欺骗了奈尔斯。

SUBTEXT: Frasier could have used simpler language: “We’re doctors, not fighters.” Instead, to dupe Niles with vanity, he names their prestigious medical specialty and the Latinate for “boxer.” The trick works.

言外之意：弗雷泽本可以用更简单的语言：“我们是医生，不是拳击手。”但他为了利用奈尔斯的虚荣心，故意用他们显赫的医学专业和“拳击手”的拉丁语说法来欺骗他。这招果然奏效。

节拍 12

Niles lets Frasier go.

奈尔斯放走了弗雷泽。

FRASIER

弗雷泽

I can’t believe you fell for that.

真不敢相信你居然信了。

Frasier spins around and clamps Niles into a fierce headlock.

弗雷泽猛地转身，用一个凶狠的锁喉动作将奈尔斯牢牢锁住。

ACTION: Niles surrendering to Frasier.

行动：奈尔斯向弗雷泽投降。

REACTION: Frasier attacking Niles.

反应：弗雷泽攻击奈尔斯。

SUBTEXT: As they regress to childhood, Frasier’s ploy suggests that they have pulled these tricks on each other many times.

潜台词：随着他们退回到童年时代，弗雷泽的计谋表明他们已经多次互相使用过这些伎俩。

节拍 13

Frasier throws Niles on the bed, jumps on top on him, grabs him by the throat, and starts strangling him.

弗雷泽把奈尔斯扔到床上，跳到他身上，抓住他的喉咙，开始掐他的脖子。

NILES

奈尔斯

My God, my God, I’m having a flashback. You’re climbing in my crib and jumping on me.

我的天哪，我的天哪，我感觉好像回到了过去。你爬进我的婴儿床，跳到我身上。

ACTION: Frasier going for the kill.

行动：弗雷泽准备致命一击。

REACTION: Niles recoiling in terror.

反应：奈尔斯惊恐地后退。

SUBTEXT: Their roughhouse releases a wild, archaic instinct in Frasier.

潜台词：他们的打闹释放了弗雷泽内心深处狂野而古老的本能。

Niles, in terror, flashes back to his babyhood and remembers the day when Frasier actually tried to kill him.

奈尔斯惊恐万分，回想起自己的婴儿时期，想起了弗雷泽试图杀死他的那一天。

BEAT 14

节拍 14

FRASIER

弗雷泽

(roaring as he throttles his brother)

（一边咆哮一边掐住他哥哥的脖子）

You stole my mommy!!

你偷走了我的妈妈！！

Shocked by his murderous actions, Frasier jumps off the bed and rushes out the door.

弗雷泽被自己的杀人行为震惊了，他从床上跳下来，冲出了门。

ACTION: Frasier strangling his brother.

行动：弗雷泽掐住他哥哥的脖子。

REACTION: Frasier fleeing the scene of the crime.

反应：弗雷泽逃离了犯罪现场。

SUBTEXT: This hugely exaggerated beat explodes laughter because it draws energy from a primal impulse. The Cain and Abel story is a foundational archetype in Western culture. Sibling rivalry leads to violence more often than we like to believe. Ask any parent. In a drama, this last beat would be tragic. But comedy bundles catastrophe in laughter. “You stole my mommy!”, delivered with Kelsey Grammer’s frenzy, takes the beat delightfully over the top.

潜台词：这个极度夸张的节奏之所以能引爆笑声，是因为它激发了人们的原始冲动。该隐与亚伯的故事是西方文化中一个基础性的原型。手足之争往往比我们想象的更频繁地导致暴力。随便问问哪个家长就知道了。在戏剧中，这最后一个节奏会是悲剧性的。但喜剧却能将灾难融入笑声之中。“你偷走了我的妈妈！”这句台词，配上凯尔西·格拉默的狂热演绎，更是将这个节奏推向了极致，令人捧腹。

Subtextual Progression

潜台词发展

This scene doesn’t arc so much as it drills down. Scan the following list of subtextual actions to sense the spiral.

这一幕与其说是起伏跌宕，不如说是层层深入。仔细阅读以下一系列潜台词，就能感受到这种螺旋式上升的趋势。

BEAT 1: Urging Niles to accept failure/Blaming their failure on Frasier.

第一幕：劝说奈尔斯接受失败/将失败归咎于弗雷泽。

BEAT 2: Calling Niles an idiot/Calling Frasier a snob.

第二拍：称奈尔斯为白痴/称弗雷泽为势利眼。

BEAT 3: Calling Niles a petulant child/Calling Frasier an upstaging ham.

节拍 3：称奈尔斯为任性的孩子/称弗雷泽为抢戏的戏精。

BEAT 4: Calling Niles a masochist/Calling Frasier a sadist.

第四拍：称奈尔斯为受虐狂/称弗雷泽为施虐狂。

BEAT 5: Calling Niles a crybaby/Calling Frasier a show-off.

第五拍：称奈尔斯是爱哭鬼/称弗雷泽是爱炫耀的人。

BEAT 6: Defending his face/Attacking Frasier’s face.

第六拍：保护自己的脸/攻击弗雷泽的脸。

BEAT 7: Calling Niles ugly/Calling Frasier ugly.

第七节：说奈尔斯丑/说弗雷泽丑。

BEAT 8: Making a fist/Making a fist.

第 8 拍：握紧拳头/握紧拳头。

BEAT 9: Deciding where to punch/Daring him to punch.

第 9 回合：决定出拳位置/挑衅他出拳。

BEAT 10: Attacking Niles/Gathering his counterattack.

第 10 回合：攻击奈尔斯/集结他的反击。

BEAT 11: Attacking Frasier/Deceiving Niles.

第 11 关：攻击弗雷泽/欺骗奈尔斯。

BEAT 12: Surrendering to Frasier/Attacking Niles.

第 12 节：向弗雷泽投降/攻击奈尔斯。

BEAT 13: Going for the kill/Recoiling in terror.

第 13 拍：全力以赴/惊恐地后退。

BEAT 14: Strangling his brother/Fleeing the scene of the crime.

第 14 段：勒死他的兄弟/逃离犯罪现场。

The brothers begin by attacking each other’s personalities, then descend into sneering at each other’s physical defects, followed by emotional assaults, bottoming out with near-lethal violence: fourteen beats of fraternal ferocity made hysterically funny.

兄弟俩先是互相攻击对方的性格，然后开始嘲笑对方的身体缺陷，接着是情感上的攻击，最后演变成近乎致命的暴力：十四个兄弟间的凶狠场面，却又滑稽可笑。

COMEDY DIALOGUE TECHNIQUE

喜剧对白技巧

Laughter inspired by brutality is made possible by an eons-old convention. Since the dawn of storytelling, artists have maintained a bright line between drama and comedy by controlling the audience’s perception of pain: In true drama, everybody gets hurt; in true comedy, nobody gets hurt. Not really.

源于残酷的笑声，源于一项古老的惯例。自故事诞生之初，艺术家们就通过控制观众对痛苦的感知，在戏剧和喜剧之间划清界限：在真正的戏剧中，每个人都会受伤；在真正的喜剧中，没有人会受伤。至少表面上不会。

Comic characters may writhe, scream, bounce off walls, and tear their hair out, but they do it with a wild spirit that allows readers and audiences to sit back, laugh, and safely feel that it doesn’t really hurt. For without a clear comic style, readers and audiences would naturally feel sorry for suffering characters. To the comic writer, empathy spells death. Compassion kills laughs. Therefore, comic technique must keep the reader/audience cool, critical, unempathetic—on the safe side of pain.

漫画人物或许会扭动、尖叫、撞墙、抓头发，但他们那种狂野不羁的精神，让读者和观众可以放松下来，开怀大笑，并安心地觉得这一切并不真的令人痛苦。因为如果没有鲜明的漫画风格，读者和观众自然会对受苦的角色产生怜悯之心。对漫画家来说，同情心意味着死亡。怜悯会扼杀笑声。因此，漫画技巧必须让读者/观众保持冷静、批判和不带同情心——始终处于痛苦的安全边缘。

Here’s a short list of four techniques designed to keep emotional distance and trigger laughs.

以下是四种旨在保持情感距离并引发笑声的技巧。

1) Clarity: Not only does empathy kill laughs, but so does ambiguity, perplexity, and all forms of confusion. To keep the laughs rolling, everything must be clear, starting in the subtext. If a character is up to no good, the audience or reader may not know exactly what that no good is, but it should be crystal that what he’s up to is no good.

1）清晰性：同理心不仅会扼杀笑点，歧义、困惑和各种形式的混乱也会如此。要想让笑声持续不断，一切都必须清晰明了，从潜台词开始就必须如此。如果一个角色心怀不轨，观众或读者可能并不确切知道他究竟在做什么坏事，但他们应该清楚地知道他正在做的事情是坏事。

Language, too. Piles of blurry, verbose dialogue suffocate laughter. If you wish to write comedy, go back and review the principles of style covered in Chapters Five, Six, and Seven. Their every point applies absolutely to comedy writing. Focus in particular on the fundamentals of economy and clarity. The best jokes always use the fewest and clearest possible words.

语言也很重要。冗长晦涩的对话会扼杀笑声。如果你想写喜剧，请回顾第五、六、七章中讲解的风格原则。它们的每一条都完全适用于喜剧写作。尤其要注意简洁和清晰的基本原则。最好的笑话总是用最少、最清晰的词语。

2) Exaggeration: Comic dialogue thrives in the gap between cause and effect. The two most common techniques of exaggeration either bloat a minor cause into a major overstatement—“You stole my mommy!”—or shrink a major cause into a minor understatement—“The Harry Potter Theme Park is a hit with both anglophiles and pedophiles.” Comic exaggerations come in a variety of modes: dialects, non sequiturs, malapropisms, impersonations, pretense, sarcasm—all the way down the line to babble and nonsense.

2）夸张：喜剧对话的精髓在于因果关系的模糊性。两种最常见的夸张手法分别是：将一个次要的原因夸大成一件大事——“你偷走了我的妈妈！”——或者将一个主要的原因轻描淡写成一件小事——“哈利波特主题公园深受英国文化爱好者和恋童癖者的喜爱”。喜剧中的夸张手法多种多样：方言、不合逻辑的对话、用词不当、模仿、装腔作势、讽刺——甚至胡言乱语。

3) Timing: As I noted above, jokes pivot around a two-part design: setup and payoff, a.k.a. punch. The setup arouses aggressive, defensive, and/or sexual emotions in the reader/audience; the punch explodes that energy into laughter. The punch, therefore, must arrive at the exact moment the setup’s emotional charge peaks. Too soon and you get a weak laugh; too late and you get a groan. Moreover, nothing must follow the punch that would stifle the laughter.

3）时机：正如我前面提到的，笑话的核心在于两部分结构：铺垫和爆发，也就是所谓的“笑点”。铺垫会激发读者/观众的攻击性、防御性或性欲；而“笑点”则会将这些能量转化为笑声。因此，“笑点”必须在铺垫的情绪达到顶峰的那一刻出现。太早只会得到微弱的笑声；太晚则会引来一片叹息。此外，“笑点”之后绝对不能有任何会扼杀笑声的元素。

These two examples from 30 ROCK:

以下是《我为喜剧狂》（30 Rock）中的两个例子：

“Avery is the most perfect woman ever created. Like a young Bo Derek stuffed with a Barry Goldwater.” Avery (Elizabeth Banks) and Bo Derek inspire sexual energy (setup); the antithesis of sex, Barry Goldwater, a right-wing politician from the sixties, explodes it (punch).

“艾弗里是史上最完美的女人。就像年轻时的波·德里克，里面塞满了巴里·戈德华特。”艾弗里（伊丽莎白·班克斯饰）和波·德里克激发了性欲（铺垫）；而与性欲截然相反的巴里·戈德华特，这位六十年代的右翼政客，则引爆了这种性欲（冲击）。

“If I give in, I’m no longer the alpha in my house. Before you know it, she’ll have me wearing jeans and reading fiction.” Here the energy of aggressive masculine dominance (setup) is undercut by a feminine act (from Jack’s POV), “reading fiction” (punch).

“如果我屈服，我就不再是家里的老大。说不定过不了多久，她就会让我穿上牛仔裤，读小说。” 在这里，咄咄逼人的男性支配能量（铺垫）被女性的行为（从杰克的角度来看）——“读小说”（反击）——所削弱。

Note that both jokes use periodic sentences. Their punch words end the gag and nothing immediately follows, giving the audience room to laugh before the next beat takes their attention. As the old vaudeville saying goes: Don’t step on your own laughs.

请注意，这两个笑话都使用了周期性句式。它们的笑点都以一句句结尾，之后并没有立即接续，让观众有时间笑一笑，然后再进入下一个笑点。正如老歌舞杂耍剧里常说的：别踩到自己的笑声。

In the FRASIER scene, notice that periodic sentences deliver all the punch words and phrases: “mister big shot radio host,” “chewed meat,” “the side of buses,” “fat face,” “spindly,” “pugilists,” and “my mommy.”

在《欢乐一家亲》的场景中，请注意周期性的句子中出现的所有关键词语和短语：“大人物电台主持人”、“嚼过的肉”、“公共汽车的侧面”、“胖脸”、“瘦弱的”、“拳击手”和“我的妈妈”。

The only line that sets its punch word back from the last is Niles’s in Beat 6: “Oh, please, I keep wondering how long you’re going to store those nuts for winter.” The punch word is “nuts.” I suspect that the phrasing “Oh, please, winter’s coming and I keep wondering how long you’re going to store those nuts” would have gotten a bigger laugh, but I couldn’t be certain until I could see the actor deliver the line.

唯一一句笑点比上一句靠后的台词是奈尔斯在第六段说的：“哦，拜托，我一直在想你打算把那些坚果储存多久过冬。” 这句话的笑点是“坚果”。我猜想，如果把台词改成“哦，拜托，冬天快到了，我一直在想你打算把那些坚果储存多久”，可能会更搞笑，但直到看到演员念出这句话，我才能确定。

4) Incongruity: To build a joke, the relationship between setup and punch must strike a spark of incongruity; two things that don’t belong together suddenly collide. The underlying incongruity in the FRASIER scene pits civilized adults against their feral childhood selves. Psychiatrists who should be able to see their obsessions do not, and so cannot control them. In fact, they do the opposite; they let them loose. The steps they take to achieve their desires become the very things they must do to make sure they never achieve them. As a result, they act out the very book they cannot write.

4）不协调：要营造一个笑点，铺垫和笑点之间必须存在不协调的火花；两个原本不相干的事物突然碰撞。《欢乐一家亲》中这一幕的潜在不协调之处在于，文明的成年人与他们野性十足的童年自我之间的冲突。本应能够洞察他们执念的精神科医生却视而不见，因此也无法控制他们。事实上，他们的做法恰恰相反：他们放任这些执念蔓延。他们为了实现愿望而采取的行动，最终却变成了他们为了确保永远无法实现愿望而必须采取的手段。结果，他们上演了一部自己无法写出的书。

#↩

15

ASYMMETRIC CONFLICT

非对称冲突

A RAISIN IN THE SUN

阳光下的葡萄干

Lorraine Hansberry’s play opened in New York on March 11, 1959, starring Sidney Poitier, Claudia McNeil, Ruby Dee, and Louis Gossett Jr. It was the first play written by a black woman to reach Broadway and won the New York Drama Critics’ Circle Award. Two years later Hansberry adapted it to the screen.

洛兰·汉斯贝瑞的剧作于1959年3月11日在纽约首演，由西德尼·波蒂埃、克劳迪娅·麦克尼尔、鲁比·迪和路易斯·戈塞特主演。这是第一部由黑人女性创作并登上百老汇舞台的剧作，并荣获纽约戏剧评论家协会奖。两年后，汉斯贝瑞将其改编成电影剧本。

The play tells the story of a black family living in a tiny apartment on Chicago’s South Side in the 1950s. The Youngers recently buried the family patriarch, Walter, who literally worked himself to death. Walter left his wife, Lena, ten thousand dollars in life insurance. Lena wants to use a third of the money for a down payment on a house; a third to help her daughter, Bennie, through medical school; and the rest for her son, Walter Lee.

这部剧讲述了20世纪50年代芝加哥南区一个黑人家庭的故事，他们住在一间狭小的公寓里。杨格一家最近埋葬了他们的一家之主沃尔特，他因工作过度而去世。沃尔特给妻子莉娜留下了一万美元的人寿保险金。莉娜想用三分之一的钱作为买房的首付；三分之一资助女儿本妮完成医学院的学业；剩下的留给儿子沃尔特·李。

Walter Lee and two of his buddies have a plan to open a liquor store, but they need cash. Walter’s scene intention drives the scene below: to persuade his wife, Ruth, to help him get the whole ten thousand dollars. Ruth doesn’t trust her husband’s business venture and knows Lena will never give him all her money for any purpose, let alone a liquor store. Her scene intention contradicts his: to evade Walter’s scheme.

沃尔特·李和他的两个朋友计划开一家酒铺，但他们需要现金。沃尔特的意图是说服妻子露丝帮他筹到一万美元。露丝不信任丈夫的生意，她知道莉娜绝不会把所有的钱都给他，更别说是开酒铺了。露丝的意图与沃尔特的意图截然相反：她想阻止沃尔特的计划。

As husband and wife block each other’s conscious desires (force of antagonism), the scene shapes an asymmetrical conflict. Walter compels the action and the turning points happen to him. Ruth does her best to avoid conflict.

当夫妻二人互相阻挠对方的欲望（对抗的力量）时，这一幕便构成了一种不对称的冲突。沃尔特主导着事件的进展，转折点也发生在他身上。露丝则竭力避免冲突。

That’s the surface conflict, but taking the scene deeper, what do these characters really want? Walter Lee is a chauffeur, a dead-end job if there ever was one. The liquor store, he feels, will give him money and with that will come pride, independence, and the admiration of his wife and their son, Travis. Walter Lee wants: to gain self-respect (super-intention).

这只是表面的冲突，但深入分析，这些角色真正想要的是什么？沃尔特·李是一名司机，这绝对是一份毫无前途的工作。他觉得，开酒铺能给他带来收入，随之而来的是尊严、独立，以及妻子和儿子特拉维斯的敬佩。沃尔特·李想要的是：获得自尊（超乎寻常的意图）。

What Walter Lee does not know, however, is that his wife is two months pregnant with a second child. Because they live in poverty, she secretly contemplates an abortion. Like her husband, she also works for rich white people, as a domestic. She dreams of a decent life with a regular income in a home of their own. Ruth desperately needs: to find security (super-intention).

然而，沃尔特·李并不知道，他的妻子已经怀了两个月的身孕，即将迎来第二个孩子。由于生活贫困，她暗自考虑过堕胎。和丈夫一样，她也为富有的白人做家政。她梦想着拥有属于自己的房子，过上体面的生活，获得稳定的收入。露丝迫切需要的是：找到一份安稳的生活（超乎寻常的意图）。

Once again, the scene is printed in bold, interspaced with my notes on its beats and writing techniques. First read the bold passages straight through as Hansberry wrote the scene. Listen to the language in your mind, or better yet, read it aloud to yourself. Note the vocabulary with its short, punchy words; note the stripped-down grammar, and in particular, note the cadence of Hansberry’s language and how the rhythm of her phrasings matches the rhythms of her characters’ emotions. Once you have a feeling for how the scene plays, reread it against my analysis.

这段场景再次以粗体字呈现，并穿插着我对其中节奏和写作技巧的注释。首先，请像汉斯贝里写作时那样，通读粗体字部分。在脑海中聆听语言，或者更好的是，大声朗读。注意那些简短有力的词汇；注意精简的语法；尤其要注意汉斯贝里语言的韵律，以及她如何使措辞节奏与人物的情感节奏相契合。一旦你对这段场景的叙述方式有了感觉，再对照我的分析重新阅读一遍。

A RAISIN IN THE SUN

阳光下的葡萄干

Act 1, Scene 1

第一幕，第一场

The Younger apartment kitchen. As Ruth makes breakfast, her husband, Walter Lee, enters.

杨格公寓的厨房。露丝正在做早餐，她的丈夫沃尔特·李走了进来。

It’s useful, I believe, to think of scenes as mini-dramas, often triggered by a mini–inciting incident of their own. In this case, Walter throws the morning out of balance by bringing up his liquor store plans. He knows Ruth scorns the idea, so as she makes breakfast in a sour mood, he opens the scene with a smile.

我认为，把场景看作是一出幕微型剧是很有帮助的，这些微型剧往往是由某个小小的诱发事件引发的。在这个例子中，沃尔特提起他开酒铺的计划，打破了早晨的平静。他知道露丝很讨厌这个想法，所以当露丝心情不好地做早餐时，他却面带微笑地开始了这场戏。

WALTER: You know what I was thinking ‘bout in the bathroom this morning?

沃尔特：你知道我今天早上在洗手间里在想什么吗？

RUTH: (She looks at him in disgust and turns back to her work) No.

露丝：（她厌恶地看了他一眼，然后继续工作）不。

BEAT 1

节拍 1

ACTION: Walter inviting her to talk.

行动：沃尔特邀请她谈话。

REACTION: Ruth snubbing his offer.

反应：露丝拒绝了他的提议。

Notice that as the scene below builds, Hansberry never repeats a beat.

请注意，在下面的场景中，汉斯贝里从未重复过任何一个节奏。

WALTER: How come you always try to be so pleasant!

沃尔特：你为什么总是那么和蔼可亲！

RUTH: What is there to be pleasant ‘bout!

露丝：有什么好高兴的呢！

BEAT 2

节拍 2

ACTION: Walter calling her a killjoy.

行动：沃尔特称她为扫兴者。

REACTION: Ruth calling their life a misery.

反应：露丝称他们的生活是悲惨的。

WALTER: You want to know what I was thinking ‘bout in the bathroom or not?

沃尔特：你想知道我在浴室里在想什么吗？

RUTH: I know what you thinking ‘bout.

露丝：我知道你在想什么。

BEAT 3

节拍 3

ACTION: Walter insisting she listen.

行动：沃尔特坚持让她听。

REACTION: Ruth dismissing his idea.

反应：露丝驳斥了他的想法。

In the first three beats, Hansberry quickly establishes that after years of struggle to make ends meet, they’re experts in hurting each other.

在前三个节拍中，汉斯贝里迅速表明，经过多年的挣扎求生，他们已经成为互相伤害的专家。

WALTER: (Ignoring her) ‘Bout what me and Willy Harris was talking about last night.

沃尔特：（无视她）关于我和威利·哈里斯昨晚谈论的事情。

RUTH: (Immediately—a refrain) Willy Harris is a good-for-nothing loudmouth.

露丝：（立即重复）威利·哈里斯是个没用的聒噪之人。

BEAT 4

节拍 4

ACTION: Walter ignoring her.

行动：沃尔特无视她。

REACTION: Ruth ridiculing him.

反应：露丝嘲笑他。

WALTER: Anybody who talks to me has to be a good-for-nothing loudmouth, ain’t he? And what you know about who is just a good-for-nothing loudmouth? Charlie Atkins was just a “good-for-nothing loudmouth” too, wasn’t he! When he wanted me to go in the dry-cleaning business with him. And now—he’s grossing a hundred thousand dollars a year. A hundred thousand dollars a year! You still call him a loudmouth!

沃尔特：跟我说话的都是些没用的家伙，是不是？你懂什么叫没用的家伙？查理·阿特金斯以前也是个“没用的家伙”，对吧！他想拉我跟他一起开干洗店。现在——他一年能赚十万美元。一年十万美元！你还叫他家伙！

RUTH: (Bitterly) Oh, Walter Lee… (She sits at the table and drops her head on her folded arms)

露丝：（苦涩地）哦，沃尔特·李……（她坐在桌旁，把头埋在抱在胸前的双臂中）

BEAT 5

节拍 5

ACTION: Walter blaming her.

行动：沃尔特责怪她。

REACTION: Ruth hiding her guilt.

反应：露丝掩饰了自己的罪恶感。

Note Hansberry’s skill: This is a superb example of how to set up a future payoff. At this point neither the audience nor any other character knows that Ruth is pregnant and contemplating an abortion. As the scene plays, the audience’s first impression may be that there’s some truth in Walter’s complaint, that Ruth’s pessimism is a drag on his life. But that’s Hansberry’s deft setup for a forthcoming payoff. When Ruth’s pregnancy is revealed, we’ll suddenly grasp the real reason she’s in a tetchy, sullen mood. We’ll see her character, this scene, and its subtext with a rush of deep, unexpected but retrospectively logical perception.

注意汉斯贝里的高超技巧：这是一个绝佳的例子，展现了如何为未来的转折埋下伏笔。此时，观众和其他任何角色都不知道露丝怀孕了，并且正在考虑堕胎。随着剧情的展开，观众的第一印象可能是沃尔特的抱怨不无道理，露丝的悲观情绪确实拖累了他的生活。但这正是汉斯贝里为即将到来的转折所做的巧妙铺垫。当露丝怀孕的消息揭晓时，我们就会恍然大悟，明白她为何如此烦躁阴郁。我们会以一种深刻、出乎意料但事后看来又合情合理的视角，重新审视她的性格、这一幕以及其中的潜台词。

Therefore, the actor playing Ruth must create the pain and dread of her secret without giving it away and spoiling the audience’s discovery when the Act 1 climax pays off this scene’s setup.

因此，扮演露丝的演员必须营造出她秘密带来的痛苦和恐惧，同时又不能泄露秘密，以免破坏观众在第一幕高潮揭晓真相时的惊喜。

For example, Hansberry calls for Ruth to drop her head on her arms at the table. It looks like frustration over Walter’s badgering, but it could actually be that she’s suppressing morning sickness.
