The actor might play this secretly to herself, but she wouldn’t, for instance, clutch her stomach and tip off the audience.

例如，汉斯贝里要求露丝在餐桌上把头埋在双臂里。这看起来像是对沃尔特的唠叨感到恼火，但实际上可能是她在强忍孕吐。演员或许会暗自表演这一点，但她不会捂着肚子，让观众察觉到。

WALTER: (Rising and standing over her) You tired, ain’t you? Tired of everything. Me, the boy, the way we live—this beat-up hole, everything. Ain’t you? (She doesn’t look up, doesn’t answer) So tired—moaning and groaning all the time, but you wouldn’t do nothing to help, would you? You couldn’t be on my side that long for nothing, could you?

沃尔特：（起身站在她面前）你累了，是不是？厌倦了一切。我，这孩子，我们的生活方式——这破败不堪的房子，所有的一切。是不是？（她没有抬头，也没有回答）真的太累了——整天呻吟抱怨，但你却什么也不肯帮忙，是吗？你不可能无缘无故地站在我这边那么久，是吗？

RUTH: Walter, please leave me alone.

露丝：沃尔特，请你别烦我。

WALTER: A man needs for a woman to back him up…

沃尔特：男人需要女人支持他……

RUTH: Walter…

露丝：沃尔特……

BEAT 6

节拍 6

ACTION: Walter calling her selfish.

行动：沃尔特指责她自私。

REACTION: Ruth giving in.

反应：露丝妥协了。

Ruth submits to listen, or at least pretends to listen. It’s easier than battling the relentless Walter. He sees it as a sign he’s getting somewhere, so he changes his manner to sweet talk.

露丝只好听，或者至少假装听着。这总比跟纠缠不休的沃尔特硬碰硬容易。沃尔特觉得露丝的这番话有点效果，于是改口说些甜言蜜语。

WALTER: Mama would listen to you. You know she listen to you more than she do me and Bennie. She think more of you. All you have to do is just sit down with her when you drinking your coffee one morning and talking ’bout things like you do and—(He sits down beside her and demonstrates graphically what he thinks her methods and tone should be)—you just sip your coffee, see, and say easy like that you been thinking ‘bout that deal Walter Lee is so interested in, ‘bout the store and all, and sip some more coffee, like what you saying ain’t really that important to you—and the next thing you know, she be listening good and asking you questions and when I come home—I can tell her the details. This ain’t no fly-by-night proposition, baby. I mean we figured it out, me and Willy and Bobo.

沃尔特：妈妈会听你的。你知道，她听你的比听我和本尼的都多。她更看重你。你只需要找个早上，一边喝咖啡一边和她坐下来，像平时那样聊聊天——（他坐在她旁边，形象地示范他认为她应该用的方法和语气）——你就抿一口咖啡，听着，然后轻松地说，你一直在想沃尔特·李很感兴趣的那笔交易，关于那家店什么的，然后再抿一口咖啡，就好像你说的那些对你来说其实并不重要——接下来，她就会认真听，问你问题，等我回家——我就可以把细节告诉她了。这可不是什么一时兴起的买卖，宝贝。我是说，我和威利还有波波都想好了。

RUTH: (With a frown) Bobo?

露丝：（皱着眉头）波波？

BEAT 7

节拍 7

ACTION: Walter seducing her.

行动：沃尔特引诱她。

REACTION: Ruth smelling a rat.

反应：露丝闻到了不对劲的味道。

It doesn’t occur to Walter that the coffee klatch scene he acts out ridicules women. In fact, the audience wouldn’t have noticed and might even have found it amusing because in 1959, offhanded sexism was commonplace and virtually invisible. But not to Hansberry. This is another of her excellent setups. She’s planting Walter’s sexism here so she can harvest it at the end of the scene when he attacks all black women for their alleged betrayal of black men.

沃尔特丝毫没有意识到他演绎的那场咖啡馆闲聊戏是在嘲讽女性。事实上，观众可能根本不会注意到，甚至会觉得好笑，因为在1959年，这种不经意的性别歧视司空见惯，几乎无人察觉。但汉斯贝里却不这么认为。这是她又一个精妙的伏笔。她在这里埋下了沃尔特性别歧视的伏笔，以便在戏的结尾，当他攻击所有黑人女性，指责她们背叛黑人男性时，能够更好地发挥这种作用。

WALTER: Yeah. You see, this little liquor store we got in mind cost seventy-five thousand and we figured the initial investment on the place be ‘bout thirty thousand, see. That be ten thousand each. Course, there’s a couple of hundred you got to pay so’s you don’t spend you life just waiting for them clowns to let your license get approved—

沃尔特：是啊。你看，我们看中的那家小酒铺要七万五千美元，我们估计初始投资大概三万美元，明白吗？也就是每家一万美元。当然，你还得交几百美元的手续费，免得一辈子都浪费在等那些家伙批准你的执照上——

RUTH: You mean graft?

露丝：你是说嫁接吗？

BEAT 8

节拍 8

ACTION: Walter playing the businessman.

动作：沃尔特扮演商人。

REACTION: Ruth foreseeing disaster.

反应：露丝预见了灾难。

WALTER: (Frowning impatiently) Don’t call it that. See there, that just goes to show you what women understand about the world. Baby, don’t nothing happen for you in this world ‘less you pay somebody off!

沃尔特：（不耐烦地皱着眉头）别这么叫。瞧瞧，这正好说明了女人对这个世界的理解有多肤浅。宝贝，在这个世界上，除非你花钱摆平别人，否则什么事都办不成！

RUTH: Walter, leave me alone!

露丝：沃尔特，别烦我！

BEAT 9

节拍 9

ACTION: Walter proving his worldliness.

行动：沃尔特展现他的世故老练。

REACTION: Ruth rejecting his folly.

反应：路得拒绝了他的愚蠢行为。

Ruth is a deeply moral woman. The thought of an abortion, which was a felony in the 1950s, eats at her. She must be desperate to talk about it, but note how Hansberry wisely keeps it in the subtext.

露丝是一位极具道德感的女性。堕胎在20世纪50年代是重罪，一想到堕胎就让她备受煎熬。她一定很想倾诉，但请注意汉斯贝里是如何巧妙地将其隐藏在字里行间。

RUTH: (She raises her head, stares at him vigorously, then says quietly) Eat your eggs, they gonna be cold.

露丝：（她抬起头，用力地盯着他，然后平静地说）吃你的鸡蛋吧，它们都要凉了。

WALTER: (Straightening up from her and looking off) That’s it. There you are. Man say to his woman: I got me a dream. His woman say: Eat your eggs. (Sadly, but gaining in power) Man say: I got to take hold of this here world, baby! And a woman say: Eat your eggs and go to work. (Passionately now) Man say: I got to change my life, I’m choking to death, baby. And his woman say—(In utter anguish as he brings his fists down on his thighs)—your eggs is getting cold!

沃尔特：（直起身子，目光移向远方）就是这样。就是这样。男人对女人说：我有个梦想。女人说：吃你的鸡蛋。（语气悲伤，但逐渐占据上风）男人说：宝贝，我得掌控这个世界！女人说：吃你的鸡蛋，然后去工作。（语气充满激情）男人说：宝贝，我得改变我的生活，我快要窒息了。女人说——（他痛苦地捶打着大腿）——你的鸡蛋都凉了！

BEAT 10

击败 10

ACTION: Ruth placating him.

行动：露丝安抚他。

REACTION: Walter accusing her of disloyalty.

反应：沃尔特指责她不忠。

RUTH: (Softly) Walter, that ain’t none of our money.

露丝：（轻声）沃尔特，那不是我们的钱。

Walter falls silent and turns away from her.

沃尔特沉默不语，转身背对着她。

BEAT 11

击败 11

ACTION: Ruth swinging a moral hammer.

行动：露丝挥舞着道德之锤。

REACTION: Walter coping with defeat.

反应：沃尔特如何应对失败。

FIRST TURNING POINT: This scene plays in not one but two movements. The first movement begins at the positive as Walter has hope that he can convince Ruth to help him get his mother’s money. He runs a guilt-tripping argument, claiming that because Ruth ruined his prior chance at business success, she owes him her help now. What’s more, as his wife, she is morally obligated to support her husband’s venture. Of course he undermines his “moral” position with his willingness to pay bribes. Ruth finally explodes his argument by pointing out that they have no right to the money. His dead father earned that money with decades of sweat and pain. It’s Lena’s money, not theirs. It would be immoral to seduce her out of it. Beat 11 creates a negative turning point that shatters Walter’s scene intention. He knows he cannot argue against that truth, so he goes silent for a moment to gather himself for an attack in a new direction with a new scene intention: to escape his overwhelming sense of failure.

第一个转折点：这一幕分为两个乐章。第一乐章以积极的心态展开，沃尔特满怀希望地认为他可以说服露丝帮他拿到母亲的钱。他使出一副道德绑架的姿态，声称露丝毁了他之前的生意机会，所以现在她应该帮他。更重要的是，作为他的妻子，她有道义上的责任支持丈夫的事业。当然，他愿意行贿的行为本身就动摇了他所谓的“道德”立场。露丝最终驳斥了他的论点，指出他们无权得到这笔钱。他已故的父亲用几十年的汗水和艰辛挣来的。这是莉娜的钱，不是他们的。用这笔钱去勾引她是不道德的。第11拍的转折点打破了沃尔特的初衷，带来了一个负面的转折。他知道自己无法反驳这个事实，所以他沉默了一会儿，整理思绪，准备以新的方向和新的意图发起进攻：逃离他那难以承受的失败感。

WALTER: (Not listening at all or even looking at her) This morning, I was lookin’ in the mirror and thinking about it. I’m thirty-five years old; I been married eleven years and I got a boy who sleeps in the living room—(very, very quietly)—and all I got to give him is stories about how rich white people live…

沃尔特：（完全没在听，也没看她）今天早上，我对着镜子想这件事。我三十五岁了，结婚十一年了，我儿子睡在客厅——（非常非常轻声地）——我能给他的只有关于有钱白人生活的故事……

RUTH: Eat your eggs, Walter.

露丝：吃你的鸡蛋吧，沃尔特。

WALTER: Damn my eggs… damn all the eggs that ever was!

沃尔特：该死的鸡蛋……该死的所有鸡蛋！

RUTH: Then go to work.

露丝：那就去上班吧。

BEAT 12

节拍 12

ACTION: Walter begging for sympathy.

行动：沃尔特乞求同情。

REACTION: Ruth ignoring his plea.

反应：露丝无视他的请求。

WALTER: (Looking up at her) See—I’m trying to talk to you ’bout myself—(shaking his head with the repetition)—and all you can say is eat them eggs and go to work.

沃尔特：（抬头看着她）你看——我正想跟你谈谈我自己的事——（摇头重复）——而你只会说吃鸡蛋去上班。

RUTH: (Wearily) Honey, you never say nothing new. I listen to you every day, every night and every morning, and you never say nothing new. (Shrugging) So you would rather be Mr. Arnold than be his chauffeur. So—I would rather be living in Buckingham Palace.

露丝：（疲惫地）亲爱的，你说的都是老生常谈。我每天早晚都听你说话，你说的都是老生常谈。（耸肩）所以你宁愿当阿诺德先生也不愿当他的司机。那么——我宁愿住在白金汉宫。

BEAT 13

节拍 13

ACTION: Walter accusing her of not loving him.

剧情：沃尔特指责她不爱他。

REACTION: Ruth accusing him of living in a fantasy.

反应：露丝指责他活在幻想中。

WALTER: That is just what is wrong with the colored woman in this world… don’t understand about building their men up and making ’em feel like they somebody. Like they can do something.

沃尔特：这就是这个世界上黑人女性的问题所在……她们不懂得如何鼓励自己的男人，让他们觉得自己很重要，能做点什么。

RUTH: (dryly, but to hurt) There are colored men who do things.

露丝：（冷冷地，但意在伤人）黑人也会做事。

BEAT 14

节拍 14

ACTION: Walter blaming her for his failure.

行动：沃尔特将自己的失败归咎于她。

REACTION: Ruth blaming him for his failure.

反应：露丝责怪他失败了。

SECOND TURNING POINT: After his self-pity and guilt trips fall on deaf ears, Walter tries this logic: All black women make all black men failures. Ruth is black. Therefore, she’s to blame for his failure. But again she destroys his argument, this time with a fact and its implication: Some black men succeed. He is responsible for his failed life. She’s right and he knows it. Her bitter truth turns the scene to a double negative.

第二个转折点：沃尔特自怜自艾、愧疚不已，却无人理会，于是他尝试用这种逻辑：所有黑人女性都会让所有黑人男性失败。露丝是黑人，所以他的失败都是她的错。但露丝再次驳斥了他的论点，这次她用一个事实及其推论：有些黑人男性会成功。他要为自己的失败人生负责。她说得对，他也明白这一点。她那番尖锐的真相让整个局面彻底崩塌。

WALTER: No thanks to the colored woman.

沃尔特：这都多亏了那位黑人妇女。

RUTH: Well, being a colored woman, I guess I can’t help myself none.

露丝：唉，身为黑人女性，我想我也没办法控制自己。

BEAT 15

击败 15

ACTION: Walter clinging to his lame excuse.

行动：沃尔特坚持他那蹩脚的借口。

REACTION: Ruth sneering at his self-deception.

反应：露丝嘲笑他的自欺欺人。

WALTER: (Mumbling) We one group of men tied to a race of women with small minds.

沃尔特：（喃喃自语）我们是一群被束缚在思想狭隘的女人种族里的男人。

Ruth looks away in silence.

露丝沉默地别过脸去。

BEAT 16

击败 16

ACTION: Walter soothing his wounded ego.

行动：沃尔特抚慰他受伤的自尊心。

REACTION: Ruth retreating into her fears.

反应：露丝退回到她的恐惧中。

Let’s look at Hansberry’s sequence of beats and how she designed their progression. She starts with a mini–inciting incident: Walter’s cheerful invitation to talk, followed by Ruth’s hostile, one-word answer, “No.” From Beat 1 to Beat 6, Hansberry builds the beats to the negative. Each exchange tops the previous beat as Ruth and Walter add pain on pain, humiliation on humiliation, putting their love and hope in greater and greater jeopardy.

让我们来看看汉斯贝瑞的节奏安排以及她如何设计这些节奏的推进。她以一个小小的诱发事件开篇：沃尔特兴高采烈地邀请露丝谈话，随后露丝却冷漠地用一个字回答：“不”。从第一节到第六节，汉斯贝瑞逐步增强了负面情绪。每一次对话都比前一节更加激烈，露丝和沃尔特不断叠加痛苦和羞辱，使他们的爱情和希望岌岌可危。

BEAT 1: Inviting her to talk/Refusing his invitation.

第一拍：邀请她谈话/拒绝他的邀请。

BEAT 2: Calling her a killjoy/Calling their life a misery.

第二拍：称她为扫兴的人/称他们的生活是痛苦的。

BEAT 3: Insisting she listen/Dismissing his idea.

节拍 3：坚持让她听/驳斥他的想法。

BEAT 4: Ignoring her/Ridiculing his idea.

第四拍：无视她/嘲笑他的想法。

BEAT 5: Blaming her/Hiding her guilt.

第五步：责怪她/掩盖她的罪行。

BEAT 6: Calling her selfish/Giving in.

第六拍：说她自私/屈服。

Ruth surrenders for a moment to listen to what he has to say.

露丝暂时放下戒备，听他说话。

As Walter acts out the “coffee klatch” in Beat 7, the scene takes on a lighter, almost amusing tone. The mood rises toward the positive, and we begin to feel that Ruth might take his side. But when he mentions Bobo, she reacts with suspicion, and the scene swings back toward a deeper negative, building to the turning point at Beat 11.

在第七幕中，沃尔特扮演“咖啡闲聊”的角色时，场景的气氛变得轻松起来，甚至有些滑稽。情绪逐渐向积极的方向发展，我们开始觉得露丝可能会站在他这边。但当他提到波波时，露丝却表现出怀疑，场景的基调又转向了更深的负面，最终在第十一幕达到了转折点。

BEAT 7: Seducing her/Smelling a rat.

第七节：引诱她/嗅到不对劲。

BEAT 8: Playing the businessman/Foreseeing disaster.

第 8 段：扮演商人/预见灾难。

BEAT 9: Proving his worldliness/Rejecting his folly.

节拍 9：证明他的世故/否定他的愚蠢。

BEAT 10: Placating him/Accusing her of disloyalty.

第 10 拍：安抚他/指责她不忠。

BEAT 11: Swinging a moral hammer/Coping with defeat.

第 11 节拍：挥舞道德之锤/应对失败。

Beat 11 climaxes Walter’s scene intention. He realizes that Ruth will never help him get his mother’s money. Walter has failed again. This blow silences him for a moment, and the scene takes a breath while Walter gathers his anger and unleashes the scene’s second movement.

第11拍将沃尔特的剧情意图推向高潮。他意识到露丝永远不会帮他拿到母亲的钱。沃尔特又一次失败了。这一打击让他沉默了一会儿，剧情也随之停顿，沃尔特积蓄怒火，释放出剧情的第二部分。

First he must somehow bandage his wounded ego. So in Beat 12 he tries pleading for Ruth’s understanding, but then in Beats 13 and 14 he turns on her to blame her and all black women for his failure. Finally she nails him with the truth.

他首先得想办法安抚自己受伤的自尊心。所以在第12节，他试图恳求露丝的理解，但到了第13和14节，他又反过来指责她，把失败归咎于她和所有黑人女性。最后，露丝用真相击垮了他。

BEAT 12: Begging for sympathy/Ignoring his plea.

第 12 拍：乞求同情/无视他的请求。

BEAT 13: Accusing her of not loving him/Accusing him of living in a fantasy.

第 13 拍：指责她不爱他/指责他活在幻想中。

BEAT 14: Blaming her for his failure/Blaming him for his failure.

第 14 拍：责怪她导致他的失败/责怪他导致他的失败。

Beat 14 climaxes both the second movement and the scene as Ruth forces Walter to confront his responsibility for his own miserable life.

第 14 拍既是第二乐章的高潮，也是这一幕的高潮，因为露丝迫使沃尔特面对他自己悲惨生活的责任。

BEAT 15: Clinging to his lame excuse/Sneering at his self-deception.

第 15 拍：他坚持自己蹩脚的借口/嘲笑自己的自欺欺人。

BEAT 16: Soothing his wounded ego/Retreating into her fears.

第 16 拍：抚慰他受伤的自尊/退回到她的恐惧中。

The last two beats are a resolution movement that eases the tension as Walter retreats into self-pity and Ruth retreats into her secret fears about her pregnancy.

最后两拍是缓解紧张气氛的转折，沃尔特陷入自怜，露丝陷入对怀孕的秘密恐惧。

A sampling of the gerunds used to name the actions and reactions of husband and wife lays out the scene’s asymmetrical conflict:

通过对用来描述夫妻二人行为和反应的动名词进行分析，可以看出场景中不对称的冲突：

Walter’s actions: inviting, insisting, blaming, seducing, proving, accusing, versus Ruth’s reactions: dismissing, hiding, giving in, placating, ignoring, retreating.

沃尔特的行为：邀请、坚持、责备、诱惑、证明、指责，而露丝的反应：不予理睬、躲藏、屈服、安抚、忽视、退缩。

A sampling of lines reveals the word choices and modals used to carry out those actions.

选取部分句子进行分析，可以发现用于执行这些动作的词语选择和情态动词。

Walter’s aggressive accusations:

沃尔特咄咄逼人的指控：

You still call him a loudmouth?

你还叫他大嘴巴吗？

You wouldn’t do nothing to help, would you?

你难道不会出手相助吗？

A man needs a woman to back him up.

男人需要女人的支持。

I’m choking to death, baby!

宝贝，我快要窒息而死了！

Ruth’s passive reactions:

露丝的被动反应：

Oh, Walter Lee…

哦，沃尔特·李……

Please leave me alone.

请别烦我。

That ain’t none of our money.

那可不是我们的钱。

I guess I can’t help myself none.

我猜我根本控制不住自己。

The scene arcs its primary values from positive to negative: hope to despair, security to danger, success to failure, self-respect to self-hatred. As the scene opens, Walter has hope to gain success and with that, self-respect. Ruth clings to her hope for security. But the scene’s ever-escalating beats of action/reaction push Ruth further and further from a secure future, while driving Walter further and further from his immediate goal of financial success, and even further from his life-fulfilling desire for self-respect. What’s more, because we sense that underneath the arguing these two people love each other, the climax of the scene puts their marriage in jeopardy. The scene ends on the deeply negative: Walter’s hope turns to despair; Ruth’s security turns to danger.

这一幕的核心价值观由积极转为消极：希望到绝望，安全到危险，成功到失败，自尊到自我厌恶。场景伊始，沃尔特满怀希望地渴望获得成功，并以此赢得自尊。露丝则紧紧抓住对安全的渴望。然而，随着剧情不断升级，冲突的节奏将露丝推离安全的未来越来越远，同时也让沃尔特离眼前的经济成功越来越远，甚至离他渴望的、能让他获得人生满足的自尊也越来越远。更重要的是，我们能感受到，在争吵之下，两人依然深爱着彼此，因此，场景的高潮将他们的婚姻置于危险之中。最终，场景以深刻的负面情绪收尾：沃尔特的希望化为绝望；露丝的安全感化为危险。

To fully appreciate Hansberry’s genius, notice that as she executes her immediate task of arcing the scene around its value changes, she also uses its second movement to set up Walter’s long-term character arc.

要充分领略汉斯贝里的天才之处，请注意，在她完成围绕价值变化构建场景的直接任务的同时，她还利用场景的第二部分来设定沃尔特的长期角色弧线。

A character arc is a profound change, for better or worse, in a character’s moral, psychological, or emotional nature, expressed in values such as optimism/pessimism, maturity/immaturity, criminality/redemption, and the like. The character’s inner nature may arc from the positive (caring) to the negative (cruel), as does Michael in THE GODFATHER PART II, or from the negative (egoist) to the positive (loving), as does Phil in GROUNDHOG DAY.

角色弧线是指角色在道德、心理或情感方面发生的深刻变化，这种变化可能是好的，也可能是坏的，体现在诸如乐观/悲观、成熟/不成熟、犯罪/救赎等价值观上。角色的内在本质可能像《教父2》中的迈克尔那样，从积极（关爱）走向消极（残忍）；也可能像《土拨鼠日》中的菲尔那样，从消极（自私）走向积极（充满爱心）。

Therefore, the writer must clearly establish the character at the positive or negative of a value early in the story, so that the audience can understand and feel the arc of change. Walter is the only character in the play that undergoes moral change, and so Hansberry ingeniously uses Beats 12 to 16 to set up his nature and need for change.

因此，作者必须在故事早期就明确地确立人物在某种价值观上的立场，使其倾向于积极或消极，以便观众能够理解并感受到人物性格的转变过程。沃尔特是剧中唯一经历道德转变的人物，因此汉斯贝里巧妙地运用了第12至16个片段来展现他的性格以及他转变的必要性。

In five progressive beats of dialogue, Hansberry expresses Walter’s desperate desire for self-respect and the respect of his family and dramatizes that he has neither. After turning Walter’s super-intention to the negative (wounded pride) in Act 1, Hansberry takes Walter down to an even deeper hell of self-loathing and familial disgust at the Act 2 climax. At last she resurrects Walter when he makes a choice and takes an action that wins him self-respect as well as the love and admiration of his wife and family at the story climax. Walter’s character arc from self-hatred to self-respect lifts A Raisin in the Sun well above conventional social dramas about racial prejudice.

汉斯贝里用五段循序渐进的对话，展现了沃尔特对自尊和家人尊重的渴望，并戏剧化地揭示了他两者皆无的境地。在第一幕中，汉斯贝里将沃尔特的积极意图（受伤的自尊）转为消极，并在第二幕的高潮部分，将沃尔特推入更深的自我厌恶和对家人的厌恶的深渊。最终，当沃尔特做出选择并采取行动，赢得自尊以及妻子和家人的爱与敬佩时，汉斯贝里使他重获新生。沃尔特从自我憎恨到自我尊重的转变，使《阳光下的葡萄干》这部作品远超传统的种族偏见社会剧。

Now let’s take this excellent scene and ruin it. I’ll demonstrate how the same dialogue beats could have been anti-progressive:

现在让我们来破坏这个精彩的场景。我将演示同样的对话段落如何变得反进步：

Suppose Hansberry had started the scene with its turning points: Walter asks Ruth whether she’d like to know what he’s thinking about and she says, “I already know. Your father’s life insurance. Walter, that is not our money! It’s your mother’s. So forget it. And what’s more, I’m tired of listening to your whining about your misery and blaming me for your failed life. You, Walter, are responsible for every mistake you’ve ever made.”

假设汉斯贝里一开始就点明了转折点：沃尔特问露丝是否想知道他在想什么，露丝说：“我已经知道了。你父亲的人寿保险。沃尔特，那不是我们的钱！那是你母亲的。所以别想了。而且，我已经厌倦了听你抱怨你的悲惨遭遇，厌倦了把你失败的人生归咎于我。沃尔特，你犯下的每一个错误都应由你负责。”

In reaction Walter could still go on about Ruth’s lack of support, the glories of the liquor store business, how easy it would be to persuade his mother, how he hates his life and blames Ruth’s typical black woman’s attitude for it all. The necessary exposition about the money, his plans, his life, and his feelings about his wife would get out. The audience would learn what it needs to know but be bored stiff because it realizes that Walter’s arguments are pointless. Ruth has said “No!” and means it. So, with zero tension and zero suspense, the scene would bump and crumble into a rubble of exposition.

作为回应，沃尔特还可以继续抱怨露丝不支持他，吹嘘酒铺生意多么风光，说说服他母亲有多么容易，抱怨自己多么厌恶生活，并把这一切都归咎于露丝典型的黑人女性态度。关于钱、他的计划、他的生活以及他对妻子的感情等必要背景信息都会交代清楚。观众会了解到他们需要知道的一切，但却会感到无比无聊，因为他们意识到沃尔特的辩解毫无意义。露丝已经说了“不！”，而且是认真的。因此，这场戏毫无紧张感和悬念，最终只会沦为一堆冗长的背景介绍。

Or I could ruin it another way by bringing in the turning points too late, elongating the scene by repeating its beats. Walter could expand on all the money he could have made in the dry-cleaning business; he could sing the praises of those extraordinary businessmen, Willy and Bobo; he could glorify the liquor store scheme and describe the furs, jewelry, and new home he would buy for Ruth and their son with the fortune he would make.

或者，我也可以用另一种方式毁掉它：把转折点引入得太晚，通过重复节奏来拉长场景。沃尔特可以大肆渲染他在干洗店生意中赚到的钱；他可以歌颂威利和博博这两位杰出的商人；他可以美化他的酒铺计划，并描述他将用赚来的钱为露丝和他们的儿子购买的皮草、珠宝和新房。

When she finally nails him with the fact that his mother’s money is not his, Walter could then launch a century-long history of the black woman as the black man’s burden—on and on until Ruth shuts him up. Again the audience loses interest as fact after fact is hammered home over and over. When the turning points finally arrive, they’d have less than half their full impact because the exposition has worn down the audience. Notice that when Hansberry does use repetition, such as Walter’s “egg” speech (Beat 7), it’s to give the actor three drumbeats to build to an emotional peak—but no more.

当露丝最终揭穿他母亲的钱并非属于他的事实时，沃尔特便会滔滔不绝地讲述黑人女性如何成为黑人男性的负担，长达一个世纪之久——直到露丝让他闭嘴为止。然而，事实被反复强调，观众的兴趣也随之消退。当转折点最终到来时，由于之前的铺垫已经让观众感到疲惫，其冲击力也大打折扣。值得注意的是，汉斯贝里运用重复手法，例如沃尔特关于“鸡蛋”的演讲（第七幕），只是为了给演员三次机会来酝酿情绪，直至达到高潮——仅此而已。

Or worse yet, she could have written the scene with no turning points at all. She could have poured out three pages of breakfast table talk about business plans, Mother’s money, their lousy marriage, and the fate of black men and women. But she didn’t. She wrote a revealing, moving, progressive scene that beat by beat hits two turning points that in turn set up her whole play.

更糟糕的是，她本可以写一个毫无转折点的场景。她本可以写三页关于早餐桌上闲聊的文字，内容包括商业计划、母亲的钱、他们糟糕的婚姻以及黑人男女的命运。但她没有。她写了一个引人入胜、感人至深、具有进步意义的场景，其中巧妙地穿插了两个转折点，而这两个转折点又为整部剧奠定了基础。

Like the scene we just studied, every scene, ideally, works as both payoff and setup. Something has changed since the last confrontation between a scene’s characters. Therefore, what is said now pays off things that happened in the past. As these payoffs reverberate through the dialogue, what is said now will in turn set up effects in future scenes.

就像我们刚才分析的场景一样，理想情况下，每个场景都应该兼具铺垫和呼应的功能。自场景中人物上次交锋以来，某些事情已经发生了变化。因此，现在所说的话是对过去发生的事情的呼应。随着这些呼应在对话中不断回响，现在所说的话反过来又会为未来的场景埋下伏笔。

And like the examples from THE SOPRANOS and FRASIER, Hansberry’s skilled creation of Walter Lee carried Sidney Poitier into nominations for a Tony Award, a Golden Globe, and a BAFTA, the British Academy of Film and Television Award.

就像《黑道家族》和《欢乐一家亲》中的例子一样，汉斯贝里巧妙地塑造了沃尔特·李这个角色，让西德尼·波蒂埃获得了托尼奖、金球奖和英国电影电视学院奖的提名。

In the three previous chapters, dramatized scenes called for actors to strike major chords of heated emotion around wrenching turning points. Let’s now look at a prose scene with cool tones and muted action.

前三章中，戏剧化的场景要求演员在扣人心弦的转折点上，充分展现强烈的情感张力。现在，让我们来看一段以冷静的语调和舒缓的笔触描绘的散文场景。

#↩

16

INDIRECT CONFLICT

间接冲突

THE GREAT GATSBY

《了不起的盖茨比》

Chapter One of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s novel introduces the reader to the story’s narrator, Nick Carraway. Nick has come to New York to begin his Wall Street career. He has rented a house in West Egg, Long Island. His neighbor is Jay Gatsby, a fabulously wealthy young man who has made a fortune as a bootlegger. West Egg is home to the well-to-do, but it is far less fashionable than its very exclusive counterpart across the bay, East Egg. Nick’s cousin, the beautiful Daisy, lives in an East Egg mansion with her wealthy husband, Tom Buchanan, a powerfully built former Ivy League athlete. The Buchanans invite Nick for dinner, and there he meets Miss Jordan Baker, a female golf star who, like the Buchanans, is also upper class.

F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的小说第一章向读者介绍了故事的叙述者尼克·卡拉威。尼克来到纽约，准备开始他在华尔街的职业生涯。他在长岛西卵租了一栋房子。他的邻居是杰伊·盖茨比，一个靠私酒发家致富的富豪。西卵是富人的聚居地，但远不如海湾对岸的东卵那样时尚。尼克的表妹黛西，一位美丽的女子，和她富有的丈夫汤姆·布坎南住在东卵的一栋豪宅里。布坎南身材魁梧，曾是常春藤盟校的运动员。布坎南夫妇邀请尼克共进晚餐，在那里他遇到了乔丹·贝克小姐，一位高尔夫球明星，她和布坎南夫妇一样，也出身于上流社会。

Fitzgerald has written his novel in the first person from Nick’s point of view. Below is Fitzgerald’s subchapter broken into eight beats. The scene begins with the foursome sipping drinks before dinner. Miss Baker turns to Nick and says:

菲茨杰拉德以第一人称视角，从尼克的视角来叙述这部小说。以下是菲茨杰拉德将章节分为八个部分。场景开始于四人晚餐前小酌。贝克小姐转向尼克说道：

BEAT 1

节拍 1

“You live in West Egg,” she remarked contemptuously. “I know somebody there.”

“你住在西卵，”她轻蔑地说，“我认识那里的人。”

“I don’t know a single—”

“我一个也不认识——”

“You must know Gatsby.”

你一定认识盖茨比。

“Gatsby?” demanded Daisy. “What Gatsby?”

“盖茨比？”黛西问道。“什么盖茨比？”

BEAT 2

节拍 2

Before I could reply that he was my neighbor, dinner was announced; wedging his tense arm imperatively under mine, Tom Buchanan compelled me from the room as though he were moving a checker to another square.

我还没来得及回答说他是我的邻居，晚餐时间就宣布了；汤姆·布坎南用他紧绷的手臂强行把我的手臂撑在我的手臂下，强迫我离开了房间，就像他要把棋子移到另一个格子上一样。

Slenderly, languidly, their hands set lightly on their hips, the two young women preceded us out onto a rosy-colored porch open toward the sunset where four candles flickered on the table in the diminished wind.

两位年轻女子身姿纤细，步伐慵懒，双手轻轻叉腰，走在我们前面，来到一个朝落日方向敞开的粉红色门廊上，桌上的四根蜡烛在微风中摇曳。

BEAT 3

节拍 3

“Why candles?” objected Daisy, frowning. She snapped them out with her fingers.

“为什么要用蜡烛？”黛西皱着眉头反对道，然后用手指把蜡烛掐灭了。

BEAT 4

节拍 4

“In two weeks it’ll be the longest day in the year.” She looked at us all radiantly. “Do you always watch for the longest day of the year and then miss it? I always watch for the longest day in the year and miss it.”

“再过两周就是一年中白昼最长的一天了。”她容光焕发地看着我们。“你们是不是总是盼着一年中白昼最长的一天到来，结果却总是错过？我总是盼着白昼最长的一天到来，结果却总是错过。”

BEAT 5

节拍 5

“We ought to plan something,” yawned Miss Baker, sitting down at the table as if she were getting into bed.

“我们应该计划一下，”贝克小姐打了个哈欠，像要上床睡觉似的，在桌边坐了下来。

“All right,” said Daisy. “What’ll we plan?” She turned to me helplessly.

“好吧，”黛西说，“我们该计划什么呢？”她无助地转向我。

“What do people plan?”

人们会计划些什么？

Before I could answer her eyes fastened with an awed expression on her little finger.

我还没来得及回答，她的目光就带着敬畏的神情落在了她的小指上。

“Look!” she complained. “I hurt it.”

“你看！”她抱怨道，“我弄伤它了。”

We all looked—the knuckle was black and blue.

我们都看了看——他的指关节青紫一片。

BEAT 6

节拍 6

“You did it, Tom,” she said accusingly. “I know you didn’t mean to do it but you did do it.

“是你干的，汤姆，”她指责道。“我知道你不是故意的，但你确实做了。”

BEAT 7

节拍 7

“That’s what I get for marrying a brute of a man, a great big hulking physical specimen of a—”

“这就是我嫁给一个粗野男人的下场，一个身材魁梧、体型庞大的——”

“I hate that word ‘hulking’,” objected Tom crossly, “even in kidding.”

“我讨厌‘魁梧’这个词，”汤姆生气地反对道，“即使是开玩笑的时候也讨厌。”

BEAT 8

节拍 8

“Hulking,” insisted Daisy.

“魁梧，”黛西坚持道。

That ends the scene.

这一幕就此结束。

Before I begin my analysis, a few words on point of view.

在开始分析之前，先简单谈谈观点。

First, a definition: Point of view is that place in the global space of a story’s world that the writer or director places us so we can witness the scene. By global space, I mean the 360 degrees of horizontal angles that surround a subject, combined with the 360 vertical degrees of angle above and below the subject.

首先，我们来定义一下：视角是指编剧或导演将我们置于故事世界整体空间中的位置，以便我们能够观看场景。这里所说的整体空间，指的是围绕主体的360度水平视角，以及主体上方和下方的360度垂直视角。

In the theatre, we look at the onstage life from that fixed POV of the seat we purchased. All of the characters’ actions and reactions are in front of us at all times. We are more or less free to glance from one character to another at any moment, but that’s our only POV choice, and that choice will be greatly influenced by the director’s staging as well as the voices and movements of the actors.

在剧院里，我们只能透过所购座位的固定视角观看舞台上的表演。所有角色的行动和反应始终呈现在我们眼前。我们或多或少可以随时将目光从一个角色移到另一个角色，但这却是我们唯一的视角选择，而且这种选择会受到导演的舞台调度以及演员的声音和动作的极大影响。

In television and film, we see what the camera sees. As it moves through the global storytelling space, it controls but does not rigidly limit our POV. For as we gather in the establishing shots, supplemented with group shots, two-shots, or close-ups, and the like, we become aware of life offscreen as well as onscreen. As a result, we often imagine actions and reactions we do not in fact see.

在电视和电影中，我们看到的正是镜头所看到的。当镜头在宏大的叙事空间中移动时，它控制着我们的视角，但并非严格限制。因为当我们聚集在场景建立的镜头中，并辅以群像、双人镜头或特写镜头等，我们便能意识到银幕内外的生活。因此，我们常常会想象出一些我们实际上并未看到的行为和反应。

Prose offers the writer the greatest freedom in point of view choices, and yet at the same time, for the reader, prose is the most controlling storytelling medium. Like other media, prose can view scenes from anywhere in the physical world, but it also adds subjective angles within a character’s mental world. Once the prose writer makes a choice of person (first, third, or the eccentric second), her eye moves from that angle like a spotlight. The author holds our perception in her fist.

散文赋予作者最大的视角选择自由，但同时，对读者而言，散文也是最具控制力的叙事媒介。与其他媒介一样，散文可以从现实世界的任何角度展现场景，但它也融入了人物内心世界的主观视角。一旦散文作者选定了叙述视角（第一人称、第三人称，或是略显古怪的第二人称），她的目光便会像聚光灯一样从那个角度聚焦。作者将我们的感知牢牢掌握在手中。

As we follow her sentences, she takes us where she wishes: through the places, times, and societies of her world; or into a single character’s thought-filled depths, there to witness rationalizations, self-deceptions, and dreams; or deeper yet, into the character’s subconscious to reveal her raw appetites, nightmarish terrors, and lost memories.

随着她的文字，她带领我们去往她想去的地方：她世界的各个地方、时代和社会；或者进入某个角色充满思考的内心深处，见证他们的理性化、自我欺骗和梦想；或者更进一步，进入角色的潜意识，揭示他们原始的欲望、噩梦般的恐惧和失去的记忆。

When skillfully executed, POV has such power that unless we deliberately stop, pull out of the telling, and put our imaginations to work, we are drawn through the tale, seeing and hearing only what the storyteller wants us to, and no more.

如果运用得当，POV（视角）具有如此强大的力量，以至于除非我们刻意停下来，从叙述中抽身出来，发挥想象力，否则我们就会沉浸在故事中，只看到和听到讲故事的人想让我们看到和听到的东西，仅此而已。

Therefore, in the following analysis, when I describe Tom Buchanan’s reaction to Daisy’s abrupt snuffing out of the candles, I am imagining the scene the way Fitzgerald might have imagined it before he wrote the final draft. Like all fine writers, Fitzgerald no doubt worked through the scene draft after draft, adding, cutting, reordering, phrasing, and rephrasing until he had a sense of its totality. And as he reworked the scene, he likely imagined it from each and every character’s viewpoint, even though he knew that he would ultimately control his prose through Nick’s point of view.

因此，在接下来的分析中，当我描述汤姆·布坎南对黛西突然熄灭蜡烛的反应时，我设想的场景是菲茨杰拉德在最终定稿前可能构思的。像所有优秀的作家一样，菲茨杰拉德无疑反复修改这一场景，增删、重组、润色、重写，直到对整体效果有了清晰的把握。在修改场景的过程中，他很可能从每个角色的视角进行想象，尽管他知道最终会通过尼克的视角来掌控叙述。

Now to the scene: Suppose you prepared a romantic candlelit dinner and your spouse abruptly snuffed out the candles without a word or look to you. What would you feel? How would you react? Tom must have been offended. So to analyze the full life of Fitzgerald’s mini-drama, I must re-create the scene as he envisioned it before he wrote it and include the reactions that Fitzgerald chose to imply but not describe.

现在回到场景：假设你精心准备了一顿浪漫的烛光晚餐，你的伴侣却一声不吭、一言不发地突然吹灭了蜡烛。你会作何感想？你会如何回应？汤姆肯定很生气。因此，为了全面分析菲茨杰拉德这出小剧的内涵，我必须重现他创作前的设想，并把那些他选择暗示却未直接描述的反应也一并呈现。

Inciting Incident

诱发事件

As the scene opens, Daisy’s and Tom’s life seems contented and in balance. The value of marriage/divorce is at its positive charge. But secretly, Daisy finds married life very tedious. Her inner charge of excitement/boredom sits at the nadir.

故事伊始，黛西和汤姆的生活看似平静美满，婚姻/离婚的价值似乎也达到了顶峰。然而，黛西内心深处却觉得婚姻生活十分乏味，她对婚姻的兴奋/厌倦感跌至谷底。

BEAT 1

节拍 1

ACTION: Jordan revealing that Gatsby lives in West Egg.

剧情：乔丹透露盖茨比住在西卵。

REACTION: Daisy concealing her surprise.

反应：黛西掩饰着自己的惊讶。

Beat 1 triggers the novel’s inciting incident: Daisy discovers that Jay Gatsby has moved nearby. What’s more, Jordan and Nick know him. This revelation immediately throws her life out of balance. The positive charge of marriage/divorce begins to erode toward the negative, while her excitement for Gatsby resurfaces.

第一幕引发了小说的导火索：黛西发现杰伊·盖茨比搬到了附近。更糟糕的是，乔丹和尼克都认识他。这个发现立刻打破了她生活的平衡。婚姻/离婚带来的积极影响开始消退，取而代之的是消极的影响，而她对盖茨比的迷恋也再次涌上心头。

In her late teens Daisy fell passionately in love with Jay Gatsby. Their rich girl/poor boy affair ended when Gatsby left to fight in World War I. Soon after their breakup, the socially ambitious Daisy married the wealthy Tom Buchanan. In recent years Gatsby has become scandalously rich and famous. Daisy has no doubt read or heard about his exploits. She may also have learned that he purchased a huge estate across the bay. In fact, Gatsby bought the home so he could look across the narrow waters to the lit windows of her home.

黛西十几岁时就深深爱上了杰伊·盖茨比。这段富家女与穷小子的恋情随着盖茨比奔赴第一次世界大战战场而告终。分手后不久，一心想跻身上流社会的黛西嫁给了富有的汤姆·布坎南。近年来，盖茨比名利双收，声名狼藉。黛西无疑听说过他的种种事迹。她或许也知道，盖茨比在海湾对岸购置了一处豪宅。事实上，盖茨比买下这处房产，就是为了能隔着狭窄的海湾眺望黛西家中灯火通明的窗户。

When Daisy asks, “What Gatsby?” she knows full well it’s Jay Gatsby, but she cleverly uses the question to conceal her genuine surprise to learn that her former lover is now a virtual neighbor and, furthermore, that her friend knows him and her cousin lives near him.

当黛西问“哪个盖茨比？”时，她其实很清楚是杰伊·盖茨比，但她巧妙地利用这个问题来掩饰自己得知前情人现在竟然是邻居，而且她的朋友认识他，她的表妹也住在附近时的惊讶之情。

The realization that Gatsby has moved close to her, undoubtedly drawn to West Egg because of her, upsets the balance of Daisy’s life and arouses in her the desire to see him. To renew their love? Have an affair? Leave her husband? Who can say how far she intends to go? Daisy’s fluidly fickle nature makes her incapable of decisive plans into the future, but this much is clear: Her super-intention is, at the very least: to see Jay Gatsby. Gatsby becomes her object of desire.

意识到盖茨比已经搬到离她很近的地方——毫无疑问，他是被她吸引到西卵来的——打破了黛西生活的平衡，也激起了她想要见他的渴望。是想重燃旧情？还是想和他发展一段婚外情？又或是想离开丈夫？谁又能说得清她究竟会走到哪一步呢？黛西性情多变，难以对未来做出明确的规划，但有一点很明确：她最根本的意图，至少是：想见杰伊·盖茨比。盖茨比成了她渴望的对象。

This puts two core values into play: marriage/divorce and boredom/passion—the security of her marriage versus her passion for Gatsby. She must risk the former to gain the latter.

这就引出了两个核心价值观：婚姻/离婚和乏味/激情——她对婚姻的安稳与对盖茨比的激情之间的抉择。她必须冒着失去前者的风险，才能获得后者。

Daisy’s choice: To keep marital peace or go to war? At the top of the scene, the value charges are positive for Daisy’s marriage (before dinner, husband and wife are amiable) but negative for Daisy’s passion (Gatsby is out of reach).

黛西面临的选择：维持婚姻的和平还是发动战争？在这一幕的开头，对黛西的婚姻而言是积极的（晚餐前，夫妻俩和睦相处），但对黛西的激情而言是消极的（盖茨比遥不可及）。

Beyond seeing Gatsby, exactly what Daisy wants from him, Fitzgerald deliberately hides in the subtext. But note Daisy’s choice: She risks her marriage and goes to war with her husband.

除了让黛西看清盖茨比的真面目之外，菲茨杰拉德刻意将黛西真正想要的东西隐藏在字里行间。但请注意黛西的选择：她冒着婚姻破裂的风险，与丈夫开战。

BEAT 2

节拍 2

ACTION: All walking to the dinner table.

行动：所有人走向餐桌。

REACTION: Daisy planning to humiliate Tom.

反应：黛西计划羞辱汤姆。

Daisy’s problem is that she cannot just pick up a telephone and call Gatsby. Her pride and vanity won’t allow her. What’s more, if her husband and the rigid, snobbish society she moves in were to discover that she pursued the notorious Gatsby, the scandal would ruin her.

黛西的难题在于，她不能拿起电话就给盖茨比打电话。她的骄傲和虚荣心不允许她这么做。更糟糕的是，如果她的丈夫和她所处的那个刻板势利的上流社会发现她追求过声名狼藉的盖茨比，那场丑闻会毁了她。

Instantly, instinctively, she decides to put on a show in front of Nick and Jordan so that one or both will carry a message to Gatsby, a message that says the Buchanan marriage is in trouble. Daisy takes command of the scene and drives it to its turning point. Her scene intention becomes: to humiliate her husband in public. Tom’s scene intention, it’s fair to assume, is: to avoid public humiliation. These directly opposed desires set the scene’s terms of antagonism.

她本能地决定在尼克和乔丹面前演一出戏，好让他们俩或其中一人向盖茨比传达一个信息：布坎南夫妇的婚姻出现了问题。黛西掌控了局面，并将其推向了转折点。她的意图变成了：当众羞辱她的丈夫。可以合理推断，汤姆的意图是：避免当众出丑。这两种截然相反的愿望构成了这场戏的对抗基础。

Tom Buchanan has had his household staff set the dinner table with candles. He may have done it for Daisy’s sake, or perhaps he intended this romantic touch to encourage Nick and Jordan. Indeed, in time those two will have a summer affair.

汤姆·布坎南吩咐家仆在餐桌上摆放蜡烛。他或许是为了黛西，又或许是想用这浪漫的举动来撮合尼克和乔丹。的确，这两个人迟早会发展出一段夏日恋情。

BEAT 3

节拍 3

ACTION: Daisy destroying her husband’s romantic gesture.

行动：黛西破坏了她丈夫的浪漫举动。

REACTION: Tom concealing his annoyance.

反应：汤姆掩饰着自己的恼怒。

But whatever Tom’s reason, as they step up to the table, the “frowning” Daisy objects to the candles and snuffs them out with her fingers. Tom reacts by concealing the hurt she causes him and saying nothing. The positive charge of marriage declines further as Daisy’s boredom changes into excitement.

但不管汤姆的理由是什么，当他们走到桌边时，皱着眉头的黛西对蜡烛表示不满，并用手指将它们吹灭。汤姆强忍着被她伤害的感觉，什么也没说。随着黛西的厌倦转为兴奋，婚姻的美好氛围进一步消退。

BEAT 4

节拍 4

ACTION: Daisy opening a conversational subject.

行动：黛西开启了一个谈话话题。

REACTION: Daisy turning the subject back to herself.

反应：黛西把话题转回到了自己身上。

In this beat Daisy starts a conversation about the summer solstice, but before anyone can respond to her strange question, she reacts to her own action and ends the topic by referring it back to herself. The value charges of marriage/divorce and excitement/boredom are unaffected and remain the same as they were in Beat 3.

在这一节拍中，黛西开始谈论夏至，但还没等任何人回应她奇怪的问题，她就对自己的行为做出反应，并以自身为切入点结束了这个话题。婚姻/离婚和兴奋/无聊的价值判断并未受到影响，与第三节拍中保持一致。

BEAT 5

节拍 5

ACTION: Jordan and Daisy wondering aloud to the others.

行动：乔丹和黛西向其他人自言自语地疑惑着。

REACTION: Daisy calling attention to her finger.

反应：黛西注意到自己的手指。

The summer season has just begun, so Jordan starts the next beat by suggesting that they plan something to do. Daisy simply continues that action by repeating the question twice, not to her husband, but to Nick. But before Nick can answer, she instantly and literally wraps the conversation around her little finger. The value charges of marriage/divorce and excitement/boredom continue on pause.

夏天刚刚开始，乔丹提议他们计划一下活动，以此开启下一个话题。黛西只是重复了两遍这个问题，但不是问她丈夫，而是问尼克。尼克还没来得及回答，她就立刻掌控了局面。婚姻/离婚的价值判断，以及兴奋/无聊的情绪，暂时搁置。

BEAT 6

节拍 6

ACTION: Daisy accusing Tom of injuring her.

事件：黛西指控汤姆伤害了她。

REACTION: Tom hiding his reaction in silence.

反应：汤姆沉默不语，掩饰着自己的反应。

Daisy faces a crisis dilemma: She could insult her husband (negative), which might send a message to Gatsby (positive), or she could protect her marriage (positive) but not win Gatsby’s attention (negative). Daisy chooses to accuse her husband of bruising her finger. Again, Fitzgerald gives Tom no visible reaction, not a word of protest. The value charge of marriage/divorce turns dark, while excitement/boredom shines.

黛西面临着一个两难的抉择：她可以侮辱丈夫（负面），这或许能给盖茨比传递某种信息（正面）；或者她可以维护婚姻（正面），但却无法赢得盖茨比的关注（负面）。黛西最终选择指责丈夫弄伤了她的手指。菲茨杰拉德再次没有让汤姆表现出任何明显的反应，也没有让他说一句抗议的话。婚姻/离婚的价值判断变得阴暗，而兴奋/厌倦的情绪则闪耀着光芒。

BEAT 7

节拍 7

ACTION: Daisy insulting her husband in public.

事件：黛西在公共场合侮辱她的丈夫。

REACTION: Tom ordering her not to insult him again.

反应：汤姆命令她不许再侮辱他。

Daisy, then, with cool irony, insults her husband with a special emphasis on a word that she knows he hates: hulking. Finally, Tom objects.

于是，黛西带着一丝冷嘲热讽，特意强调了她丈夫最讨厌的一个词：魁梧。最后，汤姆终于忍不住反驳了。

Bear in mind that these are educated, upper-class characters, so when I use the verb “ordering” to name Tom’s reaction, it’s because that’s what he’s doing in the subtext. Tom is too well behaved to say, “Damn it, Daisy, never use the word ‘hulking’ again!” But under the phrase “I hate that word…” is an indirect command.

请记住，这些都是受过良好教育的上层阶级人物，所以我用“命令”这个词来形容汤姆的反应，是因为在言外之意中，他确实是在命令。汤姆举止得体，不会直接说：“该死的，黛西，以后不许再用‘魁梧’这个词！”但在“我讨厌这个词……”这句话背后，却隐藏着一个间接的命令。

Daisy’s insult throws marriage/divorce sharply to the negative, while in the subtext, excitement for Gatsby conquers her boredom.

黛西的侮辱将婚姻/离婚的负面含义急剧拉回到了原点，而言外之意是，她对盖茨比的兴奋战胜了她的无聊。

BEAT 8

节拍 8

ACTION: Daisy attacking him a second time.

行动：黛西第二次攻击他。

REACTION: Tom retreating in silence.

反应：汤姆默默地退了回去。

Daisy climaxes the scene by defying her husband’s order and repeating the hated word with emphasis. In reaction, Tom once more falls silent.

黛西违抗丈夫的命令，重重地重复了那个令他憎恶的词，将这场戏推向高潮。汤姆闻言，再次沉默不语。

Daisy wins her marital power struggle in six beats and humiliates Tom. This duel between husband and wife, Tom’s defeat and Daisy’s victory, would not be lost on her audience of the very sensitive, observant Nick and the gossipy Jordan Baker. Daisy knows this. Now she hopes that they’ll carry the news to Gatsby. Daisy has embarrassed her husband, and it has had the effect she wants.

黛西仅用了六秒钟就赢得了这场婚姻权力之争，让汤姆颜面尽失。这场夫妻间的较量，汤姆的失败和黛西的胜利，自然不会被她那两位心思细腻、观察入微的听众——尼克和爱嚼舌根的乔丹·贝克——所忽视。黛西深知这一点。现在，她希望他们能把这个消息告诉盖茨比。黛西让丈夫难堪，而这正是她想要的效果。

As Daisy chooses Gatsby over Tom, her marriage ends in all but name while her excitement about the future peaks.

黛西选择了盖茨比而不是汤姆，她的婚姻实际上已经结束，但她对未来的憧憬却达到了顶峰。

DIALOGUE VERSUS DESCRIPTION IN PROSE

散文中的对话与描述

As mentioned previously, prose writers (with exceptions) tend to keep their dramatized dialogue economical, simple, and plainspoken. Of the scene’s 123 spoken words, 107 are of one syllable, 14 of two syllables, and just 2 of three syllables. None of the scene’s characters uses metaphors or similes when they speak.

如前所述，散文作家（除少数例外）通常会使戏剧化的对话简洁明了、通俗易懂。在这一幕的123个对白中，107个是单音节词，14个是双音节词，只有2个是三音节词。这一幕中的所有角色在对话中都没有使用比喻或明喻。

Fitzgerald, on the other hand, enriches his descriptions with figurative language such as “Tom Buchanan compelled me from the room as though he were moving a checker to another square” and “… Miss Baker, sitting down at the table as if she were getting into bed.” When he uses polysyllabic words, they tend to be adverbs that describe tones of voice (contemptuously, accusingly, crossly) and actions (slenderly, languidly, radiantly).

另一方面，菲茨杰拉德则运用比喻等修辞手法来丰富他的描写，例如“汤姆·布坎南强迫我离开房间，就像他把棋子移到另一个格子上一样”以及“……贝克小姐在桌边坐下，就像她要上床睡觉一样”。当他使用多音节词时，它们往往是描述语气（轻蔑地、指责地、恼怒地）和动作（纤细地、慵懒地、容光焕发地）的副词。

The scene’s power comes from Daisy’s actions in the subtext, actions that Nick, limited by his first-person point of view, cannot know. Instead, Fitzgerald encourages the reader to see through Daisy’s veil of innocence by dropping hints along the way such as Daisy’s “demand” to know “What Gatsby?”

这一幕的力量源于黛西在字里行间流露出的意图，而尼克由于第一人称视角的限制，对此一无所知。菲茨杰拉德并没有直接告诉读者真相，而是通过黛西“质问”盖茨比“什么事？”等暗示，引导读者看穿黛西天真无邪的伪装。

TURNING POINT/SCENE CLIMAX

转折点/场景高潮

The scene arcs the Buchanan marriage dynamically from positive to negative in eight beats. In the first beat, their marriage seems respectful and faithful. By the last beat, Daisy’s actions reveal a marriage filled with hatred and disrespect as she plots her path back to Gatsby. At the same time, each negative action against the marriage becomes a positive beat for Daisy’s desire for the adventure that Gatsby brings to her life. Daisy’s tactic works: She wins the war against her husband and gives Jordan and Nick the message they will carry to Gatsby.

这一幕以八个片段动态地展现了布坎南夫妇婚姻从积极到消极的转变。在第一个片段中，他们的婚姻看似充满尊重和忠贞。到了最后一个片段，黛西的行动揭示了婚姻中充满仇恨和不尊重，她正密谋着回到盖茨比身边。与此同时，她每一个针对婚姻的负面举动，都转化为黛西渴望盖茨比带给她的冒险的契机。黛西的策略奏效了：她赢得了与丈夫的这场战争，并将信息传递给了乔丹和尼克，让他们转告盖茨比。

The eight beat progression takes this shape:

八拍进行的形式如下：

BEAT 1: Revealing/Concealing

第一拍：揭示/隐藏

BEAT 2: Walking/Planning

第二节：步行/规划

BEAT 3: Destroying/Concealing

第三节：摧毁/隐藏

BEAT 4: Opening a subject/Turning the subject to herself

第四拍：开启话题/将话题转向自身

BEAT 5: Wondering aloud/Turning attention to herself

第五拍：自言自语/将注意力转向自己

BEAT 6: Accusing/Hiding

第六拍：指控/隐瞒

BEAT 7: Insulting/Ordering

第七节：侮辱/命令

BEAT 8: Attacking/Retreating

第8回合：进攻/撤退

Each beat tops the previous beat, progressing to the turning point when Daisy defies her husband’s order and humiliates him—each beat, that is, except Beats 4 and 5. They seem to be a hole in the dialogue’s progression because they are not aimed at Daisy’s scene intention. Indeed they’re not, because Fitzgerald uses them for another, larger purpose related to the novel’s spine of action.

每一拍都比前一拍更精彩，最终在黛西违抗丈夫命令、羞辱他时达到转折点——除了第四拍和第五拍。这两拍似乎是对话推进中的一个漏洞，因为它们并非针对黛西的场景意图。事实上也的确如此，因为菲茨杰拉德运用它们另有更深远的目的，与小说的主线情节息息相关。

Notice the pattern in Beats 4 and 5: Daisy asks a question that opens up a general topic for the others, but then without pause, before anyone can answer, she instantly draws their interest back to her. Fitzgerald repeats this pattern in Daisy’s dialogue throughout the book. In ways that are amusing, sympathetic, or mysterious, Daisy constantly steers all talk back to herself. In other words, Fitzgerald wants us to understand that Daisy is a very beautiful, very charming narcissist.

注意第四和第五段的模式：黛西提出一个问题，引出一个可以讨论的话题，但随后她毫不犹豫，不等任何人回答，就立刻把大家的注意力拉回到自己身上。菲茨杰拉德在整本书中反复运用这种模式，让黛西的对话更加生动有趣。黛西总是以一种令人忍俊不禁、引人同情或神秘莫测的方式，将所有话题引回自己身上。换句话说，菲茨杰拉德想让我们明白，黛西是一个非常美丽、非常迷人的自恋者。

What is the real reason she creates this scene? Why can’t she defy her husband, break social convention, and visit Gatsby herself? Why must she send a veiled message through Jordan and Nick? Because narcissists call attention to themselves, never others. For Daisy, it is critical that Gatsby seek her out. Gatsby must come to her. Fitzgerald uses those beats and many others elsewhere to express the dueling spines of action that drive The Great Gatsby : Gatsby’s obsession with Daisy and Daisy’s obsession with Daisy.

她精心策划这场戏的真正原因是什么？为什么她不能违抗丈夫，打破社会习俗，亲自去见盖茨比？为什么她一定要通过乔丹和尼克传递隐晦的信息？因为自恋者总是吸引别人的注意力，而不是自己。对黛西来说，盖茨比主动来找她至关重要。盖茨比必须来找她。菲茨杰拉德运用这些节奏以及其他许多手法，来展现《了不起的盖茨比》中两条相互交织的情感主线：盖茨比对黛西的痴迷，以及黛西对黛西的痴迷。

#↩

17

REFLEXIVE CONFLICT

反思性冲突

INTRODUCTION TO THE SELF

自我介绍

Chapter One defined dialogue as any words said by any character to anyone. This traffic of talk runs along three distinct avenues: said to others, said to a reader or audience, and said to oneself. The chapter that follows focuses on the latter two tracks: direct address to the reader and inner dialogue between selves. Although the stage and screen limit the use of these two modes, for the novelist and short-story writer, they are the stuff of first-person prose.

第一章将对话定义为任何角色对任何人所说的话。这种对话交流沿着三个不同的路径展开：对他人说的话、对读者或观众说的话，以及自言自语。接下来的章节将重点讨论后两种路径：直接对读者的对话和角色之间的内心对话。尽管舞台和银幕限制了这两种模式的使用，但对于小说家和短篇小说作家来说，它们却是第一人称散文的精髓所在。

When characters talk directly to the reader, the topic tends to be past events and their impact on themselves (e.g., The Museum of Innocence ), whereas when characters talk to themselves, their inner dialogue acts out intra-dynamic events in the now. These dramatizations of self versus self carry psychological nuance into the depths of the unsayable (e.g., Fräulein Else ). Once again, it’s the difference between telling and showing.

当角色直接与读者对话时，话题往往是过往事件及其对自身的影响（例如，《纯真博物馆》）；而当角色自言自语时，他们的内心独白则展现了当下内心的动态变化。这种自我与自我的戏剧化呈现，将心理层面的细微差别带入到难以言说的深处（例如，《艾尔莎小姐》）。归根结底，这就是“讲述”与“展现”的区别。

In the former, a character with less than perfect self-awareness tells us about past inner conflicts and describes their effects; in the latter, a character puts her deep psychology into action in front of us and unknowingly dramatizes inner complexities she could never describe. Needless to say, telling and showing call upon two very different dialogue techniques.

前者中，一个自我认知不够完善的角色向我们讲述过往的内心冲突，并描述其影响；后者中，一个角色将她深层的心理活动展现在我们面前，无意间戏剧化地呈现了她永远无法言说的内心复杂性。毋庸置疑，“讲述”和“展示”运用了两种截然不同的对话技巧。

An ancient literary convention grants us the godlike power to overhear a character’s thoughts, all the while knowing that she is not talking to us. If so, then to whom is she speaking? Dialogue, by definition, is a two-sided exchange between a speaker and a listener. Who besides us is listening to her? If she’s talking to another self within herself, her mind must be dual. If dual or even multiple, how does her mind divide itself into selves? Exactly how many are there? Who are they? How do they link?

古老的文学惯例赋予我们如同神明般的力量，让我们能够窥探人物的内心想法，同时又清楚地知道她并非在与我们对话。如果真是如此，那么她究竟在与谁交谈？对话的定义是说话者和听者之间的双向交流。除了我们之外，还有谁在倾听她？如果她是在与自己内心的另一个自我对话，那么她的思维必然是二元的。如果是二元的，甚至是多元的，那么她的思维是如何分裂成多个自我的？究竟有多少个自我？它们是谁？它们之间又是如何联系的？

These questions are neither new nor unique to storytelling. Twenty-five hundred years ago, the Buddha taught his followers to ignore all such wonderings because they flow from the false premise that the self exists, when in fact it does not. The sense of “me,” he believed, is an illusionary side effect of uncountable, ever-shifting physical and sensory forces.

这些问题并非新颖，也并非故事讲述所独有。两千五百年前，佛陀就教导他的信徒们忽略所有此类疑问，因为它们源于一个错误的假设——“自我”存在，而事实上“自我”并不存在。他认为，“我”的概念只是无数变幻莫测的物质和感官力量所产生的幻觉。

About the same time, Socrates argued the opposite view. He taught his students that the self not only exists, but you cannot live a meaningful, civilized life without making every effort to know who you are. In the centuries since, this debate over the nature of intrapersonal communication has swung back and forth between these two philosophical extremes and remains unsettled at best.

大约在同一时期，苏格拉底提出了截然相反的观点。他教导学生，自我不仅存在，而且如果不竭尽全力去了解自己，就无法过上有意义、文明的生活。此后的几个世纪里，关于人际沟通本质的争论在这两种哲学极端之间摇摆不定，至今仍未有定论。

Science, on the other hand, has taken a stand. 1 Like Socrates, modern science strives to know the hidden nature of consciousness, but at the same time, like Buddha, it feels misled by intuition. While our sixth sense tells us we have a core of consciousness located behind our eyes, brain scan researchers report that several different mental processes, mediated by different brain regions, collaborate to create this illusion. No single, central, physical, all-controlling self exists; “me” is indeed a side effect. On the so-called “hard question” of consciousness, neuroscience now favors Buddha over Socrates but without a clear conclusion. 2

另一方面，科学已经表明了自己的立场。 1 与苏格拉底一样，现代科学致力于探寻意识的隐秘本质，但同时，也像佛陀一样，感到被直觉所误导。虽然我们的第六感告诉我们，意识的核心位于双眼之后，但脑部扫描研究人员报告称，由不同脑区介导的多种不同的心理过程共同作用，才产生了这种错觉。并不存在单一的、中心的、物理的、全能的自我；“我”实际上只是副产品。关于意识这个所谓的“难题”，神经科学现在更倾向于佛陀的观点而非苏格拉底，但尚未得出明确的结论。 2

Although science cannot ground consciousness in the physical, and philosophy cannot locate it in the metaphysical, artists know exactly where to find the self. When art whistles, the self comes running like a bounding dog. For the storyteller, the self makes its home in the same subjective reaches where it has always lived and thrived.

尽管科学无法将意识根植于物质世界，哲学也无法将其置于形而上学的范畴，艺术家却能精准地找到自我。当艺术吹响哨声，自我便如奔腾的犬只般奔涌而来。对于讲故事的人来说，自我栖息于它一直以来赖以生存和繁荣的主观领域。

Delusional or not, consciousness of self is the essence of our humanity. If, as science tells us, the self is not confined to a specific lobe of the brain but emerges out of a composite of sources, so what? It’s my composite and I like it. If, as philosophy claims, the unreliable self shifts and changes from one day to the next and, therefore, cannot be known absolutely, so what? It’s my changing self and I enjoy watching it evolve, hopefully into a better person.

无论这种自我意识是错觉还是真实存在，它都是我们人性的本质。如果正如科学所说，自我并非局限于大脑的某个特定区域，而是由多种因素共同构成，那又如何？这是我的自我，我喜欢它。如果正如哲学所言，不可靠的自我日复一日地变化，因此无法被绝对地认知，那又如何？这是我不断变化的自我，我乐于见证它的演变，希望它能让我成为一个更好的人。

For prose writers striving to express the inner life, philosophy’s deductive logic and science’s inductive logic dull aesthetic insight. Neither leverages the inside-out power of the subjective; neither creates the meaningful emotional experience of the self that every major work of story art since Homer inspires. Story doesn’t answer the “hard question”; it dramatizes it.

对于力图表达内心世界的散文作家而言，哲学的演绎逻辑和科学的归纳逻辑都会削弱审美洞察力。两者都无法发挥主观感受由内而外的力量；也无法创造出自荷马以来所有伟大故事艺术作品所激发的那种意义深远的自我情感体验。故事并不回答“难题”，而是将其戏剧化地呈现出来。

I think the best approach to creating inner dialogue is simply this: Treat your character’s mind like a setting, a world populated with a cast of characters called selves. Let the mindscape sprawl like a cityscape, landscape, or battleground, a mental mise-en-scène for the staging of a story. Then move into that world yourself and take up residence in the protagonist’s center of consciousness. From this point of view, create inner dialogues that dramatize an answer to the question “What is it to be this particular human being?”

我认为创作内心对话的最佳方法很简单：把角色的内心世界当作一个场景，一个充满各种“自我”的世界。让这片精神图景像城市景观、自然风光或战场一样广阔无垠，成为故事上演的心理舞台。然后，你自己也进入这个世界，占据主角的意识中心。从这个角度出发，创作出能够戏剧化地回答“作为这个人，意味着什么？”这个问题的内心对话。

To return to the question that started this introduction: When a character talks to herself, who besides the reader is listening? To whom is she speaking? Answer: the silent self. As we listen to a character talk to herself, we instinctively know that another side, a quiet side of herself, is listening. In fact, we know this so instinctively that we never think about it. We don’t have to because we know, without thinking, that we talk to our personal silent self constantly.

回到引言开头提出的问题：当一个角色自言自语时，除了读者之外，还有谁在倾听？她究竟在对谁说话？答案是：她内心深处那个沉默的自我。当我们倾听一个角色自言自语时，我们本能地知道，她内心深处另一个安静的自我正在聆听。事实上，这种认知如此根深蒂固，以至于我们从未刻意思考过。我们无需思考，因为我们无需思考便知道，我们一直在与自己内心深处那个沉默的自我对话。

Inside every mind, it seems to me, a separate, silent core of being sits back, watching, listening, evaluating, storing memories. If you meditate, you know this self very well. It floats behind you, so to speak, watching you do everything you do, including meditation. If you try to meditate toward this self, it instantly swings around behind you again. You cannot face yourself within yourself, but you always know that your silent self is there and aware, listening to everything you have to say.

在我看来，每个人的内心深处似乎都存在一个独立而静默的核心，它静静地待在那里，观察、聆听、评估、储存记忆。如果你冥想，你就会非常了解这个自我。它仿佛在你身后飘荡，注视着你所做的一切，包括冥想本身。如果你试图冥想面向这个自我，它会立刻再次回到你身后。你无法直面你内在的自我，但你始终知道，你那静默的自我就在那里，觉察着一切，聆听着你想要倾诉的一切。

As inner dialogues of prose cycle between the talking self and the silent self, they generate reflexivity.

作为说话的自我和沉默的自我之间循环往复的散文式内心对话，它们产生了反思性。

REFLEXIVE CONFLICT

反思性冲突

In the physical sciences, reflexivity refers to a circular or bidirectional relationship between cause and effect. An action triggers a reaction that impacts the action so fast the two seem simultaneous. (Some theories of quantum physics argue that at the subatomic level cause and effect are in fact simultaneous.) Action and reaction then lock together, whirling in a gyre. The cause becomes the effect, the effect becomes the cause, and neither can be clearly identified as either.

在物理科学中，自反性指的是因果关系中的循环或双向关系。一个作用引发的反应，其速度之快，以至于两者看似同时发生。（一些量子物理学理论认为，在亚原子层面，因果关系实际上是同时发生的。）作用和反应相互锁定，形成一个漩涡。原因变成了结果，结果又变成了原因，两者之间无法被清晰地识别。

In the social sciences, reflexivity signals a kind of codependency between individuals, or within groups, institutions, and societies. Once the reflexive spiral begins, neither the action nor its reaction can be assigned as the cause or the effect. The two so intra-influence each other, they seem to happen instantaneously, without the need for decisions or even thought.

在社会科学中，反思性标志着个体之间，或群体、机构和社会内部的一种相互依存关系。一旦反思螺旋开始，行动及其反应都无法被明确地定义为原因或结果。二者相互影响如此之深，以至于它们似乎瞬间发生，无需决策甚至思考。

In the art of story, reflexive conflict refers to those inner battles that begin when a character’s effort to resolve an inherent dilemma boomerangs back on herself. By taking her impasse inward, her effort to deal with her crisis becomes a cause that only worsens the effect. Self-contradictions generate ever-more complex sources of antagonism as causes become effects and effects become causes in an ever-deepening whorl until the conflict itself becomes the reason it cannot be solved.

在故事创作中，反身冲突指的是角色试图解决自身固有困境却适得其反，由此引发的内心斗争。角色将困境内化，试图解决危机的努力反而加剧了后果。这种自我矛盾不断滋生出更为复杂的对抗根源，原因变成结果，结果又变成原因，形成一个不断加深的漩涡，最终冲突本身成为其无法解决的原因。

Reflexive conflict translates into dialogue the moment a troubled character starts talking to herself. As I pointed out in Chapter One, the mind, by its very nature, can step back within itself to observe itself as if it were an object. A person temporarily splits in two to develop a relationship, often critical, between her core self and other sides or aspects of herself. She can project images of her past self, her unattractive self, her better self, her future self. She can feel the presence of her conscience, her subconscious, and, above all, her silent, listening self.

当一个内心挣扎的角色开始自言自语时，反思性冲突便转化为对话。正如我在第一章中指出的，人的思维本质上可以退后一步，审视自身，如同审视一个客体。一个人会暂时分裂成两个部分，在其核心自我与其他面向或面向之间建立一种关系，这种关系往往是批判性的。她可以投射出过去的自己、不讨喜的自己、更好的自己以及未来的自己。她可以感受到良知、潜意识，以及最重要的，那个沉默倾听的自我的存在。

At times these relationships may be conflictless as, for example, when we comfort ourselves with excuses, self-deceptions, or blame placed on others. But more often than not, our inner selves strike opposing sides in the struggle to make choices, do the right thing, sacrifice for another, bring a troubled self under control—any of the tumultuous contrarieties of the inner life. 3

有时，这些关系可能不会产生冲突，例如，当我们用借口、自欺欺人或将责任推卸给他人来安慰自己时。但更多时候，我们的内心会在做出选择、做正确的事、为他人牺牲、控制内心的挣扎中出现对立——这些都是内心生活中纷繁复杂的矛盾。

Reflexive conflicts can be acted out in the present tense directly or related indirectly in the past tense. Onstage and onscreen, a character can perform the former in soliloquy and the latter in either dialogue spoken to another character or in direct address to the audience. On page, the protagonist can talk to her other self and act out her inner conflicts in the present tense ( Fräulein Else ), or talk to the reader and describe previous episodes of reflexive conflict in the past tense ( The Museum of Innocence ).

反身冲突可以直接用现在时态展现，也可以用过去时态间接关联。在舞台和银幕上，角色可以通过独白来展现前者，也可以通过与其他角色的对话或直接与观众的对话来展现后者。在文字中，主人公可以与另一个自我对话，用现在时态展现其内心冲突（如《艾尔莎小姐》），也可以与读者对话，用过去时态描述先前发生的反身冲突（如《纯真博物馆》）。

FRÄULEIN ELSE

艾尔斯小姐

Arthur Schnitzler, the Austrian novelist and playwright, experimented with stream of consciousness throughout his career, beginning in 1901 with the short story, “Lieutenant Gustl.” In the 1924 novella Fräulein Else , he invited readers to eavesdrop on the troubled thoughts of its eponymous protagonist by writing exclusively in first-person inner dialogue.

奥地利小说家兼剧作家阿图尔·施尼茨勒在其整个创作生涯中都在尝试意识流手法，最早可追溯到 1901 年的短篇小说《古斯特尔中尉》。在 1924 年的中篇小说《艾尔莎小姐》中，他完全采用第一人称内心独白，邀请读者窥探同名主人公艾尔莎内心的挣扎。

SETUP

设置

Else, a beautiful nineteen-year-old Viennese debutante, on holiday with her aunt at an Austrian mountain resort, receives a letter from her mother telling her that her father, a lawyer, has been caught stealing tens of thousands from a client’s account. He faces prison or suicide if he can’t pay the money back in two days.

艾尔丝是一位美丽的十九岁维也纳名媛，正和姑姑在奥地利山区度假。一天，她收到母亲的来信，得知身为律师的父亲因盗窃客户账户中的数万欧元而被捕。如果两天之内无法偿还这笔钱，他将面临牢狱之灾或自杀。

Else’s mother begs her to save her father by asking Herr von Dorsday, a rich art dealer staying at the spa, for a loan to cover the theft. Else, despite her suffocating shame, asks the old man for help. He says he will telegraph the funds to cancel her father’s debt the next morning, but only if she repays him in sexual currency that night.

艾尔莎的母亲恳求她去向住在温泉疗养院的富有的艺术品商人冯·多尔斯代先生借钱，以弥补父亲被盗的损失。艾尔莎虽然羞愧难当，但还是向这位老人求助。老人说他会在第二天早上电报把钱寄过来，帮她父亲还债，但前提是她当晚要用性来偿还。

These three events—her father’s theft, her mother’s scheme, Dorsday’s proposition—trigger the story’s inciting incident and throw Else’s life radically and negatively out of balance. Two contradictory desires immediately flood her mind: to save her parents and sacrifice herself versus to save herself and sacrifice her parents. Either way she chooses, a great price must be paid, because when I say “save herself,” I mean that literally. Else’s identity is tied to her morality. If she saves her family, she loses her morality; if she loses her morality, she loses her identity.

这三件事——父亲的盗窃、母亲的阴谋、多尔斯戴的提议——引发了故事的导火索，彻底打破了艾尔丝的生活平衡，使她陷入了负面的境地。两种截然相反的愿望瞬间涌入她的脑海：拯救父母而牺牲自己，还是拯救自己而牺牲父母。无论她做出怎样的选择，都必须付出巨大的代价，因为我所说的“拯救自己”并非虚言。艾尔丝的身份认同与她的道德观紧密相连。如果她拯救了家人，她就会失去道德；如果她失去了道德，她就会失去自我。

Trapped by this double bind of irreconcilable goods/lesser of two evils, Else’s only path of action runs between her inner selves. So for the rest of the afternoon and evening, Else wanders the resort alone, her mind in reflexive chaos: At first, she tells herself to give in, save her family, and endure the disgrace; then she contradicts herself, choosing instead to reject Dorsday, and force her family to pay for its ignominy. At one point, she tries to cheer herself up, imagining that surrendering to Dorsday could launch a luxurious career as mistress to rich men, but then her conscience urges her to defend her moral self and accept poverty with honor.

被这种两难困境——既有善又有恶，只能二选一——所困，艾尔丝唯一的出路便是在她内心的挣扎中徘徊。于是，整个下午和晚上，艾尔丝独自在度假村里游荡，思绪纷乱：起初，她告诉自己应该屈服，为了拯救家人，忍受耻辱；随后她又自相矛盾，选择拒绝多尔斯代，让家人为他们的耻辱付出代价。她一度试图让自己振作起来，幻想着屈服于多尔斯代或许能让她开启一段奢华的情妇生涯，但随后她的良知又敦促她捍卫自己的道德底线，体面地接受贫穷。

Moral dilemmas like this, played out on a protagonist’s mindscape, often spiral into reflexive conflict. For example, as the moment to meet Dorsday nears, Else says to herself:

这类道德困境，在主人公的内心世界中上演，往往会演变成反复的冲突。例如，在与多尔斯戴见面的时刻临近时，艾尔丝对自己说：

How huge the hotel is. Like a monstrous, illuminated magic castle. Everything is gigantic. The mountains, too. Terrifyingly gigantic. They’ve never been so black before. The moon hasn’t risen yet. It will rise just in time for the performance, the great performance in the meadow, when Herr von Dorsday makes his female slave dance naked. What’s Herr von Dorsday to me? Now, Mademoiselle Else, what are you making such a fuss about? You were ready to go off and be the mistress of strange men, one after the other. And you boggle at the trifle which Herr von Dorsday asks of you? You were ready to sell yourself for a pearl necklace, for beautiful clothes, for a villa by the sea? And your father’s life isn’t worth as much as that?”

这家酒店真大啊。简直像一座巨大的、灯火辉煌的魔法城堡。一切都那么巨大。连山也一样。高耸入云，令人胆寒。它们从未如此漆黑过。月亮还没升起。它会在演出开始前升起，草地上那场盛大的演出即将开始，届时冯·多尔斯代先生会让他那女奴赤身裸体地跳舞。冯·多尔斯代先生跟我有什么关系？艾尔莎小姐，你这是在闹什么？你之前还准备去当一个接一个陌生男人的情妇呢。现在冯·多尔斯代先生这点小要求，你却瞠目结舌？你之前还准备为了一个珍珠项链、漂亮的衣服、海边的别墅就出卖自己？而你父亲的命，难道还不如这些值钱吗？

Reflexive Dialogue

反思性对话

Fourteen thoughts ricochet through this passage of inner dialogue. In the first seven (from “How huge” to “hasn’t risen yet”) Else’s imagination projects her terror and sense of frailty onto the frightening, enormous, almost unreal world around her. The word “magic” gives away her childlike state.

十四个念头在这段内心独白中交织碰撞。在前七个念头中（从“多么巨大”到“还没升起”），艾尔丝将她的恐惧和脆弱感投射到周围那个可怕、巨大、近乎虚幻的世界中。“魔法”一词暴露了她孩童般的心智。

Then her mind grabs the last word of the seventh sentence, “yet,” and free-associates to an image of her future self, naked and dancing in the moonlight. With the rhetorical question “What’s Herr von Dorsday to me?” she tries to shrug off the insinuations in the word “slave” and feign indifference.

然后，她的思绪抓住了第七句话的最后一个词“然而”，并自由联想到未来自己赤身裸体在月光下翩翩起舞的画面。她用反问句“冯·多尔斯代先生与我何干？”试图摆脱“奴隶”一词的暗示，装出一副漠不关心的样子。

But suddenly, her mind seems to segue into another self, armed with a sharp, critical voice. For the next five lines this critical self whiplashes Else’s core self with a series of “Damned if you do/damned if you don’t” insults. The critical self calls her a hypocrite, “such a fuss” (damned if you don’t); then a slut, “mistress of strange men” (damned if you do); then a coward, “you boggle” (damned if you don’t); then a slut again, “sell yourself” (damned if you do); and finally an ingrate, “your father’s life” (damned if you don’t).

但突然间，她的思绪仿佛切换到了另一个自我，一个尖锐而批判的声音。接下来的五行，这个批判的自我用一系列“进退两难”的侮辱鞭挞着艾尔丝的核心自我。批判的自我骂她是伪君子，“真是个小题大做”（进退两难）；然后骂她是荡妇，“和陌生男人鬼混”（进退两难）；接着骂她是懦夫，“你真可笑”（进退两难）；然后又骂她是荡妇，“出卖自己”（进退两难）；最后骂她是忘恩负义的，“你父亲的命”（进退两难）。

Else’s mind spins in reflexive conflict: “Which do I want to be? A jewel-decked whore or a cowardly ingrate?” She dreads both and wants neither, but question mark after question mark paralyzes her until the passage ends in mental gridlock. Spoiler alert: At the climax of the novel, Else’s impasse explodes into an act of wild exhibitionism and a drug overdose.

艾尔斯的思绪在反复的冲突中翻腾：“我到底想成为哪一个？一个珠光宝气的妓女，还是一个懦弱的忘恩负义之徒？”她害怕这两种身份，却又都不想成为，但一个又一个的问号让她动弹不得，最终，这段文字以她精神上的僵局告终。剧透警告：在小说的高潮部分，艾尔斯的困境最终演变成一场疯狂的暴露行为和吸毒过量。

As we have seen in previous examples, emotions tend to shorten lines, while rationality tends to lengthen them. As fear races through Else, her first seven thoughts average 4.1 words each. But then the critical self takes charge and the next seven lines average 14.5 words.

正如我们在之前的例子中所看到的，情绪往往会缩短句子的长度，而理性则往往会延长句子的长度。当恐惧席卷艾尔丝时，她最初的七个想法平均每个只有4.1个词。但随后，批判性的自我占据了主导地位，接下来的七行平均每个有14.5个词。

Writing In-Character

角色扮演写作

When Arthur Schnitzler published Fräulein Else , he was a sixty-two-year-old man writing in the first-person inner voice of a nineteen-year-old socialite. How is this possible? First, he wrote plays as well as prose, so his dramatist skills must have helped him find words for this character. Then, life experience. He married a twenty-one-year-old actress when he was forty-one. In fact, over a lifetime he had many affairs with young women. Each must have given him a chance to hear a fresh voice and imagine life from a new and female point of view.

阿图尔·施尼茨勒发表《艾尔莎小姐》时，已是六十二岁高龄，却以十九岁社交名媛的第一人称内心独白来写作。这怎么可能呢？首先，他既写散文也写剧本，他的戏剧功底必然帮助他找到了适合这个人物的语言。其次，人生阅历也功不可没。他四十一岁时娶了一位二十一岁的女演员。事实上，他一生中与许多年轻女性有过恋情。每一次经历都让他有机会聆听新鲜的声音，并从女性的视角重新审视人生。

But my best guess is this: In addition to talent, skill, and a practiced ear, Schnitzler could act. Maybe not in front of an audience, but at his desk and pacing his study. He became her. He wrote in-character, a technique we will explore in Chapter Nineteen.

但我的最佳推测是：除了天赋、技巧和敏锐的听觉之外，施尼茨勒还会表演。或许他不会在观众面前表演，但他会在书桌前踱步，仿佛自己就是她。他会以角色的身份写作，我们将在第十九章探讨这种技巧。

THE MUSEUM OF INNOCENCE

纯真博物馆

Orhan Pamuk published The Museum of Innocence two years after winning the 2006 Nobel Prize in Literature. He worked long and hard with novelist Maureen Freely to perfect the English translation. The English edition, rather than the original Turkish, was the likely basis for further translations (sixty languages to date), and so its faithfulness was critical.

奥尔罕·帕慕克在荣获2006年诺贝尔文学奖两年后出版了《纯真博物馆》。他与小说家莫琳·弗里利通力合作，对英文译本进行了长时间的精心打磨。英文版而非土耳其语原版更有可能成为后续译本（迄今为止已有六十种语言译本）的基础，因此其忠实度至关重要。

SETUP

设置

Pamuk’s novel tells a story of love at first sight and its conflict-filled aftermath. Kemal, a Turkish businessman, has converted a house in Istanbul into a repository of mementos and memories he calls The Museum of Innocence . Like the Taj Mahal, the museum celebrates love. In Kemal’s case, nine passionate years with Füsun, his exquisitely beautiful lover and eventual wife, now deceased.

帕慕克的这部小说讲述了一个一见钟情的故事，以及随之而来的种种冲突。土耳其商人凯末尔将伊斯坦布尔的一栋房子改造成了一座收藏纪念品和回忆的博物馆，他称之为“纯真博物馆”。如同泰姬陵一样，这座博物馆颂扬着爱情。在凯末尔的例子中，它颂扬的是他与美艳绝伦的情人芙菘（他最终的妻子，现已去世）之间长达九年的激情岁月。

The author’s unique narrative strategy places Kemal inside the museum, where he acts as docent and guide to its exhibits. Pamuk then treats the reader as a visitor to the museum, allowing Docent Kemal to speak to the reader in first person as if the reader were the museum’s guest.

作者独特的叙事策略将凯末尔置于博物馆之中，让他担任讲解员和导览员。帕慕克随后将读者视为博物馆的参观者，让讲解员凯末尔以第一人称与读者对话，仿佛读者就是博物馆的客人。

Nine tumultuous, love-soaked years have seasoned Docent Kemal to maturity. But living in his memory is the museum’s main exhibit: Kemal’s previous, immature, ultra-romantic self. Throughout Kemal’s youth, this self feverously sought something he could not grasp. He told himself he was in love with Füsun and, up to a point, he was. But deep within, his true obsession was a passion for passion. He quested after that ancient and elusive absolute: the life-fulfilling, transcendent romantic experience. Füsun merely played a role in his all-consuming drama.

九年风雨飘摇、情爱缠身的岁月，让讲解员凯末尔逐渐成熟。然而，博物馆的主要展品，却依然活在他的记忆中：他年轻时那个不成熟、极度浪漫的自己。在凯末尔的青春岁月里，这个自己狂热地追寻着某种他永远无法企及的东西。他告诉自己，他爱上了芙荪，某种程度上，的确如此。但在内心深处，他真正痴迷的是对激情本身的渴望。他苦苦追寻着那古老而又难以捉摸的绝对真理：一种能够充实人生、超越尘世的浪漫体验。芙荪只不过是他那场吞噬一切的爱情剧中的一个角色而已。

Obsessive romantics devour the rites of romance: quiet walks in moonlight, tireless lovemaking, candlelit dinners, champagne, classical music, poetry, sunsets, and the like. But these enthralling rituals are pointless without an exquisite creature to share them, and so the man-in-love-with-romance tragedy begins when he falls for a woman because, and only because, she is gorgeous. Young Kemal, in other words, suffered from the curse of beauty: that insatiable craving for the sublime that makes living a simple life unthinkable.

痴迷浪漫的人沉迷于各种浪漫仪式：月光下的静谧漫步、酣畅淋漓的爱抚、烛光晚餐、香槟、古典音乐、诗歌、日落等等。然而，如果没有一位绝世佳人与之共度，这些令人陶醉的仪式便毫无意义。于是，当男人爱上一个女人仅仅因为她美艳绝伦时，浪漫悲剧便由此开始。换句话说，年轻的凯末尔患上了美貌的诅咒：对极致之美的永不满足的渴望，使他无法想象过简单的生活。

Having created these two selves, Docent Kemal and Romantic Kemal, the author needed to characterize the two voices and solve three dialogue problems: 1) In what tone and manner would the Docent Self speak to a visitor? 2) How would the Docent Self express the Romantic Self’s silent inner dialogue? 3) When we hear Romantic Kemal speak, what qualities would texture his voice?

作者创造了讲解员凯末尔和浪漫凯末尔这两个自我之后，需要刻画这两个自我的声音，并解决三个对话问题：1）讲解员自我会以怎样的语气和方式与参观者交谈？2）讲解员自我会如何表达浪漫凯末尔自我内心的无声对话？3）当我们听到浪漫凯末尔说话时，他的声音会呈现出怎样的特质？

The passage below answers those questions as Docent Kemal talks to us:

以下段落解答了这些问题，是凯末尔老师在与我们交谈时提出的：

I have here the clock, and these matchsticks and matchbooks, because the display suggests how I spent the slow ten or fifteen minutes it took me to accept that Füsun was not coming that day. As I paced the rooms, glancing out the windows, stopping in my tracks from time to time, standing motionless, I would listen to the pain sluicing within me. As the clocks in the apartment ticked away, my mind would fixate on the seconds and the minutes to distract myself from the agony. As the appointed hour neared, the sentiment “Today, yes, she’s coming, now” would bloom inside me, like spring flowers. At such moments I wanted time to flow faster so that I could be reunited with my lovely at once. But those minutes would never pass. For a moment, in a fit of clarity, I would understand that I was fooling myself, that I did not want the time to flow at all, because Füsun might never come. By two o’clock I was never sure whether to be happy that the hour had arrived, or sad that with every passing minute her arrival was less likely, and the distance between me and my beloved would grow as that between a passenger on a ship leaving port and the one he had left behind. So I would try to convince myself that not so very many minutes had passed, toward this end I would make little bundles of time in my head. Instead of feeling pain every second of every minute, I resolved to feel it only once every five! In this way I would take the pain of five discrete minutes and suffer it all in the last. But this too was for naught when I could no longer deny that the first five minutes had passed—when I was forced to accept that she was not coming, the forestalled pain would sink into me like a driven nail…

我这里有钟，还有这些火柴和火柴盒，因为它们摆在那里，仿佛在诉说着我是如何度过那漫长的十分钟或十五分钟，才最终接受芙蓉今天不会来的事实。我在房间里踱来踱去，不时地望向窗外，时不时地停下脚步，一动不动地站着，倾听着内心深处涌动的痛苦。公寓里的钟表滴答作响，我的思绪便会聚焦在秒和分钟上，试图以此分散自己对痛苦的注意力。随着约定的时间临近，“今天，是的，她会来的，现在就来”的念头会在我心中像春花般绽放。在这样的时刻，我多么希望时间能够快点过去，让我立刻就能与心爱的人重聚。但那些时间却仿佛永远不会流逝。在某个瞬间，我突然清醒过来，意识到自己只是在自欺欺人，我根本不希望时间流逝，因为芙蓉或许永远不会来。到了两点，我总是拿不定主意，该为时间的流逝而高兴，还是该为她到来的可能性越来越小而悲伤，我和心爱之人之间的距离就像离港的船上乘客和被他留下的亲人之间的距离一样越来越远。于是，我努力说服自己时间并没有过去多久，为此，我在脑海中把时间分成一个个小段。与其每分每秒都感到痛苦，我决定每五分钟才感受一次！这样，我就能把五分钟的痛苦全部集中到最后承受。但这一切也都徒劳无功，因为我再也无法否认前五分钟已经过去——当我不得不接受她不会来了的事实时，那被压抑的痛苦就像钉子一样深深地扎进了我的心底……

Docent Kemal begins this passage in the present tense as if he were standing in front of an exhibit case filled with heirlooms and speaking to a visitor. But The Museum of Innocence is primarily a temporal museum; its chief artifacts are episodes from a love story, taken out of time and placed in its galleries. So Docent Kemal switches to the past tense as he puts Romantic Kemal, trapped in an archived event, on display.

讲解员凯末尔以现在时开始这段叙述，仿佛他正站在摆满传家宝的展柜前，与参观者交谈。但纯真博物馆本质上是一座时间博物馆；其主要展品是一段爱情故事的片段，这些片段被从时间中抽离出来，陈列在展厅中。因此，讲解员凯末尔转而使用过去时，将那个被困于一段历史事件中的浪漫凯末尔呈现在世人面前。

Docent Kemal quotes Romantic Kemal just once with four present-tense phrases: “today,” “yes,” “she’s coming,” and “now,” uttered with the staccato of excitement. Other than this exception, Docent Kemal leaves the implied line-by-line thoughts of Romantic Kemal’s inner dialogue to the reader/visitor’s imagination. In the sixth sentence, a third self, Critical Kemal, appears briefly to chide Romantic Kemal for his childish self-deceptions.

讲解员凯末尔只引用了浪漫凯末尔一次的话，用了四个现在时短语：“今天”、“是的”、“她要来了”和“现在”，语速急促，充满兴奋。除此之外，讲解员凯末尔将浪漫凯末尔内心独白的每一行都留给了读者/参观者的想象。在第六句话中，第三个自我——批判的凯末尔——短暂出现，斥责浪漫凯末尔幼稚的自欺欺人。

Docent/guest is a ceremonial relationship, more formal than professor/student. Professors and their students engage in the excitement of ideas, but the docent and museum guest join in a solemn reverence for the past. Therefore, Docent Kemal’s dialogue pours out flowing, elegiac sentences.

讲解员/参观者是一种仪式性的关系，比教授/学生的关系更为正式。教授和学生沉浸在思想的激情之中，而讲解员和博物馆参观者则共同怀着对历史的庄严敬畏。因此，讲解员凯末尔的对话充满了流畅而哀婉的诗句。

The passage runs 325 words long in eleven sentences that average 29.5 words each. Subordinate clauses in series build each sentence to a mini-climax: “pain sluicing within me,” “distract myself from the agony,” “Füsun might never come,” and so on. The passage’s formality and grace also suggest that Docent Kemal has relived this scene again and again, recited it to many guests many times, perfecting his wording with each rendition.

这段文字共325个单词，分为11个句子，平均每个句子29.5个单词。从句层层递进，将每个句子推向一个小小的高潮：“痛苦在我体内翻涌”、“分散注意力以摆脱痛苦”、“扶桑可能永远不会来”等等。这段文字的正式性和优美也表明，凯末尔老师曾反复回味这一场景，并多次向来宾讲述，每次都力求精益求精。

Although Docent Kemal is no longer the hopeless romantic he once was, nostalgia for romance still fills his voice. He is as much poet as docent. So to characterize his protagonist’s heightened romantic imagination, Pamuk interlaces Docent Kemal’s descriptions with metaphors and similes. Here and there the docent resorts, as people do, to clichés: sugar-sweet images such as thoughts blooming like spring flowers inside Romantic Kemal, and the tear-streaked B-movie scene of a passenger on a departing ship gazing back at a beloved left on shore. Docent Kemal’s most personal language, however, goes dark and animates pain: Liquid pain flows through his body, then takes the form of a driven nail. In the most vivid image of all, he transforms time into the conduit for pain, complete with a mental valve, as it were, that can turn it on and off.

尽管讲解员凯末尔不再是曾经那个无可救药的浪漫主义者，但他话语中依然流露出对浪漫的怀念。他既是讲解员，也是诗人。为了刻画主人公丰富的浪漫想象力，帕慕克在凯末尔的描述中穿插了隐喻和明喻。讲解员偶尔也会像人一样，诉诸陈词滥调：比如浪漫的凯末尔心中思绪如春花般绽放，或是泪流满面的B级片场景——乘客在离港的船上回望岸边的爱人。然而，凯末尔最私密的语言却阴郁而生动地描绘了痛苦：剧痛如液体般流淌过他的身体，最终化作一根钉入的钉子。在所有意象中最鲜明的，他将时间转化为痛苦的通道，仿佛还配备了一个可以控制痛苦开关的心理阀门。

Of the passage’s eleven sentences, the word “would” finds its way into all but the first line. “Would” is the past tense of the verb “will,” but in this context the author uses it as a modal to create a soft sense of uncertainty.

在这段文字的十一句话中，“would”一词除了第一句之外，其余每一句都出现了。“would”是动词“will”的过去式，但在这里，作者将其用作情态动词，以营造一种淡淡的不确定感。

Feel, for example, the difference between the hard versus the soft expression of the same ideas: “I listen to” and “my mind fixates on” as opposed to “I would listen to” and “my mind would fixate on.” Instead of the phrase “pain sunk into me,” the translator uses “pain would sink into me” to give the moment a sense of melancholy. Overall, the frequent repetition of “would” softens the hard edge of reality and spreads an aura of things happening as much in its characters’ imaginations as in an actual room in the actual past.

例如，感受一下同一概念的生硬表达与柔和表达之间的差异：“我听着”和“我的思绪专注于”与“我会听着”和“我的思绪会专注于”之间的区别。译者没有使用“痛苦沉入我的内心”，而是用“痛苦会沉入我的内心”，赋予了这一刻一种忧郁的意味。总的来说，“会”的频繁重复柔化了现实的生硬感，营造出一种氛围，仿佛事情既发生在人物的想象中，也发生在过去某个真实的房间里。

The phrase “would never” intimates unknown repetitions; “would try” hints at hope and wishing. Taken together, ten “woulds” yield an air of things that may or may not happen. The word “suggests” and the phrase “ten or fifteen” further distend this shifting atmosphere, until Docent Kemal’s dialogue sounds like what it is: a memory in the mind of a failed romantic.

“绝不”暗示着未知的重复；“会尝试”则暗含希望和愿望。十个“会”加在一起，营造出一种可能发生也可能不发生的氛围。“暗示”一词以及“十个或十五个”的短语进一步加剧了这种变幻莫测的气氛，最终，凯末尔老师的对话听起来就像它本身：一个失败的浪漫主义者脑海中的回忆。

Reflexive Conflict

反思性冲突

Pamuk’s writing draws its energy from two sources of reflexive conflict: the tyranny of love and the tyranny of time.

帕慕克的写作能量来源于两种反思性冲突：爱情的暴政和时间的暴政。

The tyranny of love: While engaged to another woman, Romantic Kemal met Füsun, a beautiful shop clerk. The lightning of love at first sight struck, and his life veered out of control on a trajectory aimed at the transcendent romantic experience. Romantic Kemal blames fate, but fate is the excuse we use when our subconscious pries our hands off the wheel of life.

爱情的暴政：浪漫的凯末尔与另一位女子订婚后，邂逅了美丽的店员芙松。一见钟情的闪电击中了他，他的人生从此失控，踏上了一段追求极致浪漫体验的旅程。浪漫的凯末尔将这一切归咎于命运，但命运不过是我们潜意识挣脱人生方向盘时用来推卸责任的借口罢了。

The arch-romantic wants his beloved with him every minute of every hour of every day. Suffering her absence causes more suffering as the agony of loneliness feeds on itself, making her absence all the more acute. The more he thinks about it, the worse it gets. If and when she were to finally show up, who knows how his mood might have reversed.

这位极度浪漫的人渴望心爱之人每时每刻都陪伴在侧。她的缺席带来的痛苦与日俱增，孤独的煎熬不断滋生，令他更加难以忍受。他越是思念，就越是痛苦不堪。如果她真的出现，谁知道他的心情会如何转变呢？

The tyranny of time: The clock on the wall measures time, but our inner Big Ben has no hands. Sometimes hours vanish in a glance; sometimes a minute drags by longer than an arctic February. Romantic Kemal tries concentrating on time because he thinks it will soothe his torment: “As the clocks in the apartment ticked away, my mind would fixate on the seconds and the minutes to distract myself from the agony.” But fixating on time makes its passage all the more excruciating. He tries to bring time under control by bundling it, parsing it, speeding it, slowing it, but his battle to rein time only gives time all the more power to torture him.

时间的暴政：墙上的钟表计量着时间，但我们内心的“大本钟”却没有指针。有时，几个小时转瞬即逝；有时，一分钟却比北极的二月还要漫长。浪漫的凯末尔试图专注于时间，因为他认为这能抚慰他的痛苦：“公寓里的钟滴答作响，我的思绪便会集中在秒和分钟上，以此分散自己对痛苦的注意力。”然而，执着于时间只会让流逝更加痛苦。他试图通过捆绑、分析、加速、减缓时间来控制时间，但他试图驾驭时间的努力，却只会让时间拥有更大的力量来折磨他。

This is the nature of reflexivity: The character inflicts it on himself and then persists in stirring its poison. Needless to say, reflexive conflict offers the storyteller soaring dialogue opportunities.

这就是反身性的本质：角色将这种冲突强加于自身，然后又不断地加剧这种毒害。毋庸置疑，反身性冲突为叙事者提供了精彩纷呈的对话素材。

A final note: Docent Kemal portrays Romantic Kemal’s passion with a powerful and yet self-obsessed intensity. When Füsun doesn’t show up, he might have thought: “My God, did something happen to her? Is she hurt?” But he didn’t. Instead, he dissected his painful anticipation of pleasure to the microsecond. For the romantic, it is, as we say, always about him.

最后一点：凯末尔老师以一种既强烈又自我中心的强烈情感，刻画了浪漫主义者凯末尔的激情。当芙荪没有出现时，他或许会想：“天哪，她出什么事了吗？她受伤了吗？”但他并没有。相反，他将自己对快乐的痛苦期待细细剖析到每一微秒。正如我们所说，对于浪漫主义者而言，一切都以他为中心。

#↩

18

MINIMAL CONFLICT

最小冲突

INTRODUCTION: THE BALANCE OF TEXT AND SUBTEXT

引言：文本与潜台词的平衡

Every line of dialogue strikes a balance between the literal meaning of the words said and the unsaid meanings that the reader/audience senses resounding through the subtext.

每一句对话都力求在字面意思和读者/观众通过字面意思感受到的弦外之音之间取得平衡。

When this balance tilts so that a minor motivation causes a massive vocal response, dialogue sounds hollow and the scene feels forged. Recall the definition of melodrama from Chapter Six: the overwrought expression of limp needs. Like chefs who use rich sauces to hide spoiled food, writers who whip up blubbery stylistics to smother stale content risk the sour odor of melodrama.

当这种平衡被打破，以至于一个微不足道的动机就能引发强烈的情感反应时，对话就会显得空洞，场景也会显得矫揉造作。回想一下第六章中对情节剧的定义：对软弱无力的需求进行过度渲染。就像厨师用浓郁的酱汁掩盖变质的食物一样，作家如果用矫揉造作的文风来掩盖陈腐的内容，也会落入情节剧的俗套。

When balance levels out so that unsaid thoughts and feelings transcribe directly and fully into what is said, we call this blatancy writing on-the-nose. If a scene’s implicit and explicit meanings echo each other, subtext turns into text, depth dries up, lines sound tinny, and the acting clanks.

当平衡被打破，未言明的想法和感受直接而完整地转化为言语时，我们称之为直白的表达。如果一个场景的隐含意义和显性意义相互呼应，潜台词就变成了明文，深度消失殆尽，台词听起来单薄乏味，表演也显得生硬做作。

When the balance favors content over form, when minimal words express maximal meaning, dialogue gains its greatest credibility and power. Using Robert Browning’s famous phrase, “Less is more.” 1 Any word that can be cut should be cut, especially if its loss adds to the line’s effect. Sparseness of language gives the reader or audience a chance to peer ever more deeply into the unsaid and unsayable. With few exceptions, when understatement takes the upper hand, dialogue resonates.

当内容重于形式，当最少的文字表达最大的意义时，对话便能获得最大的可信度和力量。正如罗伯特·勃朗宁的名言：“少即是多。”任何可以删减的词都应该删减，尤其当删减反而能增强句子的效果时。语言的简洁让读者或听众有机会更深入地探究那些未说出口和不可言说的深意。几乎无一例外，当含蓄的表达占据主导地位时，对话便能引起共鸣。

What follows is a superb example of the fewest possible words used to express the maximum possible feeling and meaning.

下面这个例子堪称典范，它用最少的文字表达了最丰富的情感和意义。

LOST IN TRANSLATION

迷失在翻译中

Sofia Coppola wrote and directed LOST IN TRANSLATION when she was thirty-two. It was her fourth script to reach the screen and her second feature to direct. The film won numerous awards around the world, including an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.

索菲亚·科波拉32岁时自编自导了《迷失东京》。这是她第四部搬上银幕的剧本，也是她执导的第二部长片。该片荣获全球众多奖项，其中包括奥斯卡最佳原创剧本奖。

Coppola grew up surrounded by artists, she has traveled to Japan many times, and, like all of us, she has won and lost at love. So although it’s fair to assume that personal experience influenced Coppola’s storytelling, it would be a mistake to treat LOST IN TRANSLATION as autobiography. Rather, her writing expresses the widely read, finely tuned mind of an artist who uses fiction to express her insights into life’s secret places.

科波拉成长于艺术氛围浓厚的家庭，她曾多次前往日本，而且和我们所有人一样，她也经历过爱情的得失。因此，尽管我们可以合理地推断个人经历影响了科波拉的叙事风格，但将《迷失东京》视为自传则大错特错。更确切地说，她的作品展现了一位博览群书、思维敏锐的艺术家，她借由虚构的故事来表达自己对人生隐秘角落的深刻洞察。

In Coppola’s minimalist writing, dialogue progression does not use arguments to sling words like stones (the conjugal hostilities of A Raisin in the Sun ) or manipulations to weave words into a trap (Daisy’s malicious feigning in The Great Gatsby ).
