Instead, subtle, indirect, sparse language shapes implicit, virtually invisible but deeply felt conflicts that haunt her characters out of their pasts and into the present.

在科波拉极简主义的写作风格中，对话的推进并非依靠争论来像扔石头一样抛掷言语（如《阳光下的葡萄干》中夫妻间的敌意），也并非通过操纵语言来设下陷阱（如《了不起的盖茨比》中黛西的恶意伪装）。相反，微妙、间接、简洁的语言塑造出隐晦的、几乎难以察觉却又深刻的冲突，这些冲突如影随形地萦绕在人物的过去和现在。

In the scene below, Coppola works into the inner selves and past selves of her characters simultaneously. She reveals both in each without resorting to choices under the pressure of dilemma.

在下面的场景中，科波拉同时展现了角色的内心世界和过往经历。她巧妙地将两者融合在每个角色身上，而无需让他们在困境的压力下做出选择。

Choices between irreconcilable goods and the lesser of two evils, once poised, are profoundly revealing of true character but relatively easy to dramatize. Coppola takes another path: Her characters are not in conflict with what life imposes but with the emptiness of what life denies. This quiet scene hooks, holds, and pays off without direct, indirect, or reflexive conflict.

在不可调和的善与恶之间做出选择，或者在两害相权取其轻之间做出抉择，一旦摆在眼前，便能深刻揭示人物的真实性格，而且相对容易戏剧化呈现。科波拉另辟蹊径：她笔下的人物并非与生活强加的事物发生冲突，而是与生活所否定的空虚感抗争。这种静谧的场景无需直接、间接或反身的冲突，便能牢牢抓住观众的心，并最终达到高潮。

SETUP

设置

The key to creating a scene of minimum dialogue and maximum impact is its setup. If, prior to a scene, the storytelling has brought characters to crisis points in their lives, the reader/audience can sense their needs swirling in the subtext. These desires may or may not be conscious, but the reader/audience knows them, feels them, and waits in high tension to see how they play out. A well-prepared reader/audience reads chapters of content implied behind a phrase or gesture.

用最少的对白营造最大冲击力的场景，关键在于场景的铺垫。如果在场景开始之前，叙事已经将角色推向了人生的危机时刻，读者/观众就能感受到字里行间涌动的需求。这些需求或许是角色有意识的，或许是无意识的，但读者/观众能够感知到它们，并带着高度紧张的心情等待着剧情的发展。一个准备充分的读者/观众能够解读隐藏在字里行间或手势背后的深层含义。

LOST IN TRANSLATION perfects this technique. The film’s opening scenes crosscut to counterpoint dual protagonists: Charlotte, a recent Yale graduate, traveling with her photographer husband, versus Bob Harris, a middle-aged Hollywood star, famous for action roles. As the two settle into the Park Hyatt Tokyo, we see their differences of age (at least thirty years), fame (everyone ignores Charlotte; everyone fawns on Bob), and marriage (she needs her husband’s attention; he wishes his wife would leave him alone).

《迷失东京》将这种手法运用得炉火纯青。影片开场采用交叉剪辑，对比了两位主人公：一位是刚从耶鲁大学毕业、与摄影师丈夫一同旅行的夏洛特；另一位是中年好莱坞明星鲍勃·哈里斯，以动作片闻名。两人入住东京柏悦酒店后，我们看到了他们年龄（至少相差三十岁）、名气（夏洛特被人忽视，鲍勃却备受追捧）以及婚姻状况（她需要丈夫的关注，而他却希望妻子别来烦他）的巨大差异。

That day, they notice each other in passing twice—once in an elevator and later in the lounge. That night, neither can sleep, so they make their way to the hotel bar where they meet by chance.

那天，他们两次擦肩而过——一次是在电梯里，另一次是在休息室。当晚，两人都辗转难眠，于是前往酒店酒吧，在那里偶然相遇。

Scene Intentions

场景意图

As the scene opens, Charlotte and Bob seem to share a simple need: to kill time over a drink. But if all they really wanted was a drink, they could have opened their minibars. Instead, an unthought wish for someone to talk to sends them out of their rooms. Once they see each other, their scene intention becomes: to kill time with talk.

场景伊始，夏洛特和鲍勃似乎只是想找个人喝一杯消磨时间。但如果他们真的只是想喝酒，完全可以打开迷你吧。然而，一个想要找人聊聊天的念头驱使他们走出了房间。当他们相遇时，他们的意图就变成了：通过聊天来消磨时间。

Scene Values

场景值

As Charlotte nears Bob sitting at the bar, tension rises. Earlier that day, she and he exchanged a smile, but suppose he turns out to be an arrogant bore, or he discovers that she’s a lunatic fan. The question “Should I talk to this stranger or drink alone?” runs through the minds of both. Those doubts charge the tension of comfortable isolation versus risky intimacy that opens the scene and inflects their choices.

当夏洛特走向坐在吧台边的鲍勃时，气氛开始紧张起来。当天早些时候，她和他交换了一个微笑，但万一他其实是个傲慢无趣的人，或者他发现夏洛特是个狂热的粉丝呢？“我该和这个陌生人搭讪，还是独自喝酒？”这个问题在两人脑海中盘旋。这种犹豫不决加剧了场景开篇时那种舒适的独处与充满风险的亲密之间的张力，并影响着他们的选择。

Once they dare to converse, however, a deeper, instinctive need inspires them to move from a chat to confession. As they reveal unpleasant home truths about themselves, intimacy wins out over isolation. That step then ignites yet another value: lost in life versus found in life. Lost/found becomes the story’s core value.

然而，一旦他们鼓起勇气交谈，一种更深层次、更本能的需求便驱使他们从闲聊走向坦白。当他们袒露自己不为人知的真相时，亲密战胜了孤独。这一步又引出了另一个价值：迷失于人生还是寻回于人生。迷失/寻回成为了故事的核心价值。

As the film’s title suggests, Bob and Charlotte, each in their own way, feel lost. When the scene opens, lost/found sits squarely at the negative. Over the course of the scene, it never touches the positive; rather, it sinks to the bleakness of Beat 15. At the same time, however, the charge of isolation/intimacy arcs toward the light and by the capping beat, their relationship touches an immediate and natural closeness.

正如影片标题所示，鲍勃和夏洛特各自以不同的方式感到迷茫。场景伊始，迷失/寻回的矛盾便牢牢占据了负面情绪。在整个场景中，它始终没有触及正面，反而沉入了第15拍的阴郁之中。然而，与此同时，孤独/亲密的张力却逐渐向光明倾斜，到了最后一个拍子，他们的关系也达到了一种自然而然的亲密。

At the end of each beat, I have scored its value charge (+) for positive, (-) for negative, (++) for doubly positive, etc.

在每个节拍结束时，我都会记录它的值，正值记为 (+)，负值记为 (-)，正负值记为 (++)，等等。

Read the scene (printed in bold) straight through to get a feel of the dialogue’s minimalist language. Then review it against my notes on the arc of its beats, subtext, and value charges.

请通读这段场景（以粗体字标出），感受对话的极简语言风格。然后对照我的笔记，分析其节奏、潜台词和价值取向。

INT. PARK HYATT BAR—NIGHT

柏悦酒店酒吧内景——夜晚

Bob sits alone over a drink.

鲍勃独自一人坐在那里喝酒。

BEAT 1

节拍 1

BOB

鲍勃

(to the Barman)

（对酒保说）

He got married a couple of times to some nice women, beautiful women, too, I mean you and I would be crazy for these women, but there were always rumors. I never liked his acting, so I never gave a damn whether he was straight or not.

他结过几次婚，娶的都是些不错的女人，而且都很漂亮，我的意思是，换作你我，肯定会为她们神魂颠倒，但总是有各种传闻。我从来都不喜欢他的演技，所以他是不是异性恋我根本不在乎。

ACTION: Bob trying to impress the Barman.

剧情：鲍勃试图给酒吧招待留下好印象。

REACTION: The Barman pretending he’s impressed.

反应：酒保假装很佩服。

Intimacy/Isolation (-)

亲密/孤独 (-)

Rather than starting with that all-too-familiar image of a solitary man sitting at a bar, staring into the back of his head, Coppola opens the scene with showbiz chitchat. A Hollywood star gossiping to a Japanese Barman makes Bob’s loneliness character-specific and poignant. This first beat hits an amusing note that counterpoints the dark beat that climaxes the scene.

科波拉并没有采用人们耳熟能详的孤身男子坐在酒吧里，目光呆滞地望着后脑勺的画面，而是以一段娱乐圈的闲聊作为开场。一位好莱坞明星与一位日本酒保闲聊，使得鲍勃的孤独感更加鲜明，也更令人心酸。这轻松诙谐的开场与之后场景高潮的阴郁氛围形成了鲜明的对比。

BEAT 2

节拍 2

Charlotte steps up to the bar. The Barman pulls out a stool near Bob.

夏洛特走到吧台前。酒保拉出一张凳子，放在鲍勃旁边。

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

(to Barman)

（对酒吧招待说）

Thank you.

谢谢。

(to Bob)

（对鲍勃说）

Hi.

你好。

(to Barman as she sits)

（对坐着的酒吧老板说）

Thanks.

谢谢。

ACTION: The Barman seating her.

动作：酒保安排她入座。

REACTION: Charlotte fitting in.

反应：夏洛特融入其中。

Intimacy/Isolation (-)

亲密/孤独 (-)

When composing a scene, ask this question before committing to any line of dialogue: At this precise moment, what are my character’s choices of action? Which tactic could she take? Which does she take? Every choice of tactic suggests a quality in the character’s nature and determines the words she’ll use to carry it out. Once again, dialogue is the outer result of inner action.

构思场景时，在确定任何一句台词之前，先问自己这个问题：在这一刻，我的角色有哪些行动选择？她可以采取哪种策略？她最终选择了哪种策略？每一种策略选择都体现了角色性格中的某种特质，并决定了她将用何种语言来表达这种特质。再次强调，对话是内在行为的外在表现。

So, what are Charlotte’s reactions, choices, and tactics as she enters this all-but-deserted bar and sees a world-famous movie star sitting on a stool alone? She could be intimidated and leave, she could give him his privacy and take a table, or she could sit within talking distance.

那么，当夏洛特走进这家几乎空无一人的酒吧，看到一位世界知名的电影明星独自坐在吧台凳上时，她的反应、选择和策略会是什么呢？她可能会感到害怕而离开，她可能会尊重他的隐私而找个桌子坐下，或者她可能会坐在离他较近的地方交谈。

As the Barman offers her a stool, she makes the boldest choice of the three and joins Bob. Her choice to sit, at the risk of embarrassment, expresses poise.

酒保给她递上凳子时，她做出了三人中最勇敢的选择，坐到了鲍勃旁边。她冒着尴尬的风险选择坐下，这展现了她的沉着冷静。

BEAT 3

节拍 3

BARMAN

酒吧招待

What can I get you?

您想喝点什么？

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

Hmmm… I’m not sure… hmmm.

嗯……我不太确定……嗯。

ACTION: The Barman attending to her.

行动：酒保正在为她服务。

REACTION: Charlotte testing her welcome.

反应：夏洛特在试探大家是否欢迎她。

Intimacy/Isolation (-)

亲密/孤独 (-)

Again, choices: Charlotte could have ordered her favorite drink immediately. But tensed by the risk she’s taking, she hesitates and gives Bob a chance to react. What he does now tells her whether or not she’s actually welcome.

再次面临选择：夏洛特本可以立刻点她最喜欢的饮料。但由于担心风险，她犹豫了，给了鲍勃一个反应的机会。鲍勃接下来的举动将决定她是否真的受欢迎。

BEAT 4

节拍 4

BOB

鲍勃

(quoting his commercial)

（引用他的广告语）

For relaxing times, make it—

放松的时候，可以这样做——

BOB & BARMAN

鲍勃和酒吧老板

(in unison)

（异口同声）

“Suntory time!”

“三得利时间！”

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

I’ll have a vodka tonic.

我要一杯伏特加汤力。

Bob glances at her, impressed.

鲍勃瞥了她一眼，印象深刻。

ACTION: Bob making her feel at home.

行动：鲍勃让她感觉像在家里一样。

REACTION: Charlotte joining in.

反应：夏洛特也加入了进来。

REACTION: Bob endorsing her choice.

反应：鲍勃支持她的选择。

Intimacy/Isolation (+)

亲密/孤独 (+)

Bob’s choice of self-ridicule makes her feel welcome. As she orders a serious drink, he nods in approval, and their sense of intimacy versus isolation moves toward the positive. Two strangers settle in to talk.

鲍勃的自嘲方式让她感到自在。当她点了一杯酒时，他点头表示赞许，两人之间的亲密感从疏离感转向了积极的一面。两个陌生人就这样坐下来开始交谈。

Bob’s self-ridicule announces a character dimension: Actors take their work, even in commercials, seriously, but he chooses to mock himself. This choice of action reveals an inner contradiction between his artist’s pride and self-disdain.

鲍勃的自嘲揭示了他性格的一个侧面：演员们对待工作非常认真，即使是拍广告也不例外，但他却选择嘲弄自己。这种行为选择揭示了他内心深处艺术家的骄傲与自我厌恶之间的矛盾。

BEAT 5

节拍 5

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

(to Bob as the Barman leaves for her drink)

（酒保离开去给她倒酒时，鲍勃听了）

So what are you doing here?

你在这里做什么？

BOB

鲍勃

Couple of things… Taking a break from my wife, forgetting my son’s birthday, and, ah, getting paid two million dollars to endorse a whiskey when I could be doing a play somewhere.

有几件事……和妻子分手，忘记了儿子的生日，还有，唉，本可以去某个地方演话剧，却拿了200万美元代言威士忌。

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

(staring in disbelief)

（难以置信地瞪大了眼睛）

Oh.

哦。

ACTION: Charlotte inviting a conversation.

行动：夏洛特邀请对方交谈。

REACTION: Bob confessing to his three chief failures in life.

反应：鲍勃坦白了他人生中的三大失败。

REACTION: Charlotte concealing her shock.

反应：夏洛特掩饰着震惊。

Lost/Found (--)

失物招领 (--)

Charlotte opens a door to the unexpected. If you were her, imagine your reaction as you sit next to a world-famous movie star whom you think leads an enviable lifestyle, ask him how he’s doing, and, offhandedly, he tells you that his life is misery. The phrase “taking a break” doesn’t tell Charlotte whether Bob blames himself, his wife, or both for his marital problems, but he clearly damns himself for forgetting his son’s birthday and, most of all, for corrupting his creative life by choosing money over art.

夏洛特打开了一扇通往意想不到之事的门。如果你是她，想象一下，当你坐在一位你认为生活令人艳羡的世界级影星旁边，问他近况如何，而他却漫不经心地告诉你，他的生活糟透了。“休息一下”这句话并没有告诉夏洛特，鲍勃是在责怪自己、妻子，还是两者都有责任，但他显然在自责自己忘记了儿子的生日，更重要的是，他痛恨自己为了金钱而放弃了艺术，从而毁掉了自己的创作生涯。

Bob’s declaration of failure not only surprises Charlotte, but it crosses a red line—that formal distance we traditionally keep between strangers and ourselves. His trespass puts Charlotte under a bit of pressure. Now that the personal value of lost/found has entered the conversation, she wonders if she should take a giant step toward intimacy and add her confession to his. She does. Bob’s revelation wrenches their chat into cycles of confession.

鲍勃坦白失败，不仅让夏洛特感到惊讶，更越过了一条红线——我们传统上与陌生人保持的那种正式距离。他的越界行为让夏洛特感到有些压力。既然失而复得的个人意义已经融入到谈话中，她不禁开始思考，自己是否应该迈出亲密的一步，也向他坦白自己的经历。她最终选择了坦白。鲍勃的坦白让他们的对话陷入了坦白的循环之中。

BEAT 6

节拍 6

BOB

鲍勃

But the good news is the whiskey works.

但好消息是，威士忌确实有效。

She laughs.

她笑了。

ACTION: Bob soothing her feelings.

行动：鲍勃安慰她。

REACTION: Charlotte sympathizing.

反应：夏洛特表示同情。

Intimacy/Isolation (+)

亲密/孤独 (+)

This beat of mutual empathy takes them a smidge closer to intimacy. Bob’s confession in Beat 5 upset her, but he’s sensitive enough to see what he has done and regret it. He quickly softens the moment with a joke. She, in return, sees that he’s embarrassed, so she laughs in sympathy to ease his chagrin.

这种相互理解的默契让他们之间的亲密关系更进一步。鲍勃在第五段的坦白让她感到难过，但他足够敏感，意识到自己的错误并感到后悔。他很快用一个玩笑缓和了气氛。她也看出他很尴尬，于是笑着安慰他，减轻他的窘迫。

BEAT 7

节拍 7

BOB

鲍勃

What are you doing?

你在干什么？

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

Hmmm, ah, my husband’s a photographer, so he’s working, and, hmmm, I wasn’t doing anything, so I came along. And we have some friends who live here.

嗯，啊，我丈夫是摄影师，所以他在工作，嗯，我没事干，所以就来了。而且我们还有几个朋友住在这里。

ACTION: Bob inviting her confession.

行动：鲍勃邀请她坦白。

REACTION: Charlotte confessing to an empty, perhaps troubled personal life.

反应：夏洛特坦白自己拥有空虚、或许还有问题的个人生活。

Lost/Found (--)

失物招领 (--)

From the moment their eyes met in Beat 4, they communicate openly and honestly. Cocktail chat becomes in vino veritas. In Beat 5 Bob dared an intimate confession, and now he tempts her to join him. Once again choices: She could have replied, “Oh, I’m having a wonderful time. My husband’s on a photo shoot and I’m enjoying some old friends.” Instead, her passive, tepid phrases imply the unflattering truth of her married life. Bob reads her troubled subtext.

从第四幕他们目光交汇的那一刻起，他们便坦诚相待。酒后闲聊变成了酒后吐真言。第五幕，鲍勃鼓起勇气向她坦白心事，现在他又想引诱她加入。她再次面临选择：她本可以回答说：“哦，我过得很开心。我丈夫去拍照片了，我和老朋友们在一起玩得很开心。”然而，她被动而平淡的措辞却暗示了她婚姻生活中不为人知的真相。鲍勃读懂了她话语中隐藏的不安。

BEAT 8

节拍 8

Bob lights her cigarette.

鲍勃帮她点烟。

BOB

鲍勃

How long have you been married?

你们结婚多久了？

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

Oh, thank you.

哦，谢谢。

(pause)

（暂停）

Two years.

两年。

BOB

鲍勃

Twenty-five long ones.

二十五个长条状的。

ACTION: Bob readying his pass.

动作：鲍勃准备传球。

REACTION: Charlotte preparing to take it.

反应：夏洛特准备接球。

REACTION: Bob making his pass.

反应：鲍勃传球成功。

Intimacy/Isolation (--)

亲密/孤独（--）

Charlotte has just confessed that her married life is unfulfilling, so Bob cannot resist making a pass at this beautiful young woman by complaining about his unfulfilled married life.

夏洛特刚刚坦白说她的婚姻生活并不幸福，所以鲍勃忍不住向这位美丽的年轻女子示好，抱怨自己不幸福的婚姻生活。

Note how Coppola has the older man make his move: He reacts to his own action. He asks Charlotte how long she’s been married, knowing that whatever number she might name, he can top it with a quarter century of dissatisfaction.

注意科波拉是如何安排年长男子采取行动的：他对自己的行为做出了反应。他问夏洛特结婚多久了，他知道无论她报出什么数字，他都能用四分之一世纪的不满来超越她。

Note also Charlotte’s choice. As he lights her cigarette, she sees the pass coming and could have deflected it by answering, “Two wonderful years,” or more aggressively, with a question of her own, “Why do you ask?” Instead, she lets it skate.

还要注意夏洛特的选择。当他为她点烟时，她预感到他要搭讪，本可以回答“美好的两年”来回避，或者更主动地反问“你为什么这么问？”。但她却选择了放任不管。

But make no mistake. This is a sexual proposition. How serious is hard to say. Bob could be doing it out of masculine ritual, but when a middle-aged guy laments his lengthy, less-than-happy marriage to a young woman at a bar, he’s hoping for more than sympathy.

但请不要误会，这是一种性暗示。至于程度如何，很难说。鲍勃或许只是出于男性惯常的礼仪，但当一个中年男人在酒吧里抱怨自己与年轻女子漫长而并不幸福的婚姻时，他想要的绝不仅仅是同情。

Bob’s pass could push Charlotte away, but instead, she moves closer:

鲍勃的传球可能会把夏洛特推开，但结果却是她更靠近了他：

BEAT 9

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

You’re probably having a midlife crisis.

你可能正经历中年危机。

(pause)

（暂停）

你买保时捷了吗？

BOB

鲍勃

(amused)

（笑着）

You know, I was thinking about buying a Porsche.

你知道吗，我之前一直在考虑买辆保时捷。

行动：夏洛特破坏了他的传球。

REACTION: Bob complimenting her wit.

反应：鲍勃称赞她机智幽默。

Intimacy/Isolation (+)

亲密/孤独 (+)

Charlotte knows his pass is halfhearted at best, and so she teases him about his age in order to say “No” with a touch of kindness. He graciously acknowledges her wit.

夏洛特知道他的拒绝最多也只是敷衍了事，所以她拿他的年龄开玩笑，好委婉地拒绝他。他欣然接受了她的幽默。

BEAT 10

击败 10

Twenty-five years… that’s, ah… well, it’s impressive.

二十五年……嗯……真是令人印象深刻。

Well, you figure, you sleep one-third of your life. That knocks off eight years of marriage right there. So you’re, you know, you’re down to sixteen and change, and, you know, you’re just a teenager… like marriage… you can drive it, but you can… there’s still the occasional accident.

嗯，你想想，你一生中有三分之一的时间都在睡觉。这样一来，你的婚姻就少了八年。所以，你知道，你只剩下十六年多一点的时间，你知道，你就像个青少年……婚姻就像驾驶，你可以驾驭它，但你……还是会偶尔出点小意外。

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

(laughing)

（笑）

Yeah…

是的…

ACTION: Charlotte offering a silver lining.

行动：夏洛特带来了一线希望。

REACTION: Bob confessing his rocky marriage.

反应：鲍勃坦白自己婚姻不顺。

REACTION: Charlotte complimenting his wit.

反应：夏洛特称赞他机智幽默。

Lost/Found (--)

失物招领 (--)

From previous scenes, we know Charlotte has doubts about her husband and her future. When she tries to compliment Bob’s marriage, he reminds her of a reality she knows from her own life: Relationships rarely live up to our dreams. Bob softens that harsh truth with a deft comparison of marriage to teen driving, but his cynical answer offers no hope. Nonetheless, Charlotte laughs to compliment his insight.

从之前的剧情来看，我们知道夏洛特对丈夫和未来都心存疑虑。当她试图称赞鲍勃的婚姻时，鲍勃却提醒她一个她自己也深有体会的现实：爱情很少能如我们所愿。鲍勃用婚姻比作青少年开车来缓和这个残酷的真相，但他那愤世嫉俗的回答依然让人感到绝望。尽管如此，夏洛特还是笑着称赞他的见解。

Note that Beats 4, 5, 8, and 10 play in three steps, rather than the conventional two. Normally, a new action immediately follows an action/reaction. Instead, these beats run action/reaction/reaction. When a reaction triggers yet another reaction, it often signals a deeper connection between the characters, a greater sense of intimacy.

请注意，第 4、5、8 和 10 拍的节奏是三步式的，而非传统的两步式。通常情况下，新的动作会紧接着一个动作/反应。而这些节奏则是动作/反应/反应的循环。当一个反应引发另一个反应时，通常预示着角色之间更深层次的联系，一种更强烈的亲密感。

As Oscar-winning screenwriter Philip Yordan put it: “Do not drown your script with endless dialogue and long speeches. Every question does not call for a response. Whenever you can express an emotion with a silent gesture, do so. Once you pose the question, permit it to linger before you get a reply. Or better yet, perhaps the character cannot reply; he or she has no answer. This permits the unspoken response to hang in midair.”

正如奥斯卡获奖编剧菲利普·约丹所说：“不要让你的剧本充斥着无休止的对话和冗长的独白。并非每个问题都需要回答。只要你能用无声的肢体语言表达情感，就去做。一旦你提出问题，就让它停留片刻，然后再给予回应。或者更好的是，也许角色无法回答；他或她没有答案。这让未说出口的回应悬而未决。”

Having made his second confession in Beat 10, Bob draws Charlotte out again, and she confesses that, like her personal life, her professional life is adrift.

在第 10 节拍中，鲍勃第二次坦白后，他又把夏洛特拉了出来，夏洛特坦白说，就像她的个人生活一样，她的职业生涯也处于迷茫状态。

The world-weary Bob offers hope encrusted with irony. Charlotte’s laugh lets him know she gets it, and then she needles him with:

饱经世故的鲍勃带着一丝讽刺的希望。夏洛特的笑声让他知道她明白了，然后她又揶揄了他一句：

They both get it: Unhappy as they are, they won’t lie to themselves. Sharing this tough truth draws them closer yet.

他们都明白：尽管都不快乐，但他们不会自欺欺人。分享这个残酷的真相反而让他们更加亲近。

(toasting)

（祝酒）

REACTION: Bob joining her celebration.

This upbeat gesture prepares for the downbeat turning point that caps the scene.

这一欢快的举动为接下来令人沮丧的转折点做好了铺垫，该转折点将为这一幕画上句号。

BEAT 15

击败 15

A long pause.

一阵长久的沉默。

CHARLOTTE

夏洛特

I wish I could sleep.

我真想睡觉。

BOB

鲍勃

我也是。

Another long pause.

又是一阵漫长的沉默。

ACTION: Charlotte confessing she feels lost within herself.

剧情：夏洛特坦白说她感到迷失在自己之中。

REACTION: Bob confessing that he, too, feels lost.

反应：鲍勃坦言，他也感到迷茫。

Lost/Found (---)

失物招领 (---)

Intimacy/Isolation (++++)

亲密/孤独（++++）

The lines “I wish I could sleep” and “Me, too” intimate a subtext of suffering as moving as any I can remember.

“我希望我能睡着”和“我也是”这两句话暗示了一种痛苦的潜台词，这种痛苦是我记忆中最令人动容的。

Sleep restores sanity. Without it, existence becomes a mad, ticking clock. When you toss and turn, unstoppable racing thoughts send worries and fears swirling and churning through the mind. Charlotte and Bob cannot sleep. Why not? Jet lag? Racing thoughts?

睡眠能使人恢复理智。没有睡眠，生活就像一个疯狂滴答作响的时钟。辗转反侧时，纷乱的思绪会像脱缰的野马般在脑海中翻腾，带来各种担忧和恐惧。夏洛特和鲍勃睡不着。为什么呢？是时差反应？还是思绪纷乱？

In my reading of the subtext, their sleeplessness has a deeper cause. As their confessions reveal, they feel cast off from their marriages, adrift in their working lives, and at sea within themselves. A hollow place has opened up inside both that neither family nor work can fill. Charlotte and Bob have lost their purpose in life.

在我看来，他们的失眠背后有着更深层次的原因。正如他们的自白所揭示的，他们感到被婚姻抛弃，在工作中迷失方向，内心也一片茫然。他们内心深处出现了一个空洞，家庭和工作都无法填补。夏洛特和鲍勃失去了人生的意义。

Character and Dialogue

人物与对话

As the film’s title suggests, the co-protagonists cannot translate their emptiness into fullness; they cannot imagine their future; they cannot interpret life’s absurdity into meaning. In more romantic times, Charlotte and Bob would have been known as “lost souls.”

正如影片片名所示，两位主人公无法将内心的空虚转化为充实；他们无法想象未来；他们无法将生活的荒诞解读为意义。在更浪漫的年代，夏洛特和鲍勃会被称为“迷失的灵魂”。

Notice how Coppola’s aesthetic avoids verbal combat and uses casual, offhanded behavior to imply private battles waged behind a smile. She then squeezes vast content into the fewest, simplest monosyllables: “Well, I’m sure you’ll figure out the angles,” and “Yeah, I hope your Porsche works out.” How does she do it?

注意科波拉的审美是如何避免言语交锋，而是用随意、漫不经心的举止来暗示笑容背后进行的私人斗争。然后，她用最少、最简单的单音节词语，将丰富的内容浓缩成一句句精炼的话语：“嗯，我相信你会找到解决办法的。”以及“是啊，我希望你的保时捷一切顺利。”她是怎么做到的？

First, backstory. Like the scene from The Museum of Innocence , Coppola could have her characters narrate past conflicts vividly and explicitly. Instead, she keeps the dramas offscreen and implicit. Bob and Charlotte narrate three stories apiece—marriage, career, and private self. They end each storyline in a loss and do it with superb economy of language. Bob: “taking a break from my wife/endorsing a whiskey when I could be doing a play.” Charlotte: “he’s working and I wasn’t doing anything.” They tell each unhappy tale with a charm, wit, and self-mockery that guides us around their world-weary facades to their ongoing inner conflicts.

首先，让我们回顾一下背景。就像《纯真博物馆》里的场景一样，科波拉完全可以让她的人物生动而直白地讲述过去的冲突。但她并没有这样做，而是将这些戏剧冲突隐藏在镜头之外，以隐晦的方式呈现。鲍勃和夏洛特各自讲述了三个故事——婚姻、事业和个人生活。每个故事线都以失去告终，而且他们用极其精炼的语言表达了这一点。鲍勃说：“我本可以演话剧，却在为威士忌代言，而我却在和妻子分手。”夏洛特则说：“他在工作，而我却无所事事。”他们用一种魅力、智慧和自嘲的方式讲述着每一个不幸的故事，引导我们透过他们饱经世故的外表，最终触及他们内心持续不断的冲突。

Second, the pause for subtext. Notice how Bob and Charlotte enter sentences on glides such as “Well…,” “Yeah…,” and “Yes…,” putting a thought-filled mini-pause before most everything they say. The actors also space their words with vocalized moments of reflection such as “Oh…,” “Ah…,” and “Hmmm…,” plus non-vocalized reactions of laughter, nods, glances, pauses with eye contact, and pauses staring into space. These hesitations, short and long, halt the words coming out of the character and invite the audience inside. A mini-pause opens space for thought.

其次，是用于表达潜台词的停顿。注意鲍勃和夏洛特是如何用“嗯……”、“是啊……”、“没错……”之类的语气来切入句子的，几乎每句话前面都会有一个充满思考的短暂停顿。演员们还会穿插一些表达思考的语气，比如“哦……”、“啊……”、“嗯……”，以及一些无声的反应，例如笑声、点头、眼神交流、眼神凝视和凝视远方。这些或长或短的停顿，让角色的话语戛然而止，引导观众进入角色的内心世界。短暂的停顿为思考留出了空间。

Third, naturalistic characterizations. In many of his lines, Bob Harris, a world-famous action actor, sounds in-character. Phrases such as “I never gave a damn whether he was straight or not,” “figure the angles,” “a good buck in that racket,” and “the whiskey works” could have been said by any of the tough-guy characters he plays. Now they infuse his personality.

第三，自然主义的人物塑造。世界知名的动作演员鲍勃·哈里斯在很多台词中都听起来像是角色自带的语气。诸如“我才不在乎他是直男还是女”、“算算角度”、“这行能赚大钱”、“威士忌工厂”之类的短语，他扮演的任何一个硬汉角色都可能说过。而现在，这些台词却融入了他的人物性格之中。

Charlotte’s vocabulary, in sharp contrast to Bob’s, consists of passive verbs and generalized nouns, absent a single adjective, adverb, or superlative that might add color: “I hope,” “I wish I could,” and “I’m not sure” said twice. Her tone is pleasant but her vocabulary reflects her achromatic, motionless life.

与鲍勃截然不同，夏洛特的词汇主要由被动语态动词和概括性名词构成，缺少一个形容词、副词或最高级来增添色彩：“我希望”、“我希望我能”，以及“我不确定”，而且“我不确定”说了两遍。她的语气和蔼可亲，但她的词汇却反映了她单调乏味、毫无生气的生活。

Value Progression and Dialogue

价值发展与对话

Once we separate the activity of talk from the actions the characters take, the shape of the scene shines through, as escalating value charges progress the dialogue from the first beat to the last.

一旦我们将对话活动与角色采取的行动分开，场景的轮廓就会显现出来，因为不断升级的价值压力推动着对话从第一个节拍到最后一个节拍。

Coppola designed her scene as a downward spiral that builds its negative power three times over. She progresses it through a series of tumbling confessions that take loss from bad to worse to worst.

科波拉将这场戏设计成一个不断下坠的螺旋，其负面力量三重叠加。她通过一系列接连不断的忏悔，将失去的痛苦从糟糕推向更糟，最终走向毁灭。

First, Bob confesses that as a husband and a father, he’s a fraud, faking his way through his personal life (bad). Charlotte confesses that she’s just tagging along after a husband who loves his work more than her (bad). Bob confesses that he’s a sellout. He should be working as a serious actor; instead, he’s pushing booze (worse). Charlotte admits that she has no career or even the plans for one, and so her life outside of marriage has no direction and no purpose (worse). Then the last beat takes them to the basement. They each confess that they cannot sleep (the worst).

首先，鲍勃坦白说，作为丈夫和父亲，他是个骗子，在个人生活中一直伪装（糟糕）。夏洛特也坦白说，她只是依附于一个更爱工作胜过爱她的丈夫（糟糕）。鲍勃坦白说，他是个叛徒。他本该成为一名严肃的演员，却沦落到贩卖酒类（更糟）。夏洛特承认自己没有事业，甚至连事业规划都没有，所以婚姻之外的生活毫无方向和目标（更糟）。最后，他们来到地下室。两人都坦白说自己睡不着（最糟糕的）。

By building the scene around confessions, Coppola peels away the characters’ personae, so they can see each other for who they are. These lost souls confess to expose themselves. To be seen.

通过围绕忏悔展开的场景构建，科波拉层层剥开人物的伪装，让他们得以看清彼此的真面目。这些迷失的灵魂忏悔是为了袒露自己，为了被看见。

Why do these confessions feel progressive and not random? To begin with, Bob and Charlotte live parallel lives: Both have failed in all of life’s arenas. Coppola then composes their confessions so that they alternate in descending order. Which is worse? A personal loss in your private relationships or a professional loss in your working life?

为什么这些忏悔感觉像是循序渐进的，而不是随机的？首先，鲍勃和夏洛特的人生轨迹几乎平行：两人在人生的各个领域都遭遇了失败。科波拉巧妙地安排他们的忏悔，使之按失败程度递减的顺序交替出现。究竟哪种更糟糕？是私人关系中的个人损失，还是职业生涯中的职业挫折？

Professional failure. Why? Because failed relationships are a mutual loss. Neither person is entirely blameless, nor entirely at fault. When a relationship fails, you can lighten your load of guilt by heaping it on your partner.

事业上的失败。为什么？因为失败的感情关系是双方的损失。没有人完全无辜，也没有人完全是错的。当一段感情破裂时，你可以通过把责任推卸给伴侣来减轻自己的内疚感。

When you lose in your chosen career, however, you know the fault is yours alone. We may make excuses and blame “the system” or bad luck, but in our heart of hearts we know that if we lose in our calling, it will be due to our lack of discipline, talent, knowledge, judgment, or hard work… the usual gaps that spell professional disaster.

然而，当你在自己选择的职业道路上遭遇失败时，你明白这完全是自己的过错。我们或许会找借口，把责任归咎于“体制”或运气不佳，但在内心深处，我们明白，如果我们在事业上失败，那一定是由于我们缺乏自律、天赋、知识、判断力或努力……这些通常会导致职业生涯失败的缺陷。

But still, is professional failure always worse than relationship failure? Does losing a job mean more than breaking up a marriage? The key to the bar scene is a build toward a loss of identity. So the question is not one of getting or losing a job; it’s one of gaining or losing your identity.

但是，事业上的失败总是比感情上的失败更糟糕吗？丢掉工作比婚姻破裂更可怕吗？酒吧文化的关键在于逐渐丧失自我认同。所以，问题不在于找到或失去工作，而在于获得或失去自我认同。

If, for example, a woman were married and had a job clerking at Walmart, then a loss of relationship may prove worse than being fired, because the woman’s likely source of identity comes more from marriage than a job.

例如，如果一个女人已婚，在沃尔玛做店员，那么失去婚姻关系可能比被解雇更糟糕，因为女人的身份认同更多地来源于婚姻而不是工作。

But neither of this film’s characters identifies with a marital relationship. Bob and Charlotte find their identities in themselves as artists. Therefore, for Bob and Charlotte, professional failure is far worse than relationship failure. Charlotte has made no effort to even name her ambition, let alone build a career. Later in the film, she hints at wanting to be a writer, but to date, she hasn’t written anything. Who but Charlotte is to blame for that? Bob is rich, famous, and in demand, but he chooses to waste his time and talent mugging for a liquor spot. Again, who but Bob is to blame for that?

但这部电影中的两个角色都不认同婚姻关系。鲍勃和夏洛特在艺术领域中找到了自我认同。因此，对他们来说，事业上的失败远比感情上的失败更糟糕。夏洛特甚至从未努力去明确自己的抱负，更别提建立事业了。影片后半段，她暗示自己想成为一名作家，但至今为止，她还没有写过任何作品。除了夏洛特，还能怪谁呢？鲍勃富有、有名、炙手可热，但他却选择浪费时间和才华去抢劫一家酒吧。同样，除了鲍勃，还能怪谁呢？

Coppola’s next twist of the knife is this: Which is worse? Professional failure or loss of self? Loss of self. Why? Because if we wanted to, we could decide that careers, fame, fortune, and even creative achievement are fleeting and illusionary. We could escape the public realm. Fine, but we have to live somewhere. If we cannot find our place in personal relationships, if we cannot find self-worth in professional achievement, what’s left? We must look inside and find a life of value within our being.

科波拉接下来抛出的问题是：哪个更糟？事业失败还是迷失自我？答案是迷失自我。为什么？因为如果我们愿意，我们可以认定事业、名望、财富，甚至创作成就都只是转瞬即逝的幻象。我们可以逃离公众视野。这当然可以，但我们总得有个栖身之所。如果我们无法在人际关系中找到自己的位置，如果我们无法在事业成就中找到自我价值，那我们还剩下什么？我们必须审视内心，在自身的存在中寻找生命的价值。

The dilemma at the heart of LOST IN TRANSLATION creates an existential crisis. Bob and Charlotte have no visible reason to be unhappy. They seem well educated, well off, well married, and surrounded by friends—in Bob’s case, by a world of fans. No, Bob and Charlotte are not lonely; they are lost.

《迷失东京》的核心困境引发了一场存在主义危机。鲍勃和夏洛特似乎没有任何不快乐的理由。他们受过良好的教育，家境优渥，婚姻美满，身边围绕着许多朋友——鲍勃更拥有庞大的粉丝群体。不，鲍勃和夏洛特并非孤独；他们只是迷失了方向。

The difference is this: You’re lonely when you have something to share but no one to share it with. You’re lost when you have nothing to share, no matter with whom you live. Of course, you can be both lonely and lost, but of the two, lost inflicts the greater pain.

区别在于：当你拥有可以分享的东西却无人分享时，你会感到孤独；当你一无所有，无论与谁同住，你都会感到迷茫。当然，你可能既感到孤独又感到迷茫，但两者相比，迷茫带来的痛苦更大。

Below are the beat by beat gerunds of action/reaction with the value charges they cause. Overall, the positive charges of isolation/intimacy alternate with the negative charges of lost/found to pace the scene dynamically without repetition:

以下是动作/反应的逐节动名词及其所引发的价值含义。总体而言，孤立/亲密的积极含义与失而复得的消极含义交替出现，使场景节奏动态变化而不重复：

BEAT 1: Impressing/Pretending

第一节：给人留下深刻印象/假装

Intimacy/Isolation (-)

亲密/孤独 (-)

Intimacy/Isolation (-)

Lost/Found Life (--)

第六拍：舒缓/同情

第 8 拍：准备/准备/传球

The personal revelations of losses in Beats 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, and 13 continually top each other in terms of the damage to their lives. In Beats 10 through 12, the characters’ confessions become all the more honest and all the more sad. When Charlotte and Bob toast the wreckage in Beats 13 and 14, their newfound intimacy lifts the mood for an instant, but it turns sharply into the powerful irony of Beat 15.

在第5、7、10、11、12和13个片段中，人物对失去亲人的痛苦的揭露，在对他们生活造成的伤害方面，一个比一个严重。在第10到12个片段中，人物的倾诉变得更加坦诚，也更加令人悲伤。当夏洛特和鲍勃在第13和14个片段中举杯庆祝时，他们之间新生的亲密关系短暂地缓解了气氛，但这种氛围却在第15个片段中急转直下，充满了强烈的讽刺意味。

In the pause that follows their third and most painful confession (“I wish I could sleep”/”Me, too”), each suddenly recognizes a kindred spirit. Their immediate desire is realized in Beat 15 as their lives shift from Isolation (-) to Intimacy (++++). With irony, of course: They can’t sleep (--), but they can talk (++); they’re lost souls (---) who connect with a mirror soul (++++).

在他们第三次也是最痛苦的告白（“我真想睡着”/“我也是”）之后的那段停顿中，他们突然意识到彼此是知己。他们的渴望在第15拍得以实现，他们的生活从孤独（-）转变为亲密（++++）。当然，这其中也带有讽刺意味：他们无法入睡（--），却能交谈（++）；他们是迷失的灵魂（---），却找到了彼此的灵魂镜像（++++）。

When you survey the gerunds that name their actions, notice how Charlotte and Bob mirror each other. When two people sit at a bar, unconsciously imitating each other’s posture and gestures, then echoing each other’s subtextual actions, they connect with an intimacy they themselves may not realize.

当你仔细观察用来描述他们动作的动名词时，你会发现夏洛特和鲍勃是如何互相映照的。当两个人坐在酒吧里，无意识地模仿彼此的姿势和手势，并呼应彼此的言外之意时，他们之间便建立起一种连自己可能都没意识到的亲密感。

The scene climaxes on an overall positive irony and a glimmer of hope. This quiet but surprisingly dynamic scene arcs from easy rapport to bleak loss to the possibility of love. The last beat hooks strong suspense for the rest of the film: Now that Bob and Charlotte have joined forces, will they grow into lives found?

这一幕最终以一种积极的讽刺和一丝希望达到高潮。这段看似平静却又充满张力的场景，从轻松的融洽关系，到令人沮丧的失落，再到爱情的可能，层层递进。最后一个转折点为影片接下来的剧情埋下了强烈的悬念：鲍勃和夏洛特携手并进，他们能否找到属于自己的人生？

#↩

19

MASTERING THE CRAFT

精通技艺

LISTEN

听

To master the technique of saying little but expressing much, first train your eye to see into the depths of the unsaid and the unsayable inside the people around you, then train your ear to hear the said. William Goldman, perhaps the finest writer of dialogue in film history, has often been complimented for having “the best ear in Hollywood.” If you think about it, however, the expression “an ear for dialogue” seems odd.

要想掌握少说多言的技巧，首先要训练你的眼睛去洞察身边人内心深处那些未说出口和难以言说的情感，然后训练你的耳朵去聆听那些已经说出口的话语。威廉·戈德曼或许是电影史上最杰出的对白编剧，他常被誉为“好莱坞最懂对白的人”。然而，仔细想想，“懂对白”这个说法似乎有些奇怪。

The phrase conveys an image of a writer with reportorial or stenographic gifts riding on buses and listening to the people around him talking, and then writing down what they say quickly and accurately. Well, I know William Goldman, and it has been a long time since he got around New York on buses. But wherever Goldman finds himself, he listens in a writer’s way, in depth, and so he hears far more than words said.

这句话描绘了一位拥有新闻写作或速记天赋的作家，乘坐公交车，倾听周围人们的谈话，然后迅速而准确地记录下来。我认识威廉·戈德曼，他很久以前就没坐公交车在纽约出行了。但无论戈德曼身处何地，他都会以作家的方式深入倾听，因此他听到的远不止是人们说的话。

Listen to life. From infanthood on, the future writer actively listens to real-world voices—their rhythms, tones, and jargons. No matter where you are, now and then eavesdrop on people, take mental notes, or jot down interesting turns of phrase and what they imply.

倾听生活。从孩提时代起，未来的作家就应该积极倾听现实世界的声音——它们的节奏、语调和用语。无论身处何地，都要时不时地偷听别人说话，记下要点，或者写下有趣的短语及其含义。

Talking is doing. So like William Goldman, listen to people on two levels: text versus subtext, what they say versus what they do. Listen to their word choices and grammar, to the way they shape their talk. Listen to the way people use words not to reveal but to conceal their actions. When you sense the unspoken, you discover the subtle tactics people take. Listen deeper yet to the unsayable, to the drives and desires that move beneath awareness and motivate actions. Listen for strategy, for talk as a social ploy. Listen to the way one person uses words to cause another person to react in a way that furthers the speaker’s desires.

言行一致。所以，就像威廉·戈德曼那样，倾听人们的言辞，要从两个层面入手：字面意义和潜台词，他们说的和他们做的。注意他们的用词和语法，注意他们如何组织语言。注意人们如何运用语言，不是为了揭示，而是为了掩盖他们的行为。当你感知到言外之意，你就能发现人们使用的微妙策略。更进一步，倾听那些难以言说的，那些潜藏在意识之下、驱动行动的驱动力和欲望。注意其中的策略，注意言语作为一种社交手段的作用。注意一个人如何运用语言，引导另一个人做出符合自己意愿的反应。

When you put your ear to the wall of society, you soon learn that although dialogue is far more economical than talk, it’s talk that builds your vocabulary. Our Internet-driven world forges marvelous new words by the minute. Terms like “tweet,” “hashtag,” “selfie,” and “narcisstick” (a stick to lengthen your selfie reach) are inspired by technology. But compound puns like manspreading (splaying your legs to keep other people from sitting next to you on the bus), lumbersexual (a fashionably rugged guy), budtender (a server in a pot shop), and linguisticky (a difficult word) are born out of the natural love of talk. Listen for such words around you or make them up yourself, and then put them to work in your storytelling.

当你仔细聆听社会的声音，很快就会发现，虽然对话比说话更简洁，但正是说话积累了词汇。我们这个互联网驱动的世界每时每刻都在创造着奇妙的新词。“tweet”（推特）、“hashtag”（话题标签）、“selfie”（自拍）和“narcisstick”（自拍杆，一种用来延长自拍距离的棍子）等词汇都源于科技。但像“manspreading”（张腿坐姿，指在公交车上张开双腿不让别人坐到自己旁边）、“lumbersexual”（伐木工人，指穿着时髦的粗犷男士）、“budtender”（大麻店服务员）和“linguisticky”（一个难懂的词）这样的复合双关语，则源于人们对说话的天然热爱。留意你周围出现的这类词汇，或者自己创造一些，然后把它们运用到你的故事讲述中。

Second, read the good and rewrite the bad. Working writers spend much of their non-writing time nose-deep in a book. They read novels and plays, screen and television scripts. They watch and listen to dialogue performed onstage and onscreen, big and small. They develop an ear for dialogue as a by-product of all the stories they’ve read and seen, colored by all the living talk that’s passed through their days.

其次，阅读好的，改写坏的。职业作家在写作之余的大部分时间都沉浸在书海中。他们阅读小说、戏剧、电影剧本和电视剧剧本。他们观看和聆听舞台和银幕上各种规模作品的对话。他们阅读和观看的所有故事，以及日常生活中耳濡目染的各种对话，都让他们逐渐培养出对对话的敏锐度。

Quentin Tarantino’s dialogue strikes a brilliant balance between a natural sound and high expressivity. No one in reality has ever spoken the way Tarantino’s characters talk, but audiences believe the patter as if it were recorded off the street. The imagistic dialogue of Tennessee Williams flows like wine from a decanter. No one can match novelist Elmore Leonard for creating high-styled repartee between lowlife characters. The dialogue of these renowned writers fits the ear like everyday talk, yet at the same time, expresses authentic characters with unique voices.

昆汀·塔伦蒂诺的对白在自然流畅与极富表现力之间达到了绝妙的平衡。现实生活中，没有人会像塔伦蒂诺笔下的人物那样说话，但观众却仿佛信以为真，完全沉浸在街头巷尾的对话中。田纳西·威廉姆斯的对白极富意象，如同美酒从醒酒器中缓缓流淌。埃尔莫·伦纳德笔下的底层人物之间妙语连珠，无人能及。这些著名作家的对白既贴近日常对话，又生动地刻画了人物鲜明的个性。

If, on the other hand, you find yourself reading a badly written script or book, don’t dismiss the writer and toss his pages aside. Go back and rewrite him. Scratch out his words and insert your own. Rewriting bad dialogue is the fastest, most efficient way I know to train your talents.

另一方面，如果你读到一篇写得很差的剧本或书，不要轻易否定作者，也不要把他的作品扔到一边。回去重写。把他的文字划掉，换上你自己的。重写糟糕的对话是我所知的最快、最有效的训练技巧的方法。

WRITE IN-CHARACTER

用角色语气写作

Scenes can be imagined from two possible angles: outside in or inside out.

场景可以从两个可能的角度来想象：由外而内或由内而外。

When an author writes from the outside in, she sits as if in an audience of one, tenth row center of her characters’ lives, observing her own imagination at work, watching scenes, overhearing dialogue. Given free rein to improvise, this technique can generate unlimited variations on every possible event. The writer sorts through these choices, testing them by trial and error until she finds an ideal sequence of beats that shapes her scene to and around its turning point.

当作者采用由外而内的写作手法时，她仿佛置身于一个只有她一个人的观众席，坐在笔下人物生活的第十排正中央，观察着自己的想象力如何运作，观看场景，聆听对话。这种技巧赋予她自由发挥的空间，可以对每一个可能的事件衍生出无限的变奏。作者会筛选这些选择，通过反复试验来检验，直到找到一个理想的节奏序列，将场景塑造到转折点及其前后。

This objective method, open-minded and elastic as it is, risks superficiality. If the writer always stays on the outside, always imagines her characters “over there,” her perceptions may shallow out and lose touch with the emotional currents that run through her characters’ inner lives, driving them to action, and then from action to talk. As a result, her dialogue will fall victim to the many flaws of content and form.

这种客观的方法虽然开放灵活，但也存在流于表面的风险。如果作者始终置身事外，总是把笔下的人物想象成“远在天边”，那么她的感知就会变得肤浅，无法捕捉到人物内心深处的情感脉动，而正是这些情感驱动着他们行动，最终又从行动走向对话。如此一来，她的对话就会受到内容和形式上诸多缺陷的影响。

For this reason, a writer also works from the inside out. She places herself at the center of her character’s being, that irreducible core of humanity that answers to the name “Me.” From this inner angle, she sees life through her character’s eyes; she experiences her imaginary events.

因此，作家也常常从内心出发进行创作。她将自己置于笔下人物的中心，将自己置于人性不可分割的核心——那个被称作“我”的存在——之中。从这个内在的视角出发，她透过人物的眼睛看待生活；她体验着人物的虚构经历。

In other words, the writer is the character’s first actor. Writers are improvisationists who enter all of their characters—man, woman, child, beast—to shape them from the inside out. She becomes her character, alive in the now, struggling to get what she wants, emotions and urges surging, taking action after action against the forces that thwart her desires. She feels what her character feels, her pulse pounding apace with her character’s heart. This subjective method of creating dialogue I call writing in-character .

换句话说，作家是角色的第一位演员。作家是即兴表演者，她们会进入所有角色——男人、女人、孩子、动物——的内心世界，由内而外地塑造他们。她化身为角色，活在当下，为了得到自己想要的东西而奋斗，情感和欲望汹涌澎湃，一次又一次地与阻碍她愿望的力量对抗。她感受着角色的感受，她的脉搏与角色的心跳同步跳动。这种主观的对话创作方法，我称之为“角色内写作”。

To write in-character, use the legendary acting coach Constantin Stanislavski’s concept of the “Magic If.” Do not ask, “If my character were in this situation, what would my character do?” because that puts you outside the role looking in. Do not ask, “If I were in this situation, what would I do?” because you are not the character. What you might feel, do, or say in any situation may have little or nothing to do with your character’s behaviors. Instead, ask: “If I were my character in this situation, what would I do?” Create out of your own being, but not as yourself, as your characters.

要进行角色扮演式的写作，请运用传奇表演教练康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基的“神奇的假设”概念。不要问“如果我的角色处于这种情况，他会怎么做？”，因为这会让你置身事外，以旁观者的身份审视角色。也不要问“如果我处于这种情况，我会怎么做？”，因为你不是角色。你在任何情况下的感受、行为或言语都可能与角色的行为几乎毫无关联。相反，你应该问：“如果我是角色，处于这种情况，我会怎么做？”创作源于你自身的体验，但不是以你自己的身份，而是以角色的身份。

In fact, when we look into the background of famous playwrights from Aristophanes to Shakespeare to Molière to Harold Pinter, we discover that they all began as actors. Acting, even for prose writers, may be the best preparation for the writing of dialogue.

事实上，当我们探究从阿里斯托芬到莎士比亚、莫里哀再到哈罗德·品特等著名剧作家的背景时，会发现他们最初都是演员。即使对于散文作家而言，表演或许也是撰写对话的最佳准备。

In her biography of her father, Mamie Dickens describes watching her father, Charles Dickens, at work:

在为父亲所作的传记中，玛米·狄更斯描述了她观看父亲查尔斯·狄更斯工作的情景：

I was lying on the sofa endeavoring to keep perfectly quiet, while my father wrote busily and rapidly at his desk, when he suddenly jumped from his chair and rushed to a mirror which hung near, and in which I could see the reflection of some extraordinary facial contortions which he was making. He returned rapidly to his desk, wrote furiously for a few moments, and then went again to the mirror. The facial pantomime was resumed, and then turning toward, but evidently not seeing, me, he began talking rapidly in a low voice. Ceasing this soon, however, he returned once more to his desk, where he remained silently writing until luncheon time. It was a most curious experience for me, and one of which, I did not until later years, fully appreciate the purport. Then I knew that with his natural intensity he had thrown himself completely into the character that he was creating, and that for the time being he had not only lost sight of his surroundings, but had actually became in action, as in imagination, the creature of his pen. 1

我躺在沙发上，努力保持安静，父亲则在书桌前飞快地写作。突然，他从椅子上跳起来，冲到附近的一面镜子前，我从镜子里看到他脸上扭曲的表情。他迅速回到书桌前，奋笔疾书了一会儿，然后又走到镜子前。他继续做着面部表情的表演，然后转向我——显然他并没有看到我——开始低声快速地说着什么。不过，他很快就停了下来，再次回到书桌前，一直默默地写作到午饭时间。这对我来说是一次非常奇特的经历，直到多年以后，我才完全理解其中的含义。那时我才明白，他凭借着天生的专注力，完全投入到他所创造的角色中，在那一刻，他不仅忘记了周围的一切，而且在行动中，就像在想象中一样，真正成为了他笔下的人物。

To encourage your character to speak in a manner true to her nature, do as Dickens did: act her out. Let her thoughts flood your mind, and then shape her language in all the contours of vocabulary, grammar, syntax, diction, trope, phrasing, phonetics, idiom, and pace. Pay close attention to verbal details and create a one-of-a-kind voice that catches the audience’s ear and lasts in its memory.

为了让你的角色说话符合她的本性，不妨效仿狄更斯：把她演绎出来。让她的思想充盈你的脑海，然后从词汇、语法、句法、措辞、修辞手法、短语、语音、习语和语速等各个方面塑造她的语言。仔细琢磨语言细节，创造出独一无二、引人入胜、令人难忘的声音。

If, after that, you still find yourself mired in clichés, I have another suggestion. Turn your computer off and go take improvisation classes. If you can invent dialogue on your feet in front of a class, you can certainly do it sitting alone at your desk.

如果之后你仍然发现自己深陷陈词滥调之中，我还有另一个建议。关掉电脑，去参加即兴表演课。如果你能在课堂上即兴创作对话，那么你当然也能独自坐在书桌前做到这一点。

Once you have created a scene from the inside out, reimagine it from the outside in. To fully develop your craft, alternate imagining scenes from both angles. Lastly, sit back as if you were a first-time reader or audience and let the scene go to work on you.

当你从内到外构建出一个场景后，再从外到内重新想象一遍。为了充分提升你的写作技巧，交替从这两个角度想象场景。最后，放松下来，就像你是第一次阅读或观看的读者或观众一样，让场景在你心中发挥作用。

Develop your dialogue skill by crafting words as an inner action that becomes an outer activity, and in those hours when your work flows smoothly from imagination to page, when you sense the rightness of your words, do not pause for analysis. Just keep moving. But if your scenes war with your senses, if confusion stifles creativity, what to do? Ask questions.

要提升你的对话技巧，就要把遣词造句当作一种内在的行动，最终转化为外在的表达。当你的灵感如泉涌般从脑海中流淌到纸上，当你感觉用词恰到好处时，不要停下来分析，继续创作。但如果你的场景与你的感官产生冲突，如果困惑扼杀了创造力，该怎么办？提出问题。

KEY QUESTIONS

关键问题

During the crafting of dialogue, doubts naturally stream through the mind. For which sense do I write? The eye or the ear? Too much description may stall into portraiture; too much dialogue may drone into recitations. How much is too much? Too little?

在构思对话的过程中，各种疑虑自然而然地涌上心头。我应该为哪种感官写作？视觉还是听觉？过多的描写可能会沦为肖像画；过多的对话可能会变成枯燥的背诵。多少才算过多？多少才算过少？

Debates over design and purpose: What does this line do for my character? For the beat? The scene? My story? Like Lady Justice, blindfolded and poised with a sword in one hand and a scale in the other, every author weighs the balance of image versus word, of word versus silence, in every scene she judges.

关于设计和目的的争论：这句台词对我的角色有什么作用？对节奏有什么作用？对场景有什么作用？对我的故事有什么作用？就像蒙着眼睛、一手拿剑一手拿天平的正义女神一样，每位作者在评判的每一个场景中，都会权衡图像与文字、文字与沉默之间的平衡。

Creativity isn’t learning the right answers but asking the strongest questions. To take your newfound knowledge of scene and dialogue design into creative practice, I’ve laid out a list of questions to guide your writing and rewriting into the furthest depths and breadths your talents can reach. Whenever you are stuck, get back on track by posing the questions below from each and every character’s point of view. Clear answers will not only renew momentum but also liberate your talent.

创造力并非在于学习正确答案，而在于提出最深刻的问题。为了帮助你将新近掌握的场景和对话设计知识运用到创作实践中，我列出了一系列问题，旨在引导你的写作和修改，让你的才华得以充分发挥。每当你遇到瓶颈时，不妨从每个角色的角度出发，思考以下问题，重回正轨。清晰的答案不仅能让你重拾创作动力，更能释放你的才华。

The answers to the following questions create the subtext that makes powerful dialogue possible:

以下问题的答案构成了对话的潜台词，而正是这些潜台词使得强有力的对话成为可能：

Background desires: What complex of background desires surrounds the character’s situation in life and his relationships with other characters? How do the background desires limit and control his choices of action and his use of language? What actions can he not take, at least not yet? What words can he not use, at least not yet?

背景欲望：人物的生活境遇以及他与其他人物的关系背后，存在着怎样的背景欲望？这些背景欲望如何限制和控制他的行动选择和语言运用？他现在不能做什么，至少目前还不能做什么？他现在不能说什么，至少目前还不能说什么？

Objects of desire: What does the character tell himself he wants in order to restore life’s balance? Looking into the subtext, does he also have a subconscious desire? If so, how do these two desires contradict each other?

欲望的对象：为了恢复生活的平衡，主人公告诉自己想要什么？深入分析文本的潜台词，他是否也有潜意识里的欲望？如果有，这两种欲望是如何相互矛盾的？

Super-intention: What need drives the character down his spine of action? Is it conscious only, or does another desire from his subconscious mind oppose him? Is he his own worst enemy?

超意识：是什么需求驱使着角色采取行动？这仅仅是意识层面的需求，还是潜意识中还有其他欲望在与之对抗？他是否是自己最大的敌人？

Scene intentions: At this moment, what is the character’s scene intention? What does he seem to want? For complex, multidimensional characters, also ask: What does he really want? What is his subconscious scene intention? Is his scene intention a step in his pursuit of his super-intention? In other words, does this scene make sense in light of the overall story arc?

场景意图：此时此刻，角色的场景意图是什么？他似乎想要什么？对于复杂、多维的角色，还要问：他真正想要的是什么？他潜意识里的场景意图是什么？他的场景意图是否是他追求更高意图的一个步骤？换句话说，从整体故事弧线来看，这个场景是否合理？

Motivation: Why does this character want what he wants?

动机：这个角色为什么想要他想要的东西？

Scene driver: Who drives this scene and makes it happen?

场景驱动者：谁来驱动这个场景并使其发生？

Forces of antagonism: What are the sources of conflict in the scene? Do they come from within the character? Other characters? The setting?

对抗力量：场景中的冲突根源是什么？是来自角色内心？其他角色？还是环境？

Scene value(s): What value(s) is at stake in the character’s life in this scene? What is the opening charge of the value(s)? The closing charge of value(s)?

场景价值：在这个场景中，角色生命中哪些价值岌岌可危？这些价值的开端是什么？结尾的价值又是什么？

Subtext : Beneath what the character seems to be doing, what is he actually doing? What tactics might the character use to pursue his scene intention?

潜台词：角色表面上的行为背后，他实际在做什么？角色可能会使用哪些策略来实现他的场景意图？

Beats: What specific action does the character take in the subtext of each line? What reactions might these actions cause? On which side of the beat does this line play? Is it an action or a reaction?

节奏：每句台词的潜台词中，人物具体采取了什么行动？这些行动可能会引起什么反应？这句台词处于节奏的哪一边？它是行动还是反应？

Progression: How do the beats progress my scene? Do they progressively top each other?

节奏推进：这些节拍是如何推动我的场景发展的？它们是否逐渐超越前者？

Tactics: With these words, said in this way, what specific tactic is the character taking? What effect is he trying to cause?

策略：通过这些话语，以这种方式表达，这个角色采取了什么具体的策略？他试图产生什么效果？

Turning point: How does the scene’s value(s) move in a positive/negative dynamic? Where is the scene’s turning point? In what precise beat of behavior does the value(s) change to the final charge?

转折点：场景中的价值观是如何在正负动态中变化的？场景的转折点在哪里？在哪个具体的行为节点上，价值观转变为最终的走向？

Deep character: How do the choices of action in this scene reveal the truth about my characters?

深刻的人物刻画：这一幕中人物的行动选择如何揭示了他们的真实性格？

Scene progression: How does this scene progress my story?

场景推进：这个场景如何推动我的故事发展？

These questions guide the final step:

这些问题将引导我们完成最后一步：

Text: Outwardly, what would my character say in order to get what he wants? What words and phrases might the character use to help him carry out his tactics, actions, and reactions?

文本：表面上，我的角色会说什么来达到他的目的？角色可能会使用哪些词语和短语来帮助他实施策略、行动和反应？

Exposition: What facts of history, society, and biography does this line contain? Are they dramatized invisibly or narratized explicitly? Do they come in too soon, too late, or at just the right moment?

阐述：这句话包含了哪些历史、社会和人物传记方面的事实？它们是以隐晦的方式呈现，还是以明确的叙述方式展现？它们出现得太早、太晚，还是恰到好处？

Characterization: Do the characters’ verbal styles match their particular personalities, backgrounds, and traits of characterization?

人物刻画：人物的语言风格是否与其特定的性格、背景和人物特征相符？

Ask and answer these questions on every beat. When in the middle of writing the scene’s dialogue, ask and answer these questions again. After you’ve written the scene, ask and answer these questions for a third time. The best questions create the best answers.

在每个节奏节点上都要问自己并回答这些问题。在编写场景对话的过程中，再次问自己并回答这些问题。场景写完后，第三次问自己并回答这些问题。最好的问题才能带来最好的答案。

LAST WORDS

遗言

The technique of writing in-character may, at first, seem daunting. But instinctively you’ve done this all your life. After every confrontation you’ve ever had with another person, what have you done? You’ve rerun the scene through your imagination, re-creating it and rewriting it the way it should have gone down. You’ve put yourself inside your own head and the head of your antagonist, and then imaginatively reinvented the conflict beat by beat. And I’ll bet that your rewrites of life are always vivid, always effective. To write dialogue, you essentially do the same thing you do when you rewrite life.

角色扮演写作技巧乍看之下或许令人望而生畏。但实际上，你一生都在本能地运用这种技巧。每次与他人发生冲突后，你会怎么做？你会在脑海中重现当时的场景，重新演绎，并按照它本应有的方式改写。你会设身处地地站在自己和对手的角度思考，然后逐一想象地重构冲突。我敢肯定，你对生活的重写总是生动鲜活、引人入胜。而写对话，本质上也是在做同样的事情——重写生活。

To create character-specific dialogue, you need to gather knowledge of human behavior through close observations of people around you and through reading both fiction and nonfiction. On the balance, however, the source of all fine character writing is rooted in self-knowledge. As Anton Chekhov said: “Everything I know about human nature I learned from me.”

要创作出符合人物性格的对话，你需要通过仔细观察周围的人以及阅读小说和非小说类作品来积累对人类行为的了解。然而，总的来说，所有优秀的人物塑造都源于对自身的了解。正如安东·契诃夫所说：“我对人性的所有认识都来自我自己。”

Ultimately, you find your characters in yourself; you find their words in your imagination. Ask the Magic If: “If I were this character in these circumstances, what would I do? What would I say?” Then listen for the honest answer, for it is always correct. You would do and say the human thing.

最终，你会发现你的角色就在你自身之中；你会发现他们的话语就在你的想象之中。问问自己：如果我是这个角色，身处这样的境地，我会做什么？我会说什么？然后倾听内心真实的答案，因为它永远是正确的。你会做出和说出人之常情。

The more you penetrate the mysteries of your own humanity, the more you’re able to understand the humanity of others and the unique ways they express it. As your self-awareness grows, you will discover you can be many people. You can create them, act them, and speak in their voices.

你越深入探索自身人性的奥秘，就越能理解他人的人性以及他们表达人性的独特方式。随着自我意识的增强，你会发现自己可以成为许多人。你可以创造他们，扮演他们，用他们的声音说话。

“Here’s looking at you, kid.”

“敬你一杯，孩子。”

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

关于作者

Robert McKee, a Fulbright Scholar, is the world’s most sought-after lecturer in the art of story. Over the last 30 years, he has mentored screenwriters, novelists, playwrights, poets, documentary makers, producers, and directors. McKee alumni include over 60 Academy Award winners, 200 Academy Award nominees, 200 Emmy Award winners, 1000 Emmy Award nominees, 100 Writers Guild of America Award winners, and 50 Directors Guild of America Award winners.

罗伯特·麦基是一位富布赖特学者，也是全球最炙手可热的叙事艺术讲师。在过去的30年里，他指导过编剧、小说家、剧作家、诗人、纪录片制作人、制片人和导演。麦基的学员中包括60多位奥斯卡金像奖得主、200多位奥斯卡金像奖提名者、200多位艾美奖得主、1000多位艾美奖提名者、100位美国编剧工会奖得主和50位美国导演工会奖得主。

MISSION STATEMENT

使命宣言

Twelve strives to publish singular books, by authors who have unique perspectives and compelling authority. Books that explain our culture; that illuminate, inspire, provoke, and entertain. Our mission is to provide a consummate publishing experience for our authors, one truly devoted to thoughtful partnership and cutting-edge promotional sophistication that reaches as many readers as possible. For readers, we aim to spark that rare reading experience—one that opens doors, transports, and possibly changes their outlook on our ever-changing world.

Twelve致力于出版独具匠心、视角独特且极具权威性的书籍，这些书籍阐释我们的文化，启迪智慧，激发灵感，引人深思，并带来愉悦的阅读体验。我们的使命是为作者提供完美的出版体验，真正致力于建立深思熟虑的合作关系，并运用前沿的推广策略，力求让更多读者受益。对于读者而言，我们旨在激发他们独特的阅读体验——开启新的篇章，带他们进入另一个世界，并可能改变他们对这个瞬息万变的世界的看法。

NOTES

笔记

Chapter One The Full Definition of Dialogue

第一章 对话的完整定义

1. John L. Austin, How to Do Things with Words, ed. J. O. Urmson and Marian Sbisà (Oxford, England: Oxford University Press, 1962).
